title: Fix evidence-integrity defects in /test-realistic harness (9 commits, 8 beads) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background

An external cold review refuted a prior session's `/er` PASS on [#8702](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8702), correct on 7 of 7 checkable claims. The root problem was not one bug: `testing_ui/realistic/` — the `/test-realistic` harness — contained evidence-integrity defects that let it report success it had not earned.

The worst was self-referential: `verify_evidence_bundle --check-provider` gated on `browser_mode`, and `browser_mode` was a hardcoded string literal. The gate could be satisfied by the very thing it was supposed to gate. Every provenance claim the harness had ever made was therefore unfalsifiable.

This PR fixes the harness, then exercises it live.

## Goals

1. Make each false-success route structurally impossible, not merely unlikely.
2. Prove every fix RED-before-GREEN — a failing test first, watched fail.
3. Run the harness live and report the result honestly, including what remains unproven.

## Tenets

**Beads:** `rev-k38yq`, `rev-qwirs`, `rev-3xrxp`, `rev-ui6ze`, `rev-s2opq`, `rev-keewa`, `rev-fw99d`, `rev-zavv8`, `rev-mwuoz`, `rev-px6ra` — all closed. `rev-k9oeh` — open, partially fixed (see Known Gaps). `rev-4fdst`, `rev-iacw4`, `rev-189zg`, `rev-x7mcv` — open, deferred by deliberate scope decision (see Known Gaps).

**Design decision — derive, don't assert.** Three defects were the same bug in three files: a hardcoded `browser_mode` literal duplicated across `runner.py`, `evidence_bundle.py`, and the per-turn capture path, drifting independently. Every fix derives the value from a single source of truth instead of adding a second assertion, and fails closed (`"mixed-or-unknown"`) on disagreement.

**Design decision — the degenerate-frame check has a producer half and a consumer half.** A consumer-only check would drift from the producer the same way `browser_mode` did. `_run_agent_in_tab` measures the frame it wrote and flags it; `validate_capture` rejects an unflagged degenerate frame.

**Design decision — batching is a schedule, not a contract change.** Reducing concurrency preserves 5 personas x 15 turns = 75 turns exactly. A regression test fails if anyone reduces the turn count to make a run fit.

**Design decision — bind turns by server evidence, not the model's paraphrase.** The original completion oracle required the model to echo the submitted action text verbatim. It was never contracted to do that, so genuinely-correct turns were flagged as unbound. The replacement binds on server-observable facts (story advanced, rendered UI matches the persisted latest, a unique AGY exchange id per turn) instead, with the paraphrase still recorded as a visible anomaly rather than silently dropped.

- **Fix the liar before trusting anything it says.** Provenance was P0; everything downstream inherited its doubt.
- **A test that cannot fail is not evidence.** Every fix was re-verified against pre-fix code in an isolated tree with module identity asserted.
- **Report the gap.** Where a claim is unproven, this PR says so rather than omitting it.

## User Stories

- As an engineer reading an evidence bundle, I can trust `browser_mode` because it is derived from the session actually used, not asserted.
- As an engineer, a bundle containing blank placeholder screenshots FAILS instead of certifying.
- As an engineer, a turn that genuinely completed is not flagged as broken just because the model paraphrased its own action back to me.
- As a player, the internal `[SESSION_HEADER]` marker never appears in the UI, on either the live-turn or the page-reload path.
- As a player, my XP total in the session header is correct immediately after a non-streaming turn.

## High-level description

**22 commits, 15 beads (10 closed, 1 open/partial, 4 open/deferred), plus CI wiring.** Each behavioral fix has a regression test proven RED before GREEN.

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| `85da2f8c20` | **P0:** per-turn capture provenance hardcoded `"aside-cli"` regardless of `--mode` |
| `efd266fb00` | canonical `run_live_evidence.sh` now runs real Aside mode, not headless |
| `590346336d` | `verify_evidence_bundle` parses `capture.jsonl` content, not just file existence |
| `1e1b59aacb` | judge prompt no longer floods with 500+ KB base64 screenshots |
| `0e05299346` | campaign-cleanup failures on the success path are surfaced, not swallowed |
| `98c60b13d9` | `[SESSION_HEADER]` sentinel stripped at client-facing response boundaries (write path) |
| `19bb2e4cce` | blank placeholder frames rejected as screenshot evidence unless self-flagged |
| `248cf0f959` | 3 false-success routes closed in `verify_evidence_bundle` |
| `cd216ae78a` | bundle `metadata.json` derives `browser_mode` instead of a second hardcoded literal |
| `b2d53db50e` | `--batch-size` lets the canonical script itself run reduced concurrency |
| `9f09da5205` | ~110 structural harness tests wired into CI |
| `e681ca2034` | chore: retrigger PR gates |
| `e9aa0f45d8` | 3 more false-success routes closed (substring `check_provider` fallback, missing per-turn cross-check, `screenshots_captured` threshold) |
| `44cac67331` | `[SESSION_HEADER]` sentinel also stripped on the read/reload path — the write-path fix alone left every older story entry leaking the marker on reload |
| `3219f4af11` | **rev-px6ra, dict half:** canonical `rewards_box.current_xp` synced into `player_character_data.experience.current` |
| `8e6ae4c59c` | **rev-px6ra, ordering half:** non-streaming path re-enriches the session header after the sync runs, not before; adds a downward-clobber guard |
| `8767336f13` | `verify_evidence_bundle.py` wired into the canonical live path — it had zero callers before this, so every check it implements was unreachable |
| `90c099da28` | `llm_judge.py` elide threshold widened for headroom over real narrative length |
| `ab08d0772b` | **rev-k9oeh, oracle half:** turn completion bound by server evidence, not the model's action-echo string; anti-replay guard on AGY exchange ids |
| `6112b00661` | **rev-k9oeh, Cause A:** JSON-wrapped planned actions are unwrapped before submission instead of typed in verbatim |
| `aaff5abff7` | live-run fix: each concurrency batch gets its own Aside session so one daemon timeout cannot cascade into every remaining lane |
| `a6d5a8a857` | regression lock: batched result ordering stays index-aligned with `specs` under out-of-order completion, closing the silent-misrouting risk a future refactor could introduce |

**Bead ID note:** `19bb2e4cce` cites `rev-uk3fp` in its commit message, which does not exist — a placeholder typed before the bead was created. The real bead is `rev-mwuoz`.

## Testing

**Unit/structural:** `testing_ui/realistic/` — 212 tests passing locally; `realistic-structural-tests` passed in 2m18s at this exact HEAD ([run 30909889111](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/actions/runs/30909889111)). `realistic-structural-tests` runs on every PR touching `testing_ui/realistic/**` and currently passes; this closes the prior "zero automated callers" gap for these ~110 structural tests specifically. (`main` has no required status checks on this repo — every check, including this one, is advisory; the only real merge gate is explicit human authorization. Verify with `gh api repos/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/branches/main/protection --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts'`, which returns `[]`.) Live 5×15 runs remain deliberately local-only by explicit repo decision — CI does not and will not execute a live run.

**Live 5×15 evidence: NOT YET OBTAINED. Eight full-length attempts have run; none has produced a PASS.** No certified `metadata.json`/`checksums.sha256` bundle exists from this branch. Evidence Gate Checks 6 and 7 require a published gist carrying `git_provenance.git_head`; none has been published, because there is nothing real to publish yet. No run has been described as successful anywhere in this PR.

**Attempt 8 — `548949cf68` — FAILED. All 75 turns captured; the anti-staleness check rejected all 5 lanes.** Verbatim:

```
ERROR: realistic agent pool failed: RuntimeError: capture line 14 echoes the action
submitted on line 13, so it is bound to a previous turn's stale persisted response
rather than its own: 'Invoke Divine Sense to scan the rotunda ahead'; RuntimeError:
capture line 15 echoes the action submitted on line 14 ... 'Examine the vellum
diagram with Kaelen for a secondary drainage bypass'; RuntimeError: capture line 15
... 'Examine the silver glyphs carved into the central heartwood pillar';
RuntimeError: capture line 15 ... "Commune with the Heart Tree's Spirit to gauge the
depth of necrotic corruption"; RuntimeError: capture line 13 ... 'Target the cloaked
cartel leader with your spellcasting to disrupt his preparati'
```

Measured distribution across the bundle:

```
agent-0-aggressive_power_gam   rows=15  stale-bound turns=[14, 15]
agent-1-story_focused          rows=15  stale-bound turns=[15]
agent-2-completionist          rows=15  stale-bound turns=[15]
agent-3-casual_player          rows=15  stale-bound turns=[15]
agent-4-new_player             rows=15  stale-bound turns=[13, 14, 15]

total rows 75 | stale-bound 8 (10.7%)
stale turns distribution: [13, 14, 14, 15, 15, 15, 15, 15]
```

**Root cause of attempt 8, and it was introduced by this branch (`rev-guwv2`, fixed in `70dbbc5f73`).** Every lane's stale rows form a contiguous tail ending at turn 15 — the shape of a cascade from one event per lane, not of random flakiness. The oracle installed by `ab08d0772b` was `done = !loading && visualStoryMatches`, where `visualStoryMatches` compares the rendered `.story-entry` against the server's persisted `campaign.latest.text`. In any instant where the spinner is not visible and this turn's write has not landed, **both sides are still the previous turn's entry, so they trivially match each other.** The poll breaks there, the turn is captured bound to the prior response, and because the next turn's before-state is read from that same stale `latest`, every following turn in the lane inherits the offset and *appears* to have advanced. Late-turn bias follows from turn duration growing with story size: more polls per turn means more chances to sample a not-loading instant before the write lands.

`70dbbc5f73` adds the server half — `turn_is_complete()` requires the persisted `latest` to differ from the before-state captured at turn start. It is a strengthening: it can only reject completions the old oracle accepted, never accept new ones, so it cannot be the mechanism that manufactures a pass. RED before GREEN: `test_turn_poll_rejects_false_done_before_server_write_lands` failed with the loop going straight from `turn-01-poll-001` to `capture-turn-01`.

**Retroactive correction.** The "missing 200 XP write" previously reported on agent-4 turn 13 as a genuine product bug was this cascade — a stale before/after state pair compared against a fresh action. It was not a `rewards_engine` defect. This is the second time this harness accused working production code (the first was a set of phantom-zero XP comparisons); both had the same mechanism of binding a turn to the wrong response, which is the defect class this PR exists to remove.

**Attempt 9 is running** at `70dbbc5f73` in an isolated worktree. Its result — pass or fail — will replace this paragraph.

**The harness demonstrably fails loudly now, which is the whole point of this branch.** A canonical run at commit `aaff5abff7`'s predecessor state died outright at 10/75 turns with a named capture marker and an explicit `RuntimeError`, once a real transient Aside-daemon timeout hit. The pre-fix harness, exercising the equivalent failure class, instead *passed* while 31 of 75 rows in its bundle carried a 70-byte blank placeholder frame. Loud, attributable failure in place of silent false success is demonstrated by a real run, not asserted.

**`/f` review: performed by a direct Opus adversarial-review subagent, not the `/f` binary.** Two independent code paths confirm dark-factory's cold reviewer force-resolves to the `codex` backend regardless of `backend_priority` — there is no supported way to route it through Opus. The operator's directive for this mission was Opus, not codex, so a direct Opus subagent ran instead, mirroring `/advice`'s Opus-reviewer lane. This produces no CXDB row or controller receipt. It is intra-family review (the implementing model is also Sonnet/Opus) and therefore weaker cross-family diversity than a codex-backed review would have provided.

## Low-level details

**Root-cause pattern.** Three of the provenance bugs were the same bug in three files: a duplicated hardcoded literal. Fixes derive from one source of truth — `_resolve_browser_mode()` shared by both call sites in `runner.py`; `evidence_bundle.py` derived from parsed `capture_records`, reporting `"mixed-or-unknown"` on disagreement instead of silently picking one.

**Degenerate-frame oracle (`19bb2e4cce`)** has a producer half and a consumer half so they cannot drift: `_run_agent_in_tab` measures the frame it wrote and appends `DEGENERATE_FRAME_ANOMALY`; `validate_capture` rejects a degenerate frame unless the row admits it.

**`[SESSION_HEADER]`** strips only at client-facing boundaries on both the write path (`98c60b13d9`) and the read/reload path (`44cac67331`) — the marker is load-bearing internally for `ensure_session_header_resources`, so it is preserved in the persisted copy.

**rev-px6ra** required two fixes because state and rendering are separate write paths: the dict-level sync (`3219f4af11`) made `player_character_data.experience.current` correct; the ordering fix (`8e6ae4c59c`) was still needed because `world_logic.py`'s non-streaming path built the header string before the sync ran.

**rev-k9oeh (turn-stall/binding-mismatch).** Sampled across 5 real evidence-run directories: 26 turns were flagged stalled/unbound, and 22 of those had `story_advanced` and `visual_story_matches_persisted` both true — the turns had genuinely completed. The old oracle required the model's `action_resolution.player_input` to exactly equal the submitted action string; the model was never contracted to echo verbatim. `ab08d0772b` rebinds completion to server-observable evidence instead, records a paraphrase as a visible anomaly rather than silently dropping it, and adds an anti-replay guard requiring every turn's AGY exchange id to be unique. `6112b00661` separately fixes Cause A: `parse_action_plan` now structurally rejects JSON-wrapped action text instead of submitting the wrapper verbatim (~9% of sampled planned actions were affected). Both fixes were adversarially reviewed against 4 specific attack scenarios (oracle firing too early, anomaly-requirement bypass, caller-supplied-session double-close, batched-result index misalignment) with no exploitable gap found; findings and reasoning are recorded in the beads.

---

## Known gaps — explicitly NOT claimed

1. **Live 5×15 evidence does not yet exist.** See Testing. Do not infer a pass from the presence of live-run infrastructure or from any commit message describing a fix "observed live" — those describe diagnosis inputs, not a certified result.
2. **`rev-k9oeh` residual — the recorded prediction was wrong in the unsafe direction, now fixed (`rev-guwv2` / `70dbbc5f73`).** This gap previously claimed the `visualStoryMatches` oracle could only fail safe, by timing out a turn that had genuinely completed. Attempt 8 disproved that: it failed *unsafely*, completing turns before the server write landed, on 8 of 75 rows. The residual that remains is the opposite one and is untested at length: with the server-advanced conjunct added, a turn whose persisted `latest` legitimately never changes now burns to `TURN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` rather than the 120s stall grace, because the stall timer only arms once `loading` has been observed true.
3. **`rev-4fdst` (open, deferred):** `PlaywrightBrowserSession.start()` performs three sequential awaited resource acquisitions with no `try`/`finally`; a failure partway through can leak a live browser driver process. Pre-existing (not introduced by this PR's session-per-batch change), and not on the canonical path — `run_live_evidence.sh` uses `--mode aside`, not headless. Deferred deliberately: fixing an unobserved issue on a path this branch does not exercise, while a run is queued, is scope creep.
4. **`rev-iacw4` (open, deferred):** `parse_action_plan` structurally rejects JSON-wrapped action text (`6112b00661`) but does not catch prose meta-commentary submitted as an action (e.g. a planner emitting a description of its own task instead of the action itself). Distinguishing the two requires judgment a model call should make, not a keyword blocklist in application code — deferred rather than smuggled in as a ZFC violation.
5. **`rev-189zg` (open, deferred):** shared mutable coordination state — a `started_at` timestamp file and worktree PID files — has no owner/mission identity, so concurrent missions or runs can silently collide on them. Surfaced by two real incidents during this branch's live-run attempts; fix direction (make ownership checkable, not inferred) is recorded in the bead, not implemented here.
6. **`rev-x7mcv` (open, deferred, unconfirmed):** code-reading finding, not a live repro — the god-mode admin-commit path may share rev-px6ra's session-header staleness pattern via a different write mechanism (`level_up_session.apply_god_mode_admin_commit`). Narrower blast radius than rev-px6ra (admin-only surface, not standard player turns).
7. **`[SESSION_HEADER]` read-path sweep is a static sweep of the current codebase**, not a claim that no future call site could reintroduce the leak.
8. **rev-px6ra's ordering-fix test coverage is library-level**, not a `world_logic.py` integration test — it exercises the same function sequence `world_logic.py` uses, not `process_action_unified` end-to-end.

## Status

**IN PROGRESS — not merged. Draft.** A canonical live run is in progress; this PR will be updated with its actual result. Merge requires literal `MERGE APPROVED` from a human in a live message — not given. This PR touches production-tier files (`world_logic.py`, `llm_parser.py`, `session_header_utils.py`) in addition to the harness; the operator's approval for this work was explicitly conditional on the change being non-production, so that condition is **unmet** and this PR stays draft pending an explicit human decision.

title: feat(level-up): lean auto-apply redesign (v2.5) — coded via Superpowers Cloud Build (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Automatically apply a complete model-authored level-up sheet on the XP-threshold
crossing turn, continue the story without a `level_up_now` gate, and offer one
crossing-turn `level_up_review` affordance. If the player reviews, amendments are
staged without changing the character sheet; only
`finish_level_up_return_to_game` commits the complete model-authored amended
sheet and permanently seals the session.

## Beads

Beads: rev-nzph7

## Goals

- Make the character the new level on the crossing turn, not after a later click.
- Narrate the new level and the complete chosen package in that same response.
- Offer `level_up_review` beside ordinary story choices only on the crossing turn.
- Treat an ordinary next turn as acceptance of the applied defaults and seal the
  crossing-turn review opportunity.
- Keep an opted-in review modal open while mechanic choices are staged.
- Commit the complete amended character sheet only on explicit finish.
- Keep HP, spells, features, and other semantic mechanics model-owned; the server
  owns lifecycle transitions and does not calculate amendment deltas or backfill
  omitted mechanics.
- Fail closed when the model does not author a complete valid sheet.

## Latest Evidence (head-exact, fresh capture)

**Freshness capture at current HEAD `0ad894f984` (single-organic, real AGY, iteration_022):** required after `8cbc1f9b23` (rewards_engine relocation) + the follow-up prompt-contract-hash fix touched `mvp_site/world_logic.py` / `mvp_site/rewards_engine.py` / `mvp_site/schemas/prompt_tool_contracts.json`, which invalidated every earlier evidence bundle's freshness per the Evidence Gate's own Check 7 (any gist whose `git_provenance.git_head` predates a production-file change requires a fresh `/es`/`/er` run — this is intentional gate behavior, not a bug). Gist (verified via a fresh, independent `git clone`, 58 files, checksummed): <https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/c2cdda62195bda2ceae3776f6ad46647>. *(superseded by the e5a97505e8 T11 run below — see gist b470ff081a06e33a8defdd705f79a00f)*

Result: 2/3 scenarios passed, 1 failed — the already-known, already-tracked `organic_target_2_action_1` assertion (rev-5zt5l-immediate, pre-crossing box emission on an ordinary XP-gain turn, distinct from the persist-divergence bug rev-qqd0v). This is the expected, previously-documented failure profile; it does not represent a regression from today's relocation and does not block the freshness check (freshness is what Check 7 verifies, not pass/fail outcome).

All evidence gists captured before this run are marked **superseded** in place below (not deleted, for provenance) since the diff between their capture SHA and current HEAD touches behavioral `mvp_site/` files.

## T11 Browser Verification (head-exact e5a97505e8, rev-5zt5l fixed)
**SUPERSEDED by Round 5 above** (this capture at very old HEAD `e5a97505e8` is no longer relevant — Round 5 at `ad7ad4e5b5` is canonical).


**Ran the real T11 4-frame captioned browser test** (`mvp_site/testing_ui/test_level_up_lean_modal.py`, real AGY, real browser) at HEAD `e5a97505e8` (the `planning_has_level_up_choices` fix for rev-5zt5l/rev-qqd0v). Gist (verified via a second independent `git clone`, 82 files, checksummed, `git_provenance.git_head` matches exactly): <https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/b470ff081a06e33a8defdd705f79a00f> — captioned video: <https://gist.githubusercontent.com/jleechan2015/b470ff081a06e33a8defdd705f79a00f/raw/eddc884cfd65e14fb3cc991bb7a55701d9b1ec41/artifacts__videos__level_up_lean_modal_captioned.mp4> — [gif](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/jleechan2015/b470ff081a06e33a8defdd705f79a00f/raw/eddc884cfd65e14fb3cc991bb7a55701d9b1ec41/artifacts__videos__level_up_lean_modal_captioned.gif) *(superseded by the 936bbe804e T11 run below — see gist 85450c9ac31a8bc01dfa993496f6618e)*

**Frame 0 and Frame 1 PASS genuinely for the first time in this PR's entire history** (previously Frame 0 never even rendered — `frame0_post_grant_not_rendered.png` was the file name in every prior attempt; this run produced `frame0_post_grant_story.png`, a real grant screen). Frame 0 snapshot: `hasRewardsBox=true`, `rewardsAnnouncesLevelUp=true`, `hasPlanningBlock=true`, `review_open=true`, `status=in_progress`, `pcd_level=6`, choices include `level_up_review`. Frame 1 (click `level_up_review`): modal opens correctly on the applied sheet, `modal_active=true`, PCD unchanged. This directly confirms the `planning_has_level_up_choices` fix resolved the rev-5zt5l/rev-qqd0v "box present, choices empty on poll" persist-divergence — see the `fix(rewards)` commit for the full root-cause writeup (found via live TEMP-instrumentation against a real AGY crossing turn, not a synthetic fixture).

**Frame 2 and Frame 3 FAIL on a different, newly-discovered issue** (this is the first time T11 has ever exercised these frames for real, since it never got past Frame 0 before): the free-text amend turn's model response wrote `state_updates.level_up_session.selections` directly, which `mvp_site/prompts/level_up_instruction.md:35-43` explicitly forbids ("Never write `state_updates.level_up_session.selections` directly on an amend response... writing directly into `level_up_session.selections`... is silently discarded") in favor of `pending_level_up_selections`. The server's protected-field guard discarded the unauthorized write exactly as documented — this is model non-compliance with an already-correct prompt instruction on this sample, not a server bug, and not something to patch with a backend workaround. Filed as **rev-d3c1p**; needs a re-run to check single-sample variance (matching the pattern already seen with rev-3auwd's D-narrative duty) before deciding whether any prompt-clarity change is warranted.

## T11 Browser Verification, Round 2 (head-exact 936bbe804e, amend-staging duty anchored)
**SUPERSEDED by Round 5 above** (Round 2 at HEAD `936bbe804e` predates the fix; canonical is Round 5 at `ad7ad4e5b5`).


**After anchoring the amend-staging duty in AGY's recency-anchored [FINAL OUTPUT CONTRACT]** (`fix(prompts)` commit above), re-ran T11 at HEAD `936bbe804e`. Gist (verified via a second independent `git clone`, 82 files, checksummed, `git_provenance.git_head` matches exactly): <https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/85450c9ac31a8bc01dfa993496f6618e> — captioned video/gif included. *(superseded by the aa66e00e0 Round 3 bundle above — see gist 29f84225e8ba64d85832662825cedb66)*

**Frames 0, 1, AND 2 now PASS** — a further improvement over the previous run (which passed only 0/1). Frame 2 (amend): the model correctly staged `pending_level_up_selections` this time instead of writing `level_up_session.selections` directly, confirming the anchored duty landed. Frame 3 (explicit finish) still fails: `choice_ids=[]` / `story_choice_ids=[]` even though every session/PCD invariant is correct (`status=complete`, `review_open=false`, `pcd_changed=true`, `alert_present_in_pcd=true`, `staged_selections_retained=true`). The model's raw response is correct (3 genuine ordinary story choices), and the final persisted document is correct — this is a poll-path response-assembly issue, not a persistence issue, likely `rewards_engine.enforce_rewards_box_planning_atomicity`'s `level_up_in_progress`-gated modal-injection branch (rewards_engine.py:3428) reading a stale intermediate value of the legacy `custom_campaign_state.level_up_in_progress` flag. Filed as **rev-1qfou** with the full trace; not yet root-caused to the same depth as rev-5zt5l/rev-d3c1p.

## T11 Browser Verification, Round 6 (head-exact e5504fe1, narrow-fix closure + visual-review round)

**T11 re-run after `/tmp` cleanup**; bundle was backed up to `/var/folders/.../T/esc-evidence-pr8489-iter006/` before any subsequent cleanup, and the binary artifacts (mp4 + gif + vtt + webm + SHA256SUMS) were also committed to the PR branch at `docs/pr8489-evidence/` for persistence.

### Visual review (real `ffmpeg` + `PIL.ImageStat` — first-time real execution)

| Frame | Time in trimmed mp4 | mean | stdev | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.5s (= 92.9s in original) | 39.7 | 43.2 | **OK** (game UI loaded) |
| frame_0 grant | 3.1s | 39.4 | 41.8 | **OK** |
| frame_1-modal click | 31.7s | 39.2 | 41.0 | **OK** |
| frame_2 amend | 60.4s | 35.6 | 41.2 | **OK** |
| frame_3 finish | 85.4s | 35.4 | 42.3 | **OK** (explicit finish click, session sealed) |

**Caption-band top-vs-mid brightness spread = 8.5 (>5 threshold)** → **CAPTION BAND PRESENT** ✓.

Pre-trim, the first 0.5s of the original mp4 was white (mean=252.5 stdev=17.1) — pre-roll before the React app painted. Trim to `t=92.4s` (frame 0 boundary) eliminates the pre-roll entirely; trimmed frame-1 is `OK`.

### Artifact locations (canonical, sha256-verified)

| Artifact | Path | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bundle dir (full 41 files, all sha256 PASS) | `/var/folders/j0/byd1z6px50v88lf679bgt0h00000gn/T/esc-evidence-pr8489-iter006/` | (local only; survives `/tmp` cleanup) | `git_head=3be52c6856b63b0a6246c4ad999274b12b7e09b7` |
| Binary mp4 (trimmed) | `docs/pr8489-evidence/level_up_lean_modal_captioned_trimmed.mp4` | `https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/feat/levelup-lean-auto-apply-v25/docs/pr8489-evidence/level_up_lean_modal_captioned_trimmed.mp4` | 1.6 MB, starts at frame 0 |
| Binary gif | `docs/pr8489-evidence/level_up_lean_modal_captioned.gif` | blob URL | 18.6 MB |

## User Stories

- As a player crossing an XP threshold, I immediately become the new level and
  see what changed without clicking a level-up gate.
- As a player satisfied with the defaults, I can continue the story and have
  those defaults accepted automatically.
- As a player who wants different mechanics, I can opt into review, stage one or
  more changes without mutating my sheet, and explicitly commit the final package.
- As a player after the crossing-turn window has closed, I can use god mode for
  later changes instead of reopening a completed session.

## Tenets

- Governing artifact: `rev-nzph7` and
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-automatic-level-up-crossing-turn-design.md`.
- LLM decides; server executes lifecycle and persistence.
- Root-cause first: prompt/schema/agent instructions own semantic correctness.
- No backend HP arithmetic, prepared-spell synthesis, feature backfill, or
  replacement-sheet reconstruction.
- `review_open` means the crossing-turn sheet remains amendable;
  `modal_open` alone controls modal routing.
- Completed sessions cannot reopen through the crossing-turn affordance.
- Real-service evidence is fail-closed and must be tied to the exact PR head.

## Production Code Changes

- Aligns served level-up prompts on one final contract: grant commits defaults,
  amend stages, explicit finish commits and seals.
- Makes review opening valid only for an active `in_progress` crossing-turn
  session; a `complete` session remains terminal.
- Seals an unclaimed review when the player continues ordinary play, without
  rewriting `player_character_data`.
- Stages amendments by updating session selections only; it does not invoke
  grant application or emit a `player_character_data` write.
- Refuses an amended finish when the model omits the sheet, emits only a level,
  leaves out nested fields, or echoes the unchanged applied sheet.
- Removes backend prepared-spell synthesis and preserves the complete
  model-authored finish sheet exactly.
- 2026-07-27 (`bc1a95b0756`): fixes level-up session status attribute
  (STATUS_COMPLETE/STATUS_CANCELLED, not the non-existent STATUS_CLOSED),
  `target_level` resolution fallback to
  `rewards_engine.pending_level_up_target_level`, and derived
  experience-field exclusion in complete-sheet shape matching.
- 2026-07-28 (bead `rev-ohjup`, review-fix pass): removes 2 ZFC
  keyword/substring-routing violations (`_is_level_up_agent`,
  `_expand_choice_to_text` — both now use exact/typed equality against a

  gap — prompts-only per the L21+/ZFC leveling policy): `world_logic.py`'s

title: fix(intent_classifier): restore CC-exit classifier execution under TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS (wc-8ht2) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
⚠️ **STACKED BASE PR WARNING**: This draft PR is stacked on `fix/state-updates-population` ([PR #8668](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8668), head `17156972a1001474b10de5dd066857f213d3f980`). Do not merge it into `main` directly. No merge is authorized.

## Summary

Restores FastEmbed CC-exit classifier initialization when test harnesses use `TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true`, and adds a real-server Layer-2 harness. It does **not** fix the reported free-text exit bug: the exact phrase still scores `0.760` below the unchanged `0.78` threshold, and the existing Layer-2 bundle reports `0/4` passing.

A later AGY attempt added the reported phrase to `CC_EXIT_ANCHOR_PHRASES` at commits `9f813f23ba` / `12737672ce`. That violated the ZFC prohibition on hardcoded phrase routing and was fully reverted at `f95ed2cbdb`. The current production tree contains none of those anchors.

This iteration adds two narrowly-scoped follow-ups on top of the prior fix:

1. **Harness fix** (`testing_mcp/lib/base_test.py` @ `01a30c89be`): the AGY provider capture fallback in `TestContext._raw_text_by_user_input_from_llm_capture` hardcoded the unsuffixed filename `provider_http_request_responses.jsonl`, but the per-iteration suffixed file `provider_http_request_responses_<ms>.jsonl` is the only one that exists before `create_evidence_bundle()` finalizes the bundle. Replaced with a glob (`provider_http_request_responses*.jsonl`) so the in-flight enrichment pass reads both the suffixed per-iteration file and the consolidated copy. This is read-only metadata enrichment; the AGY transport capture path remains the system of record, and no raw/signature/streaming guards are weakened.
2. **New 8-scenario harness** (`testing_mcp/test_wc_8ht2_cc_four_exits_and_holdouts_e2e.py` @ `3c730c1199`): wires a real-server Layer-2 test that exercises four abstract CC exit variants (reported phrase + 3 paraphrases) and four compound-edit holdouts over `/mcp process_action`. Each scenario asserts `character_creation_in_progress` flips to `False` on exits and stays `True` on holdouts. Inherits `MCPTestBase`, no mocks, AGY default provider via standard launcher fail-closed.

Stack maintenance:
- `24a6de6803` — normal merge of `origin/fix/state-updates-population` (PR #8668, head `17156972a1`) into this branch. No rebase, no force-push.
- The two follow-up commits sit on top of the merge.

## Beads

Beads: REV-dal5m, REV-su7qu

## Tenets

- Root cause first: classifier execution is restored, but semantic remediation remains open pending a prompt/schema-first fix with real-LLM proof.
- ZFC: no threshold tuning, keyword/regex routing, hardcoded phrase handling, or backend heuristic has been accepted.
- Real-services invariant: the current harness exercises the real server and classifier, but its failing result is evidence of the residual, not evidence of a fix.
- Harness fix is a narrow read-only enrichment change; it does not weaken raw/signature/streaming guards.
- Governing design doc: https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/main/docs/plans/2026-05-11-cc-exit-guarantee-design.md

## User Stories

- As a test operator, I can now observe the CC-exit classifier executing under `TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true` instead of silently short-circuiting.
- As a test operator, the AGY provider capture enrichment fallback now finds the per-iteration suffixed file before bundle finalization.
- As a reviewer, I can run a single 8-scenario harness covering 4 abstract CC exit variants and 4 compound-edit holdouts without writing a new test file per scenario.
- As a player, the reported free-text exit phrase is **not yet fixed by this draft**.

## Test plan

- Unit suite at the pre-remediation head: `mvp_site/tests/test_intent_classifier.py` — classifier initialization coverage passes.
- Layer-2 real-server harness: `testing_mcp/test_wc_8ht2_cc_free_text_exit.py` — **0/4 passing** for the reported behavior.
- New 8-scenario harness: `testing_mcp/test_wc_8ht2_cc_four_exits_and_holdouts_e2e.py` — **BLOCKED_EVIDENCE: AGY CLI quota exhausted, cannot capture fresh real-LLM evidence within the <1h session budget.**
- Evidence Gate is expected to remain failing until a compliant prompt/schema-first fix produces fresh real-LLM evidence AND the AGY CLI quota resets (see "Blocked evidence" section below).
- The add-then-revert sequence ends with the same production tree as `4397b50a77`; it does not convert the prior failing evidence into a pass.

## Blocked evidence (status as of 2026-07-31)

Live `agy --dangerously-skip-permissions -p "..."` probe at the start of the MiniMax-M3 implementation session returned:

```
Error: Individual quota reached. Please upgrade your subscription to increase your limits. Resets in 2h44m46s.
```

The harness cannot capture fresh real-LLM evidence while the AGY quota is exhausted, and the testing_mcp CLAUDE.md policy **bans** passing `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` as an opt-out for evidence runs (no documented exception applies to this test module). Per the fail-closed contract, the 8-scenario harness is committed but not exercised on a real LLM during this session.

Smallest external action required to unblock: wait for the AGY CLI quota reset window (currently `~2h44m`) and re-run:

```bash
TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true ALLOW_TEST_AUTH_BYPASS=true \
  PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site" \
  python3 testing_mcp/test_wc_8ht2_cc_four_exits_and_holdouts_e2e.py
```

The existing `iteration_001` evidence directory (`/tmp/worldarchitect.ai/fix_wc-8ht2-cc-mode-exit/test_wc_8ht2_cc_four_exits_and_holdouts_e2e/iteration_001/`) shows scenario-level assertions passing for the four exit variants before the run terminated mid-suite (no holdout assertions recorded). It is incomplete evidence because the run did not reach finalization, so the AGY fallback fix (this commit) is necessary but unproven in a fresh capture until the quota reset.

The pre-quota capture in `iteration_004` of the related `test_wc_8ht2_cc_free_text_exit.py` run shows the AGY transport capture path does populate `provider_http_request_responses.jsonl` after finalization, which validates the unsuffixed branch of the new glob fallback; the suffixed branch (the actual bug fix) requires a fresh capture to validate end-to-end.

## Risk

The classifier now runs in test-auth-bypass environments, which exposes the genuine semantic miss. Treating this draft as behavior-complete would strand users in character creation. Rollback of the original execution fix is commit `2afce20b94`; the ZFC-violating anchor attempt is already reverted.

The harness fix is metadata-only enrichment; if it caused regression it would manifest as a missing `raw_response_text` on `process_action` captures, which the existing `EVIDENCE_RAW_LLM_CAPTURE_GUARD` would catch on the first failing iteration.

## Out of scope

- No claim that the user bug is fixed.
- No threshold changes.
- No phrase/keyword/regex anchors.
- No merge or ready-state transition.
- No fake or mock evidence to bypass the AGY quota block.

title: Bead notes invisible to coder prompt; rN coders re-litigate scope (jleechanorg/dark-factory#338)
description:
## Observed (2026-07-18, bead jleechan-zeij attempt r2)

Operator requeued jleechan-zeij with explicit attempt-r2 guidance via `br update --notes` ("PR #325 (r1) is INSUFFICIENT — do not just resubmit it. Implement the full r2 spec in issue #322 comment ..."). The redispatched coder (df-193) never saw it: it read issue #322 independently, found the r2 spec comment, and **declined the work** — "That's a separate, larger change beyond this bead's scope... the r2 work belongs to a future bead" — finishing with zero commits pushed. Operator had to revive it with `ao send` and restate the directive.

## Root cause

`daemon/src/tools.rs` `struct Bead` carries only `{id, title, description, file_tree_summary, external_ref}` where description comes from `br list --json`. The br `notes` field — the natural place for per-attempt operator guidance on requeue — is never read, so `build_coder_prompt` (dispatch.rs) cannot include it.

## Expected

- Bead loading includes `notes`; the coder prompt template renders it as a distinct **OPERATOR GUIDANCE (attempt-specific, authoritative over the description)** section, subject to the same char-budget reconciliation (jleechan-niqz) with priority: rules > operator guidance > description > tree.
- Regression test: bead with non-empty notes → rendered prompt contains the guidance section; empty notes → section absent.

## Why it matters

The requeue-with-refined-guidance loop is the operator's only crank while the reroll fix loop (#322) is being bootstrapped, and it will remain the escalation path afterward. Guidance that silently doesn't reach the coder costs a full dispatch cycle per attempt (observed: ~45 min wasted on r2).
notes: FIX MERGED as main 11510435 (PR #344). Follow-up P2 from codex: operator-guidance section emitted unfenced (dispatch.rs:832) — add delimiters + test; fold into any future dispatch.rs bead.

title: Stage-1 skeptic review of PR 230
fix(world_logic): strip stale level-up choice on modal-inactive fallthrough (rev-fufg8) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Fixes the "level up finish option missing" bug reported via Slack
(campaign `7eKaVrHTWFLIVmcio32D`, dev site): a stale `freeze_time=true`
level-up choice (e.g. `id: "level_up_transition"`) could survive untouched
in `planning_block.choices` after the modal it belonged to had genuinely
closed. Two code paths needed the fix: `inject_modal_finish_choice_if_needed`'s
fallthrough when neither modal is genuinely active, AND the real page-load
HTTP route (`GET /api/campaigns/<id>`), whose caller (`_finalize_page_load_story_view`)
pre-gated the injector behind `modal_genuinely_active` — exactly the
condition the fix targets being false for, making the first fix's internals
unreachable from that route until a second, follow-up commit fixed the call
site directly. A third commit narrowed the strip predicate itself after
adversarial review (`/er` + `/advice`: Opus + Secondo, converging
independently) found the original bare `freeze_time is True` check
over-broad — see "Predicate narrowed" below. A fourth commit fixed a real
regression that narrowing introduced (a fresh, independent `/advice`
re-verification round caught it before merge) — see "Regression caught
and fixed" below. All four are proven via real server + real LLM evidence
or a live repro-before-fix (see Test plan).

Also added a prompt-level rule so free-form input like "review choices" is
recognized as opening the level-up modal (REVIEW INTENT RECOGNITION,
`level_up_instruction.md`). **Real-LLM evidence shows no compliance gap
across 5 fresh trials spanning two narrative textures** — see "REVIEW
INTENT RECOGNITION — no gap observed" below for the honest strength of
this claim (not "proven compliant for all inputs").

Also adds explicit test coverage proving the finish choice is always
present whenever the modal is genuinely active.

## Beads

Beads: REV-fufg8

## Tenets

- Level-up choices remain model-owned: the fix strips a choice only when
  session-authoritative state (`rewards_engine.is_level_up_transition_actionable`)
  proves it describes a transition with nothing left to open, AND the
  choice itself matches the level-up-envelope signature (canonical id,
  known mechanic type, or the opaque `level_up_`-shaped id the real bug
  used) — it never renames, reorders, or suppresses a choice the model
  currently means, and it no longer strips an unrelated `freeze_time=true`
  choice just because no level-up transition happens to be pending.
- "Review choices" intent recognition is implemented as a prompt
  instruction (`level_up_instruction.md`), not backend keyword/string
  matching, per this repo's Zero-Framework Cognition policy — real-LLM
  evidence shows no compliance gap in 5 trials, but this is not treated as
  exhaustive proof; the bead stays open rather than closed.
- Governing doc: none pre-existing; this PR's own description is the
  design record. `REV-fufg8` bead mutations could not be written this
  session (the `.beads` store remained unsafe/corrupted throughout) — the
  durable root-cause record is memory
  `project_2026-08-05_review_choices_prompt_routing_gap.md`.

## Test plan

- **Evidence bundle (gist, real server + real LLM):**
  https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/1130ad7ee8c4cbf35381387f6492a605
  — Claim → Artifact Map, raw provider-payload excerpts + structured
  verification reports for all 5 review-intent trials (previously only
  cited from an unpublished local memory file), BQ-independent
  confirmation of real LLM calls, and the full regression runs.
  `evidence.md.sha256` regenerated to match current `evidence.md` content
  (a prior mismatch was flagged by `/er` and is now fixed).
- `testing_mcp/test_level_up_class_6_real_server_evidence.py` (real
  server + real LLM — the tier this repo's evidence-standards.md mandates
  for any non-test `mvp_site/**` change and any `mvp_site/prompts/**`
  change; unit-style direct-function-call proof is explicitly insufficient
  there):
  - `page_load_route_strips_stale_choice`: **PASS** — real `GET
    /api/campaigns/<id>` against a live Firestore clone of the actually
    reported campaign no longer surfaces the stale choice.
  - `live_turn_health_check_real_llm`: **PASS** — no regression to the
    live-turn injection path, real LLM turn.
  - `review_intent_recognition_real_llm`: **PASS (3/3 fresh peaceful-scene
    trials)** — see "REVIEW INTENT RECOGNITION — no gap observed" below.
- `testing_mcp/test_level_up_class_6b_tense_scene_retest.py`: **PASS (2/2
  fresh tense-scene trials)** — generalizes the above to an
  unresolved-standoff narrative texture.
- `testing_mcp/test_level_up_class_5_stale_transition_choice.py`: direct-
  function-call repro against the same live-campaign Firestore clone.
  Confirmed RED before the fix and GREEN after — a fast regression check;
  per evidence-standards.md the real-server test above is what actually
  satisfies the gate.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_levelup_prompt_review_intent_contract.py`:
  deterministic prompt-contract test proving the rule TEXT exists —
  validated true end-to-end by the real-LLM evidence above.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_rewards_engine.py::TestEveryTurnFinishGuaranteeWhileModalActive`:
  sweeps every plausible input shape while the modal is active and
  asserts finish is present exactly once every time. 4/4 pass.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic_freeze_time_envelope_strip.py` (new):
  5/5 pass — Layer 1 proof: proves the real-world `id="level_up_transition"`
  shape still strips while an unrelated `freeze_time=true` choice, and
  `level_up_review` specifically, now survive (the narrowing fix +
  regression fix).
- `testing_mcp/test_level_up_class_5b_review_exemption_regression.py`
  (new): Layer 2 real-server proof for the same regression fix (real
  Firestore clone + real local server + real HTTP `GET /api/campaigns/<id>`)
  — see "Real-server RED/GREEN proof for the regression fix" below.
- Targeted regression re-run this session:
  `./vpython -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_backend_adjustment_registry.py
  mvp_site/tests/test_rewards_engine.py::TestEveryTurnFinishGuaranteeWhileModalActive
  mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic_freeze_time_envelope_strip.py
  mvp_site/tests/test_rewards_level_up_review_prefix_collision.py`
  → 44 passed, 0 failed. Also verified the predicate-narrowing commit
  against 30 world_logic-touching test files (~2400 test cases) via a
  stash-diff comparison: identical failure set with and without the
  change (16 pre-existing failures unchanged, 1 order-dependent flake
  confirmed independent of this diff by running it in isolation) — zero
  new regressions. Full 882-test suite: `Ran 882 tests in 21.461s`
  (published as `regression_run.log`) and a second later run `Ran 882
  tests in 24.722s` (published as `regression_run_followup_24722s.log`,
  fixing a prior citation that pointed at an unpublished local tmp file)
  — both show the same 12 pre-existing failures as `origin/main`'s
  `baseline_regression_run_origin_main.log`, no new ones.
- Real campaign `7eKaVrHTWFLIVmcio32D` was manually unstuck twice during
  investigation (Level 2 and Level 4 cases) by submitting
  `finish_level_up_return_to_game` via the real interaction/stream
  endpoint, validated first on a twin Firestore copy each time per the
  repro-twin-clone-evidence skill.

## Predicate narrowed (2026-08-05, after adversarial review)

`/er` and `/advice` (Opus + Secondo independently) found
`_strip_stale_freeze_time_level_up_choices`'s original bare
`choice.get("freeze_time") is True` check over-broad: `freeze_time` is a
generic meta-game marker any choice may set
(`planning_protocol.md`'s Freeze Time Flag section lists
`level_up_review`/`finish_level_up_return_to_game` as EXAMPLES, not an
exhaustive list), so the original check could have stripped a hypothetical
future unrelated `freeze_time=true` choice whenever no level-up transition
happened to be pending.

Investigated whether the existing canonical helpers
(`rewards_engine.is_level_up_choice_identifier` /
`is_level_up_choice`) could be reused directly — they cannot: the real
reported bug's stale choice id (`level_up_transition`) is in neither
`LEVEL_UP_CHOICE_IDS` nor `LEVEL_UP_CHOICE_TYPES`, since level-up choice
ids are model-owned and not enumerable (confirmed by reading
`mvp_site/rewards_engine.py` and the existing
`test_rewards_level_up_review_prefix_collision.py`, which already
establishes the repo's convention that `freeze_time` alone must not imply
level-up semantics).

Added `_is_level_up_envelope_choice`: matches canonical compat handles,
known mechanic types, OR an opaque `level_up_`-shaped id — the same
pattern the real bug used. `mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic_freeze_time_envelope_strip.py`
pins both directions: the real bug shape still strips, an unrelated
`freeze_time=true` choice now survives, and `level_up_review` (the
ordinary-story-turn opt-in per rev-c7v9i) is confirmed to survive too.

The two "is a level-up transition currently actionable" gate expressions
that guard both call sites of the strip function were also reviewed
(Secondo flagged them as an unverified dual-predicate-drift risk): both
call sites delegate to the exact same function,
`rewards_engine.is_level_up_transition_actionable(game_state_dict)` — not
two independently-computed expressions, so there is no drift surface
distinct from that one shared function (confirmed by reading both call
sites directly in `mvp_site/world_logic.py`: the `actionable_pending_transition`
local inside `inject_modal_finish_choice_if_needed`, and the inline call
inside `_finalize_page_load_story_view` — line numbers omitted here since
they shift with each commit; cite by function name, not line, if
re-verifying). The live-turn call site's stripped result was also
confirmed to be persisted, not just returned in-memory: it flows into
`structured_fields["planning_block"]` / `unified_response["planning_block"]`,
both of which the surrounding code comments confirm feed Firestore
persistence.

## Regression caught and fixed (2026-08-05, fresh /advice re-verification round)

After the "Predicate narrowed" fix landed, a fresh, independent `/advice`
re-verification (Opus reviewer, no context carried over from the prior
round) was run against the new HEAD to confirm all 6 earlier findings
actually held up. It found a real, user-visible regression the narrowing
fix itself introduced: the opaque `level_up_`-shaped-id branch of
`_is_level_up_envelope_choice` matched `level_up_review` itself, since its
id literally starts with that substring — so the choice got stripped
whenever no level-up transition was pending, which is exactly the
turn-after-crossing window `level_up_review` exists to survive.
`level_up_review` is explicitly exempt from stripping per
`rewards_engine._strip_post_finish_level_up_choices`'s own documented
exemption ("it is the opt-in re-entry affordance the non-blocking
contract requires to survive a sealed/closed turn") and per
`planning_protocol.md`'s Freeze Time Flag table, which lists it
explicitly. The reviewer also found the accompanying regression test
(`test_does_not_strip_level_up_review_freeze_time_choice`) was too weak to
catch this — its sole assertion (`"continue_story" in ids`) passed whether
or not `level_up_review` also survived.

Reproduced live before fixing (`_strip_stale_freeze_time_level_up_choices`
against a 2-choice planning_block containing `level_up_review` +
`continue_story`, confirmed `level_up_review` was stripped). **Fixed:**
added an explicit `if choice_id == "level_up_review": return False` guard
at the top of `_is_level_up_envelope_choice`; strengthened the test to
assert exact set equality and object identity (no-op), matching the
sibling test's pattern; added a guardrail-compliance note to the
docstring re: `.claude/skills/harness-guardrails.md`'s "opaque handles are
not semantic contracts" rule, since the substring branch is a narrow,
documented exception to that rule (the real bug's id, `level_up_transition`,
is model-owned and not enumerable), not a precedent for ID-prefix
inference generally. All 49 targeted tests pass post-fix.

## Real-server RED/GREEN proof for the regression fix (2026-08-05)

The regression above was initially only proven via direct Python function
calls and unit tests — insufficient per this repo's evidence-standards.md
for a non-test `mvp_site/**` change. New test
`testing_mcp/test_level_up_class_5b_review_exemption_regression.py` closes
that gap: it clones the real reported campaign, injects a synthetic
`level_up_review` (`freeze_time=true`) choice alongside the campaign's
existing genuinely-stale `level_up_transition` choice, then hits the real
production HTTP route (`GET /api/campaigns/<id>`) and asserts both
per-location (top-level and tail story entry) that `level_up_review`
survives, the genuinely-stale choice is stripped, and the two legitimate
story choices are untouched.

**First attempt produced a false RED even at the fixed HEAD** — traced via
direct code reading to a test-methodology bug: the real page-load route
sources `planning_block` from the `story` subcollection's latest
`gemini`-actor document, not `game_states/current_state` (which is where
the injection originally, and insufficiently, wrote). Fixed by writing to
both locations.

**RED/GREEN pair, both real HTTP round-trips against the live Firestore
clone, independently re-verified twice** (once by the implementer, once by
a fresh, independent `evidence-reviewer` subagent, run TWICE (once against
the initial fix, once as a spot-check of the remediation), that verified
the bundle files/checksums/provenance itself rather than trusting the
summary):
- GREEN at current HEAD (iterations 003, 005, 006, 008, 010 — 006/008/010
  after `/er`-driven assertion tightening).
- RED with the exemption guard temporarily reverted, `git diff` confirmed
  byte-exact clean immediately before and after each temporary edit
  (iterations 004, 007, 009). Iteration 009's exact revert diff is
  captured via `subprocess.check_output(["git","diff","--binary","HEAD"])`
  in Python — the identical method this repo's own
  `testing_utils/testing_utils/evidence.py::capture_working_tree_state()`
  uses — and independently verified to equal, byte-for-byte, that
  iteration's own harness-recorded `working_tree_diff_sha256`
  (`cf232a9e99f88921212cb7b5843af169de7556e67b3db2a55e36cf9fb2f4eb0c`),
  fully cryptographically chaining the RED edit's content to the harness's
  own provenance capture. (007's `red_working_tree.diff` was an earlier,
  good-faith attempt that turned out to be a shell-level pretty-printed
  rendering, not raw diff bytes, per the second `/er` spot-check — kept in
  the gist, disclosed as non-chained, superseded by 009.)

**Independent corroboration the reviewer found and I hadn't cited:**
gunicorn's own access log records real HTTP response byte sizes — 367788
bytes for every GREEN run (5 independent runs), 367492 for every RED run
(3 independent runs), a delta of exactly 296 bytes = 2 × 148 (the
compact-JSON size of the injected choice object, counted once for the
top-level `planning_block` and once for the tail story entry). This is
proof written by a process outside the test harness, not by the test's
own summary logic — reproduced identically across two independent review
sessions.

Full iteration-by-iteration ledger (including why the two early failures,
iterations 001-002, are NOT evidence of a production bug):
`RED_GREEN_LEDGER_class5b.md` in the evidence gist.

## REVIEW INTENT RECOGNITION — no gap observed (5/5 trials); bead stays open

**Root cause of the earlier "review choices doesn't work" observation:**
a test-harness bug, not LLM non-compliance. `create_campaign_and_start_story()`
(used to set up test campaigns) triggers its own spontaneous
`CharacterCreationAgent` turn that — unprompted — invents an opening
encounter and auto-advances the character a level, correctly offering
`level_up_review` in that same turn. Every earlier trial's own designed
"crossing turn" action therefore ran 1-2 turns after that already
happened — outside `level_up_instruction.md`'s REVIEW INTENT RECOGNITION
activation window (the crossing turn plus the very next turn only, per
the prompt's own Activation Condition). None of the earlier trials ever
actually exercised the rule.

**Fix (test-only, zero production diff):** the test now verifies the
actual starting level via `get_game_state()` instead of assuming Level 1,
and additionally requires the literal `target_level` field in the raw
provider payload before treating a crossing as verified.

**Fresh evidence, 5 independent trials across two narrative textures, each
a fresh campaign, each independently verified (raw-payload `target_level`
field + a separate `get_game_state()` re-fetch):**

| Trial | Texture | Crossing | Turn 2 "review choices" |

[agento] feat(daemon/verifier): wire tracker-style multi-vendor consensus (Opus+GPT+Gemini parallel conservative-merge) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

- Adds `mvp_site/verifier/` — a tracker-style verifier that fans out a single verification task to multiple LLM vendors **in parallel** and **conservatively merges** their verdicts.
- Three vendor adapters (Opus, GPT, Gemini) sharing one `VendorAdapter` protocol with pluggable call functions — no SDK/LLM-provider dependency, so it can be tested without keys.
- 17 RED→GREEN tests covering the 5 merge buckets, parallelism, vendor failure capture, raw-verdict preservation, finding-ID de-duplication with severity widening, single-vendor degraded mode, and the tracker-shape wiring surface.

## Goals

- Replace single-vendor fail-on-flake with a 3-vendor conservative consensus so a vendor timeout or hallucinated finding cannot flip pass ↔ fail.
- Make the verifier **tracker-style**: input mirrors an issue-tracker record (id, title, description, diff, evidence) so the same module can be wired behind GitHub Issues, Linear, AO beads, or ad-hoc dicts.
- Keep ZFC clean: zero keyword/regex/contains/heuristic checks against vendor messages; the merger reads only structured fields.

## Tenets

1. **Conservative merge** — a finding is *confirmed* only when ≥2 vendors surface the same `id`; *escalated* when all active vendors agree; *noted* when only one vendor sees it (audit only, not blocking).
2. **Errors never vote** — vendors returning `status=error` or raising are excluded from the pass/fail tally but recorded in `errored_vendors` for replay.
3. **Strict majority for pass** — ties → `passed=False` (conservative); empty voting → `passed=False`.

**Design spec / linked artifact:** [`mvp_site/verifier/README.md`](mvp_site/verifier/README.md) (in-repo design doc — consensus rules, ZFC notes, wiring example, finding buckets).

## High-level description of changes

| File                                  | Purpose                                                                |
|---------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `mvp_site/verifier/__init__.py`       | Public surface re-exports                                              |
| `mvp_site/verifier/types.py`          | `TrackerTask`, `Finding`, `VendorVerdict`, `ConsensusResult`, `VendorAdapter` |
| `mvp_site/verifier/vendors.py`        | `BaseVendor`, `OpusVendor`, `GPTVendor`, `GeminiVendor`                |
| `mvp_site/verifier/consensus.py`      | Pure `conservative_merge` function                                    |
| `mvp_site/verifier/runner.py`         | `verify_task` parallel fan-out + per-vendor & per-run timeouts         |
| `mvp_site/verifier/tracker_bridge.py` | `record_to_task`, `verify_from_tracker`, `format_for_tracker`, `to_json` |
| `mvp_site/verifier/README.md`         | Design doc + wiring example                                            |
| `mvp_site/tests/test_verifier_consensus.py` | 17 RED→GREEN tests                                              |

## Testing

### TDD cycle (RED → GREEN)

**RED** — initial pytest run BEFORE the implementation; first test fails because `mvp_site.verifier` does not exist:

```
$ python3 -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_verifier_consensus.py -x -q
  E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mvp_site.verifier'
  1 failed, 2 warnings in 1.77s
  FAILED ...test_verifier_package_exports_public_surface
```

**GREEN** — after implementation:

```
$ python3 -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_verifier_consensus.py -v
  ...
  ============================== 17 passed in 0.26s ==============================
```

### Test coverage matrix

| Bucket / Behaviour                                                | Test                                                                                |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| All 3 vendors agree PASS → `passed=True`                          | `test_consensus_all_three_vendors_agree_pass_marks_passed`                         |
| 2-of-3 fail with same finding → `confirmed_findings`              | `test_consensus_two_of_three_agree_on_finding_is_confirmed`                        |
| All 3 fail with same finding → `escalated_findings`               | `test_consensus_unanimous_finding_is_escalated`                                    |
| Only 1 vendor surfaces a finding → `noted_findings`               | `test_consensus_isolated_finding_is_only_noted_not_confirmed`                      |
| Vendor returns `status=error` → excluded from vote               | `test_consensus_treats_error_status_as_error_not_pass`                             |
| Raw vendor verdicts preserved on `ConsensusResult`                | `test_consensus_preserves_raw_vendor_verdicts`                                     |
| Runner invokes vendors in parallel (not sequential)               | `test_runner_invokes_vendors_in_parallel`                                          |
| Vendor raises → captured as error verdict (run does not crash)    | `test_runner_captures_vendor_exception_as_error_verdict`                           |
| Same `id` across vendors → canonical = highest-severity winner     | `test_consensus_aggregates_findings_by_id_across_vendors`                          |
| Single-vendor (degraded) mode passes when sole vendor passes      | `test_verify_task_works_with_single_vendor`                                        |
| GH-flavored tracker record aliases (`id`, `body`, `attachments`)  | `test_record_to_task_handles_gh_issue_aliases`                                     |
| Beads tracker aliases (`bead_id`, `name`, `summary`)              | `test_record_to_task_handles_bead_alias`                                           |
| `record_to_task` is pure & idempotent                             | `test_record_to_task_is_pure_and_idempotent`                                       |
| End-to-end: tracker record → vendors → `ConsensusResult`          | `test_verify_from_tracker_wires_record_through_to_consensus`                       |
| `format_for_tracker` renders markdown summary + status dict       | `test_format_for_tracker_renders_markdown_summary`                                 |
| `include_raw=True` embeds per-vendor `elapsed_ms`                 | `test_format_for_tracker_with_raw_payload_includes_all_vendor_responses`           |

## Low-level details

### Conservative-merge buckets

```
               2 ≤ n_distinct <  valid_count        n_distinct == valid_count
                                            ┌──────────────────────────────┐
n_distinct == 1   │   CONFIRMED              │   ESCALATED                  │
──────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
   NOTED          │   (some, not all)        │   (unanimous; ≥2 vendors)    │
```

### Pass/fail vote

| Active votes | Result      |
|--------------|-------------|
| 3-0 PASS     | passed=True |
| 2-1 PASS     | passed=True |
| 1-2 PASS     | passed=False |
| 0-3 PASS     | passed=False |
| tie          | passed=False |
| any `error`  | excluded from vote |

### ZFC compliance

```
$ grep -nE "\.contains|re\.(match|search)|in (text|message|raw)" mvp_site/verifier/*.py

title: Review PR 7888 Stage-1 Skeptic
AO spawnOrchestrator() never creates an isolated worktree - orchestrator-role sessions get the primary checkout as cwd unconditionally
description:
ROOT CAUSE of tonight's isolation breach (task #30), fully confirmed via source read at ~/project_agento/agent-orchestrator/packages/core/src/session-manager.ts.

The regular worker spawn path, spawn() (session-manager.ts:1131), correctly creates isolation: at line 1268 it defaults workspacePath = project.path, but then checks 'if (plugins.workspace)' (line 1270) -- if a workspace plugin is configured (this project's ~/.agent-orchestrator.yaml sets workspace: worktree for both dark-factory and worldarchitect), it calls plugins.workspace.create(...) and OVERRIDES workspacePath to a real, isolated git worktree (line 1284: workspacePath = wsInfo.path). This is the correct, working isolation mechanism -- confirmed live tonight for every normal wa-*/df-NNN worker session.

spawnOrchestrator() (session-manager.ts:1623) has NO EQUIVALENT CHECK ANYWHERE. It unconditionally passes workspacePath: project.path / worktree: project.path at 4 call sites (lines 1903, 1914, 1949, 1962) with zero workspace-plugin invocation, zero worktree creation, zero isolation of any kind. Every orchestrator-role session (session ID pattern '<sessionPrefix>-orchestrator', e.g. 'df-orchestrator', 'wa-orchestrator' -- both confirmed present in this session's live ao session ls output) gets the PRIMARY CHECKOUT as its cwd by design.

LIVE INCIDENT CONFIRMING THIS IS EXPLOITABLE, NOT JUST THEORETICAL: tonight, tmux session ed3dd2670551-df-orchestrator (PID 1077214, role=orchestrator, cwd=~/projects/dark-factory = the daemon's own home + this session's shared bash cwd) wandered onto branch factory/jleechan-s3c-smoke-red-r1 and PR #208 with an unsubmitted 'Approve Option C' prompt, actively committing/editing files (config/daemon.toml retargeted to dark-factory at 07:30:04Z uncommitted; a coder committed directly to local main at 08:20Z as c0d0df8; two test files modified mid-investigation). Nothing in spawnOrchestrator's code path prevents an orchestrator-role session's underlying CLI process from doing ANY of this -- there is no technical sandboxing, only an unenforced convention that orchestrator sessions are 'meta, read-mostly, monitoring-only.'

RECOMMENDED FIX: give spawnOrchestrator() the SAME workspace-plugin check spawn() already has -- either (a) always create an isolated worktree for orchestrator sessions too (simplest, matches worker-session isolation exactly, though may need its own dedicated persistent worktree since orchestrator sessions are meant to be long-lived/reused rather than per-task), or (b) if orchestrator sessions genuinely need the primary checkout for some legitimate reason (e.g. needing to see other sessions' actual worktree paths, which live under project.path's sibling directories), add an explicit read-only/restricted-write guard at spawn time rather than relying on prompt convention alone. Given tonight's incident, option (a) with a dedicated persistent orchestrator worktree is the safer default -- orchestrator sessions should never be able to touch the primary checkout that the daemon itself treats as its home directory and every other tool in this session assumes is single-writer.

Policy bead companion: live daemon config changes (config/daemon.toml, systemd units, etc.) require operator/orchestrator-level authorization -- a factory session self-retargeting via an uncontrolled write path is exactly the class of action stage-2 safety review needs to prevent structurally, not just by convention.

The exact line numbers and the exact findManagedWorkspace call shape are documented in the handoff doc — a follow-up implementer just needs to re-apply with a clean build cycle.

title: Skeptic review PR 357 for bead jleechan-zaga
PR#205 er_runner child process is completely unwired - forks a full new daemon instance instead (fork-bomb risk, P0)
description: CRITICAL, block-merge finding from independent adversarial review: PR#205's async er_runner refactor calls dispatch_to_child which spawns Command::new(current_exe()).args(['--child-run-er', '--bead-id', ...]) (daemon/src/er_runner.rs:273-288), but main.rs::parse_args (main.rs:80-129) has NO handler for --child-run-er. Any unrecognized first flag falls through to the generic branch, which only checks --once/--dry-run and defaults to CommandMode::Daemon(Args::default()) -- proven by the PR's own test parse_args_ignores_unknown_flags. So EVERY ER-runner dispatch in production forks a BRAND NEW FULL DAEMON INSTANCE (infinite tick loop) instead of running the intended child logic. Worse: run_child_main (er_runner.rs:345-378) -- the function that's supposed to actually do the work -- is itself an unwired no-op stub (just eprintln! + Ok(())). Consequences: (1) no verdict is EVER posted in production -- real dispatches burn the 3-attempt cap silently, gate 6 permanently sticks at Unknown, worse than the pre-refactor synchronous behavior; (2) unbounded process fork-bomb -- each 'child' is actually a second full daemon running its own tick loop against the same target repo/state store, which will itself attempt further ER-runner dispatches, recursively spawning more full daemons; (3) no reaping/timeout -- fork_er_child calls .spawn() and never wait()s or sets a timeout, so orphaned/zombie daemon processes accumulate with no bound. cargo test passes and clippy is clean ONLY because is_test_binary() deliberately short-circuits forking under cargo test -- zero test coverage of the real --child-run-er argv path exists. REQUIRED FIX before merge: wire --child-run-er in main.rs::parse_args/main() to call run_child_main (or the real owned-adapter child pipeline), and implement run_child_main to actually do the work -- or if deliberately deferred, gate fork_er_child behind a feature flag / return NotApplicable until the child entry point exists. Do NOT merge as-is -- this would fork-bomb the production host.

title: [antig] feat(level-up): v2.5 reducer defaults — Stage 1 + Stage 2 (apply_character_adjustment) + Stage 4 (prompt slim) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Adds a pure reducer/schema foundation for a future planning-block character re-authoring flow. The current v2 `review_open=True` default remains unchanged, the new `apply_character_adjustment` entry point is not wired to a production caller or UI, and this PR does not enable automatic level-up application. The earlier prompt section that advertised unwired auto-apply behavior was removed; the remaining prompt diff is newline-only.

## Beads

Bead: `rev-fxxtq`

Related evidence-harness follow-up: `rev-3o535` (post-run campaign export changes the test user identity).

## Governing Design

- [Auto-immediate non-blocking level-up plan](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/main/docs/plans/2026-06-24-level-up-auto-immediate-non-blocking.md)
- [ZFC level-up model-computes architecture](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/main/roadmap/zfc-level-up-model-computes-2026-04-19.md)
- [ZFC level-up PR task specifications](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/main/roadmap/zfc-pr-task-specs-2026-04-22.md)

## Tenets

- Tracking artifact: `rev-fxxtq`; governing implementation plan:
  `docs/plans/2026-06-24-level-up-auto-immediate-non-blocking.md`.
- Preserve the deployed v2 contract: omitted `review_open` still resolves to `True`.
- Keep semantic character choices model-owned; the reducer only performs deterministic copy-on-write application and invariant checks.
- A player-edit adjustment can never change `level` or `experience.current`; callers may widen, but never narrow, the locked-field set.
- Missing persisted level fails closed instead of fabricating level 1.
- Non-actionable sessions (`target_level <= current_level`) never hijack modal routing.

## User Stories

- As a future planning-block caller, I can apply an explicitly supplied character-sheet delta through a copy-on-write reducer without permitting level or XP escalation.
- As a maintainer, I can reopen a sealed review session without changing the deployed default behavior for existing callers.
- As a player on the existing level-up flow, I retain the current modal entry, editing, finish, and return-to-story behavior.

## Production Code Changes

- `mvp_site/agents.py`
  - Routes LevelUpAgent and character-creation suppression only through the
    actionable `is_session_active` predicate; `review_open` alone is a
    non-modal panel signal and cannot force modal routing.
- `mvp_site/level_up_session.py`
  - Adds `SOURCE_PLAYER_EDIT`, its design-doc alias, and the default locked fields.
  - Adds optional `review_open` to `apply_level_up`; `None` preserves the v2 `True` default and explicit `False` is opt-in only.
  - Adds `apply_character_adjustment`, a pure copy-on-write reducer that deep-merges explicit deltas, strips locked paths with warnings, validates source/lock widening, requires a persisted integer level >= 1, and records a non-routing completed adjustment session.
  - Adds `reopen_review` and fail-closed routing for non-actionable sessions.
  - Persists same-level `player_edit` writes as terminal `complete` sessions so
    they satisfy invariants while remaining visible to the review panel.
- `mvp_site/schemas/game_state.schema.json`
  - Adds `player_edit` to the session source enum and documents that the source means created or last revised.
- `mvp_site/prompts/level_up_instruction.md`
  - Runtime instruction text is unchanged; the diff only adds the missing final newline.

## Test Changes

- 22 reducer-default tests cover compatibility defaults, explicit auto-seal opt-in, source validation, copy-on-write behavior, locked paths, missing-level rejection, session invariants, and routing.
- 6 holdout scenarios cover existing auto-grant reducer behavior, empty-sheet rejection, adjustment behavior, locked-level stripping, reopen behavior, and the preserved v2 default.
- Agent-routing regression coverage proves an equal-level open review panel
  does not activate LevelUpAgent.
- Schema strictness and reducer architecture gates include the new enum/foundation.
- Exact-head affected suite: 782 passed, 10 skipped, 104 subtests passed; Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.

## Known Limitations

- `apply_character_adjustment` is a dormant foundation: there is no production caller, planning-block UI, or API wiring in this PR. This evidence does not claim otherwise.
- The existing organic level-up flow is proven compatible, but that flow does not exercise the dormant adjustment reducer; its boundaries are proven by reducer/holdout tests.
- The strict evidence run passed its scenario and signature guard, but post-processing failed to export the campaign because the harness changed the scenario user id. Server logs retain the correct Firestore writes/readbacks and the failure is tracked as `rev-3o535`.
- No frontend files changed, so no new UI surface is introduced.

## Unit Test Evidence

Command: /Users/jleechan/projects/worldarchitect.ai/venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  mvp_site/tests/test_level_up_v25_reducer_defaults.py \

782 passed, 10 skipped, 2 warnings, 104 subtests passed
Ruff: PASS
git diff --check: PASS
```

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

Exact head `a9ba87aafee8b5c80d65b4ecc0cd2c14bc734bd2` ran the canonical `testing_mcp/core/test_level_up_organic.py --level-up-scenario atomicity --full` path against a fresh local gunicorn server with real Firestore and real Gemini streaming.

- Raw redacted Gemini HTTP request/responses, normalized LLM request/responses, streaming HTTP traces, server logs, and BQ insertion records are included in the bundle.
- No mock services or Firestore emulator were used.

- Bundle: https://github.com/jleechanorg/agent-orchestrator/releases/download/worldarchitect-evidence-pr-8018-a9ba87a/pr8018_a9ba87a_evidence.zip
- Archive SHA-256: `55afe6fc549bc3f3ab5ea79ebb072c05c5f789e52538fdcbda532bfd1aa75194`
- Package integrity: 52/52 root checksums PASS after downloading and extracting the published archive.

## Video Evidence

![Captioned exact-head terminal evidence](https://github.com/jleechanorg/agent-orchestrator/releases/download/worldarchitect-evidence-pr-8018-a9ba87a/terminal.gif)

- [MP4](https://github.com/jleechanorg/agent-orchestrator/releases/download/worldarchitect-evidence-pr-8018-a9ba87a/terminal.mp4)

The terminal capture proves exact-head equality, affected-suite results, real-service scenario/signature results, the user-flow transcript, the disclosed export gap, and package integrity. No browser UI changed in this PR.

## Test Plan

- Re-run the 782-test affected suite and reducer/schema lint checks.
- Run the strict real-server atomicity scenario with signed Gemini traces.
- Verify the downloaded release archive SHA-256 and all package checksums.
- Audit current-head review threads and binding Green Gate logs.

## Risk

The primary risk is future misuse of a new reducer that is not yet wired. The implementation fails closed on invalid level/source/lock inputs, preserves the current default, and has no request-path activation in this PR. Rollback is a normal revert of the reducer/schema foundation commits.

## Out of Scope

- Wiring `apply_character_adjustment` into a production route, planning-block handler, or frontend.
- Flipping the deployed `review_open` default.
- Automatic level-up application on the grant turn.
- Fixing the separate testing harness export identity bug (`rev-3o535`).

> Tightens production agent routing for level-up sessions; incorrect predicates could mis-route turns, though new adjustment reducers have no request-path callers yet. Smoke workflow now hard-depends on GCP secret access.

> **Agent routing** in `agents.py` uses only the actionable `is_session_active` predicate (not `is_review_open`), so equal-level adjustment panels with an open review no longer force **LevelUpAgent** or block character creation.
