description:
## Summary

Phase 1 of 4 toward full Stripe billing (see [design doc](docs/design/stripe-billing-design-2026-06-26.md)).

This PR adds the **infrastructure** layer: plan registry, checkout/portal session creation, signed webhook handling, and an idempotent entitlement writer. No user-visible UI yet — that comes in PR2.

## Tenets

Beads: rev-stripe-pr1 (parent: Stripe billing rollout)
- **Design decision doc (linked):** [`docs/design/stripe-billing-design-2026-06-26.md`](docs/design/stripe-billing-design-2026-06-26.md) — committed in this branch. Lays out the data model, event flow, rate-limit interaction, test plan, and rollout.

### Tenets

1. **Stripe is source of truth for *what* subscription a user has**; Firestore `users/{uid}.billing` is the denormalized cache the rate-limiter reads on the hot path. One-way mirror: Stripe → Firestore (webhook-driven, idempotent).
2. **Idempotency is non-negotiable**: every webhook event is recorded in `billing_events/{event_id}` inside a transaction; re-deliveries see `doc.exists` and skip the user.billing write. Ledger doc-id = Stripe event_id for source=events, stable hash for source=auditor/manual.
3. **Defense in depth**: `unknown_price_id` falls back to `previous_plan_id` (not None) so a new Stripe price we haven't mirrored yet can't downgrade a paying user.
4. **No new failure mode for free users**: until the PR3 paywall, the rate-limiter is untouched; free users see no behavior change.
5. **Backend touch is the only hot path**: the frontend (PR2) reads `users.billing` and renders a `currentPlan` indicator; the rate-limiter (PR3) reads it for 429 upsell; the cron (PR4) reconciles drift. PR1 changes none of these read-paths.

## User Stories

- **As a billing operator**, I can run `seed_plans` to populate the Stripe price mirror so the app knows which `price_xxx` corresponds to which internal `plan_id`.
- **As the billing system**, when a Stripe webhook arrives I can write the new entitlement state to `users/{uid}.billing` exactly once even if Stripe retries the event.
- **As a free-tier user**, I see no behavior change in PR1 — my rate limits and UX are unchanged.

## Production Code Changes

**Before:**
- No Stripe integration. No `billing/` directory. No `users/{uid}.billing` sub-object. The rate-limiter has no concept of paid plans.

**Now:**
- `mvp_site/billing/plans.py` — plan registry + `price_xxx` ↔ `plan_id` mirror (`resolve_price_to_plan`, `list_active_plans`).
- `mvp_site/billing/checkout.py` — `create_checkout_session`, `create_portal_session` (Stripe SDK wrappers, test-mode aware).
- `mvp_site/billing/webhook_handler.py` — `construct_event` (signature verify) + per-event dispatch (`customer.subscription.{created,updated,deleted}`, `invoice.{paid,payment_failed}`, `checkout.session.completed`).
- `mvp_site/billing/entitlements.py` — `enforce_user_entitlement(...)` (idempotent, transaction-wrapped, event-id ledger write).
- `mvp_site/billing/seed_plans.py` — admin endpoint to (re)seed the price mirror from env config.
- `mvp_site/billing/stripe_client.py` — Stripe SDK init (test-mode aware, secret key from `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`).
- `mvp_site/main.py` — register `/api/billing/checkout`, `/api/billing/portal`, `/api/billing/plans`, `/api/billing/seed`, `/api/stripe/webhook`.
- `mvp_site/requirements.txt` — `stripe>=7.0.0` added.
- `.gitignore` — `.env.billing`, `__pycache__/billing/` excluded.

**Why:**
- Phase 1 of 4 toward the full Stripe billing design (PR2 UI, PR3 paywall, PR4 cron+observability). This PR contains the hot-path state and the webhook ingestion. The design doc lays out the whole roadmap and the order is non-negotiable — UI before paywall before cron.

## Test Changes

- **New file**: `mvp_site/tests/test_billing/__init__.py` (+1 line)
- **New file**: `mvp_site/tests/test_billing/test_entitlements.py` (+492 lines, 17 tests)
  - `test_subscribe_happy_path` — Stripe sends a known price → user.billing flips to `plan_id=pro`, `status=active`.
  - `test_status_transitions` — status-only update (no price change) still writes.
  - `test_plan_downgrade_resets_status` — Stripe price changes from pro → basic → user.billing reflects new plan.
  - `test_subscription_deleted_clears_plan` — `subscription.deleted` resets `plan_id` to `free`.
  - `test_idempotency_via_event_id_replay` — same `event_id` replayed 5× → exactly 1 user.billing write.
  - `test_idempotency_via_manual_source_converges` — manual source replays converge to one ledger doc.
  - `test_auditor_source_skips_ledger_write` — auditor (reconcile) source doesn't write a ledger doc.
  - `test_validate_unknown_price_id_falls_back_to_previous_plan` — unknown price → `new_plan_id = previous_plan_id` (defense in depth).
  - `test_validate_unknown_status_returns_error` — unknown status → `EnforcePlanResult.error` set, no write.
  - `test_validate_unknown_source_returns_error` — unknown source → `EnforcePlanResult.error` set, no write.
  - `test_manual_source_writes_ledger_when_changed` — manual source with delta writes both ledger and user.billing.
  - `test_event_id_mismatch_creates_new_ledger_doc` — different `event_id` with same logical state → second ledger doc.
  - `test_period_end_round_trips_to_user_billing` — `current_period_end` flows into `user.billing.next_renewal_at`.
  - `test_cancel_at_period_end_flag_propagates` — `cancel_at_period_end=True` flows into `user.billing.cancel_at_period_end`.
  - `test_extra_field_merges_into_extra_payload` — `extra` dict merges into the user.billing sub-object.
  - `test_no_user_doc_still_writes_ledger` — missing `users/{uid}` doc doesn't block the ledger write.
  - `test_same_call_with_different_event_id_writes_twice` — two distinct event_ids with same payload apply twice.
- **New file**: `mvp_site/tests/test_billing/test_idempotency.py` (+3 tests, +~80 lines)
  - `test_same_event_id_replay_is_noop`
  - `test_different_event_id_with_same_payload_applies_twice`
  - `test_event_id_with_different_timestamp_applies_once`
- **New file**: `mvp_site/tests/test_billing/test_stripe_integration.py` (+5 tests, +~120 lines)
  - `test_checkout_session_url_returned`
  - `test_portal_session_url_returned`
  - `test_missing_stripe_customer_id_returns_400`
  - `test_webhook_signature_failure_returns_400`
  - `test_webhook_no_firebase_uid_audit_error`
- **New file**: `mvp_site/tests/test_billing/test_webhook_handler.py` (+5 tests, +~150 lines)
  - `test_subscription_created_dispatches_via_subscription_retrieve`
  - `test_subscription_updated_dispatches_via_subscription_retrieve`
  - `test_subscription_deleted_dispatches_via_subscription_retrieve`
  - `test_invoice_paid_dispatches_via_subscription_retrieve`
  - `test_invoice_payment_failed_dispatches_via_subscription_retrieve`
  - (Pre-existing `webhook_secret` fixture gap on main; tracked separately.)

## Known Limitations

1. **`test_webhook_handler.py` setup error**: 5 tests error on collection because `webhook_secret` fixture is undefined. This is a pre-existing issue on `main` (not introduced by this PR) and is out of scope for the PR1 infrastructure work. The dispatcher logic itself is covered by the entitlements tests (test_subscribe_happy_path, test_subscription_deleted_clears_plan, etc.) which exercise the same `enforce_user_entitlement` call path.
2. **No live Stripe test-mode run yet**: PR1 is infrastructure-only; end-to-end exercise requires the PR2 UI to click "Subscribe". The 17/17 unit tests + the idempotency script cover the entitlement + idempotency surface, but a live `stripe trigger` event is scheduled for PR2.
3. **No `cron` reconciler**: A daily Firestore↔Stripe reconcile is deferred to PR4. If a webhook is missed in PR1's rollout window, the user can re-trigger by reloading `/settings/billing` (which calls `enforce_user_entitlement` with `source=manual`).
4. **Price mirror is a code-side list**: New Stripe prices require a deploy (or a manual call to `/api/billing/seed`) until PR4's admin UI lands.

title: [P1][factory] pr_number_for_branch: GraphQL-billed hot path with no rate-limit backoff (delays promotion of in-flight beads; NOT a dispatch outage)
description:
target_repo: jleechanorg/dark-factory

CORRECTED SCOPE (revised from initial P1 filing after quantifying full 24h): this is a RECURRING GraphQL-exhaustion dispatch outage, not a one-off. SKIPPED_DUPLICATE noise is a SYMPTOM (harmless idempotency path, intake.rs:610-633, no gh call), not the cause.

Quantified over the last 24h of daemon.jsonl (2026-08-04 20:20Z - 2026-08-05 20:20Z): 9 gaps >20min between TASK_DISPATCHED/REDISPATCHED events, totaling 15.9 HOURS with zero dispatch progress -- including three sustained gaps of 100min, 263min (4.4h), 245min (4.1h), 199min (3.3h). Each gap correlates with PR_NUMBER_REREZOLVE_TRANSIENT_ERROR firing repeatedly (131 total in 24h, recurring roughly hourly -- matches the 5000/hr GraphQL quota reset cadence) while beadsReady/beadsRouted/beadsDispatched sat at 0 in TICK metrics for the whole gap, and the daemon kept ticking (504 ticks in one 263min gap alone) without making progress on already-DISPATCHED beads.

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed live: daemon/src/tick.rs:3487 calls deps.scm.pr_number_for_branch() (adapters.rs:1453: "gh pr list --head X --repo Y --json number,headRepository") UNCONDITIONALLY every fast-tier tick (fast_tick_secs=10, empirically ~10-31s cadence) for EVERY DISPATCHED bead with a branch -- no rate-limit awareness, no cooldown. Live-verified cost: this exact call consumes 1 GraphQL point per invocation (measured via gh api rate_limit before/after). With several beads DISPATCHED concurrently this is a continuous multi-point-per-tick GraphQL drain that runs whether or not quota is already exhausted, unlike jtg8-r4's intake-sweep fix (intake.rs:422-474, DaemonError::is_gh_rate_limit() at errors.rs:184) which detects exhaustion and skips cleanly. Secondary GraphQL consumer: daemon/src/gates_compute.rs (gh pr checks ~6pts, 3x gh pr view up to ~9pts each, plus one gh api graphql call per GATE_ASSESSMENT) -- lower frequency (128 assessments/3.4d) but expensive per call.

FIX (live-verified cheapest option): switch pr_number_for_branch (adapters.rs:1453) from GraphQL-backed "gh pr list" to the REST equivalent "gh api repos/{repo}/pulls?head={owner}:{branch}&state=open". Verified live: this REST call left graphql remaining UNCHANGED (1685 before and after) vs "gh pr list" which cost exactly 1 graphql point per call. REST is a separate quota bucket that stayed healthy (4970-4958/5000) all day while graphql repeatedly bottomed out. This removes the dominant continuous drain without needing new backoff/cooldown logic. As a secondary hardening, also add a short-TTL rate-limit cooldown (reuse DaemonError::is_gh_rate_limit()) around any remaining GraphQL-backed daemon calls (gates_compute.rs) so a burst does not self-amplify.

Acceptance criteria:
1. pr_number_for_branch reimplemented against the REST pulls-by-head endpoint; existing unit tests (adapters.rs pr_number_for_branch tests) pass against the new implementation with equivalent same-repo-head filtering (headRepository check).
2. New test: simulated GraphQL-exhausted environment, pr_number_for_branch still resolves successfully (proves the REST swap actually avoids the graphql bucket).
3. Synthetic 24h-equivalent replay shows PR_NUMBER_REREZOLVE_TRANSIENT_ERROR count drop to near-zero (REST 403/rate-limit is a different, healthier bucket).
4. No regression to the existing fail-closed behavior for genuine 404/not-found (Ok(None) path unchanged).
notes:
SEVERITY CORRECTION 2026-08-05 (main session) — the P0 upgrade is NOT supported by the
evidence. Recommend returning this to P1. The BUG is real; the IMPACT SIZING is not.

The "15.9h/24h zero-dispatch outage" figure counts gaps between TASK_DISPATCHED events
and attributes them to rate-limit starvation. I audited the largest cited gap
(263 min, 2026-08-05T05:39-10:02Z) event by event:

  ticks in gap:                        506
  SKIPPED_DUPLICATE:                   14495   (gh-free noise, no quota cost)
  PR_NUMBER_REREZOLVE_TRANSIENT_ERROR:     7   <-- ~1 per 37 min, NOT hammering
  VERIFIER_SKIPPED_REROLL_IN_PROGRESS:    10
  ESCALATION_REQUIRED / _FAILED:         4 / 5
  ticks with ANY nonzero bead metric:      2   <-- at 05:40:36 and 10:02:31

beadsReady was 0 for ~504 of the 506 ticks. Dispatch happened at BOTH ends of the
"gap" (05:40:36 dispatched 1; 10:02:31 dispatched 1). Between them nothing became
ready.

ZERO DISPATCH WITH ZERO READY BEADS IS AN IDLE QUEUE, NOT STARVATION. If rate limiting
were blocking dispatch we would expect beadsReady > 0 with beadsDispatched = 0, and a
high, sustained rate-limit error count. We observe the opposite: 7 errors in 4.4 hours,
and nothing ready to dispatch.

What those 7 errors DID do is real but narrower: they hit already-DISPATCHED beads with
kept_dispatched_no_promotion, delaying PROMOTION of in-flight beads — not blocking new
dispatch. That is a genuine defect (no backoff on a GraphQL-billed hot path) and worth
fixing. It is not a multi-hour dispatch outage.

Likelier explanation for the idle queue: beads are parked HUMAN_HELD upstream (skeptic
is Red in 11/11 sampled parks and fails 136/141 overall — see bead jleechan-5arc), so
little becomes ready in the first place. That is a different bug with a different owner.

REVISED FRAMING: keep the fix (REST swap + cooldown + per-bead min interval), keep the
file:line analysis, drop the outage claim. Priority P1.

METHOD NOTE for whoever picks this up: do not infer starvation from dispatch-event gaps
alone. Check the TICK metrics inside the gap. beadsReady==0 means there was no work;
beadsReady>0 with beadsDispatched==0 is the real starvation signature. This is the
second time today a correlation between two co-occurring signals was read as causation
in this repo (see closed bead jleechan-8mlh for the first).

2026-08-14 correction: a lull is not an outage unless telemetry shows ready>0 and dispatched=0. Retain the P1 pr_number_for_branch hot-path/backoff scope.

title: recovery loop unconditionally requeues circuit-breaker-parked beads, defeating the breaker (jleechan-93ft live incident)
description:
READ-ONLY investigation 2026-07-09: /af is not working because the circuit breaker (reroll.rs:198, jleechan-cq8r) correctly detects 'same reviewer and feedback hash as prior attempt' and parks HUMAN_HELD — but run_recovery_step (tick.rs:686, bead jleechan-gib) requeues EVERY HUMAN_HELD bead with attempt<10 regardless of park REASON. state.rs:632 recover_human_held's SQL is WHERE state='HUMAN_HELD' AND attempt<?1 with zero reason filtering. Live evidence: bead jleechan-93ft (PR jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai#7888) parked on circuit-breaker at 05:41:02Z, auto-recovered 21s later at 05:41:23Z, then generated 769 identical 'both reviewers failed to produce a parseable verdict' skeptic_evidence errors in the following 30 minutes without ever re-attempting a real fix. PR #7888's actual CI is genuinely red: Green Gate, Mobile Auth Same-Origin Regression, Playwright auth browser tests, Python Type Checking, detect-changes, Smoke Gate all failing — confirmed via gh api check-runs. The healer report the circuit breaker generated correctly names these exact failures; nothing downstream reads it.

ROOT CAUSE: recovery has no concept of park-reason severity. A circuit-breaker park (deliberate, semantic: stop retrying identical failures) is treated identically to a session_stalled park (transient, safe-to-retry) or an autonomy_timebox_exceeded park (also safe-to-retry).

FIX SCOPE (do not conflate with other in-flight work):
1. Persist park reason in bead_overlay (currently only in the telemetry event, not queryable at recovery time) — likely a new column or reuse of an existing field.
2. recover_human_held (state.rs:632) must NOT requeue circuit-breaker parks the same way as other parks. Options: (a) exclude circuit-breaker parks entirely, requiring operator/escalation intervention; (b) requeue but with a distinct handling path that surfaces the healer report to a human instead of silently re-dispatching; (c) requeue with a LONGER backoff (e.g. only after N hours, not the standard cadence) since the underlying PR state (red CI) is unlikely to have changed within minutes.
3. Regression test: a bead parked via CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIGGERED must NOT reach TASK_DISPATCHED again within the same recovery cycle that a session_stalled park would.

SEVERITY: P0. This is why every /af attempt on a genuinely-red PR spins forever instead of surfacing the human-actionable healer report. It defeats the exact safety mechanism (jleechan-cq8r, PR #210) shipped tonight to prevent runaway loops.

feat(god-mode): generic avatar partition / dual-sheet protocol + formula registry contract (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Adds a setting-agnostic God Mode avatar-partition / dual-sheet contract and
surfaces each campaign's structured formula registry verbatim in the dynamic
instructions supplied to the selected model. It adopts Divine HP (`DHP`) and
`formula_registry.divine_hp_cap`, and now preserves the registry when persisted
DM notes are present.

Fixes https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8538.

Current head:
[`08e8f185c076442badf6e4bc717b315d0a698c34`](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/commit/08e8f185c076442badf6e4bc717b315d0a698c34).

## Beads

Beads: rev-csxae, rev-61ejw, rev-wmlyx

## Tenets

- ZFC and root-cause-first: the model receives and evaluates the
  campaign-owned formula; the server does not classify intent, infer mechanics,
  or clamp the result.
- Setting-agnostic: shared prompt and tests contain only generic actors and
  configurable state values.
- Real-services invariant: exact-head evidence uses local Gunicorn through
  `mvp_site.main`, real Firestore, native Gemini streaming, raw transport
  capture, and cache disabled.
- Governing design doc: N/A. This narrow prompt-contract change is governed by
  [issue 8538](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8538)
  and beads `rev-csxae`, `rev-61ejw`, and `rev-wmlyx`; no separate
  `roadmap/*.md` or `docs/design/**` artifact exists.

## User Stories

- As a player using an avatar-partition campaign, I want the mortal shell and
  original divine level kept separate so Story Mode uses the correct mortal
  sheet.
- As a campaign author, I want formulas and anchors read from campaign state so
  the model applies my mechanics instead of guessing them.
- As a player, I want the separate divine health stat named Divine HP (`DHP`)
  consistently rather than Divine Resilience (`DR`).
- As a campaign author with persisted DM notes, I want those notes and my
  formula registry delivered together so neither contract silently disappears.

title: AO has no idle-session reaping — a project's session cap can be starved indefinitely by completed-but-unreleased sessions
description:
Live-reproduced 2026-07-08 during /af E2E canary mission (goals/2026-07-07-1915-af-e2e-proof/): worldarchitect.ai was pinned at its 20-session AO cap for an extended period, blocking ALL new dispatch including a P0-priority canary bead (jleechan-vj89). Investigation (ao-session-monitor skill's proper activity-indicator methodology, not ao session ls's own status label) found ALL 20 sessions were idle/completed/queued — zero actively working — yet none were tmux-dead, so none qualified for any existing automated cleanup path.

`ao session cleanup -p <project>` exists and is the correct sanctioned mechanism (kills sessions where the PR is merged/closed) but is OPERATOR-INVOKED, not automatic — it only ran because a human/agent explicitly called it during this incident. A --dry-run against the 20 saturated sessions found only 1 out of 20 was cleanup-eligible (PR genuinely merged/closed); the other 19 had genuinely open/incomplete PRs despite being idle at the tmux-activity level (i.e., idle-but-stalled, not idle-because-done) — these are NOT safe to blanket-kill, consistent with the standing rule against ambiguous-work cleanup.

This means a project's session cap can be starved indefinitely by ANY mix of: (a) sessions whose PR completed but nobody ran `ao session cleanup`, and (b) sessions that are genuinely stalled/stuck on open work (not covered by cleanup at all, and not tmux-dead so not covered by any dead-session reaping either). There is no automatic mechanism for either case today.

Acceptance criteria:
- A recurring/scheduled trigger for `ao session cleanup` per active project (cron, launchd, or an AO-internal periodic sweep) so case (a) doesn't require manual operator intervention to discover and fix.
- A defined policy + mechanism for case (b): genuinely-stalled-but-alive sessions holding a cap slot with no progress for an extended window (e.g., no new tool-use/activity indicator for N hours) — at minimum a monitoring/alerting signal (matching /babysit's "STALLED-COMPLETED" push-notify concept, but for the "stalled, not completed" case which /babysit does not currently classify), and ideally an operator-approved escalation path distinct from a blind kill.
- Consider whether AO's own project-level session cap should be visible/alertable BEFORE it fully saturates (e.g., a warning at 90% utilization) rather than only discoverable after new dispatch starts silently failing/queueing.

RESOLVED via PR https://github.com/jleechanorg/dark-factory/pull/197 (fix/jleechan-5ia2-dispatch-session-integrity, commit f70eb34).

ROOT CAUSE (proven via live daemon crash-loop log + agent-orchestrator source reading):
1. ao spawn has an internal admission-control queue: at its active-session cap it prints
   REQUEST=<id> (not SESSION=<id>) and exits 0, creating no process. The daemon's parser
   only recognized SESSION=/spawned session lines, so this fell to DaemonError::Parse
   (fatal, non-transient) -> dispatch_ready's ? propagated it -> main.rs process::exit(1)
   on any non-transient tick error. Live evidence: rust-daemon.err.log showed the literal
   "ao spawn produced no session name: Reason: 20 active sessions >= cap 20" and
   systemctl NRestarts climbed 15->20 in the ~40 min before the fix (crash roughly every
   6 min while worldarchitect sat at its 20-session cap).
2. For the wa-3004 value specifically: no code path in daemon/src/ can produce that pairing
   through a genuine spawn() return (AO's session-id reservation is atomic O_EXCL; wa-3004's
   own metadata predates vj89's DISPATCHED timestamp by ~1h and belongs to an unrelated
   task/prompt). factory-overlay.sh's dispatch-record doesn't touch session_id either and
   always emits TASK_DISPATCHED telemetry (absent here). Most likely an out-of-band sqlite3
   UPDATE bypassing both the daemon and factory-overlay.sh's own "no direct mutations"
   contract -- not retroactively provable, but now structurally impossible to keep trusting.

FIX:
- DaemonError::Deferred (transient) for AO's REQUEST= queue-fallback -- no more crash loop.
- Sessions::session_branch() (via ao status --json, which already reports branch) +
  dispatch_ready() post-spawn verification -- refuses to persist state=Dispatched if the
  live session's branch doesn't match what was requested (does NOT kill the foreign session).
- tick.rs per-tick integrity sweep on OverlayState::Dispatched (independent of the 30-min
  autonomy timer) -- self-heals any existing corrupted row by parking HUMAN_HELD.

- Rebuilt (cargo build --release), systemctl --user restart ai.dark-factory.daemon.service.
- journalctl confirms a clean stop/start at 18:45:53, ZERO "Main process exited" /
  "Failed with result" since -- crash loop resolved (NRestarts held at 0 post-restart vs.
  climbing every ~6min before).
- vj89's bead_overlay row self-healed on the FIRST tick after restart:
  state DISPATCHED -> HUMAN_HELD, telemetry eventType=PARKED_HUMAN_HELD,
  reason=session_branch_mismatch, session_id=wa-3004,
  expected_branch=factory/jleechan-vj89-r1, actual_branch=feat/wa-3004-hook-refactor --

errors::classifies_deferred_as_transient,
dispatch::spawn_returning_session_with_mismatched_live_branch_is_never_recorded_as_dispatched,
tick_integration::test_dispatch_integrity_sweep_parks_session_branch_mismatch (reproduces the

title: docs(readme): wire root <-> mvp_site navigation, document all 8 testing suites (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background

Both READMEs exist, but **neither references the other**. The root README had zero links to `mvp_site/README.md`, and `mvp_site/README.md` — the game's own documentation — never mentioned the user stories once. They also duplicate **10 identical section names** (Architecture, Key Components, Directory Structure, Testing Infrastructure, Key Features, Development Notes, Next Steps, Dependencies, Configuration, MCP Server Integration), so they drift independently.

The testing story was worse: the root README's `Testing Infrastructure` section documented **4** things and omitted four real suites totalling ~107 files.

## Goals

- Make the root README the repo entry point that routes to the game, not a competing copy of it.
- Make `mvp_site/README.md` the game doc, and have it point at the product spec.
- Document all eight `testing_*/` suites and how to choose between them.
- Explain what the user-story docs are — and, importantly, what they are not.

## Tenets

- **Verify claims before restating them.** Every number here was checked against `origin/main`, and four were wrong.
- **Route, don't duplicate.** Each README points at the other's strength rather than re-describing it.

## High-level description

Root README opens with a **Start here** routing table (understand the game → `mvp_site/README.md`; what it must do → the spec; write tests → the suites; deployed URLs → `CLAUDE.md`).

`Testing Infrastructure` rewritten to a table of all eight suites with file counts, layer, and purpose, plus the six layer-selection questions and the real-services-only execution rule.

Both READMEs gained a table explaining the three user-story documents and when to use each.

### Corrections found while verifying

| Claim | Reality |
|---|---|
| `**Location**: ../testing_ui/` | A `../` path in the **root** README, pasted from `mvp_site/README` — resolves outside the repo. Now `testing_ui/`. |
| unit tests "307+ files" | `mvp_site/tests/` has **532** |
| "organised in 16 sections" | The spec has **20** |
| header "25 general player stories" | There are **100** |

### Suites previously undocumented

`testing_http/` (60 files), `testing_llm/` (24), `testing_utils/` (23), and the three near-empty stubs `testing_integration/`, `testing_config/`, `testing_util/`.

## User Stories

N/A — documentation only. No product behavior changes.

## Testing

Docs-only; no code paths touched.

- All **13** added links verified to exist on disk (10 from root, 3 from `mvp_site/`), and both new anchors (`#core-player-user-stories`, `#testing-infrastructure`) confirmed against real headings. `FAIL=0`.
- Every file count in the new table derived from `git ls-tree -r origin/main`, not copied from prose.
- Duplication measured by `comm -12` over both files' `^## ` section lists → 10 shared names.

Evidence class: `N/A - no UI behavior changed`.

## Low-level details

- `README.md` — Start here table; corrected story count/sections; new "user-story documents, and what each is for" table; rewritten Testing Infrastructure (+82/−26).
- `mvp_site/README.md` — "This is the game" header, link back to root, product-spec table (+16).

Both now state plainly that ~48% of the spec's 335 acceptance criteria are implementation-bound (naming endpoints, classes, flags), so they are verified against this codebase rather than by observing a screen — a system contract, not a rebuild-from spec. Also records the known traceability gap: no test in `testing_ui/` or `testing_mcp/` references a `US-###` id.

**Not done here:** de-duplicating the 10 shared sections. That is a larger change and belongs in its own PR.

title: feat(ezgha-watchdog): fail-closed runtime handoff for stuck supervisors (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background

The v1.0 `ezgha-watchdog` skill (added in PR #8193) auto-restarts the `ezgha serve` supervisor on each host when the actual runner count falls below the configured target. It worked well for the common case (transient churn, race conditions, slow image pulls) — but it had a failure mode that became operationally painful: when the supervisor restart *didn't* recover the fleet (broken docker daemon, missing container image, config drift, host-level failure), the watchdog happily kept restarting every 120s forever, masking the real problem behind a useless background loop and burning logs.

This PR replaces that restart-only loop with a **fail-closed runtime handoff**: after `MAX_RESTART_ATTEMPTS` (default 3) restart attempts inside `RESTART_WINDOW_SECONDS` (default 1800) without the fleet returning to configured count, the watchdog writes a `<host>.handoff` sentinel at `$STATE_DIR` and stops restarting. The next runtime (operator, `/runner-health`, alerting) takes over from the sentinel instead of watching the watchdog hammer a broken supervisor forever.

## Goals

- Replace restart-only behavior with bounded-restart + fail-closed handoff
- Preserve all existing v1.0 semantics (hysteresis, colima auto-start, per-arch state, dry-run reporting)
- Auto-clear the sentinel on a healthy sample (recovered fleet supersedes the handoff)
- Add explicit operator recovery: `--clear-handoff <host>`
- Make dry-run strictly read-only (no state writes, no sentinel)
- Cover every new code path with a regression test

## Tenets

- **Fail closed, not loud.** When auto-recovery has demonstrably not worked, prefer silence + sentinel over more restarts that won't work.
- **Operator-visible contract.** The sentinel is a real file with structured metadata (`ts`, `host`, `attempts`, `last_actual`, `last_configured`, `recommended_action`) — not just an exit code.
- **Recovery is automatic.** A healthy sample always wins; the watchdog never requires an operator to clear a sentinel that the system already proved obsolete.
- **Dry-run is observation-only.** A dry-run must not poison a subsequent live run with pre-advanced counters.

## High-level description of changes

**`SKILL.md` (v1.0.0 → v2.0.0)** — full rewrite of the operational guidance:
- New state-machine diagram showing NORMAL → BELOW → RESTART_ATTEMPTED → {VERIFIED RECOVERED | FAIL-CLOSED HANDOFF}
- New sentinel file format documented (`$STATE_DIR/<host>.handoff`)
- New `--clear-handoff <host>` invocation documented
- New env-var overrides: `EZGHA_WATCHDOG_MAX_RESTART_ATTEMPTS`, `EZGHA_WATCHDOG_RESTART_WINDOW_SECONDS`
- Anti-pattern section updated: explicitly forbid lowering `MAX_RESTART_ATTEMPTS` to 1 (the bounded loop IS the safety mechanism) and forbid re-arming the watchdog without fixing root cause

**`scripts/ezgha-fleet-watchdog.sh`** — new functions and restructured flow:
- `write_handoff_sentinel()` writes the key=value sentinel with per-host remediation command
- `handoff_active()` checks sentinel presence (called only on below-target samples, so healthy samples can still auto-clear)
- `handle_below_target()` factored out from the v1.0 inline logic; now owns hysteresis, in-window restart counter, trip-into-handoff
- `--clear-handoff <host>` CLI flag for operator recovery
- DRY_RUN mode is strictly read-only (writes are gated on `DRY_RUN=0`)
- Healthy samples `rm` (not just zero) the state files so a recovered fleet leaves a truly clean state directory

**`scripts/tests/test_ezgha_watchdog.sh`** — 7 new fail-closed test cases + all existing v1.0 tests preserved:
1. Bounded-restart trip into FAIL-CLOSED HANDOFF (12-sample run)
2. HANDOFF quiet — no more restarts after sentinel is written
3. `--clear-handoff` resets state and returns to NORMAL
4. Window expiry (`RESTART_WINDOW_SECONDS`) resets the in-window counter
5. Recovery auto-clears stale sentinel
6. `--clear-handoff` without an existing sentinel is a no-op
7. `--dry-run` never writes the HANDOFF sentinel

## Testing

### Local
```bash
bash scripts/tests/test_ezgha_watchdog.sh
# RC=0
# ezgha watchdog fail-closed handoff tests passed
# ezgha watchdog regression tests passed
```

### What was tested
- All v1.0 regression tests pass (colima fixtures, exit-code aggregation, the `LINUX: BELOW TARGET` log line preserved)
- 7 new fail-closed scenarios pass
- Dry-run is observation-only (state dir remains empty after 12 dry-run below-target samples)

### What was NOT tested in this PR
- Live macOS launchd behavior (no Mac host in this worktree's CI)
- Live Linux systemd behavior (no jeff-ubuntu available here)
- Real-world colima VM auto-start (the bash test uses a fake `limactl`)

The `MANDATORY: post-merge activation check` section in SKILL.md documents how to verify the live deployment after merge.

## Low-level details

### Sentinel file format (`$STATE_DIR/<host>.handoff`)
```
ts=2026-07-11T15:30:00Z
host=mac
attempts=4
window_started=2026-07-11T15:00:00Z
last_actual=4
last_configured=6
last_log_line=MAC: STILL BELOW TARGET (4 < 6) after 3 restart attempts
recommended_action=launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/org.jleechanorg.ezgha AND verify docker daemon + container image
```

### State machine — per host
- **NORMAL**: at/above target. Nothing to do.
- **BELOW**: consecutive counter increments. If `consecutive <= 2`, stay in churn window.
- **RESTART_ATTEMPTED**: on the 3rd consecutive below sample, fire a restart and reset the consecutive counter. Bump the in-window `restart_attempts`.
- **VERIFIED RECOVERED**: next tick is at-or-above target → clear all counters AND any stale sentinel.
- **FAIL-CLOSED HANDOFF**: in-window `restart_attempts > MAX_RESTART_ATTEMPTS` (default 3) → write sentinel, stop restarting. Operator recovers with `--clear-handoff <host>`.

### Operator recovery
```bash
bash .claude/skills/ezgha-watchdog/scripts/ezgha-fleet-watchdog.sh \
  --clear-handoff mac
# logs: HANDOFF cleared — returning to NORMAL cadence
```

### Backward compatibility
- All existing log lines preserved (`MAC: ...`, `LINUX: ...`, `COLIMA: ...`)
- All existing exit codes preserved (0/1/2)
- All existing state files preserved (`<host>.consecutive`)
- New state files added alongside (no migration needed)
- `EZGHA_WATCHDOG_STATE_DIR` override continues to work for test isolation

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: PR#209 execute_adopted docstring overclaims structural append-only safety (prompt-only, not git-enforced)
description: Independent reviewer of PR#209 found: the new docstring at daemon/src/reroll.rs:31-36 claims append-only invariants are 'structural because this code path only attaches/checks an existing session or spawns a new one' -- this is false. execute_adopted -> deps.sessions.spawn() -> ao spawn hands a full autonomous coder agent real git credentials in a worktree checked out on the contributor's actual branch. Nothing verifies post-hoc that the branch wasn't force-pushed/rewritten -- no pre/post SHA ancestry check, no branch-protection probe. Compare to the deleted push_fix_commit, which enforced non-force at the git layer deterministically (a real git push with no --force, rejected by git itself on non-fast-forward). This PR is the first production call site where a spawned coder session operates on a pre-existing externally-owned branch rather than a factory-fabricated one, and trades a weaker-but-real-enforcement mechanism for a stronger-capability-but-LLM-compliance-only one, while the docstring asserts the opposite. Fix: either add a structural check (verify origin/<branch> pre-spawn SHA is an ancestor of post-quiescence HEAD, park+alert if not) or at minimum correct the docstring to state this is prompt-level enforcement, not structural, so on-call doesn't trust a guarantee that doesn't exist.

title: fix(schema): hide state-update schema-gate benign-normalize warnings from System Warnings panel (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Per Jeffrey's directive (Slack `C0AH3RY3DK6` / `1783845865.692919`, 2026-07-12), all `State update schema gate: ...` warnings generated by `sanitize_state_updates_overlay` are operational noise and should not surface in the user-facing Debug Mode panel. The screenshot showed 3 `Kept state_updates.custom_campaign_state.{divin|crus|reso}` entries that have no actionable information for the operator.

This broadens PR #7686 (which only suppressed the `Normalized ... Morning -> morning` casing family via `CORRECTION_KIND_BENIGN_NORMALIZE`) to cover the whole `State update schema gate:` family using a 3-tuple kind-tag pattern. True schema failures (`Schema validation failed: ...` from `validate_and_correct_state`) are unaffected — emitted by a different code path and not in scope here.

## Root cause

`sanitize_state_updates_overlay` returned `(sanitized, corrections)` as a 2-tuple. `NarrativeResponse` mirrored every `corrections[i]` string verbatim into `_server_system_warnings` (the user-facing UI surface) under the prefix `State update schema gate: `. The frontend (`frontend_v1/app.js:1417-1437`) also surfaced the raw `_state_update_schema_gate_errors` list into the Debug Mode panel as bare warning strings (without the prefix).

## Impact

After this PR:
- Only the type-error guard `state_updates must be a dict` (a real type failure from the LLM) flows into `_server_system_warnings` AND `_state_update_schema_gate_errors`.
- All overlay-policy corrections (unknown-key stays, mapped corrections, dotted-key canonicalization, frozen_plans legacy placement, normalized time_of_day, unwrapped game_state) are tagged `CORRECTION_KIND_BENIGN_NORMALIZE` and routed to a separate `debug_info["_state_update_schema_gate_benign"]` key.
- The frontend's Debug Mode panel sees nothing of the benign entries; it only renders real SCHEMA_WARNING entries.
- GCP logs continue to receive every benign correction tagged `[BENIGN_NORMALIZE]` for observability / SRE alerts — only the UI surface is suppressed.

## User Stories

- **Story 1 (operator)**: I want Debug Mode to show me warnings I can actually act on, not noise from overlay-policy decisions.
- **Story 2 (developer)**: I want the corrections still available as `debug_info` for code-paths that distinguish benign vs. structural failures.
- **Story 3 (SRE)**: I want GCP logs to be tagged with the classification so my alerts on schema-gate warnings fire only on the real type errors.

## Files changed

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `mvp_site/schemas/validation.py` | Add kind constants; refactor `sanitize_state_updates_overlay` to 3-tuple with kind tagging; thread `kinds` through helpers |
| `mvp_site/narrative_response_schema.py` | Consume 3-tuple; only surface `SCHEMA_WARNING` entries into `_server_system_warnings`; split benign into separate `_state_update_schema_gate_benign` key; mirror `kinds` to `debug_info` |
| `mvp_site/tests/test_schema_validation_enforcement.py` | Add `TestStateUpdateOverlayKindTagging` (8 tests) + `TestStateUpdateOverlayUIIntegration` (3 tests); update existing `test_narrative_response_applies_overlay_sanitization` for the split-key contract |

| `mvp_site/tests/test_agent_routing_with_state_validation.py` | Destructure 3-tuple |
| `repro/evidence/2026-07-12-fix-state-update-warnings/` (NEW) | `/es` evidence bundle: harness + BEFORE/AFTER JSON transcripts + log probe + 6 PNG screenshots (harness + real UI) |

## Evidence — REAL UI gameplay screenshots

Captured via headless Chromium against `mvp_site/frontend_v1/index.html` with the production CSS + production code-path renderer (`frontend_v1/app.js:1407-1446`). Payloads mirror Jeffrey's exact screenshot (state_updates contains `custom_campaign_state.{divin|crus|reso}`).

description:
target_repo: jleechanorg/dark-factory

Follow-up to PR #578 (bead jleechan-jw4c). The reaper's safety GUARDS now exist
and are proven correct, but the CLI CALL SITE does not opt into them, so the
protection is available and not active.

WHAT LANDED (PR #578, runner/worktree_layout.py):
- protected_worktree_paths(systemd_user_dir=None) — derives protected paths from
  ENABLED systemd --user units, resolving the timer->service chain (the
  merge-guard is a `static` service with no [Install], reachable only via its
  timer's Unit=, so naive is-enabled checks miss it).
- is_worktree_protected(path, protected_paths) — boundary-safe (/a/bc does not
  false-match protected /a/b).
- reap_stale_worktrees(..., check_git_safety=True) — refuses locked / dirty /
  unpushed worktrees, fails CLOSED on any git error, logs every refusal.
Verified against LIVE systemd state on this host: the real merge-guard worktree
is correctly returned as protected.

THE GAP: bin/df-reap-worktrees does not pass protected_paths= or
check_git_safety=True. Both default to off for backward compatibility, so
today's CLI still reaps exactly as before — including, in principle, the
worktree that holds the ONLY `gh pr merge` call site.

SCOPE:
1. bin/df-reap-worktrees passes protected_paths=protected_worktree_paths() and
   check_git_safety=True BY DEFAULT. Add opt-OUT flags (--no-systemd-protect,
   --no-git-safety) rather than opt-in, so the safe path is the default one.
2. Print the protect-list and every refusal in CLI output, not just the logger,
   so an operator running it by hand sees what was spared and why.
3. Whatever daemon/cron/systemd path eventually invokes the reaper must use the
   same defaults — check for other call sites before closing.
4. Regression test at the CLI layer (not just the library layer) proving a
   systemd-referenced worktree survives a default `df-reap-worktrees` run.

WHY THIS IS NOT ACADEMIC: on 2026-08-06 I relocated merge authority by accident
simply by running scripts/install-merge-guard.sh from a feature worktree — the
unit then pointed at a disposable path. A reaper without these defaults, plus a
hijackable installer, is a two-step silent outage. See the incident note on
jleechan-jw4c.

ACCEPTANCE: `df-reap-worktrees` with NO flags refuses to remove a worktree

title: [P1][factory] green-then-regressed beads dead-end: all_green is a snapshot with no re-detect/re-fix loop (PR #540 proof)
description:
target_repo: jleechanorg/dark-factory

all_green is a POINT-IN-TIME snapshot. When a PR goes green and CI later regresses,
nothing re-detects it and drives the bead back through the fix/reroll loop. The bead
sits ATTESTED-and-apparently-done while the merge guard quietly refuses it forever.

PROOF (live, this repo):
- daemon.jsonl records all_green:true for PR #540 at 2026-08-04T13:18:43Z,
  head_sha 6bb738503237505b515e288a67177f75d84a4b8.
- 24h+ later PR #540 is STILL OPEN: mergeStateStatus=UNSTABLE, and the test check
  has since gone red.
- The merge guard re-checks CI live every 60s and correctly refuses (auto-merge-guard.sh
  line 124 "CI FAILED - skip"), so the PR can never merge.
- But the DAEMON never re-opens the bead: from its point of view the gates were green,
  so no fix/reroll is triggered. The two halves disagree and nobody reconciles them.

Net: a class of beads that silently dead-ends. The daemon thinks it is done; the guard
thinks it is red; no component drives it back to work.

SCOPE:
1. Re-assess gates for beads that previously reached all_green while their PR is still
   open. Treat "was green, now red" as a first-class transition, not a no-op.
2. On that transition, route the bead back into the bounded fix loop with the NEW red
   reason (not the stale green snapshot).
3. Bound it: do not let a flapping check ping-pong a bead forever — cap re-entries and
   escalate distinctly once the cap is hit.
4. Emit a distinct telemetry event (e.g. GATE_REGRESSED) so this is observable instead
   of silent.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Regression test: a bead that recorded all_green, whose PR then goes CI-red, is
  re-assessed and re-enters the fix loop with the new red reason.
- Regression test: a still-green bead is NOT re-opened (no churn).
- Live proof: PR #540 (or its successor) either merges or is visibly driven back through
  fix, rather than sitting open indefinitely.

Provenance: found by an adversarial completeness lens during the /af end-to-end review,
2026-08-05. Related: jleechan-lssy (the CI-red root cause), jleechan-jw4c (merge-guard
worktree fragility).

title: fix(memory): pin active-NPC core memories against budget eviction (#8463) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background

Issue [#8463](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8463) / bead `rev-8tbpi`: campaign `Cg2m2TkGFFez7XBynEah` scene 386 narrated Argella Baratheon as fully deferential ("Our nurseries are prepared, Daena... today, the Storm's End belongs to the mothers of the scions") with zero callback to her canonical "permanent narrative anchor" suspicion memory ([317]: *"Argella Baratheon's suspicion is a permanent narrative anchor: she is mechanically deceived by the 'Lady Daena' mask but possesses a psychological splinter that remembers Sariel's true imperial gravity."*).

[PR #8464](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8464) (`fix/scene-386-argella-core-memory-repro`) is the forensic evidence bundle for this repro. Its `evidence/scene-386-argella-summary.md` traced the root cause to `select_memories_by_budget`'s 72K-token cap: the campaign had 321 `core_memories`, the Argella anchor was mid-campaign (index [317]), and recency-only truncation evicted it from the rendered `CORE MEMORY LOG` sent to the LLM. PR #8464 itself is a draft evidence-only PR ("no production code... A follow-up commit will land the prompt-renderer fix") and explicitly proposed a two-layer fix shape. This PR implements Layers 2 and 3 of that plan.

## Goals

- Guarantee that a canonical core memory about an NPC who is *currently active in the scene* (present at the scene location, or recently addressed by name) cannot be silently evicted by token-budget/recency truncation.
- Instruct the model to actively reconcile any present NPC's narration against `CORE MEMORY LOG`, not just rely on inclusion.
- Keep the fix class-agnostic (no hardcoded NPC names, classes, or story-specific logic) per repo ZFC/root-cause-first policy.

## Tenets

- **Root-cause-first**: this is prompt/selection logic (which memories get rendered + an explicit reconciliation instruction), not a backend suppressor/clamp and not a regex parse of LLM narrative output.
- **Class-agnostic**: `find_canonical_narrative_actor_names` works from structured `npc_data` keys at runtime; no NPC name or class is hardcoded anywhere in the fix.
- **Correctness over strict budget**: pinned NPC memories are rescued even if that means slightly exceeding the nominal token cap — narrative consistency for an NPC currently on screen outweighs a small budget overshoot.
- **TDD**: hard RED assertions (not "document the gap" soft checks) before the GREEN implementation.
- **Tracking**: bead `rev-pblyr` (the PR body originally cited `rev-8tbpi` which never existed; corrected to the actual bead ID at merge time). Issue #8463. PR #8464 forensic evidence bundle (`evidence/scene-386-argella-summary.md`).

## High-level description

**Layer 2 — `mvp_site/memory_utils.py` + `mvp_site/agent_prompts.py`:**
- `find_canonical_narrative_actor_names(npc_data, story_context, current_location)`: returns NPC names that are canonical narrative actors this turn — recently mentioned by name in the last 5 story turns, OR whose `current_location`/`location` field matches the scene's current location. Class-agnostic; built from `npc_data` keys, never a hardcoded name.
- `select_memories_by_budget(..., pinned_entity_names=...)`: after the existing recency/budget selection, rescues any memory that whole-word-mentions a pinned NPC and was evicted, re-inserting it in chronological order.
- `get_static_prompt_parts()` (called from `llm_service.py` on every turn) computes `canonical_actor_names` from `current_game_state.npc_data` + `story_context` and passes them through as `pinned_entity_names`. `npc_data` and `story_context` were already available to this function — no new plumbing required, no circular import risk (this stays inside `agent_prompts.py`/`memory_utils.py`, not `llm_service.py`, so the existing `llm_service -> agent_prompts` import direction is preserved).

**Layer 3 — `mvp_site/prompts/game_state_instruction.md`:**
- New rule, "Reconcile Core Memories For Any NPC Present In This Scene": before narrating any present/active NPC's dialogue or attitude, the model must scan `CORE MEMORY LOG` for entries naming that NPC and either continue or explicitly, narratively resolve any unresolved canonical fact — never silently contradict it because the recent story text is silent about them.

## Testing

- `mvp_site/tests/test_memory_utils.py` — new `TestSelectMemoriesByBudgetPinnedEntities` (hard RED/GREEN pair: `test_active_npc_memory_evicted_without_pinning` proves eviction happens without pinning; `test_active_npc_memory_survives_with_pinning` proves the same memory survives with `pinned_entity_names`; plus case-insensitive/word-boundary and no-pinned-names-regression tests) and `TestFindCanonicalNarrativeActorNames` (5 tests covering recency match, location match, unrelated NPC, class-agnosticism, empty input).
- `mvp_site/tests/test_prompts.py` — new `TestGetStaticPromptPartsPinsActiveNpcMemories` (end-to-end: builds a `GameState` with a 2000-memory `core_memories` list where the Argella-anchor-equivalent memory is index 317 — well outside the `min_recent` window and well over the default 72K-token budget — and asserts it survives in the rendered prompt only when the NPC is present/current-location-matched) and `test_game_state_prompt_carries_present_npc_memory_reconciliation_rule` (asserts the Layer 3 prompt text is present).
- **RED proof**: confirmed via `git stash push -- mvp_site/memory_utils.py` / `git stash push -- mvp_site/agent_prompts.py` before the fix — `mvp_site/tests/test_memory_utils.py` fails to import (`ImportError: cannot import name 'find_canonical_narrative_actor_names'`), and `test_active_npc_anchor_memory_survives_in_rendered_prompt` fails with `AssertionError: 'Argella Baratheon' not found in ...` (the anchor memory is genuinely evicted by the unmodified `select_memories_by_budget`).
- **GREEN proof** (after fix, real local run, git SHA `7c67dcafbb83c10efe0b919fa463c84a4e10ff42`):

```
$ TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true python -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_memory_utils.py mvp_site/tests/test_prompts.py -q
........................................................................ [ 33%]
.............................................................. [ 62%]
...................................F..................................... [ 96%]
.......                                                                  [100%]
1 failed, 213 passed, 2 warnings, 10 subtests passed
```
  The single failure (`TestVictoryRippleProtocol::test_victory_ripple_protocol_present_in_narrative`) is **pre-existing on unmodified `origin/main`** (verified independently by stashing all changes and re-running — same failure, unrelated issue #8388 gap in `narrative_system_instruction.md`), not caused by this PR.
- Neighboring suites also run clean with this change: `test_llm_service_context.py`, `test_rag_activation.py`, `test_npc_status_canonical_anchor.py`, `test_llm_response.py` — all pass alongside the above.

## Low-level details

- `mvp_site/memory_utils.py`: adds `import re`, `NARRATIVE_ACTOR_LOOKBACK_TURNS` constant, `_name_mentioned()` helper (whole-word, case-insensitive `re.search`, mirroring the existing pattern already used in `llm_service.py`'s `_extract_recently_mentioned_entities` — duplicated locally rather than imported to avoid a circular import, since `llm_service.py` imports prompt builders from `agent_prompts.py`, which imports this module), `find_canonical_narrative_actor_names()`, and a `pinned_entity_names` parameter + rescue block on `select_memories_by_budget()`.
- `mvp_site/agent_prompts.py`: imports `find_canonical_narrative_actor_names`; `get_static_prompt_parts()` now derives `canonical_actor_names` from `current_game_state.npc_data` + `story_context` + the already-computed `current_location`, and threads them into `select_memories_by_budget(..., pinned_entity_names=canonical_actor_names)`.
- `mvp_site/prompts/game_state_instruction.md`: new subsection under the existing "Core Memories Replace Dropped Middle Story Entries" section.

## Known Limitations

- Pinning is a rescue pass on top of the existing recency/budget algorithm, not a redesign of it — `select_memories_by_budget`'s inner loop still scans the full "older" list without an early `break` on the first non-fitting item (pre-existing behavior, unchanged by this PR).
- `find_canonical_narrative_actor_names` uses a 5-turn lookback and exact `current_location` string match; it will not catch an NPC who is narratively relevant but neither recently named nor location-matched (e.g. referenced only by title/epithet). This is the same class of gap the PR #8464 evidence flagged for the *named-entity index* fix-shape option; a fuller index-based approach remains a possible follow-up.
- **Packaged evidence bundle is pending.** This PR ships with real local pytest output (above) but does not yet include a real-LLM/testing_mcp end-to-end run reproducing the original scene-386 prompt with the fix applied (that would require replaying against the real campaign/BigQuery data referenced in PR #8464's evidence, which is out of scope for this fast-follow). Kept as **Draft** until that evidence lands, matching PR #8464's own precedent.
- CI's `## Real LLM Evidence` requirement (triggered because `mvp_site/prompts/game_state_instruction.md` changed) is expected to be flagged by the PR description gate until the above evidence is packaged; noting this proactively rather than fabricating evidence.
- **Parallel-lane file overlap (flagged by this repo's `merge_train` pre-tool hook, warn-only):** `mvp_site/agent_prompts.py` is also touched by concurrent PRs #8477 and #8456; `mvp_site/prompts/game_state_instruction.md` is also touched by concurrent PRs #8471 and #8411; `mvp_site/tests/test_memory_utils.py` is also touched by PR #8464 itself. This PR's diffs are additive and scoped (new function + new parameter + new prompt subsection), so conflicts should be mechanical, but whoever merges next should diff against the other PR before merging.

## Unit Test Evidence

See **Testing** above for the full real pytest run (`7c67dcafbb83c10efe0b919fa463c84a4e10ff42`, 213 passed / 1 pre-existing unrelated failure) covering `test_memory_utils.py` and `test_prompts.py`.

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

N/A — pending. This is a unit-level fix to prompt-construction selection logic and a prompt-instruction addition; a real-LLM/`testing_mcp` end-to-end run against the scene-386 repro campaign is the natural non-unit proof and is tracked as outstanding work (see Known Limitations). No UI surface changed.

## Real LLM Evidence

A real LLM HTTP raw request/response demonstrating the reconciliation rule firing on a present NPC has not yet been captured. title: Replace restart-only WorldAI ezgha watchdog guidance with fail-closed runtime handoff
description:
## Summary

The WorldAI operator guidance currently treats supervisor restart as normal self-healing and tolerates partial fleet counts as expected churn. The July 9-11 runner audit showed that restarts can interrupt active jobs, create offline-busy 422 registrations, and cannot repair a dead or wrong-namespace backend. Runtime mutation belongs in `jleechanorg/ez-gh-actions`; WorldAI should consume a fail-closed health contract and remain a read-only SLO/consumer layer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mark restart-only mutation unavailable until ez-gh-actions graceful drain and recovery controller are deployed.
- [ ] Point the WorldAI skill to exact `ezgha doctor` and recovery-controller evidence.
- [ ] Require canonical Docker identity plus functional runner/job proof.
- [ ] Keep WorldAI code limited to read-only SLO and consumer checks.
- [ ] Update the mirrored Codex skill and regression-load both copies.

title: Stage-1 skeptic review PR 455
Green Gate Precheck (Gates 1-6) fixed 30-poll budget can exhaust right as dependencies finish
description: Green Gate Precheck is a self-contained polling script with a fixed ~30-poll budget (~11s apart, ~5.5min total) waiting for other required checks to resolve before evaluating gate eligibility. On PR jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai#7888 head 8c678397d06, it exhausted all 30 polls still showing CI-pending at 01:19:30, while the actual slow checks (Directory tests) finished at 01:19:14 - right as the precheck was giving up. This produces a false-negative Green Gate failure on a genuinely-green PR, matching the pattern already documented in bead jleechan-o8pt (a7green-pr-monitor.sh reads stale mergeable_state). Root cause found by team-lead via gh run view --log-failed on run 29061737065's Precheck job. Was moot on this specific SHA (superseded by a newer push before it mattered) but the underlying timing-fragility in the precheck script is real and will recur on any busy self-hosted-runner night where Directory tests / other slow jobs run close to the poll budget's edge. Fix options: (a) lengthen the poll budget relative to observed self-hosted job durations, or (b) distinguish genuinely-still-pending from timed-out-waiting and fail-open-with-retry instead of fail-closed-permanently in the latter case. Acceptance: a regression test that simulates a dependency finishing at T=poll_budget-1s and confirms the precheck no longer reports a false failure.

title: gh issue/pr list --limit 1000 and REST per_page=100 lack fail-closed truncation check
description:
Context: PR #191 (dark-factory) added fail-closed truncation detection for br list pagination in daemon/src/adapters.rs, using has_more/total fields to reject silently-truncated output. Adversarial codex review (2026-07-07) found the same silent-truncation bug class is NOT closed for two other call sites in the same file:
- gh issue list / gh pr list --limit 1000 (adapters.rs ~line 252, ~line 291) — no has_more-equivalent check; if labeled issues/PRs on a target repo ever exceed 1000, results are silently truncated with no error.
- REST fallback per_page=100 (adapters.rs ~line 274) — same gap. The PR description flags the REST case as "out of scope" but does not flag the gh-list --limit 1000 case with the same caveat, so it reads as covered when it isn't.

Currently latent (target repos have single-digit labeled issue/PR counts) but will silently reintroduce the exact bug class #191 fixed once any tracked repo crosses the ceiling.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a fail-closed check (e.g. compare returned count to --limit / per_page and error loudly if a full page came back with no indication that's the true total) for both the gh --limit 1000 and REST per_page=100 paths, matching the fail-closed pattern already used for the br list path.
- Add a test simulating exactly N=limit results returned (ambiguous "exactly full page" case) and confirm it now surfaces a truncation error instead of silently proceeding.

Adds `.github/workflows/ci-dispatch-watchdog.yml`, a schedule-triggered
detector for a GitHub-platform-side fault where a push is delivered
normally but GitHub's own Actions component never creates a check-suite
for it — making a silently-untested PR head indistinguishable from a green
one. Root-caused live on PR #8489 (`feat/levelup-lean-auto-apply-v25`):
6 consecutive pushes over ~6h40m on 2026-08-02 produced zero Actions
check-suites while the pushes immediately before/after fired 15-16 runs
each, and every third-party GitHub App reacted normally to all 6 in
between. Full evidence chain in
`roadmap/worldarchitect.ai/sidekick/ci-not-firing/docs/`.

## Beads

Beads: rev-8voe4

## Tenets

- All production code paths must have evidence: this PR is CI-infra only
  (a new `.github/workflows/*.yml`), no `mvp_site/**` change, so the
  `/es` real-services evidence requirement doesn't apply; verification is
  `actionlint` + this repo's own `scripts/lint_workflow_discipline.py` +
  `.github/scripts/check_runner_checkout.sh`, all run locally with real
  output (see Test plan), plus a live `workflow_dispatch` run against a
  real PR.
- Ties back to `roadmap/worldarchitect.ai/sidekick/ci-not-firing/STATE.md`
  (sidekick mission, bead rev-8voe4) and the accompanying docs writeup.

## Test plan

- `actionlint .github/workflows/ci-dispatch-watchdog.yml` — exit 0, no
  findings.
- `python3 scripts/lint_workflow_discipline.py` — `0 new violations
  (blocking)` (1 pre-existing grandfathered R2 finding in an unrelated
  file, unaffected by this change).
- `bash .github/scripts/check_runner_checkout.sh .github/workflows` —
  `OK: runner workflow checkout policy passed`.
- Detection logic dry-run against the real historical SHAs from the PR
  #8489 incident (via `gh api`, not simulated):
  `commits/ee7f7d42afddb6dcf71b063ec611f440f67570b6/check-suites` filtered
  to `app.slug=="github-actions"` -> length 0 (the actual silent SHA);
  same query against `f619043750d1228c64f1424ec8ede933e06986e0` (the SHA
  immediately before, which fired) -> length 16. Confirms the exact
  predicate this workflow uses would have flagged the real incident.
- Live `workflow_dispatch` end-to-end run against this very PR once open
  (see follow-up comment on this PR for the run URL and resulting
  `ci-dispatch-watchdog` commit status) — proves the comment-posting and
  status-setting code paths execute against the real GitHub API, not just
  the read-only detection query.

## Risk

- Adds a new scheduled workflow (`cron: */15 * * * *`) running on
  `ubuntu-latest` (GitHub-hosted, not self-hosted — deliberate: a
  lightweight `gh api` polling job with no build/test tooling needs,
  consistent with `workflow-lint.yml`/`pr-cleanup.yml` precedent, and
  decoupling it from this repo's self-hosted fleet makes it strictly more
  robust as a detector).
- Blast radius: read-only GitHub API calls plus, only when a PR head is
  flagged, a `POST .../statuses/{sha}` and an idempotent PR comment
  (single comment per PR, updated in place via a `<!-- ci-dispatch-
  watchdog:v1 -->` marker, never duplicated). No repository code, test, or
  deploy paths are touched. No secrets beyond the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (repo default `default_workflow_permissions: read`; this workflow
  explicitly requests `pull-requests: write` + `statuses: write`, nothing
  else).
- False-positive risk: a PR pushed <10 minutes ago is skipped (grace
  period) to avoid flagging normal Actions queue latency.
- Rollback: revert this file; no other files touched.

## Out of scope

- Does not (and cannot) fix or prevent the underlying GitHub-side dispatch
  fault — root cause is outside this repository's control (see writeup for
  the exhausted list of repo-side causes ruled out).
- Does not touch PR #8489 or any of its branches/worktrees.
- Does not add Slack alerting (the repo already has a
  `secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` pattern via `deploy-staleness-gate.yml`;
  intentionally left out here to avoid guessing at a channel/thread owner
  — the per-PR status + comment is the primary signal, follow-up bead
  filed for optional Slack escalation).

title: daemon/src/state.rs: SqliteStateStore::configure() swallows PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL failures on file-backed DBs
description:
Found by minimax Skeptic adversarial review of PR https://github.com/jleechanorg/dark-factory/pull/145 (jleechan-6ug), 2026-07-04 verifier tick. SqliteStateStore::configure() in daemon/src/state.rs issues PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and unconditionally discards the Result, with a comment claiming this is only needed because WAL is a no-op against :memory: connections. But the discard applies equally to the file-backed path used by open(). If WAL genuinely fails on a real file (unsupported filesystem, permissions, NFS), the daemon silently falls back to the default journal mode with no error surfaced and no test distinguishing WAL-succeeded from WAL-silently-failed for the file-backed path. Non-blocking per Skeptic (Stage-1 scope, all 3 required tests present and correct) but should be tracked. Fix: only discard the Result for in-memory connections; propagate/log the error for file-backed opens.

DISPATCH NOTE (2026-07-04): file-disjoint from in-flight PR #154 (verifier.rs). This bead touches ONLY daemon/src/state.rs — SqliteStateStore::configure() must not swallow a PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL failure on a file-backed DB (propagate as DaemonError::Config, or verify WAL actually took via 'PRAGMA journal_mode' readback). Add a test. cargo test + clippy green. Open a PR, never merge.

title: harness: factory-lite loop's shared cwd got switched off main, breaking spawned claude -p ticks
description: Discovered 2026-07-04 ~20:51 PDT while executing an on-demand 'invoke factory-lite-coder, one tick' request. /Users/jleechan/projects/dark-factory is the cwd of a live 12h loop (pid 33910/33912 'bash ./daemon/run-factory-lite.sh coder 240 43200', pid 33913/33924 verifier equivalent, started 12:03PM PDT). That loop spawns 'timeout 2700 claude -p ... Invoke the factory-lite-coder skill ... execute exactly one tick' per interval (confirmed: pid 4265/4266 IS this exact session, ppid of my own bash tool pid). The shared cwd is currently checked out to feat/qw5-followups (49 commits behind origin/main, 3 ahead), which lacks daemon/factory-lite-harness.sh, .claude/skills/factory-lite-coder/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/factory-lite/CONTRACT.md, daemon/contracts/* — all merged to origin/main via PR #144 today. Because bash keeps the already-open run-factory-lite.sh script running via its held file descriptor even after the on-disk file changes/vanishes, the OUTER loop kept ticking, but each spawned 'claude -p' child does a fresh disk read and silently fails to find the skill. Telemetry (~/Library/Logs/dark-factory/daemon.jsonl) shows a coder-role gap starting around 2026-07-04T19:57-20:50 PDT (successful ticks stop, only a lone verifier tick logged at 20:50 PDT) consistent with the branch switch happening in that window. Fix: (1) never run long-lived factory-lite loops against a shared, mutable working directory that other sessions/branches also check out in — use a dedicated worktree pinned to the branch/ref the loop needs (e.g. origin/main or a tag), so an unrelated 'git checkout <feature-branch>' in the same folder cannot silently starve it; (2) daemon/run-factory-lite.sh and/or factory-lite-harness.sh should fail loudly (non-zero exit, alert) when required contract files are missing instead of the child claude -p session quietly no-op'ing; (3) reconcile with the 2026-07-04 factory-lite decommission decision (memory: project_2026-07-04_factory_lite_decommission_decision.md, bead jleechan-732a, timebox 2026-07-11) — if factory-lite is being decommissioned in favor of the Rust daemon, this loop should have been stopped already, not left running against a stale checkout.

title: feat(campaign): add optional intake questions to custom campaign flow (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background
During custom campaign creation, players often want to anchor their story in a favorite fictional universe, play a specific favorite character, explore a pivotal "what if" alternate decision branch, and supply custom story flavor. Previously, the intake form only exposed generic character, setting, and description fields with a required title.

## Goals
- Add structured, optional intake fields to the Custom Campaign wizard and underlying form:
  1. Favorite TV show, book, movie, genre, etc.
  2. Favorite character you want to play
  3. One decision you would have made differently (alternate story branch)
  4. Additional details about your story
  5. Campaign description prompt
- Make Campaign Title optional with an automatic fallback to "My Epic Adventure" when left blank.
- Build structured intake_answers payload, preserve it in custom_campaign_state, and integrate formatted components into _build_campaign_prompt.

## Tenets
- Purely Additive & Optional: Every intake field is optional. If left blank, the system cleanly defaults/auto-generates without crashing or blocking launch.
- State Fidelity: Intake answers are preserved across wizard tab navigation, Custom <-> Dragon Knight toggles, and saved into custom_campaign_state for downstream engine awareness.
- Fast-Path & Backwards Compatibility: Existing Dragon Knight template fast-paths and legacy prompt strings remain 100% compatible.

**Linked artifacts** (required by Gate 0):
- Bead: rev-inta1
- Roadmap doc: `roadmap/2026-08-14-custom-intake-questions-contract.md`
- PR: https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8864

## High-Level Description
- Frontend Wizard & Form (campaign-wizard.js, index.html, app.js):
  - Added intake question inputs to Step 1 of Custom Campaign.
  - Made title input optional with auto-fallback placeholder.
  - Updated collectFormData(), populateOriginalForm(), populateFromOriginalForm(), and handleCampaignTypeChange() to preserve and synchronize intake fields.
  - Form submission forwards favorite_media, alternate_decision, story_details, and intake_answers to /api/campaigns.
- Backend & Prompt Construction (prompt_utils.py, world_logic.py):
  - Updated _build_campaign_prompt to format favorite media, character, alternate decisions, and story details.
  - Updated create_campaign_unified to handle empty titles, accept intake arguments, and store intake_answers in custom_campaign_state.

## Testing
- Frontend Unit Tests (mvp_site/frontend_v1/tests/test_custom_intake_questions.test.js):
  - Verified intake field template rendering, collectFormData extraction, optional field handling, and populateOriginalForm synchronization.
  - All 33 frontend wizard tests pass (node --test).
- Backend Unit Tests (mvp_site/tests/test_custom_intake_questions.py):
  - Verified _build_campaign_prompt formatting, fallback generation, empty title handling, and custom_campaign_state["intake_answers"] persistence.
  - 6/6 pytest tests pass.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Additive, optional UI and API fields with backward-compatible defaults; Dragon Knight path unchanged aside from hiding new inputs.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Custom campaign creation** now collects optional premise fields—favorite media/universe, favorite character, an alternate “what if” decision, and extra story details—on both the legacy form and the Step 1 wizard. **Campaign title** is no longer required; blank titles default to `"My Epic Adventure"`.
> 
> The wizard **hides** those intake sections for Dragon Knight and **saves/restores** them when toggling types or syncing with `#new-campaign-form`. Submit sends `favorite_media`, `alternate_decision`, `story_details`, and a structured `intake_answers` object.
> 
> **Backend:** `create_campaign_unified` merges intake into prompt building via `_build_campaign_prompt` (new labeled sections when non-empty) and persists answers on `custom_campaign_state.intake_answers`. Legacy clients without these fields are unchanged.
> 
> Adds frontend/backend unit tests and a roadmap design contract doc.
>

title: Auth ordering/routing tests fail deterministically under CI load, pass locally (2 tests, cross-platform)
description: test_app_auth_persistence_ordering.py::test_no_auth_observer_registers_before_persistence_settles and test_app_auth_routing_7576.py::test_no_auth_reroute_for_transient_null_with_later_signed_in_user both spin up a real node subprocess (shutil.which('node')) to probe JS event-ordering (onAuthStateChanged registration vs setPersistence resolution). Failed deterministically 2/2 times on PR jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai#7888 (jleechan-93ft) across TWO DIFFERENT self-hosted runners (ez-mac-runner-b-6 first attempt, ez-runner-c-3 second attempt) - rules out a single quarantined-runner explanation. Neither test file is touched by PR#7888's diff (git diff bfe4b26d05e..HEAD --stat shows empty for both files). Verified both pass cleanly and instantly (2 passed in 0.35s / 3 passed in 0.15s) when run locally on an idle machine against the exact same PR code. Working hypothesis: timing-sensitive JS ordering probes that assume certain event-loop scheduling are flaky under heavy self-hosted-runner CPU load (consistent with the broader fleet-contention pattern seen elsewhere on this PR tonight - Directory-tests(claude) 25min timeout, PR-Coverage-Report 5min timeout, Mobile-Auth 15min timeout, all under load). Root cause not fully isolated (CI test-runner's compact reporter truncates the actual pytest traceback before the raised exception, only showing the test docstring + first 2 lines of test body) - needs either (a) full untruncated CI log capture for a future occurrence, or (b) deliberately reproducing under artificial CPU load locally (e.g. stress-ng) to confirm the race. Acceptance: identify the actual race (probably a fixed sleep/timeout in _run_ordering_probe() that's too tight under load) and either widen the tolerance or make the probe deterministic instead of timing-based.
notes:
2026-07-10T~08:20Z CORRECTION: root cause was NOT a load-related flake as originally
hypothesized. wa-3084 (the /af coder) found the real cause itself and fixed it for real:
commit 672bb4e339fa "install Node.js for mcp test group" -- the "mcp" test-group matrix
leg in test.yml never had a Node.js setup step (only core-mvp-* legs did), so
test_app_auth_persistence_ordering.py / test_app_auth_routing_7576.py deterministically
failed every time via shutil.which('node') returning None -- 100% reproducible, not
intermittent. Confirmed green on the next 2 CI runs after the fix landed. Closing as
fixed-for-real rather than leaving mislabeled as an open flake investigation.
close_reason: Fixed for real by /af coder session (commit 672bb4e339fa, PR#7888) — was deterministic missing Node.js setup, not a flake. See notes.

title: Audit worldarchitect.ai PR 7955 for bead jleechan-3om7
reroll::execute() sets bead.state=ReRoll unconditionally before circuit-breaker check - any post-check error strands the bead forever
description: Disclosed (not fixed, correctly out of scope) by the PR#210 amendment agent, independently confirmed by the scoped re-verifier: reroll::execute() sets bead.state = ReRoll unconditionally at the very top of the function, before the circuit-breaker check runs. Any error after that point (including the just-fixed ComparatorUnparseable case, or any other future error in this path) leaves the bead permanently stuck in ReRoll state, since the fast-tier dispatch loop only reconsiders beads in Attested state -- there is no sweep/recovery mechanism analogous to PR#197's Dispatched-state integrity sweep for ReRoll. Needs: either (a) a dedicated ReRoll-state staleness/recovery sweep mirroring the Dispatched one, or (b) defer the state=ReRoll write until after the circuit-breaker check passes (if that's architecturally safe -- check whether anything downstream depends on the state being ReRoll during the check itself).
