title: [P2] Add gate_strict=true to every gate_es/er/cs node in factory/*.dot (G6)
beads.db corruption RESOLVED: rogue Go bd binary (steveyegge/beads v0.56.1) + br upgraded 0.1.38->0.2.16
description:
RESOLUTION SUMMARY (recreated by sidekick 2026-07-08T~06:40Z as jleechan-wuks per team-lead request -- original bead of this name from the corrupt-db window appears to have been lost, along with i7c7 and noqw, in a subsequent db swap; neither exists in current DB or JSONL export as of this writing).

ROOT CAUSE: ~/.local/bin/bd was a completely unrelated 39MB Go binary (github.com/steveyegge/beads v0.56.1, built Feb 22 2026), NOT beads-mcp and not a schema-migration issue. bashrc's 'alias bd=br' only works in INTERACTIVE shells; every AI agent tool-call context (Bash tool calls, daemon's claude --print gate-handler subprocesses) is non-interactive and resolved past the alias straight to the real Go binary, since ~/.local/bin is first on PATH everywhere. Confirmed 3 ways: bd --version matched .local_version exactly (0.56.1); Go buildinfo showed steveyegge/beads v0.56.1+dirty; strings on bd contained the literal .local_version marker-file logic that br has zero knowledge of. Two structurally incompatible SQLite engines (br's custom frankensqlite vs bd's Go sqlite driver) touching one file, each bd call a fast open-touch-close, explains the 'new corruption signature every ~2min, empty lsof' watchdog finding exactly.

FIX APPLIED (first pass): mv ~/.local/bin/bd -> bd.DISABLED-go-steveyegge-beads-v0.56.1-corrupts-shared-db; rm ~/.local/bin/beads && ln -s br ~/.local/bin/beads.

ESCALATION: falsification watchdog fired AGAIN at 06:03:33Z with bd removed -- meaning bd alone wasn't the full story. Root cause #2: ~/.local/bin/br itself was version 0.1.38, predating an upstream fix (Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust#242, 'Recurring SQLite corruption / DB-vs-JSONL drift under concurrent multi-agent br writes on v0.1.38', same build hash v0.1.38@8c5b245, same symptoms, closed 2026-05-07 -- fixed a month before this install). team-lead upgraded br 0.1.38 -> 0.2.16 (latest, sha256-verified), old binary kept as ~/.local/bin/br.0.1.38-pre-242-fix.bak. Clean 331-issue db restored a third time with the daemon STOPPED (both prior swaps may have raced live br writers, itself possibly contributing to recurrence -- any future db swap requires daemon stopped AND no br lanes active). Round-3 falsification watchdog armed; if corruption recurs now, both hypotheses are dead and next step is strace-level forensics.

CURRENT STATUS as of this writeup: br --version confirms 0.2.16 live. br doctor shows sqlite.integrity_check and sqlite3.integrity_check both OK (corruption genuinely gone as of this check). HOWEVER a real, separate issue: br doctor flags 'counts.db_vs_jsonl: DB and JSONL counts differ' and 'sync.metadata: Database and JSONL have diverged (merge required)' -- and 3 specific beads (i7c7, noqw, and this bead's original wuks) are confirmed absent from BOTH the live DB (br list --json) and the raw JSONL file (grep issues.jsonl), not just a stale-read illusion. Flagging to team-lead as a fresh, small data-loss gap from the swap/upgrade sequence -- STANDING RULE (do not run br sync --merge) means this divergence should NOT be resolved via sync; team-lead should decide how to reconcile.

Durable guard (drafted, not yet filed, approved by team-lead to file): upstream beads_rust issue proposing br hard-refuse to open a workspace carrying a foreign .local_version marker; companion ask on steveyegge/beads for the reverse check. Both approved, awaiting go-ahead to actually submit.
notes: 2026-07-08T07:05Z VALIDATED: round-3 integrity watchdog ran a full 60-min window with ZERO corruption after br 0.1.38→0.2.16 upgrade + bd removal (rounds 1-2 had corrupted within 2-5 min). Both root causes confirmed: rogue Go bd (steveyegge/beads 0.56.1) AND stale br predating upstream #242 concurrency fix. Ongoing coverage: factory-watch haiku agent checks integrity every 5 min. Remaining follow-ups in this bead: upstream guard issues (approved, sidekick filing), version-mismatch write guard.

title: fix(god-mode): translate narrative-sounding requests into state, never refuse (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary
- Implements the owner-approved "Translate, Never Refuse" fix for God Mode's filler-response defect (bead rev-cly5l, after its 2026-07-25 CORRECTION): God Mode was correctly following its "no narrative advancement" rules but had no instruction for what to do with a narrative-sounding request, so it improvised generic "Administrative Update... fully synchronized" filler with empty `state_updates` instead of applying the change.
- Adds `## Translate, Never Refuse (Mandatory Protocol)` to `mvp_site/prompts/god_mode_instruction.md` as the FIRST body section (immediately after the file's opening `**Purpose:**` line and before `## Core Principle`, `## What You Can Do`, `## What You MUST NOT Do`, and `## What You CAN Include`). This is NOT the placement described in the original draft — see "Body-vs-code corrections" below.
- Adds a new real-LLM testing_mcp test (`testing_mcp/core/test_god_mode_translate_never_refuse.py`) covering 3 of the real production defect strings (see Known Limitations for the scope note and an important RED-proof gap discovered while producing this evidence).
- Two owner open questions are intentionally left unresolved: (b) any `MAX_OPERATIONS_PER_TURN`-style bound on `state_updates`, (c) the positive restatement of `world_time` permission. Both remain owner calls, not decided in this PR.

## Production Code Changes
- `mvp_site/prompts/god_mode_instruction.md`: net +18 lines across the PR (one new `##` section plus a CRITICAL MANDATE block and 5 bullets; some lines were later refactored by follow-up commits — see attribution below). Before: 9 "What You MUST NOT Do" prohibition rules with zero guidance for narrative-sounding requests, so the model improvised filler. Now: an explicit CRITICAL MANDATE to translate such requests into `state_updates`, keep `narrative` empty, and never refuse. Why: owner directive, verbatim — "god mode shouldnt refuse any requests. if it sounds like narrative it should just directly change the game state."
- **Body-vs-code corrections (must read before quoting this section):** this PR's body originally described the section as `## Narrative-Sounding Requests: Translate, Never Refuse` placed "between What You MUST NOT Do and What You CAN Include" and claimed its text was "verbatim from the owner-approved draft." The actual final section in the file is `## Translate, Never Refuse (Mandatory Protocol)`, sits FIRST (above Core Principle), and contains 5 bullets whose content goes BEYOND the bead rev-cly5l "REPLACEMENT PROMPT CONTRACT TO DRAFT" 5-item list. The expansion came from three follow-up commits that landed on this branch after the initial fix commit, all touching the same file:
  - `cbe1c1456612` (bead rev-acawr) — added the `## Translate, Never Refuse (Mandatory Protocol)` `##` header, the `**CRITICAL MANDATE**` paragraph, and the `NEVER REFUSE` / `NEVER LEAVE MUTATIONS EMPTY` / `UNBOUNDED STATE MUTATIONS` bullets. This commit reordered the section to the top of the file (above Core Principle), not the "between MUST NOT and CAN Include" placement described in the original body.
  - `598378dd81c9` (bead rev-zxc18) — removed a duplicate section and the "what happens if" phrasing left behind by an earlier commit. No behavioral change to the rule itself.
  - `d3d4ca92030` (bead rev-zxc18) — added the `BEST-JUDGMENT INTERPRETATION` bullet (the "best-judgment escape hatch" for owner open question (a)) and the `NO NARRATIVE ADVANCEMENT CLARIFICATION` bullet. These two bullets are NOT in the rev-cly5l contract and are NOT owner-approved via that bead; they are owner-approved via rev-zxc18 (separate owner decision logged in that bead).
- **Story-mode redirect prohibition (bead rev-cly5l contract item 1):** the rev-cly5l contract explicitly says "Never redirect the user to Story mode" and "Never emit synchronization, acknowledgement, or 'reviewed and verified' filler." The anti-refusal prohibition IS present in the prompt (the `NEVER REFUSE` bullet and the banned-response-pattern sentence name "Administrative Update: ... fully synchronized" as banned). The anti-Story-mode-redirect prohibition is NOT named in the prompt section — the existing `god:return_story` planning_block choice (in `## What You CAN Include`) still offers Story-mode return as a UI affordance, but nothing in the new section prohibits the model from narrating "go to Story mode for that" in `god_mode_response`. Enforcement of the Story-mode prohibition is test-side only: the new test (`test_god_mode_translate_never_refuse.py`) checks `narrative == ""` and the absence of banned filler substrings; it does not assert the model never tells the user to switch to Story mode. This gap is a known limitation of this PR — fixing it requires either a follow-up prompt edit or a stronger test assertion. Not adding the prohibition here because there is no in-thread owner approval for that specific prompt edit on this PR.

## Test Changes
- New file `testing_mcp/core/test_god_mode_translate_never_refuse.py` (MCPTestBase pattern, real services only, real `agy` LLM provider — no mocks). Exercises `mode="god"` (verified via `constants.is_god_mode()` as the correct activation path, not a `"god:"` text prefix) with 3 of the real BigQuery-sourced defect strings from bead rev-cly5l's classification, plus one duplicate-retry run reproducing the documented duplicate-turn defect pair. Asserts `state_updates` non-empty, `narrative == ""`, and the banned filler substrings ("fully synchronized", "reviewed and verified") are absent.
- Scope note: the test covers 3 of the 4 documented failing production turns in bead rev-cly5l. The "Why are you ignoring my requests?" string was dropped from the test to bound real-agy-CLI wall-clock time (~60-90s per call, run sequentially, twice across RED/GREEN worktrees). No results are fabricated for the dropped scenario.
- **Post-CodeRabbit hardening (commits `ad98e9c003f`, `085042d80c5`, bead rev-mx3rt, closed):** CodeRabbit's 2026-07-25T07:51:35Z review (head `e04c1aa1eee`) flagged 4 findings on this test file, all since fixed and independently re-verified against the remote branch: (1) `endpoint="stream"` now used (line 158) so the test exercises the production `/interaction/stream` SSE path instead of the legacy call; (2) `run_scenarios()` collects per-scenario errors instead of aborting on first failure (0 bare `assert` statements remain); (3) a module-level `_directive_rules()` helper now asserts the persisted `custom_campaign_state.god_mode_directives` in Firestore contains the requested "34%"/"xp" rule, so the test discriminates an actual state mutation rather than any non-empty response; (4) `firestore_service` import moved to module scope (line 49).

## Known Limitations

**IMPORTANT — RED-proof gap found while producing this evidence, disclosed in full rather than glossed over:**

The new test was run against BOTH an unmodified worktree (RED, detached HEAD at the pre-fix `origin/main` commit `1877dbf7d93`, confirmed 0 matches for "Translate, Never Refuse" in the prompt file) and this PR's fixed worktree (GREEN, commit `3f04eda0735`). **Both RED and GREEN passed all tested scenarios** — the fresh, minimal, single-turn test campaign did not reproduce the original filler/empty-`state_updates` defect on either the old or new prompt.

This means this specific test does **not** satisfy the repo's "RED PROOF IS HARD GATED" bar (a fresh test that genuinely FAILS before the fix and PASSES after). The real production defect (documented in bead rev-cly5l with real BigQuery citations — the documented 4 failing production turns) all occurred in a single **hours-long, complex, established campaign session** (campaign `vPqka4Bz0N3si7quXXfM`, real time span 13:11–18:42, level-100 characters, many accumulated NPCs/directives). The likely explanation is that this defect is session-length/context-accumulation-dependent, not reproducible from these exact strings in isolation on a fresh campaign.

Filed bead `rev-0d8mh` tracking the follow-up: replay the actual long/complex production campaign (or an equivalently complex synthetic one) against the RED worktree to obtain genuine unit-level RED proof, before this evidence bundle is treated as fully satisfying the hard RED-gate policy. As of this PR's head, that follow-up is **OPEN and unfinished**; the only evidence in this bundle is the local fresh-campaign Layer-2 E2E real-LLM run cited under "Real LLM Evidence" below.

  - Before: `if is_god_mode or has_mutations: ... is_god_mode=is_god_mode or has_mutations`

  - Removed `has_directives` / `has_mutations` helper variables (no remaining consumers).
- **Why**: df5664ec0e7 (PR #8583's prior gate commit) LOOSENED the gate under a misleading subject ("Gate StateMutationExecutor behind if is_god_mode") by adding `or has_mutations` to the predicate. rev-nmr31 / rev-b175i intended the gate to be strict; this PR restores the strict form.

## Test Changes
- `mvp_site/tests/test_end2end/test_state_mutation_contract_e2e.py`:
  - **NEW**: `test_process_action_unified_skips_executor_on_non_god_mode_turn` (+129 lines)

The bug class is "wrong code shape" (predicate leaked on standard turns), not "model ignored instruction". Mock-tier unit tests at the direct-call layer (above) are the appropriate evidence tier.

The detector tracks the branch's full diff history, not the diff of this PR specifically.

## Background
Following the implementation of God Mode Type A/B structured mutations (PR #8554), non-god-mode agents (Story, Combat, Level-Up, Character Creation) continued to rely on ad-hoc, untyped `state_updates` dictionary merging. This created state fragmentation, lack of schema enforcement, and missing BigQuery forensic telemetry across standard gameplay turns.

## Goals
- Unify state mutation execution across all agent types using a single, centralized `StateMutationExecutor` (bead: rev-1gdjj).
- Implement a 3-type hybrid mutation taxonomy: `DirectiveMutation` (Type A rules), `StatePatch` (validated open schema), and `HistoryEdit` (Type B retcons/corrections).
- Preserve the "LLM decides, server executes" principle without requiring LLM prompt schema changes.
- Add field-level alias reconciliation (`health_points` -> `hp`, `experience` -> `xp`, `gold_pieces` -> `gold`, `position` -> `location`) to prevent state fragmentation.
- Emit BigQuery forensic telemetry events (`directive_added`, `directive_dropped`, `state_patch_applied`, `history_edit_applied`, `mutation_rejected`) carrying before/after snapshots for changed fields.
- **Restore strict `if is_god_mode:` gate around `StateMutationExecutor.execute()` in `world_logic.py` (rev-nmr31, rev-b175i)** — this PR.

## Tenets
1. **Zero LLM Prompt Changes**: Server-side classification sorts raw `state_updates` into typed mutations (Design Decision: rev-1gdjj).
2. **Deterministic Field Classification**: Classification uses schema key names—never regex on LLM output.
3. **Open Schema Safety**: Known fields are type-checked; un-modeled fields pass through (`extra="allow"`).
4. **Complete Auditability**: Every mutation produces a structured BigQuery telemetry row.
5. **Strict Gate Around Mutation Executor**: `StateMutationExecutor.execute()` must NEVER run on a standard (non-god-mode) turn, even if the LLM payload accidentally includes `state_updates` or `directives`. The gate is `if is_god_mode:` and nothing else (rev-nmr31, rev-b175i).
6. **Design Artifact**: `docs/plans/2026-07-24-unified-state-mutation-contract.md` (bead: rev-1gdjj).

## High-Level Description
This PR introduces `mvp_site/state_mutation_schema.py` and `mvp_site/state_mutation_executor.py`, and wires them into `process_action_unified` in `mvp_site/world_logic.py`. Follow-up fixes from adversarial read-only review (rev-1gdjj, rev-nmr31, rev-ljy23, rev-qmrgy, rev-b175i):
- Restored strict `if is_god_mode:` gate around `StateMutationExecutor.execute()` in `world_logic.py` (rev-nmr31, rev-b175i). **This commit (72cb822cdd9).**
- Corrected retcon core_memories target location to `custom_campaign_state["core_memories"]` (rev-ljy23).
- Added `CANONICAL_NESTED_PATHS` resolution for flat state patch aliases (`hp`, `xp`, `gold`, `location`) so writes hit canonical GameState structures (rev-qmrgy).

## Testing
Verified across all three testing layers (`/testing-layers`) and RED proof scripts:
- **Layer 1 (Unit)**: `mvp_site/tests/test_state_mutation_schema.py` (5 tests passing), `mvp_site/tests/test_state_mutation_executor.py` (3 tests passing).
- **Layer 2 (End-to-End)**: `mvp_site/tests/test_end2end/test_unified_mutation_e2e.py` (1 test passing), `mvp_site/tests/test_end2end/test_state_mutation_contract_e2e.py` (5 tests passing at HEAD 72cb822cdd9).
- **Layer 3 (MCP API)**: `testing_mcp/test_unified_mutation_contract.py` added for real-LLM MCP server verification.
- **RED Proofs (Green)**: `/tmp/redproof/red_core_memories.py` and `/tmp/redproof/red_alias_flat_writes.py` both pass against canonical readers.
- **Gate-restoration regression guard** (rev-b175i): `TestStateMutationContractE2E.test_process_action_unified_skips_executor_on_non_god_mode_turn` drives `world_logic.process_action_unified(...)` directly with `is_god_mode=False` plus a non-empty `state_updates` + `directives` payload, and asserts `StateMutationExecutor.execute` is NEVER called. RED proof captured before fix landed (revert `world_logic.py` to bypass state and re-run pytest → both this test and the HTTP test fail with explicit rev-nmr31 attribution message); both pass after restoration.

## Evidence
**Evidence**: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/12acd8ed46c32a3cbba0c64b3026b00b (PR #8583 Gate-Restoration Evidence Bundle — commit `72cb822cdd9`, sha256 of touched files inside gist)
- Full Evidence Bundle: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/e356650d51bf93e113c790d205730f37 (PR #8583 Full Evidence Bundle — commit `72cb822cdd9`)

- RED proof method documented in `metadata.json` inside the gist.


## Low-Level Details
1. `mvp_site/state_mutation_schema.py`: Added Pydantic v2 schemas (`DirectiveMutation`, `StatePatch`, `HistoryEdit`, `MutationEnvelope`).
2. `mvp_site/state_mutation_executor.py`: Implemented 4-phase pipeline (`Classify → Validate → Apply → Audit`) with `ALIAS_MAP` key normalization and `CANONICAL_NESTED_PATHS` nested path resolution.

6. `/Users/jleechan/roadmap/2026-07-24-unified-state-mutation-contract-design.md`: Created architectural design specification.

- Worktree: `/private/tmp/pr8583-gate-fix`

This is the rev-nmr31 / rev-b175i regression".

> Changes how persisted game state and god_mode_directives are written on admin turns and fixes a prior gate bypass that could apply LLM mutations on normal story turns; incorrect gating or apply logic could corrupt campaigns or leak directives.

> **Overview**

title: runner/handler_holdout.py: Firebase emulator hardcoded as universal infra assumption
description:
HIGH-severity finding from 2026-06-27 runner/handler domain-bias audit.

File: runner/handler_holdout.py
- Lines 110, 125, 160-163: firebase_json.exists() branch hardcodes 'firestore,auth,storage,functions' as the universal emulator set.
- Lines 144-149, 182: prepends /opt/homebrew/opt/java/bin to PATH and sets JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/java — macOS-only assumption baked in.
- Lines 96-99: same homebrew java injection in another path.
- Lines 102-103: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS strip is Firebase/Google-shaped.

Impact: any non-Firebase benchmark whose impl/ happens to contain firebase.json (or whose holdout_eval node lands there) gets biased toward Firebase infra. The /opt/homebrew paths also leak macOS-only assumptions into Linux CI.

Repro: a benchmark that uses Postgres/Supabase/DynamoDB will be silently routed through the Firebase emulator branch if the worktree happens to contain firebase.json. Triggers misleading 'Java not found' or 'emulator start failed' errors.

Acceptance:
1. _holdout_eval handler discovers the emulator backend from the worktree's manifest (Makefile target, package.json scripts, or a dark-factory.yaml emulator.kind field), not from file existence alone.
2. PATH/JAVA_HOME injection is gated on darwin only, or moved to a per-worktree env file.
3. The Google Cloud cred strip is gated on Firebase-detected, not always-on.
4. Add a benchmark (e.g. fibonacci) unit test that confirms the holdout handler doesn't reach for Firebase or homebrew Java when neither is present.

Touch: runner/handler_holdout.py, tests/test_holdout_*.py (new).

title: fix(prompt_cache): eliminate four sources of cached-prefix churn — dice double-render and three turn-conditional blocks (rev-r30ki, rev-jvdcr, rev-d7n50, rev-qgi8d) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background

Four defects found while proving `rev-ow59h` at runtime ([#8844](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8844)), all in the **cached** `system_instruction`: dice rendered twice (`rev-r30ki`), and three turn-conditional blocks that appear and disappear mid-prefix — LLM-requested detail sections (`rev-jvdcr`), deferred rewards on every 10th turn (`rev-d7n50`), and the character-creation handoff on turns 1–4 (`rev-qgi8d`).

## Goals

Remove per-turn churn and duplicated bytes from the cacheable prefix without changing what the model is told.

## Tenets

Governing artifacts: `rev-r30ki` (dice double-render), `rev-jvdcr` (detailed sections), parent `rev-ow59h`. Evidence: [#8844](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8844) bundle; BQ report `~/roadmap/bq-prefix-forensics-2026-08-10.md`.

- **Idempotence, not suppression.** The dice guard must not drop dice when nothing loaded it first.
- **Both block lists or neither.** A block relocated into only one list is deleted on turn 1, not relocated — that was the `rev-eas3z` P0.
- **Rewrite tests to assert the new location**, never delete them.

## User Stories

- As a player, every request stops carrying ~10KB of duplicated dice rules, and the prefix stops churning when the model asks for different detail sections.

## High-level description

**`rev-r30ki` — dice rendered twice.** `build_from_order` appends dice and sets a *local* `dice_loaded` flag; `add_selected_prompt_instructions` then appends it again unconditionally, blind to that flag. `StoryModeAgent.build_system_instruction_parts` calls both in sequence. Fixed with `_dice_instructions_already_loaded(parts)`, which inspects the list itself — the only guard that holds across both callers.

**`rev-jvdcr` — detailed sections in the cached prefix.** Contents are chosen by the *previous* turn's `debug_info.meta.needs_detailed_instructions` plus an auto-injected `social_hp` when a high-tier NPC is present, so the block appears and disappears mid-prefix. Moved to the uncached tail via a new zero-arg `build_detailed_sections_block()`.

## Testing

**Measured, full `StoryModeAgent.build_system_instructions("native_two_phase")`:**

| | dice blocks | sysinstr chars |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` | **2** | 547,631 |
| this branch | **1** | 537,444 |

**10,187 chars (~2,547 tokens) of duplicated cacheable prefix removed from every request.**

**Prefix stability across turns** (full build, `character_creation_completed=True`, native_two_phase):

| | turn 1 | turn 5 | turn 9 | turn 10 | turn 11 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` | 548,261 | 547,631 | 547,631 | **563,410** | 547,631 |
| this branch | 537,444 | 537,444 | 537,444 | **537,444** | 537,444 |

Main spikes **+15,779 chars** on turn 10 and carries **+630** on turns 1–4. This branch is byte-identical at every turn tested.

9 test files pass: `test_prompts` (202), `test_agents`, `test_prompt_assembly_routing`, `test_initial_story_god_mode_dynamic_instructions`, `test_dice_single_include` (8 new), `test_social_hp_prompt_content`, `test_agent_dispatch_table`, `test_compression_lever1`, `test_rag_activation`.

Four existing tests were **rewritten, not deleted**, to assert the new location. The routing test now asserts the 8th block explicitly instead of relying on `Mock` auto-vivification (which would have let a missing block pass silently).

**Not included:** a production A/B. The dice saving is deterministic and measured above; the `rev-jvdcr` cache benefit needs the [#8844](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8844) harness re-run post-merge.

## Low-level details

`agents.py`: both conditional appends and the now-unused `_add_deferred_rewards_instruction` helper removed. `agent_prompts.py`: `_dice_instructions_already_loaded()`; `build_deferred_rewards_block()` and `build_character_creation_handoff_block()` (with the handoff text and turn limit lifted to module constants, plus a local custom-state reader — importing `agents.py`'s equivalent would be circular); `_has_high_tier_npc()` extracted so the early reminder and the new block share one tier scan instead of adding a third copy; `build_detailed_sections_block()`; detailed-sections append removed from `add_selected_prompt_instructions`. `llm_service.py`: `turn_number` threaded through `_assemble_relocated_blocks` and `_reserve_relocated_block_budget`; new blocks added to that list **and** to `get_initial_story`'s parallel list.

The deferred-rewards block is deliberately **not** in the turn-1 list: its gate requires `turn_number >= 1`, so it is structurally dead at turn 0. That absence is intentional, not the `rev-eas3z` two-list gap.

Neither conditional block could simply be made unconditional — both are presence-conditional, so baking them in would inject irrelevant text every turn (a cost regression) rather than stabilizing anything.

### Why the suite missed the dice bug

`TestDuplicateDiceLoading` exercises `build_from_order` alone; the `add_selected_prompt_instructions` tests run it alone on an empty list. Neither reproduces the two-call sequence, so the duplication was structurally invisible. The new tests assert on the **assembled** instruction.

### Not a regression

`a02fdf26` added the `dice_loaded` guard for CombatAgent + code_execution inside `build_from_order` only. The unconditional append in `add_selected_prompt_instructions` predates it by ~18 hours (`3b159c9e59`, citing PR #4334). StoryModeAgent + native_two_phase was never in that fix's scope.

### Overlap

`merge_train` flags [#8839](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8839), [#8731](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8731), [#8730](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8730), [#8611](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8611), [#8594](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8594) on `llm_service.py`. My edits are two small additions to the relocated-block lists. Sibling PR [#8850](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8850) touches only `context_compaction.py` — no overlap with this one.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes which instructions reach the model and when (cached vs dynamic), with agent-type gating for StoryMode-only blocks; wrong list sync could drop prompts on turn 1, but coverage targets those paths explicitly.
> 
> **Overview**
> Stabilizes the **cacheable** `system_instruction` by fixing duplicate dice content and moving turn-conditional text off the cached prefix onto **uncached** `dynamic_instructions`.
> 
> **Dice (rev-r30ki):** `add_selected_prompt_instructions` now skips appending dice when `_dice_instructions_already_loaded(parts)` sees an existing dice file header—the only guard that works across `build_from_order` and the second append on the same `parts` list.
> 
> **Relocated blocks (rev-jvdcr, rev-d7n50, rev-qgi8d):** LLM-requested **detailed sections**, **deferred rewards** (10/20/30…), and the **character-creation handoff** (early turns) are no longer baked into `StoryModeAgent.build_system_instructions` or the cached prefix. New `PromptBuilder` helpers (`build_detailed_sections_block`, `build_deferred_rewards_block`, `build_character_creation_handoff_block`) assemble them for the dynamic tail; high-tier NPC detection is centralized in `_has_high_tier_npc()`.
>

Turn 1 uses `_assemble_turn_one_relocated_blocks` (hand-synced list, includes detailed sections + handoff at turn 0, excludes deferred rewards). Budget reservation threads `turn_number` through.
> 
> Tests were updated to assert content on the dynamic channel and to lock turn-1 vs continuation block lists; new `test_dice_single_include` covers the two-call assembly path.

title: refactor(llm_service): extract duplicated generate_content_stream_sync call (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background

`mvp_site/llm_service.py`'s `_gemini_stream_with_cache_fallback` (nested inside `_continue_story_streaming_impl`) makes two near-identical calls to `gemini_provider.generate_content_stream_sync`: an initial call, and a stale-cache retry call inside the `except` block. The two call sites shared 13 identical keyword arguments (`model_name`, `temperature`, `safety_settings`, `max_output_tokens`, `json_mode`, `api_key`, `enable_code_execution`, `code_execution_evidence_out`, `tier2_tokens_est`, `pre_roll_server_seed`, `agent`, `request_id`, `usage_out`), differing only in `prompt_contents`, `system_instruction_text`, and `cache_name`.

## Goals

- Eliminate the duplicated kwargs block between the initial call and the stale-cache retry call.
- Zero behavior change — this is a pure refactor.
- Keep the change scoped to `_gemini_stream_with_cache_fallback`; no signature changes visible outside the function.

## Tenets

- Tracked by bead rev-ygrrs

- Behavior-preserving refactor only, no new logic, no new branching.
- Minimal diff footprint for the target function.
- Root-cause-first: the duplication was structural (copy-pasted kwargs), so the fix is a plain extraction, not a workaround.

## High-level description

Added a small nested helper `_call_stream_sync(prompt_contents, system_instruction_text, cache_name)` inside `_gemini_stream_with_cache_fallback`. It forwards the 3 varying arguments plus the 13 shared kwargs (read via closure from the enclosing function's locals) to `gemini_provider.generate_content_stream_sync`. Both call sites (`_initial_iter = ...` and the `yield from ...` stale-cache retry) now call this helper instead of repeating the full kwargs list.

No change to `gemini_provider.generate_content_stream_sync`'s public signature, and no change to the values passed for any kwarg at either call site — this is purely a call-site consolidation.

## Testing

Targeted test files (found via `grep -rln "_gemini_stream_with_cache_fallback\|stream_cache_fallback\|cache_fallback" mvp_site/tests/` plus `find mvp_site/tests -iname "*streaming_contract*"`):

```
PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site" ./venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  mvp_site/tests/test_llm_service_error_handling.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_streaming_contract_integration.py -q
```

Result (with this change): **2 failed, 40 passed**

Both failures are pre-existing and unrelated to this refactor — confirmed identical on `origin/main` baseline (same test, same failure, before this change was applied):
- `TestStreamCacheFallback::test_failed_precondition_without_cache_name_reraises`
- `TestStreamingContractIntegration::test_streaming_contract_suppresses_stale_rewards_box`

Baseline run on `origin/main` (via `git stash`) reproduced the exact same 2 failures with the exact same error messages, confirming this refactor introduces no regressions.

Additional checks:
- `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('mvp_site/llm_service.py').read())"` → syntax OK
- `ruff check mvp_site/llm_service.py` → all checks passed (after fixing pre-existing lint debt below)
- `ruff format --check mvp_site/llm_service.py` → clean

## Low-level details

- New nested function `_call_stream_sync(prompt_contents, system_instruction_text, cache_name)` defined inside `_gemini_stream_with_cache_fallback`, placed right before the first call site. It closes over `prepared`, `effective_temperature`, `SAFETY_SETTINGS`, `max_output_tokens`, `user_api_key`, `_code_execution_enabled`, `stream_code_execution_evidence`, `stream_pf_seed`, `request_id`, and `_stream_usage_out` — all already local to the enclosing function, so no new parameters or globals were introduced.
- First call site: `_initial_iter = gemini_provider.generate_content_stream_sync(...)` → `_initial_iter = _call_stream_sync(prompt_contents=_effective_prompt_contents, system_instruction_text=_effective_system_instruction, cache_name=stream_cache_name)`.
- Second call site (stale-cache retry, inside `except Exception as _e:`): `yield from gemini_provider.generate_content_stream_sync(...)` → `yield from _call_stream_sync(prompt_contents=([json_string, _seed_content] if _code_execution_enabled else [json_string]), system_instruction_text=prepared.system_instruction_final, cache_name=None)`.
- **Unrelated collateral from the repo's mandatory husky pre-commit hook** (`ruff check --fix` + `ruff format` run on the whole staged file, not diff-scoped): the hook auto-fixed 5 pre-existing RET505 (unnecessary elif/else after return) violations in the unrelated `_make_stream_iter` mock-provider dispatch chain, plus 1 pre-existing SIM102 (nested-if) in `_get_context_window_tokens`, plus one pre-existing formatting normalization in `_validate_level_up_modal_action_contract` (line ~6274). All of these were verified to reproduce identically when the same `ruff check --fix` / `ruff format` commands are run against `origin/main`'s copy of the file in isolation — i.e. they are pre-existing lint/format debt in this file, not introduced by this change, and were forced by the mandatory hook (which lints/formats whole staged files, not just touched lines). No logic changed in these spots — purely elif→if / nested-if→combined-if / formatting.
- **`.beads/issues.jsonl`**: the same mandatory pre-commit hook also unconditionally runs `scripts/deduplicate_beads_jsonl.py` and stages the result on every commit in this worktree, regardless of which files are being committed. This reduced the file from 4219 to 2533 rows via a deterministic id-keyed merge (newest `updated_at` wins). Verified this is not specific to this branch: running the same dedupe script against `origin/main`'s own `.beads/issues.jsonl` produces the identical 4219→2533 reduction. This is pre-existing repo-wide dedupe debt surfaced by the mandatory hook, not created by this PR's code change.

**Cross-link note**: no open PR touches this `_gemini_stream_with_cache_fallback` region of `llm_service.py`. A sibling lane PR (modal-validator move, `llm_service.py:6251-6288`) touches a *different* region of the same file (the `_validate_level_up_modal_action_contract` area, which is also where this PR's hook-driven formatting normalization landed at line ~6274). Whichever of the two PRs lands second should rebase on the other.

User Stories: N/A — internal refactor, no user-visible behavior change

Closes #8721

title: fix(routing): allow explicit mode="god" to bypass the CC modal lock (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

- Explicit `mode="god"` routing requests (the player-facing "God" interaction
  mode in the stock chat UI) now bypass the character-creation (CC) modal
  lock in `_resolve_god_mode` **by design** — God Mode is the player's own
  administrative tool for their single-player game/world state (adjust
  stats, spawn items, fix a stuck CC state), not a privileged/admin-only
  escape hatch. **Human-confirmed design decision, 2026-07-11.**
- Freeform `"GOD MODE: ..."` input text alone (no explicit `mode` param)
  still cannot bypass the lock — the CC lock binds normal story/think chat
  and the LLM's own narrative-driven CC flow; it does not bind an explicit,
  player-issued god-mode command.
- Adds 3 unit dispatch-table tests + 1 real end-to-end scenario
  (`testing_mcp/core/test_godmode_cc_modal_exit_real_e2e.py`) proving the
  intentional bypass, the CC-flags-untouched invariant, and (added after a
  Cursor Bugbot HIGH finding, see `## Bugbot HIGH Fix` below) that a
  leftover `mode="god"` selection cannot swallow a CC exit choice.

## Production Code Changes

- **Before**: `_resolve_god_mode` computed `cc_modal_active` purely from
  `state.character_creation_in_progress_raw and not state.char_creation_completed`.
  Any god-mode-shaped request (including the explicit `mode="god"` API/UI
  path) was blocked back to `CharacterCreationAgent` while CC was active,
  with no way to reach `GodModeAgent` to fix a stuck CC state.
- **Now**: `_resolve_god_mode` also computes `is_explicit_god_mode = mode is
  not None and mode.lower() == constants.MODE_GOD and not is_cc_conclude_choice`
  (the `is_cc_conclude_choice` guard was added after a Cursor Bugbot HIGH
  finding — see `## Bugbot HIGH Fix` below) and ANDs its negation into
  `cc_modal_active`. When the caller explicitly passes `mode="god"` on a
  non-CC-conclude input, `cc_modal_active` becomes `False` and routing
  proceeds to `GodModeAgent` exactly as it does outside of character
  creation. Freeform `"GOD MODE:"` prefix text without the explicit `mode`
  param is unaffected — it still hits the same `cc_modal_active` block as
  before.
- **Why**: PR #8292 (lineage/character-identity provenance fix) had already
  merged this exact change as an unrelated rider commit with zero test
  coverage. Per human scope decision (2026-07-10), it is split out here as
  its own PR with dedicated tests and design justification, so it gets its
  own review separate from the lineage fix. See `## Background` below for
  full provenance.

## Test Changes

- `mvp_site/tests/test_agents.py::TestGetAgentForInput` — 3 new dispatch-table
  unit tests: (1) `"GOD MODE:"` prefix text stays blocked during CC without
  explicit `mode`; (2) explicit `mode="god"` bypasses CC and returns
  `GodModeAgent`; (3) `test_get_agent_god_mode_does_not_swallow_cc_exit_choice`
  — a leftover `mode="god"` selection combined with a structured CC exit
  choice (`CHOICE:start_adventure`) still reaches `CharacterCreationAgent`'s
  conclude phase, not `GodModeAgent` (see `## Bugbot HIGH Fix` below).
- `testing_mcp/core/test_godmode_cc_modal_exit_real_e2e.py` — new Scenario 4
  (`_scenario_explicit_mode_god_bypasses_cc_lock`) added to the existing
  `GodModeCCReviewThenExitE2E` real-server/real-LLM test class, proving the
  same bypass end-to-end through the real `/interaction/stream` HTTP path
  and confirming CC flags are untouched by the routing-only bypass.

## Background

PR #8292 (lineage/character-identity provenance fix) accumulated an unrelated
rider commit: a change to `mvp_site/agents.py::_resolve_god_mode` that lets
God Mode bypass the character-creation (CC) modal lock when explicitly
requested. This touches the CLAUDE.md critical rule *"user cannot exit
character creation until selecting a specific planning_block choice"* and had
zero test coverage in #8292. Per human scope decision (2026-07-10), it is
split out here as its own PR with a dedicated dispatch-table test and design
justification, so it gets its own review separate from the lineage fix.

## Goals

- Let an explicit `mode="god"` routing request — the stock, player-reachable
  "God" radio option in the chat interaction form (`mvp_site/frontend_v1/index.html`)
  — reach `GodModeAgent` even while the CC modal is active, so the player can
  use their own God Mode tool (adjust stats, spawn items, fix a stuck CC
  state) without first being forced through a different exit path. This is
  an intentional design exemption, not an admin-only backdoor: God Mode is
  reachable by any player of their own campaign, the same way it already is
  outside of character creation.
- Do NOT let freeform input text (`"GOD MODE: ..."` prefix) alone bypass the
  lock — the CC lock binds the normal story/think chat path (LLM-driven
  narrative + FastEmbed CC-exit detection), not an explicit god-mode command.

## Tenets

- **CC modal lock scope**: the lock binds *normal* player input — story/think
  chat routed through the LLM's narrative flow, exitable only via explicit
  `CHOICE:` / FastEmbed CC-exit detection. It does not bind an explicit
  `mode="god"` request: God Mode is the player's own administrative control
  surface for a single-player game, structurally outside the narrative loop
  the CC lock protects (no story advancement, world paused). This PR does not
  weaken the text-based lock for normal chat input — it only recognizes that
  explicit god-mode commands were never meant to be inside its scope.
  **Human-confirmed this reading of the design in-thread on 2026-07-11**
  (an earlier framing of this PR incorrectly described the bypass as
  "admin/debug-tool-only" / "not player-reachable" — see the code review
  discussion below for the correction; the code itself, `is_explicit_god_mode`,
  was always player-reachable via the stock God radio button and is
  intentionally so).
- **Root-cause-first / minimal surface**: single 1-line guard
  (`and not is_explicit_god_mode`) added to the existing `cc_modal_active`
  computation, no new state, no new flags.

## High-level description

`_resolve_god_mode` now computes `is_explicit_god_mode = mode is not None and
mode.lower() == constants.MODE_GOD` and ANDs its negation into
`cc_modal_active`. When `cc_modal_active` is `False` (bypass engaged),
routing proceeds to `GodModeAgent` exactly as it already does outside of
character creation. When the bypass is not engaged, the existing
`GOD_MODE_BLOCKED_BY_CC_MODAL` log line and fallthrough (usually to
`CharacterCreationAgent`) are unchanged.

## Testing

RED→GREEN TDD, `mvp_site/tests/test_agents.py::TestGetAgentForInput`:

- `test_get_agent_god_mode_text_prefix_blocked_during_character_creation` —
  `"GOD MODE:"` prefix text with CC modal active and no explicit `mode`
  param stays blocked (falls through, does NOT return `GodModeAgent`).
- `test_get_agent_god_mode_explicit_mode_bypasses_character_creation` —
  explicit `mode="god"` with CC modal active returns `GodModeAgent`.

Confirmed RED on `main` (68461ef6a9's parent / current main head) before the

## CodeRabbit Review Fixes (commit d2659463df)

CodeRabbit's first formal review at head `f1116bd27e` (2026-07-11 04:27 UTC) requested
CHANGES on Scenario 4 of `test_godmode_cc_modal_exit_real_e2e.py`:

1. **Major**: `process_action(...)` for the god-mode request didn't force
   `endpoint="stream"`, so `MCP_PROCESS_ACTION_ENDPOINT=mcp` could silently route the
   scenario through JSON-RPC instead of the required SSE streaming path. Fixed by
   passing `endpoint="stream"` explicitly and asserting `_stream_chunk_count > 0`.
2. **Minor**: the post-request invariant check only asserted `cc_in_progress` was
   untouched, not `cc_completed` — a response that silently completed CC while leaving
   `cc_in_progress=True` would have passed undetected. Added the matching assertion.

Re-ran the real e2e suite locally after the fix (AGY quota was exhausted again at run
time, same known infra issue as before — `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` Gemini SDK
fallback used, disclosed below): **5/5 scenarios pass**. Scenario 4's
`streaming_evidence.json` shows `chunk_count_observed: 14` for the god-mode request
(positive → confirms the streaming path was actually used), and
`post_god_mode_cc_flags.cc_completed` is unchanged (`null` before and after).
Evidence: `/tmp/worldarchitect.ai/feat_god-mode-cc-modal-bypass/godmode_cc_review_then_exit/iteration_007/`.

## Design Ruling: God Mode CC-lock exemption is intentional (2026-07-11)

An unresolved `chatgpt-codex-connector` P1 review comment on `mvp_site/agents.py:3634`
correctly pointed out that this PR's original description was factually wrong: it framed
the `mode="god"` bypass as an "admin/debug tool" / "not player-reachable" escape hatch,
but the God interaction mode is in fact a stock, always-visible radio option in the
normal chat UI (`mvp_site/frontend_v1/index.html:355-356`,
`mvp_site/frontend_v1/app.js:4377-4379`) that any player can select at any time,
including mid-character-creation — there is no separate admin/role signal.

**Human ruling (2026-07-11, in-thread): this is INTENDED, not a bug.** God Mode is the
player's own administrative tool for their own single-player game/world state — there is
no privilege boundary being crossed by letting a player use their own God Mode control
during character creation. The CC modal lock's purpose is to keep *normal* story/think
chat (LLM-driven narrative) from prematurely exiting character creation; it was never
meant to also block a player's explicit, self-issued administrative command. The PR's
description (Summary/Goals/Tenets above) has been corrected accordingly — the previous
"caller-controlled, not player-reachable" framing is removed. The code (`is_explicit_god_mode`
in `_resolve_god_mode`) is unchanged; only the stated justification was wrong and is now
fixed.

## Bugbot HIGH Fix: leftover mode="god" could swallow a CC exit choice

Cursor Bugbot flagged a HIGH-severity finding on `mvp_site/agents.py:3629-3633`:
the unconditional `mode="god"` CC-modal-lock bypass could intercept a CC exit
choice. Traced end-to-end and confirmed:

- `mvp_site/frontend_v1/index.html:355-356` — the "God" radio is a stock,
  always-visible option in the same interaction form used for everything else.
- `mvp_site/frontend_v1/app.js:4377-4400` (the form's `submit` handler) reads
  whichever `interactionMode` radio is *currently checked* — independent of
  what triggered the submit.
- `mvp_site/frontend_v1/app.js` `handleChoiceClick` (~line 2100) sets
  `userInputEl.value = "CHOICE:<id>"` for CC-exit buttons (e.g.
  `start_adventure`) and then **dispatches a `submit` event on that same
  form** — so if the player used God Mode earlier in the same CC session and
  never switched the radio back, clicking "Start Adventure" still sends
  `mode="god"` alongside `"CHOICE:start_adventure"`.
- `GodModeAgent.matches_input` / `constants.is_god_mode` has zero `CHOICE:`
  exclusion — it matches purely on `mode == "god"` or a `"GOD MODE:"` text
  prefix.

Net effect (pre-fix): `mode="god"` + `"CHOICE:start_adventure"` during CC
review routed to `GodModeAgent` instead of `CharacterCreationAgent`'s conclude
phase — the modal could never complete. Reproduced with a dispatch-table
test that failed exactly this way against the pre-fix code (RED), confirmed
passing after the fix (GREEN).

**Fix** (root-cause-first, reuses the existing `modal_conclude_policy.py`
single-source-of-truth already imported in `agents.py`): `_resolve_god_mode`
now computes `is_cc_conclude_choice = extract_modal_choice_id(user_input) in
(CHARACTER_CREATION_EXIT_CHOICES | CHARACTER_CREATION_CANCEL_CHOICES)` and the
god-mode bypass no longer applies when `is_cc_conclude_choice` is true. A
leftover `mode="god"` selection still reaches `GodModeAgent` for any other
input (fixing stats, granting items, etc.) — only the specific structured
CC-conclude signal is exempted, so the CC modal's own exit path stays intact.

Cursor's own auto-generated `CURSOR_SUMMARY` for the fix commit independently
confirms the read: *"CC exit/cancel choices are protected from that
bypass... a leftover mode='god' no longer routes to God Mode—the input goes
to CharacterCreationAgent conclude handling so the modal can finish."*

**Evidence layer disclosure**: this fix is proven at the unit-dispatch layer
(`get_agent_for_input` exercised directly against real production code, not
mocked — RED confirmed against pre-fix code, GREEN after) rather than a fresh
real-server/real-LLM E2E run. The production delta is a small, non-prompt
routing change (~12 lines in `_resolve_god_mode`, no new state/flags), which
falls under this repo's unit-only-proof exception for changes under 100 delta
lines of non-test code — flagging explicitly per evidence-standards policy
rather than silently relying on unit coverage alone.

## Known Limitations

- Scenario 4 uses `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` (Gemini SDK) for this run only, after
  AGY hit a sustained `agy quota exhausted` error across 4 consecutive attempts over
  ~9 minutes — see the gist for the full disclosure. Same AGY-quota-exhausted condition

- Split out of #8292; rebase/merge order does not matter (no shared files

- An external FixPR/auto-factory automation repeatedly pushed unrelated

title: [P1][factory] Isolate agent worktrees out of primary checkout + add reaper (511 worktrees, 60G, 0 prunable)
description:
target_repo: jleechanorg/dark-factory

Agent worktrees are not properly isolated from the primary checkout, and nothing
prunes them.

MEASURED 2026-08-05 on Jeff-Ubuntu:
  git worktree list  -> 511 registrations
  453 of them under  ~/projects/dark-factory/.claude/worktrees/agent-*
  24G  ~/projects/dark-factory/.claude/worktrees   <-- INSIDE the primary checkout
  36G  ~/.worktrees
  git worktree prune --dry-run -> 0 prunable (all registrations are live dirs)

PROBLEM 1 - agent worktrees live inside the primary working directory.
`.claude/worktrees/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:21`) so it does not pollute
`git status`, but 24G of nested checkouts inside the repo still slows tree walks
(find/rg/pytest collection), inflates backups, and blurs the isolation boundary
the operator expects. Agent worktrees belong OUTSIDE the primary checkout, e.g.
under ~/.worktrees/<repo>/<agent-id>.

PROBLEM 2 - no reaper. 0 of 511 are prunable because every directory still
exists; they accumulate without bound. There is no TTL, no post-merge cleanup,
and no cap. Same failure shape as the spawn-queue incident (jleechan-la67): an
unbounded producer with no consumer is an outage timer, just measured in disk
instead of latency.

PROBLEM 3 - observed cross-worktree write. AO session df-372 HAD its own
worktree (~/.worktrees/dark-factory/df-372, branch factory/jleechan-sk55-r3),
yet daemon/src/tick.rs and daemon/src/config.rs in the SHARED checkout
(~/projects/dark-factory) were modified with content matching that branch's work
while the operator had an unrelated branch checked out. Preserved as git stash
entries labelled DO NOT DROP. Root cause not yet established - candidates are a
worker cd-ing to the shared repo path, or a subagent inheriting the parent cwd
instead of the assigned worktree.

WHY IT MATTERS: a worker writing into the operator's checkout can silently land
its changes in an unrelated PR. That is a correctness risk, not just hygiene.

SCOPE:
1. Relocate agent worktrees out of the primary checkout (config or wrapper), so
   nothing creates checkouts under ~/projects/<repo>/.
2. Add a reaper: TTL + post-merge cleanup + a depth/size telemetry probe, and a
   documented flush command. Mirror the queue-hygiene rule from jleechan-la67.
3. Add a guard that fails closed when a dispatched worker's cwd is not its
   assigned worktree, with the violation logged to daemon telemetry.
4. Regression test for (3): a worker whose cwd is the shared checkout is
   rejected before it can write.

ACCEPTANCE: after this lands, `git worktree list | grep -c "projects/dark-factory/.claude"`
is 0, total worktree disk is bounded by the reaper, and a worker attempting to
write outside its assigned worktree is refused and surfaces in telemetry.

DO NOT bulk-delete the existing 24G/36G without operator approval - some
worktrees are locked and may hold unpushed work.
notes:
LIVE INCIDENT 2026-08-06 09:37 UTC — I triggered this hazard myself. It is not
theoretical.

While verifying an unrelated fix I ran the REAL (non-dry-run)
scripts/install-merge-guard.sh from a feature worktree. It silently rewrote the
live systemd unit:

  BEFORE (canonical):
    WorkingDirectory=/home/jleechan/projects/dark-factory-worktrees/fix-jleechan-s3c-merge-guard-scheduler
  AFTER (my worktree):
    WorkingDirectory=/home/jleechan/.worktrees/dark-factory/lssy-ci-green

That unit is the ONLY thing in the system that runs `gh pr merge`. So a single
command relocated merge authority onto a disposable feature worktree, with no
warning and no confirmation prompt. If that worktree were later pruned — which
is exactly what this bead's reaper is meant to do — merge authority would
vanish silently.

RESTORED: re-ran the installer from the canonical worktree; verified
ExecMainStatus=0, timer active, guard writing fresh verdicts.

ROOT CAUSE (new, distinct from the reaper problem): install-merge-guard.sh has
NO notion of a canonical install root. It installs whatever tree it happens to
be invoked from. Any agent or human running it from a worktree — a completely
reasonable thing to do while testing — silently hijacks merge authority.

ADD TO THIS BEAD'S SCOPE:
1. install-merge-guard.sh should refuse to install from a non-canonical root
   unless given an explicit --force/--root flag, and should print the path it
   is about to bind BEFORE writing the unit.
2. A check (test or health probe) asserting the live unit's WorkingDirectory
   equals the canonical checkout, so a drift like this is caught within a tick
   instead of at the next merge attempt.
3. The reaper's systemd protect-list (already in scope) is necessary but NOT
   sufficient: it protects the path the unit currently points at. If the unit
   has been hijacked to a feature worktree, the protect-list will faithfully
   protect the WRONG path and leave the canonical one prunable.

Item 3 is the important interaction: the protect-list and this hijack risk
compound. Fix both or the guard is only as good as whoever last ran the installer.

2026-08-14 observed: 190 registered worktrees, 818 controller snapshots, and eight ~10h sessions with stale lifecycle indicators. Acceptance: terminal-session-owned worktrees and snapshots are reaped without touching active or canonical roots.

title: fix(prompts): anchor NPC knowledge of player-character identity (#8468) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background

PR #8469 anchors NPC knowledge of player-character identity at the prompt layer, ensuring NPCs cannot act on hidden PC identity when active constraints forbid it.

## Rebase & Campaign-Agnostic Compliance

- **Rebased onto latest `origin/main`**.
- **100% Campaign-Agnostic**: Prompt instructions across `mvp_site/prompts/` enforce generic mechanics applicable to any campaign, with ZERO campaign-specific hardcodes in prompt rules (replaced Aegon, Visenya, Sariel, Lady Daena, Argella, Kaelar, Targaryen with generic placeholders like `[Ruler]`, `[Ally]`, `[Family Member]`, `[Target Character]`, `[NPC Name]`, `[Mask Identity]`).
- All prompt unit tests (`test_prompts.py`, `test_npc_knowledge_of_pc_constraint_8468.py`) pass 100%.

## Changes

1. **`mvp_site/prompts/narrative_system_instruction.md`**: §NPC Knowledge of Player-Character Identity section providing prompt-layer canonical-state anchors, fully sanitized with campaign-agnostic placeholders.
2. **`mvp_site/prompts/planning_protocol.md`**: Parallel §NPC Knowledge of Player-Character Identity (Choice Premise Validation) mirror that DROPs choices whose premise requires an NPC to act on hidden PC identity.
3. **`mvp_site/prompts/` (other prompts)**: Sanitized all specific campaign names (`master_directive.md`, `game_state_instruction.md`, `divine_leverage_system.md`).
4. **`mvp_site/schemas/prompt_tool_contracts.json`**: Updated prompt tool contract hashes.
5. **`mvp_site/tests/test_npc_knowledge_of_pc_constraint_8468.py`**: Prompt-contract unit tests updated for generic placeholders.

## Verification

```bash
python3 -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_prompts.py mvp_site/tests/test_npc_knowledge_of_pc_constraint_8468.py
python3 scripts/validate_prompt_tool_contracts.py
```

**Evidence**: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/2514f253a49d4dd84b901a06280e119c

title: feat(prompts): preserve parity-band personal-scale pressure at high tier (Visenya v9 diagnosis) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background

A campaign analysis of Visenya v9 surfaced a high-tier-pressure regression: scenes under level 15 felt dynamic/challenging/engaging with named-NPC personal-scale zero-sum stakes, while scenes past the parity band collapsed to mythic-tier abstraction. The diagnosis tracks:

- Two-way dialog share dropped from 23.6% (pre-L15) to 18.0% (post-L15).
- Concealed-consequence density dropped from 0.072 / 1k to 0.050 / 1k.
- The LLM correctly escalates to mythic antagonists past L15; it fails to *preserve* the original-tier peer band that made pre-L15 dynamic.

The prompts already encode NPC Autonomy, Victory Ripple, and Living World Momentum Counterpressure. The fix is **tier preservation**, not new mechanics.

## Goals

1. Keep 3-5 named peer-tier NPCs in play across the entire campaign (level-locked / -banded), not auto-scaling with the PC.
2. Force the LLM to file downstream consequences silently and surface them asymmetrically (via NPC body language, messenger, rumor) on a 1-3 turn delay.
3. Render NPCs at or above the PC's level with the same emotional granularity as low-tier NPCs.
4. Reorder verbal-conflict outcomes so the NPC's *cost* is named but the *consequence* of refusal is not (Force-a-trade first).
5. Down-shift major-event tier by one notch in personal-scale encounters past the parity band, reserving mythic-tier for arcs the user explicitly frames as mythic.

## Tenets

- **Prompt-only.** Zero backend enforcement, no new server-side guards/clamps/sanitizers/retry.
- **Setting-agnostic.** None of the new sections reference Visenya, Blood Dragon, Rook's Rest, Alysanne, Targaryen, Dunk-and-Egg, or any campaign-specific NPC. The contract test pins this guard.
- **Shared rules, one source.** Tier Compression + Consequence-Hiding Heuristic live in `mvp_site/prompts/shared/tier_pressure.md` and are loaded by every narrative-emitting agent (Story / Dialog / HeavyDialog / Spicy) so the parity-band contract reaches dialog turns — the primary flow this PR is supposed to improve.

## High-level description

Five prompt edits + one shared-prompt registration, all append-only or narrowly scoped.

### Shared prompt — `mvp_site/prompts/shared/tier_pressure.md`

Authoritative copy of two rules. Registered as `PROMPT_TYPE_TIER_PRESSURE` in `constants.py`, `agent_prompts.PATH_MAP`, and the `REQUIRED_PROMPT_ORDER` of DialogAgent, HeavyDialogAgent, SpicyModeAgent (Story mode reaches it via the same shared loader). Per `mvp_site/prompts/AGENTS.md` "Shared rules across agents": one rule, one authoritative file.

#### Tier Compression (Anti-Scaling Whiff)

Four numbered rules:

1. **Preserve the original-tier peer band** — retain 3-5 named NPCs at the campaign-start tier range across the entire campaign, *level-locked or -banded*.
2. **Maintain the disguise / concealment game** — peer NPCs still hold information the PC lacks; the Persona (disguise, frame, social mask) converts that gap into advantage.
3. **Inject "long-tail consequences" at the parity band** — parity-band NPCs keep acting across levels (returning to a farm she burned, calling in a favor ten years late).
4. **Choose NORMAL pressure over MYTHIC pressure when both are possible** — a disinherited cousin suing for the barony is preferred to a world-war alliance unless the world-war is genuinely called for by state logic.

#### Consequence-Hiding Heuristic (MANDATORY when stakes warrant it)

Four numbered rules:

1. **Asymmetric disclosure** — the least-informed NPC in the scene says aloud the part of the consequence they noticed; the rest is filed silently.
2. **NPC body-language signal** — readable only on a successful Perception (or Insight) check; the player must roll or explicitly probe. The character cannot passively notice it.
3. **Ship the deferred event with the full v2 envelope** — `id`, `actor`, `action`, `location`, `scheduled_for.turn`, `hidden: true`, `event_type: "long_term"`, `op: "create"`, `dependent_effects: []`. `hidden: true` alone is not enough — without `id`, `op: "create"`, and `scheduled_for.turn`, `_stamp_living_world_events_v2()` cannot fire the event later. To delay disclosure, set `scheduled_for.turn = current_turn + 1..3` and emit a second op entry later with `op: "fire"` plus an `outcome`.
4. **Mirror the user's instinct** — if the player is delighted by not knowing what they did, the LLM is doing it right.

### Edit 1 — `mvp_site/prompts/dialog_system_instruction.md` — High-tier NPCs are still people

New row appended to the Section 1.1 Voice Construction Framework table:

> | **Power standing vs PC** | NPCs whose standing *equals or exceeds* the PC are not monolithic elder beings; they have the same mundane private anxieties as any tier (debts, sick children, lovers, pride). Power does not erase personhood. Render NPCs at the PC's level or above with the same emotional granularity as low-tier NPCs. |

### Edit 2 — `mvp_site/prompts/dialog_system_instruction.md` — Force-a-trade (Section 5.3)

Replaces the existing 4-bullet `**Verbal conflict can:**` list with a 5-item priority-ordered list beginning with Force-a-trade:

1. **Force-a-trade** — NPC names the cost, hides the consequence of refusal.
2. **Conditional acceptance** — NPC accepts only if PC first pays something already earned.
3. **Accept and betray later** — asymmetric disclosure applies.
4. **Deny-and-redirect** — NPC refuses and offers an alternative that still costs the player.
5. **Flat refusal** (last resort) — only when Hard Limit applies AND no alternative path exists.

The surrounding section (5.3 heading, "If combat becomes likely:" block) is preserved verbatim.

### Edit 3 — `mvp_site/prompts/living_world_instruction.md` — Major Event Tier Rule (anti-escalation creep)

New `### Major Event Tier Rule (anti-escalation creep)` section appended immediately after the Major Event Rarity Budget closing paragraph. Setting-neutral form (the original Westeros-specific examples were replaced so non-medieval campaigns don't import `squires / sellsword captains / Sept-priests / Septon-Archbishop`). Two rules:

1. Down-shift the major-event tier by one notch in personal-scale encounters past the parity band.
2. Reserve mythic-tier for arcs the user explicitly frames as mythic; if campaign state genuinely calls for mythic pressure without the user literally framing it as such, the shared Tier Compression rule permits that — the two rules are complementary at different cadences (major-event cadence vs narrative cadence), not in conflict.

The surrounding Major Event Rarity Budget section is preserved verbatim.

### Edit 4 — `mvp_site/prompts/narrative_system_instruction.md`

Replaced the previously-inlined Tier Compression + Consequence-Hiding blocks with a pointer to `mvp_site/prompts/shared/tier_pressure.md`. NPC Autonomy and CRITICAL NPC BEHAVIOR RULES bullets are preserved verbatim.

## Testing

### Contract tests

`mvp_site/tests/test_prompt_tier_compression_contract.py` — 18 unittest assertions, all green. The test pins:

- shared/tier_pressure.md carries Tier Compression + Consequence-Hiding with the full v2 event envelope and the Perception-check gate on body language
- DialogAgent, HeavyDialogAgent, SpicyModeAgent all load `PROMPT_TYPE_TIER_PRESSURE`
- `agent_prompts.PATH_MAP` registers `PROMPT_TYPE_TIER_PRESSURE` to `shared/tier_pressure.md`
- dialog_system_instruction.md carries the Power standing row + Force-a-trade ordering
- living_world_instruction.md Major Event Tier Rule is setting-neutral (no squires, sellsword captains, Sept-priests, Septon-Archbishop) and explicitly cross-references the shared file

`mvp_site/tests/test_prompts.py` — `test_all_registered_prompts_are_actually_used` extended to mark `PROMPT_TYPE_TIER_PRESSURE` as conditional (loaded by 4 of ~12 agents).

Run locally:

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site" python3 -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_prompt_tier_compression_contract mvp_site.tests.test_prompts
```

Result: `Ran 179 tests in 0.445s — OK`.

## Evidence — diagnostic sample scenes (gist)

8 representative scenes documenting the parity-band diagnosis are at the public gist below. They are NOT in the PR branch — diagnostic evidence lives in gists, not in the repo.

Gist: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/2b8ec2956958b3d74ddbe2b8e4bab381

| # | File | Level | What it shows |
|---|------|-------|---------------|
| 1 | `01-scene-02-L6-character-creation.md` | L6 | Quiet LLM behavior — UI flow, no NPC body. The floor. |
| 2 | `02-scene-88-L8-coldmoat-disguise-peak.md` | L8 | Gold standard — 4 named NPCs, active disguise, dice roll, 706 words. **The pre-L15 register.** |
| 3 | `03-scene-145-L9-natural-quiet.md` | L9 | Natural-quiet pacing — quiet because the narrative called for quiet. |
| 4 | `04-scene-158-L10-companion-drift.md` | L10 | High-water line — companion reshuffling starts crowding out personal stakes. |
| 5 | `05-scene-180-L10-gilded-huntress-gold.md` | L10 | L10 gold standard — 3 NPCs, dice rolls, hidden consequence being filed. |
| 6 | `06-scene-252-L15-rooks-rest-quiet.md` | L15 | Quiet collapse — the regression this PR fixes. |
| 7 | `07-scene-292-L16-mander-supply-node.md` | L16 | Most-dynamic post-L15 — mythic-tier antagonists, abstract stakes. |
| 8 | `08-scene-405-L21-mirror-alysanne.md` | L21 | Mythic endgame — the carve-out this PR explicitly preserves. |

## Low-level details

### Files changed (current branch state)

title: [worldai] /af pipeline never triggers real-mode /smoke — Gate 8 permanently unreachable without manual intervention
notes:
2026-07-10T~19:00Z Found live driving PR#7888 to green. Smoke Gate Wait (Gate 8) polls
GitHub for a REAL-mode mcp-smoke-tests run or /smoke pass comment for the PR's exact
head SHA, up to 45 polls (~25min), then hard-fails: "GATE-8 FAIL: timed out waiting for
a REAL-mode mcp-smoke-tests pass ... the default smoke runs in MOCK mode and does not
satisfy the gate; run /smoke on the PR for real-service coverage."

Root cause: NOTHING in the daemon's stage-2 remediation loop (dispatch coder -> push fix
-> re-review cycle) ever triggers a real-mode smoke run. The mcp-smoke-tests.yml workflow
only fires on (a) a human-authored issue_comment starting with /smoke (requires
sender.type==User + author_association in [OWNER,MEMBER,COLLABORATOR] -- explicitly
excludes bot senders), or (b) workflow_dispatch with pr_number+test_mode=real inputs.
Neither path is ever invoked by the daemon itself. This means EVERY PR /af drives to the
point of reaching Gate 8 will hit this exact same permanent wall, 25 minutes at a time,
forever -- confirmed happened 2x in a row on PR#7888 tonight before I manually fired
`gh workflow run mcp-smoke-tests.yml -f pr_number=7888 -f test_mode=real`, which
succeeded and unblocked the gate immediately.

Real fix needed: the daemon's remediation/gate-assessment logic (daemon/src/tick.rs,
likely near the GATE_ASSESSMENT/skeptic_evidence machinery, or a new step before final
merge-readiness check) needs to trigger this workflow_dispatch itself (with
test_mode=real) once all other gates are green but Gate 8 is specifically the only thing
still pending/absent, rather than relying on a human or operator to notice and fire it
manually. Until fixed, this is THE structural reason /af cannot reach true green
end-to-end without a manual nudge on any repo using this Gate-8 pattern.

title: Sweep configured repos for factory-labeled GitHub intake
description:
## Background

The daemon now routes existing beads through configured `[repos.*]`, but GitHub intake still constructs only one `CliScm` from top-level `target_repo` (`daemon/src/main.rs`). A `factory`-labeled issue in `jleechanorg/dark-factory` is therefore invisible while `target_repo` is `jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai`. This blocked issue #278 until an operator manually added a local bead label, which violates label-to-merge zero-touch proof.

## Goal

Sweep factory-labeled issues and PRs across every configured repository, normalize them idempotently into the tracker, and preserve their repository identity for existing dispatch routing.

## Requirements

- Enumerate the top-level target plus every `[repos.*]` key; do not hardcode repository names.
- Fetch labeled issues and PRs per repository with REST/GraphQL fallback and isolated caching.
- Preserve exact `owner/repo#number` external refs and target repo.
- Carry that repository identity through downstream SCM lifecycle operations (snapshot, comments/reviews, and close/update); never resolve a bare PR number against the top-level repo.
- One repository failure must be observable and must not silently erase successful intake from other repositories.
- Deduplicate overlaps and intake races idempotently.
- Add tests for two repos with colliding issue numbers, partial API failure, duplicate config entries, and PR/issue mixtures.
- Add a collision test where both repos have PR #42 and prove each downstream SCM operation targets the intended repository.
- Keep ZFC: this is deterministic config enumeration and syntax parsing, not text classification.

## Acceptance

- A real `factory`-labeled issue created in `jleechanorg/dark-factory` becomes a tracked bead automatically without operator `br` mutation.
- Telemetry records repository, external ref, bead ID, and intake outcome.
- Existing `worldarchitect.ai` intake remains working.
- A dark-factory PR created from the ingested bead is gated and updated in dark-factory, not `worldarchitect.ai`.

Related bead: `jleechan-lwte`. Related prior routing issue: #265.

Scope limitation: the campaign shell is directly seeded using the repository's established evidence pattern so the sole real LLM call exercises the streaming propagation seam. This proves authoritative NPC level delivery into the ACTIVE-tier LLM request; it does not claim to rewrite historical narrative echoes.

## Summary

- Surfaces authoritative `npc_data[<id>].level` into the ACTIVE-tier `entity_tracking` channel so the LLM can reconcile its current narration against Firestore truth.
- Adds a +16-line prompt-contract fix in `_trim_entity_fields` (`mvp_site/llm_service.py`); no backend enforcement, no invigilator, no fall-through logic.

## Production Code Changes

**Before (`mvp_site/llm_service.py:1084-1091`, `_trim_entity_fields` ACTIVE tier):**

```python
# ACTIVE tier — drops `level`
return {
    "name": name,
    "role": role,
    "attitude": attitude,
    "status": status,
    "hp": hp,
    "location": location,
}
```

The only channel that could carry authoritative NPC stats from Firestore into the LLM bundle was the ACTIVE-tier `entity_tracking` path — but `level` was silently dropped, so the LLM had no way to reconcile stale "level 10" story-history claims against `Queen Rhaenyra Targaryen.level = 14` in Firestore. (`_prepare_story_continuation` at `llm_service.py:7058` explicitly excludes `npc_data` itself.)

**Now (`mvp_site/llm_service.py:1084-1091`):**

```python
# ACTIVE tier — surfaces `level` (positive int or None)
level_field = _coerce_positive_int_or_none(data.get("level"))
return {
    "name": name,
    "role": role,
    "attitude": attitude,
    "status": status,
    "hp": hp,
    "location": location,
    "level": level_field,
}
```

**Why:** Per ZFC + root-cause-first, the authoritative truth lives in Firestore and the prompt contract surfaces it. No backend clamp on the LLM's emitted `level` — the LLM owns D&D knowledge of what level means and how it changes. PRESENT and DORMANT tiers stay name+role only (~10 tokens/entity) to protect the bundle token budget; ACTIVE is "recently mentioned" (50 tokens/entity) and is the tier where `level` matters for combat math and tier checks.

## Test Changes

**New unit test:** `mvp_site/tests/test_entity_tracking_active_level_field.py` (182 lines) — `TestActiveEntityLevelField` with two test methods:
- `test_all_active_entities_with_source_level_surfaced` — every ACTIVE NPC whose source dict has `level` must surface it in the trimmed entity.
- `test_queen_active_entity_includes_authoritative_level` — the queen subTest pins the wire-level contract (`level == 14`) using `with self.subTest(entity="Queen", ...)`.

**New E2E test:** `testing_mcp/streaming/test_entity_tracking_level_propagation_e2e.py` (264 lines) — twin-repro that creates a fresh campaign, seeds `Queen Rhaenyra Targaryen.level = 14` directly in Firestore, issues a streaming turn mentioning the queen, and walks `llm_request_responses.jsonl` to assert the queen's captured payload includes `"level": 14`. - Does NOT erase stale story-history echoes. The new wire-level `level` field lets the LLM reconcile against Firestore, but a long campaign with strong "level 10" claims in old turns may still see partial contamination. A follow-up PR could add a RAG-side Firestore-reconcile hint or memory canonicalization pass.
