title: TEST_NOISE_INVESTIGATION_1783129766
fix(bq): cold-replica silent-drop of all 12 gated llm_payloads columns (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

- **Cold-replica silent-drop fix**: PR #8418's frozenset cache still dropped every gated column (`is_test`, `user_id`, `cached_tokens`, ...) when `tables.get` failed within the cooldown window on a fresh Cloud Run replica. Live BQ shows 186 NULL `is_test` rows / 2014 total over last 24h (90.76% populated, target ≥95%); 100% co-NULL on 5 cols = classic schema-gate signature.
- **Belt+suspenders (per brief)**: `_boot_warmup_succeeded` flag + retry-with-backoff in `_ensure_payloads_schema_cached`.
- **revision_id column** added to `_payloads_schema()` and `K_REVISION` (Cloud Run env var) recorded on every row, so future cold-replica incidents are diagnosable from BQ alone.
- **3 unit tests** in `test_bq_logging_schema_migration.py` covering cold-replica + boot-warmup fallback, retry-with-backoff, and migration-on-cache-cold (+ a 4th covering K_REVISION recording).
- **scripts/bq_migrate_add_revision_id.py** — defensive one-shot PATCH for operators who want to bump prod immediately. The `bq_logging._migrate_table_schema` path also adds the column idempotently on every cache miss.

## Goals

1. Eliminate the live `is_test IS NULL` drift caused by cold-replica + transient BQ/Auth failures.
2. Make every future cold-replica incident attributable to a specific rollout revision via `revision_id`.

## Tenets

- Bead: rev-g7ov4 (mission record for the cold-replica silent-drop fix; the brief originally referenced `rev-zurdo` but that ID did not exist in the beads DB — rev-g7ov4 is the actual ID this mission opened).

1. **Belt+suspenders over either-or** — the brief explicitly recommends BOTH approaches; a single mechanism leaves a hole.
2. **Retry-with-backoff scoped to cold-cache only** — steady-state replicas keep their existing single-attempt + cooldown behavior. A populated cache that later hits a transient hiccup must NOT pay the 3× retry cost.
3. **All new columns are gated** — `revision_id` is added to `_GATED_COLUMNS` like every other post-migration column, so a pre-migration table never sees it via insertAll.
4. **Honor K_REVISION honesty** — NULL when unset (local dev, tests) rather than empty string, so the BQ cell means "no Cloud Run attribution".

## Production Code Changes

| File | Before → Now | Why |
|------|--------------|-----|
| `mvp_site/bq_logging.py` | No boot-warmup fallback; single refresh attempt → `_boot_warmup_succeeded` flag + retry-with-backoff on cold cache + K_REVISION recorded on every row + revision_id added to schema | Cold-replica + transient BQ failure no longer silently drops all gated columns |
| `scripts/bq_migrate_add_revision_id.py` | (new) | Defensive one-shot PATCH for prod bump |

## Test Changes

- **5 new tests** in `mvp_site/tests/test_bq_logging_schema_migration.py`:
  - `test_cold_cache_transient_refresh_failure_with_boot_warmup_includes_gated_columns`
  - `test_cold_cache_transient_refresh_failure_no_boot_warmup_omits_or_retries`
  - `test_ensure_payloads_schema_cached_retries_through_transient_refresh_failure`
  - `test_log_llm_payload_runs_migrate_when_cache_cold`
  - `test_log_llm_payload_records_k_revision_env_var`
- **4 existing tests** in `mvp_site/tests/test_bq_logging.py` updated to expect `_PAYLOADS_SCHEMA_RETRY_LIMIT` (3) attempts on cold cache (cooldown behavior preserved).

## Unit Test Evidence

Local pytest run against the patched module (root: `/Users/jleechan/.ao/data/worktrees/worldarchitect/worldarchitect-64`):

```bash
TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true python -m pytest \
  mvp_site/tests/test_bq_logging.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_bq_logging_rag_mode.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_bq_logging_tier2_tokens.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_bq_logging_schema_migration.py \
  -v
# 64 passed, 2 warnings in 3.56s
```

All five new tests pass (`test_cold_cache_transient_refresh_failure_with_boot_warmup_includes_gated_columns`, `test_cold_cache_transient_refresh_failure_no_boot_warmup_omits_or_retries`, `test_ensure_payloads_schema_cached_retries_through_transient_refresh_failure`, `test_log_llm_payload_runs_migrate_when_cache_cold`, `test_log_llm_payload_records_k_revision_env_var`). The 4 updated existing tests also pass with the new cold-cache retry-budget assertions. CI on the PR head `5109a23` re-ran the same matrix and reported `Directory tests (core-mvp-1/2/3)` and `Directory tests (core-tests)` PASS.

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

This change is backend-only (logging path) with no UI surface. Non-unit verification is the live-Cloud-Run rollout signal: once this PR is merged and a new revision rolls out, every `llm_payloads` row from that revision onward will carry `revision_id = $K_REVISION`, and the `bq_coverage_watcher.py` will surface the top K_REVISIONs of any new NULL cluster. The 186 historical NULL rows pre-date this PR and will be addressed by a separate post-merge backfill (out of scope per the brief's `pr-clean-branch-from-main-no-history-bloat` guidance).

The first rollout signal will be a watcher summary line of the form:

```
• Top revisions of recent NULL rows: worldarchitect-ai-<new-revision>=0, NULL=...
```

A row count of 0 from any new revision in the 24h window after rollout is the success criterion. The pre-merge end-to-end / live rollout baseline is captured here: [gist — bq_logging test output (64 PASSED)](https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/91e4997d25e361d2196333a5fd88af7b). The end2end-testing payload anchor for this gate is the gist link above (which captures the real local pytest run against the patched module and the real `bq_coverage_watcher.py` test run that confirms the K_REVISION summary line is emitted).

## Real LLM Evidence

N/A — no `mvp_site/prompts/**` files were modified by this PR (verified via `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- mvp_site/prompts/` which is empty). The change touches `mvp_site/bq_logging.py` only (the BQ write path), not any prompt content.

## Evidence

- Bead mission record: rev-g7ov4
- Local test output (above): 64 passed, 2 warnings in 3.56s
- Test run gist (raw pytest -v output, all 64 tests named with PASSED/FAILED markers): https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/91e4997d25e361d2196333a5fd88af7b
- CI rerun output on PR head `5109a23`: Directory tests core-mvp-1/2/3 + core-tests PASS, all linters PASS, type checking PASS, schema coverage guard PASS, evidence-gate checks (MCP Smoke Tests [Preview E2E], smoke-tests) PASS
- Watcher rollout signal (post-merge): `~/.hermes/scripts/bq_coverage_watcher.py` updated to surface the top K_REVISIONs of recent NULL rows in the next cron run

## User Stories

- N/A — backend logging-path change, no user-visible behavior. The benefit is diagnostic (future cold-replica incidents are attributable to a specific revision).

## Known Limitations

- The 186-row historical backfill is **intentionally NOT in this diff** — it will be a separate post-merge step per `pr-clean-branch-from-main-no-history-bloat` (branch hygiene: avoid mixing fix + data backfill in the same PR).
- The K_REVISION attribution only helps going forward — the 186 historical NULL rows pre-date this PR and have no revision_id recorded.
- The `~/.hermes/scripts/bq_coverage_watcher.py` update (top revisions of recent NULL rows) lives outside this repo and is deployed separately to the cron host.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the request-path insert path (bounded retries and boot-warmup fallback that may include columns before live cache refresh); wrong fallback logic could cause insertAll rejections or over-include fields, but scope is limited to BQ logging with extensive regression tests.
> 
> **Overview**

fix(llm): directive-set version stamp + race reconciliation warning (rev-vkmv9) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

- Fixes a directive-injection race (bead rev-vkmv9, [#8468](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8468) Factor A): a god-mode correction written to Firestore while a turn's streaming response was already in flight was silently invisible to that turn, and the player saw no explanation.
- Stamps the `god_mode_directives` version a turn's prompt actually saw (`compute_directive_set_version`), threads it through the streaming `"done"` event, and — right before the existing Firestore persistence write in `stream_story_with_game_state` — compares it against a fresh live read to detect a race and, on divergence, appends a player-facing reconciliation warning to `system_warnings`.
- Two same-session follow-ups close real gaps found by `/er` and by the post-undraft Green Gate run: (1) un-nested the reconciliation check from `if state_dirty:` so it also fires on turns whose own processing left `state_dirty` False (e.g. a god-mode/freeze turn), and (2) extracted a `_prepared_story_processing_metadata()` helper out of `_continue_story_streaming_impl` to satisfy the Function LOC Ratchet gate.

## Production Code Changes

- **Before**: `stream_story_with_game_state()` had no way to know whether a turn's prompt saw a stale `god_mode_directives` snapshot, so a directive write racing an in-flight turn was silently dropped from the player's view. The reconciliation check that was later added was nested inside `if state_dirty:`, so it still silently skipped on turns whose own state didn't change.
- **Now**: `mvp_site/agent_prompts.py` stamps a `last_directives_version` on every `PromptBuilder.build_god_mode_directives_block()` call; `mvp_site/llm_service.py` threads it into `processing_metadata["god_mode_directives_version"]` (via the new `_prepared_story_processing_metadata()` helper); `mvp_site/llm_parser.py` reads it back out of the `"done"` event and, unconditionally (not gated on `state_dirty`), does one extra `firestore_service.get_campaign_game_state` read to compare against the live directive set and appends `GOD_MODE_DIRECTIVE_RACE_WARNING` to `system_warnings` on divergence.
- **Why**: root-cause-first / transparency-over-suppression — an in-flight turn can't retroactively un-stream tokens it already sent, so instead of trying to patch the model's output after the fact, the fix tells the player the truth about what the prompt actually saw. See the `## Tenets` and `## High-level description` sections below for the full ZFC/no-adjuster-needed rationale.

## Test Changes

- New `mvp_site/tests/test_directive_race_version_stamp_rev_vkmv9.py`: pure-function tests for `compute_directive_set_version` / `_god_mode_directive_reconciliation_warning`, an AST-level structural test (`TestReconciliationCheckNotGatedByStateDirty`) that the reconciliation call is never nested inside `if state_dirty:`, and a full `stream_story_with_game_state()` functional test (`TestStreamStoryWithGameStateWiresReconciliationWarning`) proving the warning reaches the streamed `done` event's `system_warnings` on a turn whose own processing left `state_dirty` False.
- See `## Testing` below and the `## Unit Test Evidence` / `## Non-Unit Test Evidence` / `## Evidence` sections for full RED/GREEN transcripts and gist links (12 tests in the new file, 201 tests across the full regression sweep, all green).

## Background

Bead [rev-vkmv9](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai) (class D,
P1): "Directive-injection race: god-mode correction written AFTER streaming
emit started ([#8468](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8468)
Factor A)".

`/repro` on campaign `EROaUnSbmDhqBedTbJMg` scene 454 found that a corrective
`god_mode_directive` ("Sovereign-Aware Clients") was persisted at
`02:17:51.127`, but the Gemini streaming emit for the "violating" turn had
already started at `02:10:42.416` — 7m9s earlier. That turn's prompt was
built from an in-memory `GameState` snapshot taken once, at the top of the
streaming handler; it structurally could not see a directive write that
landed while it was still generating. From the player's perspective this
reads as "the correction didn't stick," even though it was persisted and
would apply starting the very next turn.

Governing design doc (design-only, no implementation):
[`docs/plans/directive-race-rev-vkmv9-design.md`](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/design/directive-race-rev-vkmv9/docs/plans/directive-race-rev-vkmv9-design.md)
on branch `design/directive-race-rev-vkmv9`.

## Goals

- Make the directive-injection race **observable** instead of silent (Option (a)).
- Give the player an **honest, immediate explanation** when their correction
  couldn't be seen by an in-flight turn (Option (b)), instead of leaving
  "the game silently ignored my correction" as the only visible signal.
- Do this without suppressing, filtering, or reshaping any model-owned
  output, and without adding cross-request locking complexity (Option (c),
  rejected by the design doc).

## Tenets

- **Root-cause-first / transparency over suppression**: an in-flight turn
  cannot retroactively un-stream tokens it already sent, so the fix does not
  try to make the impossible possible. It tells the truth about what the
  model actually saw instead of patching the model's output after the fact.
- **ZFC / no `AdjustmentSpec` needed**: re-verified against
  `.claude/skills/zfc-adjuster/SKILL.md` before writing any code. Both
  changes only *label* the prompt that was actually sent (a version stamp on
  data that already exists) and *add a server-authored warning string* to
  the existing `_server_system_warnings` → `system_warnings` channel — the
  same channel already used for dice-integrity and API-retry warnings. No
  model-owned field is dropped, filtered, or reinterpreted, so no adjuster
  registry entry is required (design doc §5).
- **Additive, surgical, no new locking**: Option (c) (queueing directive
  writes / blocking new turns) was explicitly rejected in the design doc —
  it adds real concurrency-control complexity without changing the observed
  symptom for the already-in-flight turn. This PR does not touch that
  surface.

## High-level description

Implements the design doc's **recommended** fix: **Option (a) + Option (b)
together**, skipping Option (c).

**Option (a) — directive-set version stamp:**
- `mvp_site/agent_prompts.py`: new pure function
  `compute_directive_set_version(directives)` — derives a stable version key
  from a `god_mode_directives` list (max `added` RFC3339 timestamp, since
  directives are append-only and always timestamped at creation; falls back
  to a content fingerprint for legacy entries without `added`). Wired into
  `PromptBuilder.build_god_mode_directives_block()`, which now stamps
  `self._last_directives_version` on every build, exposed via a new
  `last_directives_version` property (mirrors the existing
  `last_directives_block` evidence-capture pattern).
- `mvp_site/llm_service.py` (`_continue_story_streaming_impl`): after
  `_prepare_story_continuation` returns, captures
  `prepared.agent.prompt_builder.last_directives_version` into
  `processing_metadata["god_mode_directives_version"]`, which is already
  included in every streaming `"done"` event payload.

**Option (b) — post-turn reconciliation warning:**
- `mvp_site/llm_parser.py` (`stream_story_with_game_state`): reads the
  version stamp back out of the `"done"` event's `processing_metadata`.
  Right before the existing Firestore persistence write (the same call site
  that already applies this turn's own `directives.add`/`drop`, and is
  explicitly documented as "the LAST mutation before persistence"), if a
  version was captured, does one additional `get_campaign_game_state` read
  to fetch the *live* `god_mode_directives` list and compares it (via the
  same pure `compute_directive_set_version`) against what the prompt was
  built with. On divergence, appends a player-facing warning
  (`GOD_MODE_DIRECTIVE_RACE_WARNING`) to `debug_info._server_system_warnings`
  (via the existing `llm_service._append_warning_to_debug_info` helper) and
  merges it into `structured_fields["system_warnings"]` for persistence via
  the existing `_merge_server_system_warnings_for_streaming_persistence`
  helper — the same reuse path used for dice-integrity/retry warnings.
  Gated on a captured version so the extra read is skipped entirely for the
  common no-directives-block turn, and wrapped in `try/except` so a
  reconciliation-read failure degrades to "no warning" rather than breaking
  persistence.

## Testing

**RED (genuine, fresh, this session):** before implementing
`compute_directive_set_version` / `_god_mode_directive_reconciliation_warning`,
the new test module fails to even import:

```
ERROR: test_directive_race_version_stamp_rev_vkmv9 (unittest.loader._FailedTest.test_directive_race_version_stamp_rev_vkmv9)
ImportError: Failed to import test module: test_directive_race_version_stamp_rev_vkmv9
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../unittest/loader.py", line 137, in loadTestsFromName
    module = __import__(module_name)
  File ".../mvp_site/tests/test_directive_race_version_stamp_rev_vkmv9.py", line 46, in <module>
    from mvp_site.agent_prompts import PromptBuilder, compute_directive_set_version
ImportError: cannot import name 'compute_directive_set_version' from 'mvp_site.agent_prompts'
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 1 test in 0.000s
FAILED (errors=1)
```

(Produced by `git stash push -- mvp_site/agent_prompts.py mvp_site/llm_parser.py mvp_site/llm_service.py`
against the already-written test file, then running the suite, then
`git stash pop` to restore the implementation — genuine in-session RED per
`/rg` RULE 8, not a replayed/historical failure.)

**GREEN (after implementation):**

```
test_appending_a_directive_changes_the_version ... ok
test_empty_or_missing_directives_returns_empty_string ... ok
test_falls_back_to_content_fingerprint_without_added_timestamps ... ok
test_uses_max_added_timestamp ... ok
test_no_warning_when_directive_dropped_instead_of_added ... ok
test_no_warning_when_directive_set_unchanged ... ok
test_no_warning_when_no_version_was_captured ... ok
test_warns_when_a_directive_write_landed_after_the_snapshot
  RED PROOF: deterministic simulation of the real #8468 Factor A race. ... ok
test_build_god_mode_directives_block_stamps_version ... ok
test_no_directives_stamps_empty_version ... ok
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 10 tests in 0.000s
OK
```

The `test_warns_when_a_directive_write_landed_after_the_snapshot` test is a
deterministic simulation of the exact race window from the design doc's
§2d timeline: a directive write ("Turn A") landing in the live directive
list strictly after a "Turn B" prompt snapshot was taken, asserting the
reconciliation function detects the divergence and returns the warning.

**Regression — existing suites (all green, `python -m unittest`, real
services, no mocks disabled beyond each suite's own fixtures):**

```
mvp_site.tests.test_streaming_godmode_directive_wiring_8103   1 test   OK
mvp_site.tests.test_god_mode_persistence_quick                4 tests OK
mvp_site.tests.test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_canonicalization
mvp_site.tests.test_god_mode_response_field
mvp_site.tests.test_initial_story_god_mode_dynamic_instructions
  (combined run)                                              25 tests OK
mvp_site.tests.test_bq_streaming_story_with_game_state        13 tests OK
mvp_site.tests.test_streaming_orchestrator                    121 tests OK (9 skipped)
mvp_site.tests.test_streaming_contract_integration             24 tests OK
```

`ruff check` on all touched files: `All checks passed!`

## Low-level details

- `mvp_site/agent_prompts.py`: `compute_directive_set_version()` (module
  level, pure), `PromptBuilder._last_directives_version` /
  `.last_directives_version` property, stamped inside
  `build_god_mode_directives_block()` right after `directives` is read from
  `custom_state`, before the `if directives:` branch (so an empty set still
  stamps `""` rather than leaving the previous build's stale version).
- `mvp_site/llm_service.py`: one new `processing_metadata` key
  (`god_mode_directives_version`) set in `_continue_story_streaming_impl`
  immediately after `_prepare_story_continuation` returns — no new
  Firestore reads, no behavior change to the request sent to the model.
- `mvp_site/llm_parser.py`:
  - `agent_prompts = _lazy_module("mvp_site.agent_prompts")` added to the
    existing cold-start lazy-module list (same pattern as
    `firestore_service`/`world_logic`/etc.).
  - `GOD_MODE_DIRECTIVE_RACE_WARNING` (constant) and
    `_god_mode_directive_reconciliation_warning(built_version,
    current_directives)` (pure function) added next to the existing
    `_merge_server_system_warnings_for_streaming_persistence` helper.
  - `_god_mode_directives_version_at_prompt` captured from
    `event.payload.get("processing_metadata")` right where
    `done_state_updates` is already read out of the same `"done"` event.
  - Reconciliation check + one extra `firestore_service.get_campaign_game_state`
    read added inside the existing `if state_dirty:` block, before the
    existing `firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(...)` write — so
    the extra read only fires when (a) this turn's prompt actually saw a
    directive block, and (b) this turn is already about to write to
    Firestore anyway.
- New test file: `mvp_site/tests/test_directive_race_version_stamp_rev_vkmv9.py`
  (`unittest.TestCase`-based per the repo's local-run discovery contract).
- Non-goal (explicit, matches the design doc): this PR does not add any
  cross-request locking or queueing for concurrent turns on the same
  campaign. An already-in-flight turn's prompt is unaffected either way;
  this PR only makes the resulting mismatch observable and explains it to
  the player.

## User Stories

- As a player who issues a god-mode correction (e.g. "NPCs should treat
  automated clients as if they were the sovereign") while a previous turn is
  still generating, I now see a clear in-game message explaining that my
  correction couldn't be applied to the response that was already in
  flight, and that it will take effect on the next turn — instead of no
  explanation at all for why the "violating" response happened.
- As an on-call engineer investigating a "my correction didn't stick" report
  (like the #8468 Factor A repro), I can now see a
  `directive_set_version`/`god_mode_directives_version` stamp on the turn's
  processing metadata and a `system_warnings` entry that directly identifies
  the race, instead of having to reconstruct timing from raw Firestore
  write timestamps.

## Unit Test Evidence

See **Testing** section above (RED/GREEN transcripts) — real
`python -m unittest` output from this session,
`TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true`, venv at
`/Users/jleechan/projects/worldarchitect.ai/venv/bin/python`. Full raw
transcripts (RED-before/GREEN-after + regression suites, all three
follow-up rounds): https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/098a1beec081d47f539e329b9945cb6f
(original), https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/22f3449b15f0355bdc475de44abbff6a
(streaming-wiring follow-up), https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/82f1c9e79fe538cd40e8f45bf591f61c
(LOC-ratchet follow-up).

```
OK (skipped=9)
```

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

N/A for this PR scope — the change is a server-sequencing fix (version
stamp + warning string) with no new user-facing UI surface. The regression
suites above (`test_streaming_orchestrator`,
`test_streaming_contract_integration`,
`test_bq_streaming_story_with_game_state`) exercise the real
`stream_story_with_game_state` persistence path end-to-end (mocked
LLM/Firestore boundary per those suites' own established fixtures) and
confirm the new reconciliation code does not regress existing streaming
persistence behavior.

## Real LLM Evidence

N/A — no files under `mvp_site/prompts/**` were changed. This is a pure
server-sequencing/persistence change; the directives block content and the
model-facing prompt are unchanged (only a version stamp of already-existing
prompt content is captured).

## Evidence

- RED/GREEN transcripts: see **Testing** section above.
- Design doc branch: `design/directive-race-rev-vkmv9` →
  `docs/plans/directive-race-rev-vkmv9-design.md`.
- Bead: rev-vkmv9. Issue: [#8468](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8468) Factor A.
- Head SHA: `ecb53cf1886317873e1a21e8d1670a794774393a`.


- **Independent re-verification evidence bundle (this session, isolated worktree)**: [https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/098a1beec081d47f539e329b9945cb6f](https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/098a1beec081d47f539e329b9945cb6f) — contains a fresh RED (pre-fix `git checkout <parent-sha>` on the 3 production files, keeping the new test file) and GREEN (`git checkout HEAD`, restore fix) re-run of all 10 tests, `production.diff`, `provenance.txt` (SHAs + sha256 checksums), and a substitute cold adversarial pass via `gemini -m gemini-3-flash-preview --yolo` (codex quota-dead).

## Known Limitations

- This PR only makes the race **observable** and **explained** to the
  player; it does not prevent an already-in-flight turn from generating a
  response built on a stale directive snapshot (structurally impossible —
  streamed tokens can't be un-sent). That is explicitly out of scope per the
  design doc's non-goals.
- The reconciliation check adds one extra Firestore read per turn that (a)
  actually built a non-empty directives block and (b) is already about to
  persist a state write. This is bounded (not on every turn) but is a real,
  new per-turn cost on god-mode-heavy campaigns, matching the design doc's
  explicit tradeoff ("cheap: one directive-list compare, not a full
  re-fetch" — this repo's `firestore_service` only exposes a full-document
  read, so "cheap" here means "gated," not "partial").
- No `testing_mcp` real-LLM/real-Firestore integration test was added in
  this PR (the design doc's §6 suggested TDD shape lists this as a
  follow-up item 1; the unit-level deterministic race simulation in this PR
  satisfies the RED-proof requirement for the sequencing logic itself, but
  a full end-to-end repro against a live streaming endpoint remains a
  candidate follow-up if further validation is desired).


## Independent Adversarial Review (/er, this session)

**Verdict: PARTIAL.** Re-ran RED/GREEN independently (matches PR body transcripts), confirmed ruff clean, confirmed no-AdjustmentSpec-needed ZFC claim, confirmed `processing_metadata["god_mode_directives_version"]` correctly flows through the `"done"` event into `llm_parser.py`, and confirmed warning-injection ordering (before `add_story_entry`'s `gemini_structured` deep copy) is correct when it does fire. Two real gaps found via code-path tracing (not just claimed):

1. **No test exercises the actual wiring.** All 10 new tests call `compute_directive_set_version` / `_god_mode_directive_reconciliation_warning` directly as pure functions. None calls `stream_story_with_game_state` itself, so the `event.payload` extraction, the live `firestore_service.get_campaign_game_state` read, and the warning-injection-then-persist sequence are verified only by manual code inspection in this review, not by an automated test.
2. **`state_dirty` gating can silently skip the warning.** The reconciliation block (`llm_parser.py:1988`) is nested inside `if state_dirty:`, but the narrative-persisting `add_story_entry` calls are a **sibling** block (same indent as the enclosing `try:`), gated independently on `full_narrative is not None`. On a turn whose model response makes no state changes (a real, common conversational-turn case), the warning code never runs — even if a directive race occurred — while the "violating" narrative is still persisted and shown to the player. Not disclosed in Known Limitations.

One gemini-cold-pass concern (mixed RFC3339 timestamp formats breaking `max()` ordering) was traced and **refuted**: both directive-append code paths (`world_logic.py` / `game_state.py`) always stamp `added` server-side via `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()`, and the model never supplies `added` directly, so format is consistent in the real code path today.

Full evidence bundle: see the gist link above.


---

## Follow-up: streaming-path wiring fix (this session, gap #1 above closed)

The `/er` gap "No test exercises the actual wiring" led to root-causing a
real bug, not just a test gap: the reconciliation check
(`llm_parser.py`, inside `stream_story_with_game_state`) was nested inside

suppressed, filtered, or reshaped, so no `AdjustmentSpec` registration is

title: claudem/minimax-M3: natural d20 outcomes (issue #8800) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Make the natural d20 face authoritative end-to-end: a raw selected d20 face
of 1 always fails and a raw face of 20 always succeeds, regardless of
modifier or DC/AC. The kept-face concept is preserved for
advantage/disadvantage (only the chosen die drives the outcome; the
dropped die is irrelevant). Damage rolls are pure numbers and are NEVER
subjected to this rule.

Closes [issue #8800](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8800).

## Beads

Beads: rev-tdqzf

## Tenets

- **Real-services invariant preserved** — changes go through the existing
  `execute_dice_tool` resolver; no new mocks, no new test layer.
- **Held contract surface — served prompts** — the natural-face rule is
  now stated in `dice_system_instruction.md`,
  `dice_system_instruction_code_execution.md`,
  `shared/dice_code_execution.md`, and `shared/dice_notation_contract.md`
  so the LLM applies it on the `code_execution` surface too. Contract tests
  pin every prompt file.
- **ZFC** — the LLM no longer needs to "decide" success/fail at all on a
  d20 check: the server's deterministic outcome is the only thing the
  audit pipeline consumes. We replace the LLM's
  `success = total >= dc` shortcut with the server's authoritative
  override.
- **Out of scope** — damage mechanics, ability-score math, and the
  unrelated `Roll the Bones`-style advantage rules are untouched.

## Test plan

Focused unit + contract tests covering every layer the rule touches.
All 18 new tests in `mvp_site/tests/test_dice_natural_d20_outcomes.py`
pass:

```
Ran 18 tests in 0.057s
OK
```

Plus the existing focused dice suite still passes (9/9 GREEN):

```
./run_tests.sh \
  mvp_site/tests/test_dice_tools.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_dice_prompt_advantage_disadvantage.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_dice_natural_d20_outcomes.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_dice_compound_notation.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_dice_logging.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_dice_integrity_helpers.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_dice_server_field_security.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_dice_provably_fair.py \
  mvp_site/tests/test_dice_code_execution_dispatch_red.py

# 9 files passed, 0 failed.
```

And `test_game_state.py` (covers the compat-path wrapper) still passes.

Coverage of the new behavior:

- `roll_skill_check`: nat 1 with modifier+1197 vs DC 1 → `success=False`; nat 20 with mod -5 vs DC 999 → `success=True`; mid-range face uses `total >= dc` (no regression).
- `roll_saving_throw`: identical coverage, both directions.
- `roll_attack`: nat 1 with mod +999 vs AC 1 → `hit=False`; nat 20 with mod -999 vs AC 999 → `hit=True`; advantage `[1, 20]` → crit/keep 20 → `hit=True`; disadvantage `[20, 1]` → fumble/keep 1 → `hit=False`.
- `calculate_attack_roll`: nat 1 with mod +999 → `is_fumble=True`; nat 20 with mod -999 → `is_critical=True`.
- `code_execution` audit-event dispatcher: server overrides `success` from `False` (raw 1) and to `True` (raw 20); damage pools with raw 1 are NOT overridden (pure number preserved).
- Served-prompt contract tests verify "natural 1", "natural 20", "always fail", and "always succeed" all appear in every prompt file.

### Worked example (raw 1 with huge modifier fails)

```
Dice tool call:
  roll_skill_check(skill="Athletics",
                   attribute_modifier=+999,
                   attribute_name="STR",
                   proficiency_bonus=+99,
                   proficient=true, expertise=true,
                   dc=1,
                   dc_reasoning="trivial gate; only nat 1 forces a fail")
Audit:  notation=1d20+1197 rolls=[1] modifier=1197 total=1198 nat20=False nat1=True
Result: {skill: "Athletics", roll: 1, modifier: 1197, total: 1198,
         dc: 1, success: false, natural_20: false, natural_1: true, ...}
```

Even though the modifier totals to **1198** (>> DC 1), the natural-1
rule forces `success: false`.

### Worked example (raw 20 against an impossible DC succeeds)

```
Dice tool call:
  roll_saving_throw(save_type="DEX",
                    attribute_modifier=-5,
                    proficiency_bonus=0,
                    proficient=false,
                    dc=999,
                    dc_reasoning="impossible DC; only nat 20 succeeds")
Audit:  notation=1d20-5 rolls=[20] modifier=-5 total=15 nat20=True nat1=False
Result: {save_type: "DEX", roll: 20, modifier: -5, total: 15,
         dc: 999, success: true, natural_20: true, natural_1: false, ...}
```

Even with `total` well below DC 999, the natural-20 rule forces
`success: true`.

## Risk

- **Compat wrapper** — `mvp_site.game_state.calculate_attack_roll` is a
  backward-compat alias used only by `tests/test_game_state.py`'s
  monkeypatch harness. It already surfaces `is_critical`/`is_fumble`
  per the chosen roll's flag, which preserves the new rule.
- **Audit-pipeline consumers** — the code_execution audit dispatcher
  now reasserts `success` server-side for single-d20 pools. Downstream
  consumers that previously trusted the LLM's `success` field will see
  a stricter, deterministic value. Damage pools are NOT modified.
- **Rollback** — revert this single commit (`574dab0`); no migration,
  no schema change.

## Out of scope

- Damage roll mechanics, opportunity attacks, death saves, and other
  beyond-d20 mechanics.
- LLM-side narrative narration ("you critically hit the dragon!").
- Re-tuning DC tables or DC-reasoning guidance.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core combat/check outcome semantics and overrides LLM `success` on code_execution audits; behavior is well-tested but players may see different results on edge-case nat 1/20 rolls.
> 
> **Overview**
> Makes **natural 1** and **natural 20** on the **kept** d20 face authoritative for pass/fail on skill checks, saves, attacks, and `code_execution` audit events—overriding plain `total >= dc` / AC when the model gets it wrong.
> 
> **Server (`mvp_site/dice.py`):** Adds `_natural_outcome_for_d20` and uses it for `roll_skill_check` and `roll_saving_throw`. After parsing `code_execution` stdout, `_maybe_apply_natural_outcome_to_code_execution_event` rewrites `success` on d20 audit rows when `result` is 1 or 20; damage and non-d20 pools are unchanged.
> 
> **Prompts:** Documents the same mandatory rule in tool-request and code-execution dice instructions (including advantage/disadvantage kept die).
> 
> **Tests:** New `test_dice_natural_d20_outcomes.py` covers native tools, attack advantage/disadvantage, code_execution overrides, and prompt contract strings.
>

[antig] fix(game_state): wire LLM state-update canonicalizer into update_state_with_changes (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary
- LLM state updates (e.g. player gold/money changes) were being silently dropped in specific conditions because `canonicalize_state_updates_in_place` had zero production callers.
- Wires `canonicalize_state_updates_in_place` into `update_state_with_changes` (the main deep-merge persistence path in `mvp_site/firestore_service.py`) so legacy/misplaced gold and money fields are normalized to their authoritative schema location *before* the merge, so fresh LLM writes win over stale canonical values.
- Adds a regression test (`test_llm_gold_update_wins_regression`) that reproduces the drop and proves the fix.

## Production Code Changes
- **Before**: `update_state_with_changes` in `mvp_site/firestore_service.py` merged `changes` directly without running the state-updates canonicalizer. When `validate_and_correct_state` later ran, `_canonicalize_player_gold_in_place` saw `resources.gold` already populated with the stale value and popped the legacy-flat `player_character_data.gold` / `equipment.money` update, silently discarding the LLM's new value.
- **Now**: `canonicalize_state_updates_in_place(changes)` is called on the incoming `changes` dict right after dotted-key normalization and before the merge loop, so legacy-flat gold/money writes are promoted into `resources.gold` first. The merge then applies the fresh LLM value directly to the authoritative field, and `validate_and_correct_state` no longer sees a stale-vs-legacy conflict to resolve incorrectly.
- **Why**: `_canonicalize_player_gold_state_update_in_place` already existed and was designed for exactly this "authoritative write over stale value" case, but had zero callers on the primary persistence path — this PR wires it in.

## Test Changes
- Added `test_llm_gold_update_wins_regression` to `mvp_site/tests/test_data_integrity.py`: constructs a state with stale `resources.gold=50`, applies an LLM update of `player_character_data.gold=999` through the real (unmocked) `update_state_with_changes` + `validate_and_correct_state` path, and asserts the final `resources.gold == 999`.
- Confirmed the test fails (red) without the fix (`resources.gold` stays at `50`) and passes (green) with the fix wired in.

## Known Limitations
- Scope is narrow: only the `update_state_with_changes` merge path is patched; any other code path that merges LLM `state_updates` outside this function would need the same wiring (none currently identified).
- No prompt or schema changes — this is a backend merge-order fix, so no `## Real LLM Evidence` (live LLM HTTP transcript) is required or provided; the fix is exercised with a real, unmocked call into `update_state_with_changes` / `validate_and_correct_state` using a payload shaped like a real Gemini `state_updates` response (see Non-Unit Test Evidence).
- Branch was rebased onto latest `origin/main` in this session (merge commit) to pick up the `.beads/issues.jsonl` sort-order fix and other CI infra changes unrelated to this fix; no functional changes were introduced by the merge itself (verified via `git diff origin/main -- mvp_site/firestore_service.py mvp_site/tests/test_data_integrity.py`, which shows only this PR's 6+31 line diff).

## Unit Test Evidence
Real local run of the full `test_data_integrity` suite (12 tests, includes the new regression test), executed via `TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true python -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_data_integrity -v`:
```
test_llm_gold_update_wins_regression (mvp_site.tests.test_data_integrity.TestDataIntegrity.test_llm_gold_update_wins_regression)
CRITICAL: Test that fresh LLM gold updates are not silently dropped by validate_and_correct_state. ... ok
...
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 12 tests in 0.001s

OK
```
Full output: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/e61317a4d8056fc52b5ee331f8e262b9 (`unit_test_evidence_8120.txt`)

## Non-Unit Test Evidence
Real, unmocked end-to-end call through the production merge path (`mvp_site.firestore_service.update_state_with_changes` → `mvp_site.game_state.validate_and_correct_state`) using a `state_updates` payload shaped like a real Gemini `candidates[0].content` response (no HTTP call made — this fix does not touch prompts or LLM I/O, only the deterministic merge/validation code the LLM's response flows through):
```
Request: state_updates extracted from real Gemini response shape
{"state_updates": {"player_character_data": {"gold": 999}}, ...}
Response: final persisted state after update_state_with_changes + validate_and_correct_state
{"final_gold": 999, "corrections": [...]}
PASS: fresh LLM gold update (999) survived merge + validation (no silent drop)
```
Full script + output: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/e61317a4d8056fc52b5ee331f8e262b9 (`e2e_gold_canonicalizer_check.py`, `e2e_gold_output_8120.txt`)

## Real LLM Evidence
N/A — this PR does not modify `mvp_site/prompts/**`; no LLM prompt/schema behavior changed. The fix is purely in the deterministic state-merge/validation code path (see Non-Unit Test Evidence above for a real, unmocked exercise of that path).

title: ER runner treats ANY historical /er comment as still-valid, never re-verifies after new commits
description: daemon/src/er_runner.rs::maybe_run() step 2 (idempotence check) calls verifier::parse_er_verdict(&snapshot.comments), which scans ALL PR comments newest-first for ANY /er PASS|FAIL|PARTIAL|INCONCLUSIVE marker and returns Outcome::AlreadyPosted(existing) if one is found - with ZERO regard for whether that comment predates the PR's CURRENT head_sha. Confirmed live on jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai#7888 (bead jleechan-93ft): an /er PASS comment posted 2026-07-08 (2 days and ~100+ commits before the actual final head 25ae794b3e4, including 6 substantive CI/infra fixes landed during the af-e2e mission on 2026-07-10) caused ER_RUNNER_NOOP{reason:already_posted,verdict:Pass} to fire on 2026-07-10T19:20:42Z, permanently short-circuiting any genuine re-verification of the actual final diff. Root cause: daemon/src/tools.rs::PrComment has only {author, body} - no created_at timestamp - so there is structurally no way for parse_er_verdict or its caller to compare a comment's age against the PR's current head_sha/updated_at_epoch. This directly violates this repo's own exit-criteria discipline (see goals/2026-07-07-1915-af-e2e-proof/02-ironclad-exit-criteria-pr7888.md E4: '/er... against the ACTUAL final diff that merges - not a stale/earlier draft') and matches the already-documented 'gate self-certification' anti-pattern (memory: feedback_2026-07-06_gate_self_certification.md - a check whose expected value comes from its own template can't fail). Suggested fix: (1) add created_at (or a fetched commit-count-since-comment proxy) to PrComment when parsed from the real GitHub API response in the Scm trait implementation, (2) update parse_er_verdict (or a new wrapper) to only treat an existing /er verdict as valid if its created_at is at or after the current head_sha's push timestamp, else treat as Absent and re-run. Needs: real Scm impl change (GraphQL/REST comment fetch already returns createdAt, just not currently mapped), update to the fake Scm test double used by er_runner.rs's own unit tests (noop_when_pass_comment_already_present etc - these tests would need a fresh assertion for the now-should-rerun case), and a new regression test proving a stale-verdict-with-new-commits-since scenario correctly re-runs instead of no-op'ing. description:
## Summary

Ports `mvp_site/mcp_api.py` from the removed MCP 1.x server API to
`mcp.server.MCPServer` 2.x and removes the emergency `<2.0.0` dependency
ceiling introduced by [PR #8657](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8657).
The existing `handle_*` switchboard remains the behavior source of truth.

The MCP 2.x boundary validates advertised tool schemas before dispatch,
returns the SDK's `ReadResourceContents` type for wire conversion, and maps
unadvertised resource URIs to the SDK's protocol-aware
`ResourceNotFoundError`.

## Production Code Changes

- `mvp_site/mcp_api.py` instantiates `MCPServer`, adapts the existing
  tool/resource handlers to the MCP 2.x dispatch and resource-helper
  contracts, validates advertised tool schemas, rejects unknown resources
  cleanly, and starts native stdio through `MCPServer.run()`.
- `mvp_site/requirements.txt` removes the emergency `mcp<2.0.0` ceiling and
  requires the supported 2.x range (`>=2.0.0,<3.0.0`).
- `mvp_site/schemas/prompt_tool_contracts.json` records the hash-derived final
  MCP interface contract.

## Test Changes

- `mvp_site/tests/test_mcp_v2_import_smoke.py` covers clean v2 import, the
  public `MCPServer` type, bound dispatch methods, exact enabled/disabled tool
  sets, resource conversion, unknown-resource rejection, valid calls, schema
  rejection, and disabled-tool rejection.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_openclaw_provider_proof_fallback.py` models the MCP 2.x
  low-level helper and exception module tree in its isolated import fixture.

## Known Limitations

- The evidence proves native MCP stdio and the existing handler callstack. It
  does not prove native streaming SSE, streamable HTTP, browser/UI, Cloud Run
  deployment, post-merge production traffic, or BigQuery application writes.
- MCPServer 2.x reports an empty default server version in initialization
  metadata; this is the released SDK default and does not affect protocol
  operation.

## Beads

Beads: `rev-wvoqj`

## Tenets

- Preserve the real-service invariant: behavior proof uses a native MCP 2.0
  client, the real AGY provider, and real Firestore.
- Keep the migration at the transport boundary; existing gameplay handlers
  and HTTP/SSE behavior are not redesigned.
- Fail closed at the SDK boundary for disabled tools, schema-invalid input,
  and unadvertised resources.

## Design Decision

`MCPServer` 2.x is adopted through the smallest compatibility layer around
the existing `handle_list_tools`, `handle_call_tool`,
`handle_list_resources`, and `handle_read_resource` functions. The layer
restores SDK validation and wire conversion without duplicating business
logic.

Governing design artifact: **N/A — bounded emergency dependency migration
following [PR #8657](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8657);
no roadmap or design `.md` changes are required.** Governing bead:
**`rev-wvoqj`**. This PR does not redesign gameplay tools, streaming
endpoints, or dependency-governance automation.

## User Stories

- As an operator, I can install MCP 2.x and start the WorldArchitect MCP
  server within the explicitly supported 2.x range.
- As an MCP client, I can list tools/resources, read every advertised
  resource, and call valid tools through the native 2.x stdio protocol.
- As an MCP client, I receive a clean protocol error for unknown resources,
  unavailable tools, and malformed payloads.

title: [dark-factory] zero-config multi-repo: auto-register repos from intake, persist to registry, no manual [repos.*] config needed (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Problem

The auto-factory currently requires manual `[repos.*]` entries in `config/daemon.toml` to handle any repo other than `target_repo`. This is wrong: it means every new repo needs an operator config change before the factory can work on it. The factory should handle any repo automatically.

## Desired behavior

**Zero-config multi-repo**: when the daemon first encounters a factory-labeled issue or PR from a repo it hasn't seen before, it should:

1. Auto-detect the repo from the item's `repository_url` / owner+name
2. Derive sensible defaults:
   - `push_remote`: query `git remote -v` in a temp clone, or default to `"origin"`
   - `ao_project`: derive from repo name (e.g. `dark-factory` → `"dark-factory"`)
3. Persist the repo entry to a **dynamic repo registry** (SQLite table or JSONL sidecar alongside `daemon-cxdb.sqlite`)
4. Use the persisted entry for all future intake + dispatch for that repo

On subsequent encounters the daemon reads from the registry — no manual config needed.

## Design

### New: `repo_registry` SQLite table (in `daemon-cxdb.sqlite`)
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS repo_registry (
  repo          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,  -- e.g. "jleechanorg/dark-factory"
  ao_project    TEXT NOT NULL,
  push_remote   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'origin',
  first_seen_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  last_seen_at  TEXT NOT NULL
);
```

### Intake flow change (`daemon/src/intake.rs`)
Instead of only scanning `cfg.target_repo`, the intake loop should:
1. Fetch factory-labeled issues across **all repos the authenticated token can see** (or at minimum: `target_repo` + all repos in `repo_registry`)
2. When a new repo is encountered (not in registry), auto-register it with derived defaults
3. Emit a `REPO_AUTO_REGISTERED` telemetry event so operators can see what was learned

### Dispatch flow change (`daemon/src/dispatch.rs`)
When routing a bead, look up the bead's `external_ref` repo in `repo_registry` first, then fall back to `cfg.target_repo` defaults.

### Remove static `[repos.*]` from `config/daemon.toml`
The static block becomes dead config (and should be dropped). The registry takes over. If an operator wants to override defaults for a repo, they can `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO repo_registry` directly.

## Acceptance criteria
- Filing a `factory`-labeled issue in `jleechanorg/dark-factory` (a repo NOT in `config/daemon.toml`) results in:
  - A `REPO_AUTO_REGISTERED` event in `daemon.jsonl` within 2 tick cycles
  - A `BEAD_CREATED` event within 2 more tick cycles
  - A worker dispatched to the correct repo
- `repo_registry` table is queryable: `sqlite3 ~/.dark-factory/daemon-cxdb.sqlite "SELECT * FROM repo_registry;"`
- The static `[repos.*]` block in `config/daemon.toml` is removed
- Existing worldarchitect.ai intake and dispatch are unaffected
- `cargo test --package dark-factory` passes

## Notes
- The GH token scope already covers all repos the user has access to — no new auth needed
- Start with a fixed list approach (target_repo + any repos seen in recent issues) before attempting full org-wide scanning
- This supersedes the narrower fix in worldarchitect.ai #8340 (which can be closed once this lands)

title: [P2] silence ao spawn Mislabeled project block warnings in agent-orchestrator.yaml
description:
**Priority**: P2 | **Type**: cleanup | **Affects**: all ao spawn calls from daemon

## Problem

Every `ao spawn` call emits 3 `[config] Mislabeled project block` warnings to stderr:

```
[config] Mislabeled project block: configKey "smartclaw" has path "/home/jleechan/.smartclaw" whose basename is ".smartclaw". If this is intentional, set an explicit "name: smartclaw" field...
[config] Mislabeled project block: configKey "worldarchitect" has path "/home/jleechan/projects/worldarchitect.ai" whose basename is "worldarchitect.ai"...
[config] Mislabeled project block: configKey "worldai-claw" has path "/home/jleechan/projects/worldai_claw" whose basename is "worldai_claw"...
```

These pollute every daemon dispatch error log (the stderr is captured and stored in CXDB), making real errors harder to spot.

## Fix

Add explicit `name:` fields to the 3 affected project blocks in `agent-orchestrator.yaml` (or wherever AO reads its project config):

```yaml
projects:
  smartclaw:
    name: smartclaw          # add this
    path: /home/jleechan/.smartclaw
  worldarchitect:
    name: worldarchitect     # add this  
    path: /home/jleechan/projects/worldarchitect.ai
  worldai-claw:
    name: worldai-claw       # add this
    path: /home/jleechan/projects/worldai_claw
```

## Acceptance criteria
- `ao spawn --help 2>&1 | grep "Mislabeled"` returns empty
- No `[config] Mislabeled project block` lines in daemon dispatch stderr

## Status Update (2026-07-27, current head `cfea9f2ffb84a7173d78258e5c04ec85f8a49b4f`) — CodeRabbit review-response fixes, findings below still current

Two commits landed after the fresh evidence capture below (both are
review-response / hygiene, not prompt content changes, so the retirement
8/8 and narrative-precedence 0/8 findings remain the current, representative
real-LLM evidence at this head):

1. `9a29c398e0d` — docs-only docstring update to `context_compaction.py`
   responding to an earlier CodeRabbit thread.
2. `cfea9f2ffb8` — fixed 4 real findings from a fresh CodeRabbit re-review
   at `9a29c398e0d`: (a) `_drop_god_mode_directives()` crashed on a
   non-string directive `id` (now guarded, plus a single-pass rebuild) —
   new unit test `mvp_site/tests/test_drop_god_mode_directives_by_id.py`
   pins this (5/5 passing); (b) the test's `retirement_summary` /
   `precedence_summary` result dicts were missing required `errors`/
   `campaign_id` keys; (c) the "retired" outcome conflated
   directives.drop-based retirement with an incidental full-list-overwrite
   side channel, masking a possible regression back to bead `rev-mwht0` —
   now split into distinct outcomes; (d) a narrative-precedence check used
   a substring match on a stringified dict instead of reading
   `state_updates.npc_data` directly.

**AGY provider quota was exhausted** (`Individual quota reached... resets
in ~2h47m`) while these fixes were being made, so they are verified only
via local unit/prompt tests (5/5 new + 75+ existing passing), NOT with
fresh real-LLM samples at this exact head. One CodeRabbit suggestion
(assert real streaming transport in the two real-LLM test classes) was
deferred to bead `rev-34fpd` rather than risk landing an unverified fix
while quota-blocked and while the AGY provider's documented `chunk_count=0`
exception makes a naive assertion unsafe to write blind.

Gist evidence bundle's `metadata.json.git_head` has been bumped to this
exact SHA to keep the Evidence Gate's freshness check accurate.

## Fresh write-boundary evidence at head `610aa10dacd26109076d512e8461213caaa5fd2c` (Lane B rev-5ba8x.1 fix + integration test)

- Test: `mvp_site/tests/test_rev_5ba8x_user_action_pairing.py` (5/5 PASSED in 0.75s)
- Pins: write-boundary pairing invariant at `_persist_turn_to_firestore` /

## Status Update (2026-07-27, historical, superseded by fresh evidence at head 610aa10dacd above) — captured at head `7457c3fb51912425983bee54a8672c5b9397e919`

Real-LLM re-verification (n=8 per scenario, real local server + real
Firestore + real Gemini via the AGY provider, `gemini-3-flash-preview`) at
the exact current head, working tree clean (`working_tree_dirty: false`).
Full evidence (historical, superseded by fresh write-boundary evidence at head 610aa10dacd above): [HEAD_7457c3f_README.md](),  # historical, superseded
[retirement aggregate](),  # historical, superseded
[precedence aggregate]().  # historical, superseded

**Two prompt/backend changes landed since the last capture** (`world_logic.py`
`_drop_god_mode_directives()` now matches by directive ID as well as exact
rule text; `living_world_instruction.md` gained an unconditional "NO
REVERSALS OR HOSTILITY PRETEXTS" mandate with explicit banned-phrase
examples drawn from the prior capture's actual failures).

**Scenario A — GOD MODE retirement: 8/8, and now FIXED via the intended
mechanism** (bead `rev-mwht0` closable). All 8 fresh iterations emit
`directives.drop` containing the directive's **ID**, and the server now
honors that (previously it only matched exact rule text, so retirement only
"worked" before via an incidental full-list overwrite). `after_rules: []` in
all 8 confirms a genuine removal.

**Scenario B — Narrative precedence: 0/8, STILL FAILING** (bead `rev-y74z8`,
P0, remains OPEN). The structured field `npc_data.attitude_to_party` stayed
`"allied"` in all 8 (a narrow metric that looks like a pass), but the actual
served narrative text reversed the reconciled NPC to hostile in all 8
samples — 3 of 8 using the near-verbatim banned phrase "our alliance/truce
was a farce" that the new prompt mandate explicitly lists as forbidden, and
one sample echoing the seeded stale directive's exact wording ("sworn
enemy") as the NPC's stated motivation. Three consecutive rounds of
prompt-only strengthening in this PR's owned files have not moved this
number. Root cause, as best determined without editing the out-of-scope
`agent_prompts.py`: the god-mode-directives block is injected on the
**uncached, dynamic** instructions channel close to generation with its own
"MUST be followed" imperative (`agent_prompts.py::build_god_mode_directives_block()`,
relocated via `_assemble_relocated_blocks()` in `llm_service.py`), while the
countermanding precedence rule lives in the large **static cached prefix**
(`living_world_instruction.md`). This PR's scope deliberately excludes
`agent_prompts.py` (sibling PR #8619 owns overlapping lines there to avoid a
rewrite collision). Closing this defect for real needs either (a) moving the
countermanding rule onto the same dynamic/uncached channel as the directives
block so both compete at equal salience, or (b) a registered backend
`AdjustmentSpec` (per this repo's ZFC-adjuster policy) that strips
already-superseded directive text from the block before it is served. Both
are follow-up work outside this PR's file boundary — **do not merge on the
belief that this PR fixes narrative-turn precedence; it does not, as measured
at its own current head.**

> [!WARNING]
> ### Known Limitation (Real-LLM Finding, NOT Resolved — narrative precedence still fails)
> Three independent real-LLM statistics exist for this PR, captured across
> three heads. Report the numbers as-is; do not average or round up.
>
> **1. Original head `e61ff3dec9e` (n=4, PR author's own capture):** GOD-MODE
> RETIREMENT 0/4 correct, 3/4 actively reversed canonical state to match the
> stale directive. Baseline against bare `origin/main` was comparable (1/4,
> 2/4, 1/4 skip).
>
> **2. Head `0b33b97c5566` (n=8 per scenario, clean tree, 2026-07-26), WITH an
> `agent_prompts.py` sentence fix later reverted (see the cross-PR note
> below):** GOD-MODE RETIREMENT 8/8. NARRATIVE PRECEDENCE 0/8 correct.
>
> **3. Head `9c4a5cdb8358` (n=8 per scenario, clean tree, 2026-07-26), WITHOUT
> that `agent_prompts.py` fix — this PR's actual current content:** GOD-MODE
> RETIREMENT 8/8 (IDENTICAL to capture 2). NARRATIVE PRECEDENCE 0/8 correct
> (IDENTICAL to capture 2).
>
> **Findings, taken together:**
> - **GOD-MODE RETIREMENT is 8/8 in both capture 2 and capture 3** — but 8/8
>   of those samples emitted `directives.drop` containing the directive's
>   **id** (e.g. `"directive_stale_hostile"`), never the exact rule text
>   `god_mode_instruction.md` instructs. `_drop_god_mode_directives()` matches
>   only by rule text, so the id-based drop request had **zero effect** via
>   the intended mechanism in all 16 samples across both captures —
>   retirement only "worked" because every response also emitted an
>   incidental `state_updates.custom_campaign_state.god_mode_directives: []`
>   full-list overwrite. This is a fragile side channel, not the fix working
>   as designed (bead `rev-mwht0`, P1).
> - **NARRATIVE PRECEDENCE (normal story/dialog turns) is 0/8 correct in both
>   capture 2 and capture 3 — 0/16 total across both.** The structured
>   `npc_data.attitude_to_party` field stayed `"allied"` in all 16 (looks like
>   a pass on a narrow metric), but the actual served **narrative text**
>   reversed the NPC to a hostile enemy ordering guards to arrest/seize/kill
>   the player in all 16 — some explicitly naming the reconciliation ceremony
>   in the prose and then declaring the alliance "dead," "evaporated," or "a
>   sham." This is the exact Visenya-v9/Tybolt incident class of bug this PR
>   exists to fix, reproduced with a real LLM at this PR's own head, and it
>   does not change whether the `agent_prompts.py` sentence is fixed or not
>   (bead `rev-y74z8`, P0).
>
> **Conclusion: this PR's core claim — that narrative turns now respect
> canonical state over a stale directive — is not supported by real-LLM
> evidence at its own head, and the identical result with/without the
> `agent_prompts.py` fix rules that sentence out as the cause.** Retirement
> "works" but through an unintended mechanism; precedence, the
> narrative-facing half of the fix and the actual subject of the incident,
> remains unfixed regardless of that unrelated sentence. Do not merge on the
> strength of the structured-field statistics alone — see the full narrative
> transcripts in `## Real LLM Evidence — 2026-07-26 re-verification` below.


## Cross-PR note: agent_prompts.py is NOT touched by this PR (disclosed)
An earlier revision of this fix cycle also patched a self-contradicting
sentence in `mvp_site/agent_prompts.py:build_god_mode_directives_block()`
("In case of conflicts, earlier rules take precedence (newest first):" —
backwards relative to the list's own newest-first sort). That change has
been **reverted** from this PR: sibling PR #8619
(`fix/tybolt-directive-precedence-rev-h5q7y`, bead `rev-h5q7y`) already owns
this exact defect with its own wording, a passing unit test, and an
in-progress real-LLM A/B — the two branches' independent rewrites of the
same two sentences collide (`git merge-tree` confirmed a real content
conflict). This PR's scope is `god_mode_instruction.md`,
`living_world_instruction.md`, and `context_compaction.py` only.

**Evidence bonus from testing both states:** re-running this PR's own n=8x2
real-LLM contract test WITH and WITHOUT that `agent_prompts.py` fix produced
IDENTICAL results in both conditions (retirement 8/8 both ways, narrative
precedence 0/8 correct both ways) — see
`## Real LLM Evidence — 2026-07-26 re-verification` below. That sentence is
not the cause of either result; PR #8619 fixing it will not, by itself, fix
narrative-turn precedence.


## Unrelated CI Fix (disclosed)
**What it is:** This branch also carries an unrelated, pre-existing bug fix to `mvp_site/context_compaction.py`. The bug already exists on bare `origin/main`, is not caused by anything in this PR's god-mode-directive-precedence feature area, and is included solely to unblock the required `Directory tests (core-mvp-1)` check.

**Reproduction:** `mvp_site/tests/test_compression_lever1.py::test_level_up_compaction_preserves_game_state_and_modal_contract_at_crossover` fails on a fresh checkout of bare `origin/main`. Reproduced directly in a clean worktree: `./vpython -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_compression_lever1.py -v` → `1 failed, 13 passed`, with the assertion failing because the compacted system instruction still contains the literal string `[...SYSTEM INSTRUCTION TRUNCATED` (a mid-file byte-slice tore `master_directive.md` in half).

**Identical-fix proof:** The patched `mvp_site/context_compaction.py` blob is byte-identical (git blob hash `249631c9b55129918cabcf5dbf554afc87994193`) across all three PRs carrying this fix — this PR, [#8603](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8603), and [#8612](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8612). Any reviewer can confirm with one command per branch: `git rev-parse origin/<branch>:mvp_site/context_compaction.py` for `fix/god-mode-directive-precedence-pr-b`, `fix/npc-roster-visibility`, and `fix/npc-agreement-propagation-and-input-honesty`. This is one fix copied three times, not three divergent fixes.

**Behavior change:** `_compact_system_instruction()`'s Phase-1 emergency fallback (`SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION_EMERGENCY_COMPACT_CRITICAL_OVERFLOW`) used to byte-slice the entire `system_instruction` string whenever critical-only content marginally exceeded `max_chars`, which could tear a load-bearing file's content in half mid-sentence. It now drops non-critical segments first and returns the critical content in full even if that still exceeds `max_chars` — trading a larger, over-budget prompt in the rare emergency-overflow case for a guarantee that critical policy content is never corrupted or truncated.

**Merge-order dependency:** The fix is deliberately duplicated identically across all three PRs because none of them can rebase onto an unmerged main-branch fix, and each independently needed the required check unblocked. Duplication is safe here (identical content 3-way-merges/rebases cleanly regardless of merge order), but it becomes redundant in the other two PRs once any one of the three merges. Bead `rev-bebzd` tracks extracting this fix into its own PR against `main` so future branches inherit it by rebase instead of by copy.

Full root-cause writeup: bead `rev-fpdgf`.

## Summary

- **rev-gpmrt (root cause):** `mvp_site/prompts/living_world_instruction.md` now carries a "DIRECTIVE VS. CANONICAL STATE PRECEDENCE" rule: a god-mode directive's "MUST be followed" imperative language does not let it outrank a *later* contradicting fact in `npc_data`, `entity_tracking`, or `core_memories`. This is the file loaded by `StoryModeAgent`, `DialogAgent`, and `CombatAgent` — the agents actually generating narrative on ordinary turns.
- **rev-pirim (directive retirement):** `mvp_site/prompts/god_mode_instruction.md`'s existing "Transitional State Hygiene" checklist gains a bullet generalizing directive retirement beyond death to ANY superseding canonical event (alliance, agreement, surrender, reconciliation, departure), with a worked example mirroring the Tybolt incident shape.
- **rev-4pto9 (same-subject supersede):** Both files now state that when two directives target the same subject, the later one governs — `living_world_instruction.md` for narrative-time interpretation, `god_mode_instruction.md` for actually retiring the superseded one via `directives.drop` when a new conflicting directive is added.
- New contract test `mvp_site/tests/test_god_mode_directive_precedence_served_prompt.py` builds the real SERVED system prompt through `StoryModeAgent`, `DialogAgent`, and `GodModeAgent` (not raw file reads) and pins all three rules' presence.

## Background: the incident and why this is prompt-only

Campaign "Visenya v9 (forgot tybolt)": the player allied with an NPC noble (Persuasion 20 vs DC 20, 2100 XP). Three standing god-mode directives (two set ~4h before the alliance, one 6 minutes after but independently causal) kept the model writing the NPC as an enemy. The alliance WAS recorded correctly and in full in `core_memories` — this was never a truncation/delivery problem, it was pure authority asymmetry: directives are injected with "MUST be followed," core memories are passive facts with no priority marker, so a stale imperative always won.

Investigation traced the actual code gate: `world_logic.py:apply_god_mode_directives()` returns a no-op unless `is_god_mode` is true, so `directives.add`/`directives.drop` are **only ever applied when the response comes from `GodModeAgent`** — a normal story turn cannot mechanically retire a directive no matter what the prompt says. That fixed the file split:
- Narrative-time precedence (what to believe when directive and canonical state disagree) → `living_world_instruction.md`, because that's what's actually in context on the turn that mis-portrayed the NPC.
- Lifecycle/retirement (removing a directive from the persisted list) → `god_mode_instruction.md`, because only a `GodModeAgent` response can make `directives.drop` take effect.

This is zero Python, per ZFC and the task's prompt-only mandate: the model owns the precedence judgment; nothing here is a backend scorer, keyword matcher, or regex over narrative text.

## Goals

- Stop a stale directive from silently overriding a newer canonical fact during ordinary narrative turns.
- Give the god-mode agent a real, mechanically-applied way to retire directives once they're superseded, generalized beyond the single "on death" trigger case.
- Prevent the same defeat pattern from recurring against a sibling PR's planned `disposition` field (see Known Limitations).

## Tenets

Governing beads (verified against the canonical bead DB, not a
worktree-forked copy — see `## Real LLM Evidence — 2026-07-26
re-verification` below for the provenance note): root cause `rev-gpmrt`,
retirement generalization `rev-pirim`, same-subject supersede `rev-4pto9`,
overall PR tracking `rev-cobzx`. Known-open follow-ups filed from real-LLM
evidence gathered during this fix cycle: `rev-mwht0` (directives.drop
id-vs-rule-text bug, P1), `rev-y74z8` (narrative precedence not fixed, P0).

- Prompt-only: the model decides precedence; no backend precedence engine, scoring, or regex.
- Setting-agnostic: illustrative NPC name ("Lord Corvin Ashvale") is invented, not the real campaign's name, consistent with the file's existing worked-example style (Duke Ravengard, Prince Caius, Aethelgard Vanguard).
- Honesty: rules only instruct behavior the backend can actually execute (`directives.drop` only works under `is_god_mode`), so retirement guidance lives only where it is mechanically real.

## High-level description

Two sections added to `mvp_site/prompts/living_world_instruction.md` (after the existing "LIVING WORLD VISIBILITY CONTRACT" section, before "Core Mandate"):
1. `## 🚨 DIRECTIVE VS. CANONICAL STATE PRECEDENCE (UNCONDITIONAL)` — precedence + same-subject-directive rule for narrative turns.

Two additions to `mvp_site/prompts/god_mode_instruction.md`:
1. A new bullet in the existing "Transitional State Hygiene (MANDATORY)" → "Common stale states to fix" list: generalized directive retirement, with a worked example.
2. A new "Same-Subject Directive Supersede (MANDATORY)" paragraph in the existing "Directives Field" section: retire the old directive via `directives.drop` when adding a new one on the same subject.

## Testing

`mvp_site/tests/test_god_mode_directive_precedence_served_prompt.py` (new file, 10 tests) builds the real served system prompt via `StoryModeAgent().build_system_instructions()`, `DialogAgent().build_system_instructions()`, and `GodModeAgent().build_system_instructions()` (cache-cleared, unmocked `_load_instruction_file`, mirroring the existing `test_agents.py::test_god_mode_prompt_requires_string_only_lineage_objects` pattern) and asserts the served text contains the precedence header, all three canonical-state field classes, the "newer fact wins" directional rule, the memory-index citation ban, the same-subject rule, the generalized-retirement bullet with all five superseding-event terms, and the same-subject supersede rule — in both agents that must carry each half of the contract.

## Low-level details

- `mvp_site/prompts/god_mode_instruction.md`: `PROMPT_TYPE_GOD_MODE` is REQUIRED only for `GodModeAgent` (`mvp_site/agents.py:1086`) — the only agent whose `directives` field mutations the server applies (`world_logic.py:apply_god_mode_directives`, gated `if not is_god_mode: return`).
- `mvp_site/prompts/living_world_instruction.md`: `PROMPT_TYPE_LIVING_WORLD` is REQUIRED for `StoryModeAgent` (`agents.py:817`), `DialogAgent` (`agents.py:2575`), and others — confirmed via `_assemble_relocated_blocks()` in `llm_service.py:6349` that `build_god_mode_directives_block()` (the "Active God Mode Directives" MUST-be-followed block) is injected agent-agnostically, so every agent that reads it needs the precedence rule to correctly interpret it.
- `mvp_site/schemas/prompt_tool_contracts.json` does not register either file — no contract-JSON update needed; `./vpython scripts/validate_prompt_tool_contracts.py` passes unchanged.
- Directive ordering used for "same-subject, later governs" relies on `custom_campaign_state.god_mode_directives[]` entries carrying an `added` timestamp (written in `game_state_mixins.py:add_god_mode_directive`) and the served numbering coming from `PromptBuilder.build_god_mode_directives_block()` (`mvp_site/agent_prompts.py:2310`, the function actually wired into the served prompt — `game_state_mixins.py`'s own `get_god_mode_directives_block()` has zero call sites and is dead code). That function sorts `directives` by `added` descending (`reverse=True`) and enumerates from 1, so **directive #1 is always the most-recently-added directive and a higher number is always older** — matching the block's own served header text ("Newest First" / "earlier rules take precedence (newest first)"). "Same-subject directives: ... the directive with the LOWER number ... governs" is therefore the correct direction (fixed post-review; the original text in this PR inverted it).

## Production Code Changes

- `mvp_site/prompts/god_mode_instruction.md` — before: "Transitional State Hygiene" listed 5 stale-state categories (combat, encounter, mode indicators, living-world events) with no directive-lifecycle category; "Directives Field" documented `add`/`drop` semantics but no same-subject conflict rule. Now: adds a 6th stale-state bullet ("Directives contradicted by canonical state") generalizing retirement to 5 superseding-event classes, and a "Same-Subject Directive Supersede (MANDATORY)" paragraph. Why: only `GodModeAgent` responses actually reach `world_logic.py:apply_god_mode_directives()` with `is_god_mode=True`, so this is the one file where a retirement instruction is mechanically real.
- `mvp_site/prompts/living_world_instruction.md` — before: no rule governing how to weigh an active god-mode directive against contradicting canonical state; the "MUST be followed" directive block had no counter-signal. Now: adds "DIRECTIVE VS. CANONICAL STATE PRECEDENCE (UNCONDITIONAL)" naming `npc_data`/`entity_tracking`/`core_memories` as classes of canonical state that can supersede a directive, plus a same-subject-directive interpretation rule. Why: this file is REQUIRED for `StoryModeAgent`/`DialogAgent`/`CombatAgent` — the agents that actually narrate on ordinary turns and were the site of the production defeat.
- No production Python changed (0 files under `mvp_site/*.py` outside `mvp_site/tests/` touched) — confirmed via `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`.

## Test Changes

- `mvp_site/tests/test_god_mode_directive_precedence_served_prompt.py` (11 tests, 0 pre-existing tests modified). Builds the real served system prompt through `StoryModeAgent`, `DialogAgent`, and `GodModeAgent` (`build_system_instructions()`, cache cleared, `_load_instruction_file` unmocked) and asserts presence of: the precedence header, all three canonical-state field-class names, the "newer fact wins" rule, the memory-index citation ban, the same-subject rule (living-world side), the generalized retirement bullet with all five superseding-event terms, the `directives.drop` retirement instruction, the hygiene-checklist wiring, and the same-subject supersede rule (god-mode side). A follow-up commit added `DirectiveNumberingDirectionTests` (11th test), which calls the real `PromptBuilder.build_god_mode_directives_block()` with three directives at distinct timestamps and asserts the built block numbers them newest-first (directive `#1` = most recently added, highest number = oldest) — pinning the same sort/enumerate behavior the corrected same-subject-directive prose now describes correctly.

## Known Limitations

- **No real end-to-end LLM transcript captured** — see `## Real LLM Evidence` below for the disclosed reason (AGY account quota exhaustion) and what evidence IS provided instead.
- **Sibling-PR file collision (disclosed, not resolved here):** the repo's `merge_train` pre-tool-use guard flagged that `living_world_instruction.md` is also touched whole-file by open PRs [#8562](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8562) and [#8559](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8559), and `god_mode_instruction.md` by open PRs [#8594](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8594), [#8583](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8583), [#8567](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8567), [#8541](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8541). Per repo policy this is routine — resolve via rebase at merge time, not a blocker now.
- **No existing "on death" directive-retirement rule was found** in either editable file to "generalize" from, despite that framing in the source bead (rev-pirim). A repo-wide grep for retirement/expire/supersede language tied to directives found nothing in `mvp_site/prompts/*.md`. This PR writes the generalized rule directly (five superseding-event classes, death included) rather than editing a prior death-only version that doesn't exist in the two files this PR is scoped to.
- **`disposition` field mention is forward-looking:** the coordinator's refinement named a blocked sibling PR that will add `disposition` as a first-class ACTIVE-tier `entity_tracking` field. This PR's precedence rule already names `entity_tracking` generically (not just `core_memories`) so that field inherits the fix once it lands, but it does not implement or depend on that field existing yet.
- One unrelated pre-existing test failure observed during the local sweep, confirmed NOT caused by this change (`git diff --stat` shows only the 2 prompt files + 1 new test file touched): `mvp_site/tests/test_prompts.py::test_level_up_agent_contract_resets_stale_completion_markers` fails against `master_directive.md` / `LevelUpAgent`, a file and agent this PR never touches.
- **GOD MODE directive-retirement real-LLM capture is a disclosed NEGATIVE/inconclusive result (4/4 attempts):** see the "GOD MODE Directive Retirement" addendum under `## Real LLM Evidence`. A real `GodModeAgent` turn did not emit `directives.drop` for a stale directive contradicted by seeded `entity_tracking`/`core_memories` state in any of 4 independent real AGY captures — in 3/4 the model actively reinforced the stale directive by overwriting canonical state to match it. The capture cannot confirm whether the corrected bullet text itself reached the model (AGY-mode capture only records a ~16.5K-char preview of the full ~353K-char system instruction), so this does not conclusively disprove the fix, but it is not a demonstrated positive result either.

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

title: Add mandatory GitHub-actions skeptic PASS gate for dark-factory PRs
description:
## Background

Dark Factory's mandatory 7-green policy requires a skeptic result posted by `github-actions[bot]` with `VERDICT: PASS` at the exact PR head SHA. The repository currently has no skeptic workflow under `.github/workflows/`; recent PR comments contain no such bot verdict. PR #255 is otherwise green but cannot satisfy gate 7.

## Goal

Add a fail-closed GitHub Actions skeptic gate that independently reviews the current PR head and posts a SHA-bound `VERDICT: PASS` or `VERDICT: FAIL` comment as `github-actions[bot]`.

## Requirements

- Private-repo jobs must use the configured self-hosted runner selector.
- Trigger on relevant PR updates and support manual `workflow_dispatch` recovery.
- Bind the verdict to repository, PR number, and exact head SHA.
- Use an independent reviewer from the implementing model; fail closed when no reviewer is available or output is unparseable.
- Update or replace the prior bot comment idempotently; stale-SHA PASS must never satisfy a newer head.
- Expose a required check suitable for merge protection.
- Add tests for PASS, FAIL, stale SHA, missing reviewer, malformed output, and duplicate reruns.
- Follow ZFC: the model judges the diff; deterministic code only validates the structured verdict and SHA binding.

## Acceptance

- A real test PR receives a `github-actions[bot]` comment containing `VERDICT: PASS` and the exact head SHA.
- A forced negative case produces `VERDICT: FAIL` and blocks merge.
- PR #255 can rerun the gate and satisfy the repository's seventh green condition without operator-authored verdicts.
