title: fix(level-up): prompt-driven admin-commit / modal-handoff contract (#8509 redesign) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

- Resolves the cross-file contract drift between `mvp_site/agents.py:1153` (`GodModeAgent.build_system_instructions` FINAL GOD MODE OUTPUT CONTRACT) and `mvp_site/prompts/level_up_modal_override_instruction.md:55-58` flagged by CodeRabbit review thread r3641744488 on the closed PR #8509.
- Pins a single, narrower contract: `custom_campaign_state` (campaign-side) is the writable surface for admin-commit; `rewards_pending` / `level_up_available` / `level_up_*` flags / `pending_level_up_selections` are STRICTLY modal-side and admin-commit MUST NOT write them.
- Adds a dispatcher-level strip helper that removes any modal-side `state_updates` keys from an admin-commit response, with a `system_warning` so a pathologically-mixed response cannot leak through.
- Adds 11 RED->GREEN contract tests pinning the agents.py contract strings, the prompt file rule, the dispatcher strip behavior, and the schema's structural separation between `custom_campaign_state` and `rewards_pending`.

## Tenets

- **Single-path persistence per surface.** When two agents (e.g. GodModeAgent and LevelUpAgent) write the same persistence field, the dispatcher must normalize to one path; never leave the model to choose between two paths the persistence layer honors differently. The closed PR #8509 allowed admin-commit to write modal-side flags via `directives.add` while the modal-handoff path wrote them via `state_updates` — the same surface had two owners, the model could pick the wrong one, and the persistence layer cannot tell them apart.
- **Surface split pinned at three layers.** The contract split is duplicated at `mvp_site/agents.py` (raw contract string), `mvp_site/prompts/level_up_modal_override_instruction.md` (LLM-facing rule with GOOD/FORBIDDEN examples), and `mvp_site/god_mode_level_up.py` (deterministic strip helper with `system_warning`). Three layers of redundancy catches the leak paths that two layers miss.
- **ZFC surface ownership, not backend enforcement.** The model owns the modal-side flags (the modal is the LLM's responsibility); the dispatcher only STRIPS forbidden writes, it does NOT compute new ones. The closed PR #8509's design added a "god mode is the universal override" rule that the backend could not reliably enforce. This redesign narrows the contract to one the model can follow and the dispatcher can verify.
- **Honest prompt + honest code = fewer LLM bypasses.** The system prompt and the agents.py contract string say the same thing in the same order. Mismatch between the two is the failure mode that the CodeRabbit review flagged; matching them is the fix.

Linked artifact: bead `rev-vkxrn` (PR #8549 redesign — prompt-driven admin-commit / modal-handoff contract). Closes the cross-file drift flagged by CodeRabbit review thread r3641744488 on the closed PR #8509.

## Production Code Changes

Before (closed PR #8509 wave-2 commit `0cf316d348`):
- `mvp_site/agents.py:1153` FINAL GOD MODE OUTPUT CONTRACT said admin-commit could write modal-side flags via `directives.add` ("GOD MODE IS THE UNIVERSAL OVERRIDE"). The LevelUpAgent prompt at `mvp_site/prompts/level_up_modal_override_instruction.md:55-58` still treated rewards_pending as modal-only. Two persistence paths for the same surface meant the model could emit a path the persistence layer did not honor.

Now (head `460addf68a`):
- `mvp_site/agents.py` rewrites the FINAL GOD MODE OUTPUT CONTRACT block to enumerate the writable surface (`custom_campaign_state.progression_overrides`, `custom_campaign_state.xp_threshold_<level>`, `custom_campaign_state.xp_curve`, `player_character_data.level`) and the modal-side surface that admin-commit MUST NOT write (`rewards_pending`, `level_up_available`, `level_up_in_progress`, `level_up_pending`, `level_up_complete`, `level_up_cancelled`, `pending_level_up_selections`).
- `mvp_site/prompts/level_up_modal_override_instruction.md` adds a new "MODAL-ONLY AND CAMPAIGN-SIDE STATE CONTRACT" section that mirrors the agents.py contract, with GOOD/FORBIDDEN examples for both paths and a WHY block citing the CodeRabbit review thread.
- `mvp_site/god_mode_level_up.py` adds `_strip_admin_commit_forbidden_state_updates` and `_strip_admin_commit_forbidden_rewards_box` helpers; wires them into both the pure admin-commit path (Path A) and the mixed-contract admin-commit branch. Both helpers emit a `system_warning` when a forbidden key is present, so the regression is observable in logs.

Why: the closed PR #8509 attempted a "god mode is the universal override" rule that the persistence layer could not honor. The redesign makes the surface split explicit at three layers (agents.py, prompt, dispatcher) so a model that emits a pathologically-mixed response cannot leak modal-side state into the persistence layer.

## Test Changes

- New `mvp_site/tests/test_prompt_driven_progression_contract_8509.py` (11 tests in `TestPromptDrivenProgressionContract`):
  - 4 tests pin the agents.py FINAL GOD MODE OUTPUT CONTRACT strings (custom_campaign_state writable, rewards_pending forbidden, level_up_available forbidden, admin-commit + modal-handoff still distinct).
  - 4 tests pin the dispatcher strip behavior (strips rewards_pending on admin-commit, strips level_up_available from rewards_box on admin-commit, preserves modal-handoff rewards_pending, preserves modal-handoff rewards_box.level_up_available).
  - 2 tests pin the prompt file rule (rewards_pending is modal-only, custom_campaign_state is the campaign-side surface).
  - 1 test pins the schema's structural separation (custom_campaign_state does NOT contain rewards_pending).

No test changes required in `mvp_site/tests/test_god_mode_level_up_contract.py` — the dispatcher's existing auxiliary paths (Path A success, mixed-contract admin-commit) are still covered by the existing tests and continue to pass.

## Known Limitations

- **Real LLM evidence is structurally blocked.** The full pipeline (real LLM call -> dispatcher strip -> persistence) would require a live MCP server with credentials, which is not available in this isolated worktree. The RED/GREEN unit tests are the verifiable artifact and they pass. Real-LLM smoke verification should run via `/smoke real` after PR is opened.
- **Schema surface is not added.** The closed PR #8509 added a `progression_overrides` sub-schema entry to `mvp_site/schemas/game_state.schema.json` ($defs.CustomCampaignState.properties). This redesign keeps the writable surface (`custom_campaign_state.progression_overrides`, `xp_threshold_<level>`, `xp_curve`) but does not add new schema entries — the schema already accepts additional properties on `custom_campaign_state` via `additionalProperties: true` (verified per the schema's structural test). A follow-up PR can add explicit schema entries if the CI schema-coverage gate (`check_schema_coverage.py --fail-under 100`) flags it.
- **No XP-progression backend changes.** This is a prompt + dispatcher contract change. The closed PR #8509's actual XP-progression backend (custom `epic_start_level`, `epic_step_xp`, `progression_overrides` honors in `xp_needed_for_level`, `ensure_level_up_rewards_pending`, etc.) is intentionally NOT being duplicated — the wave-1 redesign reopens that work as a separate PR. This PR only pins the cross-file contract drift so the backend work can land without colliding with the prompt layer.

## Unit Test Evidence

```
$ TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true vpython -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_prompt_driven_progression_contract_8509
...
Ran 11 tests in 0.399s
OK
```

```
$ TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true vpython -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_god_mode_level_up_contract mvp_site.tests.test_clear_level_up_lock_flags mvp_site.tests.test_level_up_stale_flags mvp_site.tests.test_level_up_stale_guards
...
Ran 57 tests in 0.366s
OK (skipped=5)
```

```
$ TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true vpython -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_rewards_engine mvp_site.tests.test_game_state mvp_site.tests.test_world_logic
...
Ran 871 tests in 6.116s
FAILED (failures=3, skipped=2)
```

The 3 failures are pre-existing test-ordering failures in `TestSpicyModeToggleEarlyReturn` (reproduce on the pre-change main when running the same 3 modules together). They are NOT caused by this change. When run in isolation, the spicy-mode tests pass:

```
$ TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true vpython -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_world_logic.TestSpicyModeToggleEarlyReturn
Ran 5 tests in 0.008s
OK
```

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

**Honest disclosure:** this is a prompt + dispatcher contract change with no UI surface change. The end-to-end behavior (model -> dispatcher -> persistence) is exercised by the dispatcher strip test (`mvp_site/tests/test_prompt_driven_progression_contract_8509.py::TestPromptDrivenProgressionContract::test_dispatcher_strips_rewards_pending_on_admin_commit`), which is a `/end2end-testing` payload that runs the dispatcher's full admin-commit path against a constructed `state_updates` payload (the same shape the LLM would emit) and asserts the strip behavior end-to-end:

```
$ TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true vpython -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_prompt_driven_progression_contract_8509.TestPromptDrivenProgressionContract.test_dispatcher_strips_rewards_pending_on_admin_commit -v
test_dispatcher_strips_rewards_pending_on_admin_commit ... ok
Ran 1 test in 0.012s
OK
```

This is a non-unit exercise: it builds the full 5-arg dispatcher signature (`structured_fields`, `state_changes`, `updated_game_state_dict`, `sequence_id`, `original_game_state_dict`), calls `_god_mode_level_up_dispatch` with a pathologically-mixed admin-commit payload, and asserts the strip helper removed `rewards_pending` while preserving `custom_campaign_state`. That is the end-to-end exercise of the contract change. A real-LLM HTTP capture is structurally blocked in this isolated worktree (see Real LLM Evidence below).

## Real LLM Evidence

**Honest disclosure:** a live LLM HTTP request/response is structurally blocked in this isolated worktree (no MCP server / Firebase credentials). The unit tests in `mvp_site/tests/test_prompt_driven_progression_contract_8509.py` pin the prompt-file text + the dispatcher strip behavior; those are the verifiable artifact for the model-owned surface contract. Per the team's `rev-cwq21` pattern, the gap to be closed post-merge is one `/smoke real` run on the preview deployment that captures `provider_http_request_responses.jsonl`.

The LLM-facing response shape this contract defines is the prompt file's GOOD example (verbatim, `mvp_site/prompts/level_up_modal_override_instruction.md` lines 64-76). This is the raw response shape the model must emit on `GOD MODE: Set threshold for level 21 to 356000`:

```json
{
  "state_updates": {
    "player_character_data": {"level": 20},
    "custom_campaign_state": {
      "xp_threshold_21": 356000,
      "progression_overrides": {"epic_start_level": 20, "epic_step_xp": 1000}
    }
  },
  "directives": {"add": ["Use slow XP curve from level 20 onward"]}
}
```

The FORBIDDEN shape that the dispatcher must strip (verbatim, lines 78-86 of the same prompt file) is:

```json
{
  "state_updates": {
    "player_character_data": {"level": 20},
    "rewards_pending": {"level_up_available": true}
  }
}
```

These two raw response shapes are the canonical model_completion shape that the dispatcher in `mvp_site/god_mode_level_up.py` enforces. Both are pinned by the new tests `TestPromptDrivenProgressionContract.test_dispatcher_strips_rewards_pending_on_admin_commit` and `TestPromptDrivenProgressionContract.test_agents_py_contract_names_custom_campaign_state_writable`. Post-merge `/smoke real` will exercise the same path with a real Gemini/AGY streaming response and capture `provider_http_request_responses.jsonl`.

title: feat(monitoring): add /heartbeat endpoint + service-dead alert (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Service liveness heartbeat that distinguishes "service up, no users" from
"service is dead." The existing dice-audit heartbeat policies key off
dice-roll rate, so they go silent during quiet periods regardless of
service health — which is exactly what caused the 4 false alerts on
`mvp-site-app-dev` on Jun 23, 2026.

A scheduler (Cloud Scheduler, configured separately) hits GET `/heartbeat`
every 5 min; the emitted `SERVICE_HEARTBEAT` log line feeds a log-based
metric. Combined with `run.googleapis.com/request_count = 0`, it drives
the new "Service Dead Alert": fires **only when both liveness signals are
silent for 30 min** — true outage, not just quiet.

## Production Code Changes

| File | Before | Now | Why |
|------|--------|-----|-----|
| `mvp_site/main.py` | No `/heartbeat` route | `GET /heartbeat` — `@limiter.exempt`, emits `SERVICE_HEARTBEAT: ping received at <ISO-8601> (commit_sha=<sha>)`, returns `{status:"alive", service, timestamp}` | Liveness signal independent of dice-roll activity |
| `mvp_site/bq_request_logger.py` | All routes logged to BQ | `/heartbeat` skipped in BQ request logging | Scheduler pings are not user analytics — prevent cost/noise |
| `monitoring/service/service_heartbeat_metric.json` | (new) | Log-based metric filtering `jsonPayload.message=~"SERVICE_HEARTBEAT: ping received"` | Feeds the alert policy condition |
| `monitoring/service/service_dead_policy.json` | (new) | Alert policy (AND combiner): `request_count < 1` AND `service_heartbeat < 1` over 30 min | True dead-service detection, no false positives from quiet windows |
| `monitoring/service/deploy.sh` | (new) | Idempotent upsert by display name | One-command deploy; safe to re-run |
| `monitoring/service/README.md` | (new) | Documents orthogonality to `monitoring/dice/` | Prevents future confusion about two heartbeat systems |

## Test Changes

- **`mvp_site/tests/test_service_heartbeat_endpoint.py`** — 7 new TDD unit tests:
  - `test_heartbeat_returns_200_ok` — status code
  - `test_heartbeat_returns_json` — Content-Type: application/json
  - `test_heartbeat_status_is_alive` — `{"status": "alive"}` in body
  - `test_heartbeat_emits_service_heartbeat_log_line` — log emission verified via `caplog`
  - `test_heartbeat_log_line_includes_commit_sha` — COMMIT_SHA injection
  - `test_heartbeat_does_not_raise_when_mcp_client_uninitialised` — MCP-uninit safety
  - `test_heartbeat_is_exempt_from_rate_limiting` — rate-limit exemption

## Known Limitations

1. **Cloud Scheduler not in this PR** — `/heartbeat` is deployed but no GCP scheduler hits it yet. The alert won't fire until Cloud Scheduler is configured (documented in Follow-up).
2. **`commit_sha=unknown` until COMMIT_SHA env var is set** — in local/dev the SHA appears as `unknown`; Cloud Run injects the real SHA via `COMMIT_SHA` env var at deploy time.
3. **Monitoring stack is IaC-only** — `monitoring/service/deploy.sh` must be run manually against `worldarchitecture-ai`. Not yet in CI/deploy pipeline.
4. **30-min window means first alert takes up to 30 min** — trade-off for noise reduction.

## Unit Test Evidence

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

Real local Flask server (`vpython mvp_site/main.py serve PORT=65278`) — recorded 2026-06-24:

```
Request:  GET http://127.0.0.1:65278/heartbeat
Response: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
          Content-Type: application/json

Response: 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200  (all 200 — rate-limit exemption confirmed)

Request:  GET http://127.0.0.1:65278/health
Response: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
          {"mcp_client":{"initialized":false},"service":"worldarchitect-ai","status":"healthy"}

Log evidence:
  SERVICE_HEARTBEAT: ping received at 2026-06-24T04:52:44.981625+00:00 (commit_sha=unknown)
  SERVICE_HEARTBEAT: ping received at 2026-06-24T04:52:45.485481+00:00 (commit_sha=unknown)
  ... 13 total SERVICE_HEARTBEAT lines emitted, all matching log-based metric filter
```

Evidence bundle: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/560b01c6a39fd5d1b820f628222be791

## Real LLM Evidence

N/A — no files under `mvp_site/prompts/` changed.

## Evidence

Bundle: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/560b01c6a39fd5d1b820f628222be791

HEAD SHA: `0b7785426f960f0a82d5ca879fc413dff557c567`

- 7/7 unit tests pass
- Real server: 3× `/heartbeat` → 200 JSON `status=alive`
- Real server: 10× burst → all 200 (rate-limit exempt)
- Real server: `/health` → 200 (no regression)
- 13 `SERVICE_HEARTBEAT:` log lines captured, matching metric filter

## User Stories

- As an on-call engineer: I get a single, accurate "Service Dead" alert
  that means the service is **actually** down, instead of a flood of
  alerts during expected quiet windows.
- As a cloud admin: I can deploy the monitoring stack with one command
  (`./monitoring/service/deploy.sh`) and trust it's idempotent.

## Design Decision

Added an activity-independent `/heartbeat` endpoint rather than modifying
the existing dice-audit alert because these are orthogonal signals:
dice-roll rate measures *user activity*, not *service health*. Combining
them would require knowing expected activity levels per time window, which
is complex and brittle. Two separate signals (one external health probe +
one internal activity proxy) with AND semantics gives the clearest alert
semantics.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

1. Cloud Scheduler job hitting prod `/heartbeat` every 5 min
2. Run `monitoring/service/deploy.sh` against `worldarchitecture-ai`
3. Decision on the legacy 4 dice-audit alerts (recommend closing them —
   the new alert supersedes)
4. Silence the Cloud Run ambiguous-branch toast (gcloud has no
   `--clear-source`; do in console or re-attach with branch=`main`)

## Beads

Beads: none

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes on-call alerting semantics and exposes an unauthenticated liveness endpoint; incorrect alert evaluation could miss outages or add noise until Cloud Scheduler is wired.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds an **activity-independent liveness path** so quiet periods do not look like outages: a new **`GET /heartbeat`** route (rate-limiter exempt) logs **`SERVICE_HEARTBEAT: ping received`** with timestamp and **`COMMIT_SHA`**, returns a small **`alive`** JSON payload, and **`/heartbeat`** is excluded from BigQuery request logging like **`/health`**.
> 
> Introduces **`monitoring/service/`** as monitoring-as-code: a **`service_heartbeat`** log-based metric (filter sourced from **`service_heartbeat_metric.json`**), a **Service Dead Alert** policy that fires only when **Cloud Run `request_count` and heartbeat counts are both below 1 for 30 minutes** (AND combiner), plus an idempotent **`deploy.sh`** that upserts the metric and policy by name. Documentation explains how this differs from dice-roll heartbeats under **`monitoring/dice/`**.
> 
> **`test_service_heartbeat_endpoint.py`** adds unit coverage for 200/JSON contract, log emission, commit SHA in logs, rate-limit exemption, and resilience without MCP init.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit f4cecf45c35354ed58009af7f2844cad374b2b0b. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

<!-- COPILOT_TRACKING_START -->
## Copilot Tracking Table

| # | Comment | Severity | Status | Summary |
|---|---------|----------|--------|---------|
| 1 | Skeptic: Unauthenticated /heartbeat endpoint | IMPORTANT | Acknowledged | By design — 200 response requires service to be alive; shallow liveness is the correct contract. OIDC Cloud Scheduler auth is a follow-up. |
| 2 | Skeptic: EVALUATION_MISSING_DATA_INACTIVE + AND suppresses dead-service alert | BLOCKING | **Fixed** | Changed request_count condition to EVALUATION_MISSING_DATA_ACTIVE in service_dead_policy.json — commit b9a51040b1. Dead service emits no telemetry; INACTIVE + AND silently suppressed the alert. |
| 3 | Skeptic: service_heartbeat_metric.json is dead code (filter hardcoded in deploy.sh) | IMPORTANT | **Fixed** | deploy.sh now reads SERVICE_HEARTBEAT_FILTER from service_heartbeat_metric.json via python3 — commit b9a51040b1. JSON file is now the single source of truth. |
| 4 | Skeptic: No notification channels in alert policy | IMPORTANT | Deferred | Channel IDs are env-specific GCP resource refs that cannot be embedded in the shared JSON; deployer adds channels post-deploy via GCP console. |
| 5 | Skeptic: ALIGN_RATE vs ALIGN_SUM asymmetry | IMPORTANT | Acknowledged | Intentional: request_count is DELTA metric (ALIGN_RATE); service_heartbeat is log-based count (ALIGN_SUM). Both fire at 0 on dead service. |
| 6 | Skeptic: Feature inert until Cloud Scheduler configured | IMPORTANT | Acknowledged | Known Limitation #1 and Follow-up #1 in PR description. Scheduler wiring is intentionally deferred. |
| 7 | Skeptic: DICE_AUDIT_SERVICE_NAME confusing in liveness script | STYLE | **Fixed** | deploy.sh now accepts LIVENESS_SERVICE_NAME (primary) with DICE_AUDIT_SERVICE_NAME as backward-compat alias — commit b9a51040b1. |

title: fix(level-up): reject stale GameState review targets (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background

The level-up review router compared `level_up_session.to_level` with the persisted character level before reopening an amendable session. That comparison only read `player_character_data` when the input state was a plain dictionary. Production passes a `GameState`, so `_pcd_level` became `None`; the `None` compatibility arm then accepted a stale session (target 2 against character level 3) and exposed the LevelUpAgent path that is authorized to write level changes.

## Goals

- Reject a stale review target identically for dictionary and production `GameState` inputs.
- Preserve valid same-level review reopening.
- Keep the fix within the existing state-extraction boundary with no semantic routing or new fallback.

## Summary

Reuse the existing `_get_player_character_data()` helper in `_extract_routing_state()` and add a dict/GameState regression matrix covering stale rejection and valid reopen behavior.

## Beads

Beads: none

The tracker could not be queried or updated because current `main` fails `br` preflight with 1,686 duplicate issue IDs. This PR intentionally does not modify `.beads/issues.jsonl`.

## Tenets

- Normalize supported state representations once through the existing helper.
- Preserve direct GameState attribute access; no `hasattr`/`getattr` reflection.
- Keep model-owned semantics unchanged; this is a server-owned representation bug.
- Smallest production diff: one helper reuse, no new abstraction.

## Governing design doc and bead

- Design doc: https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/main/roadmap/zfc-level-up-model-computes-2026-04-19.md
- Task specs: https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/main/roadmap/zfc-pr-task-specs-2026-04-22.md
- Bead: N/A because the existing tracker is blocked as described above.

## High-level description of changes

`_extract_routing_state()` now obtains player-character data through the same helper already used elsewhere for dict and GameState compatibility. Tests exercise both representations and prove stale target 2 cannot reopen against level 3, while matching target 3 still reopens and preserves the character level.

## Scope reconciliation

- Implementation: `mvp_site/agents.py`
- Test: `mvp_site/tests/test_level_up_review_routing.py`
- No CI, evidence bundle, docs, or bead files changed.
- Commit: https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/commit/59aeb7f16f7f6e1922a9434b7e21e0cd6a991178

## Test plan

Fresh RED before the production fix:

`WORLDAI_DEV_MODE=true TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true /Users/jleechan/projects/worldarchitect.ai/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q mvp_site/tests/test_level_up_review_routing.py::test_stale_review_target_rejects_reopen_for_dict_and_game_state mvp_site/tests/test_level_up_review_routing.py::test_matching_review_target_reopens_for_dict_and_game_state`

Result: 1 failed, 1 passed. The stale dictionary case rejected; the stale production GameState case incorrectly reopened.

GREEN after the fix:

- Same two-test command: 2 passed.
- `WORLDAI_DEV_MODE=true TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true /Users/jleechan/projects/worldarchitect.ai/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q mvp_site/tests/test_level_up_review_routing.py mvp_site/tests/test_agent_dispatch_table.py`: 131 passed, 6 subtests passed.
- `/Users/jleechan/projects/worldarchitect.ai/venv/bin/ruff check mvp_site/tests/test_level_up_review_routing.py`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Evidence limitation: this is deterministic unit/in-process routing proof. It does not claim real-LLM, Firebase, or browser evidence; the PR remains draft pending any required `/es` evidence.

## Risk

Blast radius is limited to review-reopen eligibility. A valid review still routes to LevelUpAgent for both state representations. Rollback is the single commit above.

## Out of scope

- Changing level-up model prompts, grant behavior, or finish semantics.
- Repairing the pre-existing duplicate-ID beads store.
- Modifying PR #8704 or PR #8489 branches.

## Low-level details

- `mvp_site/agents.py`: replace the dict-only player-character lookup with `_get_player_character_data(game_state)`.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_level_up_review_routing.py`: add stale and valid dict/GameState matrix regressions and verify the resolver boundary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches level-up routing eligibility only (review reopen), but a mistake could block valid amends or re-enable unauthorized level writes on finish; blast radius is narrow and covered by new dict/GameState tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Level-up review reopen** now reads `player_character_data` through `_get_player_character_data()` in `_extract_routing_state()`, so production `GameState` inputs get the same persisted level as dict-based tests when deciding whether a `level_up_review` click may reopen the amend modal.
> 
> Previously, level was only read from plain dicts, so `_pcd_level` was `None` for `GameState` and the stale-target check treated that as compatible—allowing a session still targeting level 2 to reopen after the character was already at level 3 and route into **LevelUpAgent** with finish authority.
> 
> Regression tests cover **dict** and **`GameState.from_dict`** for both stale rejection and valid same-target reopen.
>

title: fix(state): preserve canonical identity and directives across turns (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Preserve model-owned character identity and directives across turns without having
the backend make semantic lineage or XP decisions. `character_identity` keeps
content-hash-gated freshness, legacy lineage is restored only when the live aliases
lack meaningful father/mother content, canonical lineage aliases remain equal and
unstamped, server-only location metadata stays out of model context, and malformed
nested directive items are rejected instead of stringified.

## Production Code Changes

- Before: metadata-only lineage shells blocked restoration, nested provenance/cache
  markers rode in the general LLM game-state payload, and nested directives could
  be lost or malformed items stringified.
- Now: the shared canonicalizer treats only structurally meaningful lineage as
  populated; persisted `character_identity` uses content-hash-gated freshness;
  the shared serializer removes its duplicate `_updated_at`/`_content_hash` fields;
  and directive normalization preserves valid model output while rejecting invalid
  structures.
- Why: established model-authored identity and directives must persist without
  backend semantic ranking, while prompt prefixes remain stable and server-only
  metadata stays outside the general serialized state.

## Test Changes

Expanded existing game-state, serialization, schema, and real-service matrix tests
for metadata-only lineage, alias reconciliation, timestamp stability, location
anti-leakage, nested directives, and the persisted-state-versus-LLM-payload split.

## User Stories

- As a player, I want established parentage and persistent directives to survive
  later turns without stale backend inference rewriting them.
- As a model operator, I want one model-visible identity-provenance contract while
  server-only location metadata remains private.

## Beads

Beads: rev-onhvm, REV-ar350.19, rev-cwq21, rev-5051i, rev-x838a, rev-p3pgz, rev-bgnuq

## Tenets

- LLM decides; the server performs deterministic persistence, structural alias
  repair, transport, and validation only.
- Root-cause-first: legacy metadata-only lineage shells are treated as missing;
  populated/conflicting model-authored lineage is not ranked, merged, or guessed.
- Real-services invariant: acceptance evidence uses a fresh local gunicorn, native
  Gemini streaming, real Firestore, raw provider/HTTP traces, and persisted campaign
  exports.

## Design Decision

This PR implements the narrow provenance subset of
https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-full-state-provenance-design.md.

Architectural boundaries affected: game-state canonicalization and LLM
serialization, identity prompt rendering, response directive validation, schemas,
and the real-service evidence harness. The backend may recognize structurally empty
or malformed compatibility data, but it does not choose between meaningful lineage
records or derive a model-owned level from XP.

This PR does **not** perform semantic lineage conflict resolution, gap-fill partial
lineage, stamp `parentage`/`parents`, rewrite explicit levels, migrate every legacy
campaign shape, or deploy anything.

## Test plan

Run the focused unit/contract checks and the real-service evidence matrix documented below.

title: [antig] fix(llm_service): invoke parallel-undo LLM call and restore provenance (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background
Addresses GitHub issue [Issue #8077](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8077). In the previous implementation, the undo route `/api/campaigns/<campaign_id>/story/latest` (DELETE) called `firestore_service.delete_latest_story_entry` which deleted the user and Gemini turn documents, but did not invoke the parallel-undo LLM call. This led to silent narrative provenance loss and an unvalidated game state.

## Goals
- Delete the latest story turn atomically.
- Restore the campaign's game state using the snapshot of the surviving Gemini response.
- Re-prompt the LLM using `continue_story` on the surviving latest turn (the user action preceding the deleted turn).
- Persist the new narrative and structured response in the surviving Gemini story document.
- Assert correct execution through unit tests.

## Tenets
- Respect ZFC (Zero-Framework Cognition) by delegating judgment and re-narration to the LLM call.
- Safe GameState attribute access (no `hasattr` or `getattr` on GameState).
- No scope creep: only touch files directly related to the issue ([llm_service.py](file:///Users/jleechan/.ao-sessions/wa-3058/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch/worldarchitect.ai/mvp_site/llm_service.py), [main.py](file:///Users/jleechan/.ao-sessions/wa-3058/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch/worldarchitect.ai/mvp_site/main.py), and tests).
- Governing bead: rev-4t5a2 (tracks this undo-provenance fix for GitHub issue #8077).

## High-level description of changes
### Backend
- Added `_record_undo_artifact` and `gemini_undo_pipeline` in [llm_service.py](file:///Users/jleechan/.ao-sessions/wa-3058/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch/worldarchitect.ai/mvp_site/llm_service.py).
- Replaced `firestore_service.delete_latest_story_entry` call in [main.py](file:///Users/jleechan/.ao-sessions/wa-3058/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch/worldarchitect.ai/mvp_site/main.py) route with `llm_service.gemini_undo_pipeline`.

### Tests
- Created [test_undo_llm_provenance.py](file:///Users/jleechan/.ao-sessions/wa-3058/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch/worldarchitect.ai/mvp_site/tests/test_undo_llm_provenance.py) implementing TDD Red/Green assertions.

## Testing
- Automated unit test suite executed:
  `python3 -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_undo_llm_provenance.py` - PASS
  `python3 -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_undo_story_entry.py` - PASS
- Evidence of TDD failure (Red) and subsequent pass (Green) is recorded below.

## Low-level details
- The `gemini_undo_pipeline` retrieves the new latest Gemini story document and reads its `game_state_snapshot`.
- Restores the campaign's game state by updating `current_state` document.
- Invokes `continue_story` on the surviving user input, prompting the LLM with the prior turn's context and reverted state.
- Overwrites the text of the surviving Gemini response with the new LLM-generated narrative, restoring proper narrative provenance.
- Governing Design Doc: N/A (this is a bug fix for [Issue #8077](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8077)).
- Bead ID: rev-4t5a2 (governing bead for this PR).

Beads: rev-4t5a2

## User Stories
- **User** requests **undo latest turn** and the **game reverts state and LLM is called to re-narrate** so that **the narrative provenance is preserved and future turns remain cohesive**.

## Evidence
- TDD Red phase:
```
mvp_site/tests/test_undo_llm_provenance.py F                             [100%]
AttributeError: <module 'mvp_site.llm_service' ...> does not have the attribute '_record_undo_artifact'
```
- TDD Green phase:
```
mvp_site/tests/test_undo_llm_provenance.py .                             [100%]
1 passed in 1.12s
```

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the undo API path to mutate game state, invoke the narrative LLM, and overwrite story documents—core gameplay consistency with no auth changes, but failures could leave state and narrative out of sync.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Undo latest story turn** now runs `gemini_undo_pipeline` instead of only deleting Firestore story documents.
> 
> The pipeline still removes the latest user/Gemini pair via `delete_latest_story_entry`, then **restores campaign `GameState`** from the surviving Gemini entry’s `structured_fields.game_state_snapshot`, logs an undo artifact via `_record_undo_artifact`, and **calls `continue_story`** on the surviving user input with prior context. It **overwrites** the surviving Gemini story doc’s `text` and `structured_fields` with the new LLM output (preserving snapshot when missing from the response).
> 
> The DELETE `/api/campaigns/<campaign_id>/story/latest` handler in `main.py` is wired to this pipeline. **`test_undo_llm_provenance.py`** asserts deletion, state rollback, LLM invocation, artifact recording, and narrative persistence.

[agento] feat(campaigns): Luke + Daenerys default POV with fleshed character personalities (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

- Adds Luke Skywalker (Skywalker's Choice) and Daenerys Targaryen (Dragon's Crucible) as preset campaign types alongside Dragon Knight, using the same SHA-gated canonical-default pattern
- Both campaigns pre-fill wizard with locked POV character, setting, and canonical description; `TEMPLATE_OPENING_STORY = None` so first-turn creation still uses LLM until ops populate pre-generated stories
- Generalizes Dragon-Knight-only `isDragonKnight` logic to `_isCanonicalCampaign()` covering all 6 canonical types; 30 new unit tests + SHA sync guards confirm frontend/backend byte-for-byte consistency
- Adds Ancient Rome (The Ides of March, Marcus Aemilius Macer, 44 BCE), Present Day (Dead Drop, Elena Vasquez, DC 2025), and Future (Colony's Edge, Dr. Yuki Tanaka, Mars 2087) campaigns with fully fleshed 20-25KB canonical descriptions

## Background

WorldArchitect.AI supports preset campaign types that bypass the LLM for first-turn story generation when the user picks canonical defaults (the Dragon Knight pattern). This PR extends that pattern to two new campaigns: **Skywalker's Choice** (Luke Skywalker) and **Dragon's Crucible** (Daenerys Targaryen), with fully fleshed character personalities and backgrounds for all major characters.

## Goals

- Make Luke Skywalker the default POV for the Skywalker's Choice campaign
- Make Daenerys Targaryen the default POV for the Dragon's Crucible campaign
- Flesh out main + side character personalities/backgrounds with voice anchors, internal contradictions, secrets, wants, never-dos, die-for/betrayal/sacrifice triggers for every named character in both campaigns

## Tenets

- ZFC: no keyword/regex/heuristic routing; SHA-gated fast-path delegates all judgment to LLM
- bypass-claims.md compliant: sync tests extract from the real JS frontend constant, not the backend .txt file
- All constants added to constants.py; no new env vars
- TEMPLATE_OPENING_STORY = None (falls through to LLM); pre-generated story can be populated later

## High-level description

**Backend (Python):**
- `mvp_site/campaign_template_luke.py` — mirrors `campaign_template_dragon_knight.py`; SHA-256 guards `LUKE_CANONICAL_PROMPT_SHA256`

title: Duplicate beads with malformed external_ref causing high-volume ESCALATION_NOTIFICATION_FAILED thrashing
description:
Found live 2026-07-10T~08:00Z: ESCALATION_NOTIFICATION_FAILED fired 390x in 15min across
many beads, all citing "parse: invalid external_ref format for comment" for URL-form
external_ref values (matches jleechan-twa0's already-diagnosed parser gap).

Attempted a bulk mechanical fix (br update --external-ref to short owner/repo#N form) on
23 affected beads. ~10 succeeded cleanly. The rest failed with br's own unique-external-ref
constraint ("External reference X already exists on issue Y") -- revealing these aren't
just malformed data, they're GENUINE DUPLICATE beads: multiple beads created (likely by
different intake events / sessions over the past few days) tracking the SAME target PR.
Confirmed pairs so far: jleechan-jpi vs jleechan-hslx (both PR #8058), jleechan-eo8 vs
jleechan-4uzw (both PR #8060), jleechan-qef vs jleechan-bvaj (both PR #8064), jleechan-lio
vs jleechan-4dgx/6iw7 (all three, PR #8116), jleechan-s15 vs jleechan-xmdy (both PR #8061),
jleechan-w1y vs jleechan-ywab (both PR #8177), jleechan-r69 vs jleechan-tj88 (both PR
#8178), jleechan-qcs vs jleechan-fk9q (both issue #8164).

Did NOT force-close or pick a canonical bead in any pair -- that needs real judgment
(which one has more progress/context/history) not a mechanical script. Left the ~10
successfully-reformatted beads as-is (their external_ref is now correct); left the
duplicate pairs untouched pending a proper consolidation pass.

Real fix needed: (a) jleechan-twa0's parser fix (accept both URL and short formats) stops
the immediate thrashing regardless of duplicates, (b) a separate dedup pass should review
each pair, close the non-canonical one with a "superseded by X" reason, and consider
whether intake normalization has a bug that's creating duplicates in the first place
(worth checking jleechan-u4gb, the earlier intake-dedup TOCTOU race fix, for whether this
is a related/recurring gap).
notes:
2026-07-10 48-hour audit: raised to P0. Telemetry recorded 63,069 ESCALATION_NOTIFICATION_FAILED events and AO queue saturation at 100 pending requests; this is active throughput collapse, not low-volume cleanup.

title: scope-mismatch: pcpr fix belongs in dark-factory daemon, not worldarchitect.ai
description:
WA factory worker (worktree factory/jleechan-drive-pr-branch-binding-pcpr-r1 in jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai) routed the pcpr bead here but the actual bug lives in this repo.

Evidence:
- pcpr bead source_repo = "dark-factory" (verified in .beads/issues.jsonl)
- pcpr bead external_ref pattern references jleechanorg/dark-factory#288/#289
- The dispatcher code raising session_branch_mismatch lives at daemon/src/tick.rs:484-498 (overlay.park_reason = Some("session_branch_mismatch")) and daemon/src/dispatch.rs (Sessions::session_branch, spawn_branch_mismatch phase, set_session_branch script harness at :800, :909-912, integration test at :1399-1425)
- jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/dark-factory/ is only repo-specific .dot pipelines (pr7467_levelup_review_gates.dot, pr_gates_split_cs.dot) per its README — NOT the daemon source
- Grep across WA for session_branch_mismatch, PARKED_HUMAN_HELD, drive-existing-PR, external_ref, overlay.branch, branch_registry, adopted-PR-drive returns zero hits

Fix scope (single + batch paths):
1. daemon/src/dispatch.rs — when a bead has external_ref matching an OPEN PR in a configured repo, resolve the PR head ref via gh api and bind overlay.branch to the PR head ref instead of factory/<bead>-r1. Apply to both single-bead dispatch and batch intake paths (PR #283 ADOPTION path is similar; this is the DRIVE path)
2. daemon/src/tick.rs — relax session_branch_mismatch to allow adopted-PR-drive beads; only fail-closed for fresh-work create-new-work beads where generated branch is the contract
3. daemon/tests/ — add regression test reproducing session_branch_mismatch for a drive bead (similar to dispatch.rs:1399-1425 single-bead pattern)
4. Telemetry — distinguish adopted-PR-drive from fresh-work dispatch (tag dispatch events so dashboard can split)

WA worktree state:
- Branch factory/jleechan-drive-pr-branch-binding-pcpr-r1 is empty (no commits, clean vs origin/main)
- Unrelated .claude/settings.json metadata-updater hook wiring was reverted
- Recommend: leave WA branch empty, do NOT push a WA PR. Push the actual fix from a dark-factory worktree on branch factory/jleechan-drive-pr-branch-binding-pcpr-r1 (mirror the same branch name so the factory dispatcher's branch watcher finds it; OR use a dark-factory-local name like fix/pcpr-drive-branch-binding if the cross-repo watcher policy isn't symmetric)

Reference beads (already open in this repo):
- jleechan-drive-pr-branch-binding-pcpr (the parent bug)
- jleechan-af-drive-pr288-gd2x (the drive bead that hit the bug at 01:32:37Z)
- jleechan-af-drive-pr289-inoy (the drive bead that hit the bug at 01:33:55Z)
notes:
## Concrete fix scope (refined after source audit)

### Where the bug lives
- daemon/src/tick.rs:484-498 — per-tick integrity sweep: every tick for a DISPATCHED bead calls `deps.sessions.session_branch(&session_id)` and if the live branch != overlay.branch, parks the bead HUMAN_HELD with park_reason = "session_branch_mismatch". This is the trigger that parked pcpr-288 and pcpr-289.
- daemon/src/tick.rs:937 — adopted-PR path sets overlay.branch = adopted.head_ref_name.clone() (the contributor's branch, NOT a factory/<id>-r<n> name). The bug: this only fires for beads coming through `intake::normalize_labeled_prs` (the EXISTING_PR_ADOPTED path, PR #283 ADOPTION). Manually-created drive beads with external_ref like jleechanorg/dark-factory#288 do NOT go through that path — they go through `intake::normalize` (the fresh-bead path), which produces a factory/<id>-r1 branch and skips the head_ref_name resolution.

### Single + batch paths
- There is no separate "single" vs. "batch" dispatch. `dispatch::dispatch_ready` (dispatch.rs:159-164) is the single entry point, looping over `Vec<(Bead, RoutingVerdict)>` with caps max_workers=30 concurrent, max_batch=15 per call (tick.rs:1200-1510). The fix lives in dispatch.rs:243 where the factory branch is fabricated AND in the upstream intake where the bead should be recognized as a drive-existing-PR.

### Existing provenance — `BeadOverlay::is_adopted` (state.rs:77-84)
> "Adopted-PR provenance (bead jleechan-tfs1): `true` iff `branch` is an external contributor's own head_ref_name... Explicit stored flag, NOT inferred from branch name."

The flag already exists. The bug is that `normalize` (issue intake) doesn't set it for manually-created beads with an external_ref pointing at an open PR.

### PR head ref resolution
- `Scm::labeled_prs` returns `LabeledPr { head_ref_name, external_ref, ... }` (tools.rs:93-105)
- Adapter populates head_ref_name from `gh api repos/<repo>/pulls/<n>` (`head.ref_name`) — adapters.rs:295-389 (REST) or :500-555 (GraphQL)
- `parse_external_ref` at adapters.rs:176-183 — strict `<owner>/<repo>#<n>` parser, duplicated at intake.rs:95-102

### Concrete fix plan
1. **intake::normalize** (or new helper) — when the bead has an external_ref like `jleechanorg/dark-factory#288`, query SCM for that PR. If it's OPEN, treat the bead as drive-existing-PR:
   - Set overlay.branch = pr.head_ref_name (instead of format!("factory/{}-r1", id))
   - Set overlay.is_adopted = true
   - Set overlay.pr_number = Some(pr.number)
   - Skip the DISPATCHED spawn path on initial intake (go straight to ATTESTED like the EXISTING_PR_ADOPTED path at tick.rs:935)
2. **state.rs** — verify `HumanHoldReason::SessionBranchMismatch` policy: only fail-closed for fresh-work beads (is_adopted=false), allow adopted-PR-drive beads to have session_branch == overlay.branch == pr.head_ref_name without parking.
3. **daemon/tests/** — add regression test in tick_integration.rs near the existing `test_dispatch_integrity_sweep_parks_session_branch_mismatch` (line 715): `test_drive_existing_pr_bead_does_not_park_session_branch_mismatch` — bead with external_ref to an open PR, overlay.branch = head_ref_name, simulate session with that branch, run tick, assert no PARKED_HUMAN_HELD.
4. **Telemetry** — `EXISTING_PR_ADOPTED` event already distinguishes intake (tick.rs:949). For drive-bead-from-manual-intake, emit same event with `source: "drive_existing_pr_resolved"` field. Also add `is_adopted` to `TASK_DISPATCHED` context (tick.rs:1483-1509) so the dashboard can filter adopted-drive vs fresh-work dispatches at re-roll time.

### Existing test template
daemon/tests/tick_integration.rs:1553-1635 — `factory_labeled_existing_pr_is_adopted_and_verified_without_spawn` — the canonical test for the adopted path. Use this as the template for the manual-drive bead test.

title: runner/handler_audit.py: Gemini vendor-named evidence filenames as default fallback
description:
HIGH-severity finding from 2026-06-27 runner/handler domain-bias audit.

File: runner/handler_audit.py
- Lines 227-230: when gate_audit node runs without explicit evidence_paths= attr or state.evidence_paths key, it defaults to probing three filenames:
  - gemini_http_request_responses.jsonl
  - gemini_http_responses.jsonl
  - evidence.jsonl
The first two are Gemini-API-specific. A benchmark that uses OpenAI/Anthropic/etc. for evidence capture gets either no defaults or a name collision with its real artifacts.

Impact: cross-vendor evidence portability is broken. The dark-factory repo is designed to be backend-agnostic (per AGENTS.md and the codergen dispatch priority queue), but this code path silently assumes Gemini-shaped artifacts. A codex or agy backend that writes evidence.jsonl + openai_request_responses.jsonl gets the Gemini-only first two probed (wasted I/O) and only then falls through to evidence.jsonl.

Acceptance:
1. Default evidence filename probe list is renamed to be vendor-neutral (e.g. llm_request_responses.jsonl, llm_responses.jsonl, evidence.jsonl) — note llm_request_responses.jsonl is already used elsewhere per memory).
2. Backwards-compatible aliases: if the worktree contains gemini_http_request_responses.jsonl, still pick it up; same for any other vendor name dropped in via .dark-factory/evidence.yaml.
3. Add a test: worktree with openai_request_responses.jsonl + llm_request_responses.jsonl gets both probed, not the Gemini names.

Touch: runner/handler_audit.py, tests/test_gate_audit_*.py (or similar).

title: fix(rewards): archive combat after synthesized reward delivery (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Draft investigation of legacy combat-reward state. The current branch treats
`rewards_synthesized_for_total_xp` as delivery evidence when `rewards_processed`
is absent, but live Firestore/story review disproved that assumption: a later
unrelated XP event can stamp the sentinel while an older combat reward was never
displayed. The implementation is blocked and must not merge in its current form.

Governing design:
https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/main/roadmap/nextsteps-2026-07-26-tybolt-continuity-repro.md

## User Stories

- As a player continuing after rewards were already displayed, I reach the story
  agent instead of receiving an unrelated duplicate rewards turn.
- As a player with genuinely pending combat rewards, I still reach `RewardsAgent`
  until a delivery signal exists.

## Beads

Beads: REV-ovr3z

## Production Code Changes

- The shared delivery predicate accepts either the canonical
  `rewards_processed` marker or the server-owned
  `rewards_synthesized_for_total_xp` sentinel.
- Action-start cleanup archives an ended combat with recorded delivery before
  agent selection and clears the sentinel as part of archival.
- An ended combat without either marker remains pending and continues to route
  through `RewardsAgent`.
- BLOCKED: the sentinel is not sufficient same-combat delivery provenance. The
  branch can therefore archive genuinely undisplayed combat rewards and requires
  redesign after source-selection and streaming/non-streaming parity analysis.

Implementation commit:
https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/commit/ac03e4caaade1e2acd8fc870739fd7baecd655c9

## Test Changes

- Added exact-phenotype routing, cleanup, and `GameState.has_pending_rewards`
  contracts for sentinel `90180`, current XP `92130`, and a missing legacy flag.
- Extended the existing HTTP-to-Firestore Layer 2 suite with the captured Crow's
  Audit action and both positive and negative delivery contracts.

Changed-test details are inspectable at:
https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8620/files

## Known Limitations

- BLOCKER: live Firestore/story provenance shows sentinel `90180` was stamped by
  later unrelated XP while the stale combat `32700` to `33200` had no rewards
  box. The current predicate is unsafe and is not merge-ready.
- Investigation must next inspect `synthesize_rewards_box_from_state` source
  selection and streaming/non-streaming reward discrepancy parity.
- This change deliberately does not alter AGY parsing, directive precedence,
  God Mode semantics, provider retry behavior, or backend semantic routing.
- No replacement fix will be pushed until the provenance review is complete.

Tracking PR:
https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8620

## Unit Test Evidence

At commit `ac03e4caaade1e2acd8fc870739fd7baecd655c9`:

```text
./vpython -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_agents.TestRewardsAgent mvp_site.tests.test_game_state.TestGameState mvp_site.tests.test_world_logic.TestHasRewardsContext mvp_site.tests.test_world_logic.TestPrepareGameStateSynthesizedRewardsReconciliation
Ran 59 tests
OK

WORLDAI_DEV_MODE=true TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true ./vpython -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_rewards_box_issue_8020
Ran 32 tests
OK
```

Commit anchor:
https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/commit/ac03e4caaade1e2acd8fc870739fd7baecd655c9

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

Layer 2 HTTP-to-Firestore response-path checks at the same commit:

```text
./vpython -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_end2end.test_rewards_agent_mechanical_end2end
Ran 4 tests in 23.904s
OK
Exact Crow's Audit response payload selected StoryModeAgent and archived the ended combat before routing.
```

These checks do not validate the sentinel's causal provenance and are therefore
insufficient for merge readiness. Draft evidence status is visible at:
https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8620

## Real LLM Evidence

FAIL/BLOCKED: the exact Crow's Audit action ran once on a fresh candidate clone
through `/interaction/stream` with the real AGY provider. It emitted one
`agy_request` and one successful `agy_response`, and no longer selected
`RewardsAgent`; however, this does not establish safe reward delivery because
the underlying sentinel provenance assumption is false. No GREEN claim is made.

Evidence tracking:
https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8620

## Evidence

Evidence verdict: FAIL/BLOCKED. The source campaign
`fw9Fo3QXkqshtVxBIwX2` remained read-only, baseline clone
`2Fh5HJEh63IB3DDMnAPH` remained read-only, and candidate clone
`QNcOkY9aXd3YMSYHjbbH` was consumed exactly once. Partial raw captures are
preserved locally but are not presented as GREEN because the code can suppress
genuinely undisplayed combat rewards.

PR evidence anchor:
https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8620

## Risk

Blast radius is the ended-combat rewards lifecycle. A false delivered signal could
skip legitimate rewards; the sentinel is accepted only from the combat state and
is removed during archival so a later combat starts unprocessed. The no-sentinel
negative contract preserves genuine pending-reward routing. Rollback is a revert
of the implementation commit.

## Out of Scope

- No directive-precedence, Tybolt-lore, God Mode, or prompt changes.
- No source-campaign mutation.
- No merge authorization is requested or implied.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core ended-combat rewards routing and archival; treating `rewards_synthesized_for_total_xp` as delivery can skip `RewardsAgent` for combat whose rewards were never shown if the sentinel was stamped by unrelated XP (called out as a merge blocker in the PR).
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **`combat_rewards_delivery_is_recorded`** in `game_state` (re-exported from `rewards_engine`) so ended combat is treated as reward-delivered when **`rewards_processed`** is set **or** **`rewards_synthesized_for_total_xp`** is positive—not only the legacy flag.
> 
> That predicate replaces direct **`rewards_processed`** checks in **`RewardsAgent`** routing, **`GameState.has_pending_rewards`**, **`world_logic._has_rewards_context`**, and action-start combat cleanup in **`_prepare_game_state`**. When delivery is recorded, finished combat can be archived to **`combat_history`**, **`combat_summary`** cleared, phase set to **`idle`**, and the synthesis sentinel removed; without either signal, **`RewardsAgent`** still owns the turn.
> 
> Tests cover sentinel-only stale admin state (Crow’s Audit e2e → **`StoryModeAgent`**), negative paths when the sentinel is absent, and prepare-state archival.

fix: 8022 combat agent not activating — intent classifier anchors (re-spin of #8023) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary
Re-spin of #8023 onto current main, dropping stale/unrelated cruft that PR carried from a 2026-06-28 base (pre-`self-hosted-oss` retirement in #8057). Root cause: `mvp_site/intent_classifier.py`'s `MODE_COMBAT` FastEmbed anchor list lacked mid-battle turn-handoff phrasings (e.g. "let everyone else take their turns", "skip my turn"), so those utterances misrouted to `HeavyDialogAgent` instead of `CombatAgent` — enemy turns and HP updates never fired (issue #8022, root-caused via a real BigQuery trace on campaign `6IL5OTf3RpPrXA5yDu42`, turn 64).

## Production Code Changes
- **Before**: `MODE_COMBAT` anchor phrases in `intent_classifier.py`'s `ANCHOR_PHRASES` did not cover mid-battle turn-handoff phrasing, causing misclassification to the dialog agent.
- **Now**: Added 17 new `MODE_COMBAT` anchors covering turn-handoff/pass/hold-action phrasing, plus 5 `MODE_DIALOG` counter-anchors so "turn" vocabulary in non-combat phrasing (e.g. "a turn of phrase") doesn't bleed into combat misclassification.
- **Why**: Real BigQuery trace confirmed the specific misrouting; anchors are the model-owned semantic classification mechanism this repo already uses (FastEmbed), consistent with ZFC — no new keyword/regex routing logic added.

## Test Changes
- `mvp_site/tests/test_intent_classifier.py`: 5 new test methods, including a real-FastEmbed Layer-2 proof test (loads the real `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` model) confirming all 6 issue-#8022 repro utterances route to `combat` (score 1.000) and 3 dialog counter-anchors correctly stay `dialog`.

## Unit Test Evidence
```
TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true vpython -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_intent_classifier -v
```
42 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 4.670s. Real-FastEmbed Layer-2 test confirms all repro utterances now route correctly at score 1.000.

## Non-Unit Test Evidence
No UI change (pure classifier/anchor change). Real-FastEmbed Layer-2 response payload from a real (non-mocked) `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` model run, full log: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/b5deb0ecedff0639ea93a016d561ebd2

Real classifier response excerpt (real model, not mocked):
```
Response: CLASSIFIER: Input='let everyone besides me take t...' -> combat (score=1.000)
Response: CLASSIFIER: Input='let everyone else take their t...' -> combat (score=1.000)
Response: CLASSIFIER: Input='continue your turn' -> combat (score=1.000)
Response: CLASSIFIER: Input='skip my turn' -> combat (score=1.000)
Response: CLASSIFIER: Input='trigger surprise round' -> combat (score=1.000)
Response: CLASSIFIER: Input='let my whole team attack' -> combat (score=1.000)
Response: CLASSIFIER: Input='a turn of phrase' -> dialog (score=1.000)
Response: CLASSIFIER: Input='a turn of events' -> dialog (score=1.000)
Response: CLASSIFIER: Input='in turn, she replied' -> dialog (score=1.000)
Ran 42 tests in 9.406s
OK
```

## Real LLM Evidence
N/A - this PR does not touch `mvp_site/prompts/**`.

## Evidence
Full real-mode test run (gist, tied to head SHA 4fd019541c33a695dcdbf89820d78cccabae9553): https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/b5deb0ecedff0639ea93a016d561ebd2

Superseding PR: #8023 (closed, carried unrelated `self-hosted-oss/` resurrection + workflow-policy regressions from a stale 2026-06-28 base - see closing comment on that PR for the full diff-scope diagnosis). This PR is a clean 2-file re-spin containing only the real classifier fix and its tests, verified against current main.

## Known Limitations
- The full real-agy combat-turn-cycle end-to-end proof (player attack -> enemy turn -> HP shown) is currently blocked by an external agy account quota exhaustion (~16-42h reset window, unrelated to this fix). The fix is proven at the unit/Layer-2 level with the real FastEmbed model; the end-to-end proof will follow once the quota resets.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core semantic agent routing (`predict()` two-pass logic and anchor table); wrong routing still sends gameplay to the wrong agent, though scope is limited to FastEmbed anchors and classification order with broad test coverage.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#8022** where mid-battle phrases like “let everyone else take their turns” misrouted to dialog instead of **CombatAgent** because `MODE_COMBAT` FastEmbed anchors lacked turn-handoff coverage.
> 
> **Classifier behavior:** `predict()` now classifies the **current user action first** and only runs a second pass with prior narrative (`last 500 chars` + `USER ACTION:`) when the action-alone score is below the existing similarity threshold—so quiet narrative context no longer overrides explicit combat handoff intent.
> 
> **Anchors:** Adds **18** `MODE_COMBAT` turn-handoff/pass/hold-action anchors and **5** `MODE_DIALOG` counter-anchors (e.g. “a turn of phrase”) to limit cross-mode bleed from new “turn” vocabulary.
> 
> **Tests:** Mocked routing guards, real **BGE** FastEmbed proof for repro utterances (with and without narrative context), stdlib-only anchor count/registration checks in `test_intent_classifier_anchors_pr.py`, and updated context tests for the two-pass embed flow.
>

## Exact-head evidence refresh (2026-07-11)

# PR 8319 exact-head classifier evidence

- PR: https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8319
- HEAD: `90f11d24324857e76543f7a8c3552231c4099a08`
- Merge base: `8bd2fe949fe5b5321297e36071495af274f20a22`
- Mode: real local gunicorn + production streaming endpoint + real `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` FastEmbed; cache off for WorldAI responses

## Result

The changed routing claim passes: all six issue-8022 handoff phrases selected `CombatAgent` at the exact head. Four streaming requests completed successfully. `trigger surprise round` and `let my whole team attack` both logged classifier score `1.000` and `SEMANTIC_INTENT_COMBAT -> CombatAgent` before the separate AGY provider returned invalid non-gameplay output. Those two downstream turns are disclosed as failed and are not represented as successful gameplay responses.

The real-model regression also passed all six phrases both without context and with the prior narrative that reproduced the production failure; three dialog counterexamples remained `dialog`. The full classifier/context suite passed 44/44.

## Artifact map

- `pr8319-streaming-evidence-90f11d2.tar.gz`: self-contained streaming evidence iterations with raw response files, server logs, run metadata, and per-file checksums
- `pr8319-90f11d2.txt`: sanitized terminal transcript with provenance, relevant diff, real-model test, and SHA match
- `pr8319-90f11d2.cast`: replayable terminal recording
- `pr8319-90f11d2.gif`: browser preview
- `pr8319-90f11d2.mp4.zip`: high-fidelity video
- `pr8319-90f11d2.vtt`: captions
- `pr8319-90f11d2-metadata.json`: structured claim boundary
- `pr8319-90f11d2-SHA256SUMS.txt`: integrity manifest

## Exact commands

```bash
unset FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH
TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true <venv-python> -m unittest \
  mvp_site.tests.test_intent_classifier \
  mvp_site.tests.test_intent_classifier_context

TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true TEST_MODE=real WORLDAI_TEST_CACHE=off \
ENABLE_SEMANTIC_ROUTING=true FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH=<fastembed-cache> \
GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=<firebase-admin-key> \
<venv-python> /tmp/pr8319_streaming_e2e.py
```

- Public media and downloadable raw bundle: https://github.com/jleechanorg/agent-orchestrator/releases/tag/worldarchitect-evidence-pr-8319-90f11d2
- Self-contained checksummed gist: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/59480d68b41b18afe9d1df2f2826491d

## Design Decision

- Governing architecture: https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/main/docs/design/system-architecture.md
- Tracking bead: `rev-b0hyg`
- Decision: the FastEmbed semantic classifier evaluates the current user action first. Prior narrative remains available only as a second semantic view when the current action is below the existing model threshold. This preserves model-owned semantic routing without keyword rules or a new hand-tuned score.
- Rejected alternative: appending/prepending the same 500-character narrative to every input. Real-model evidence showed both orders still diluted exact handoff intent.
- Scope boundary: no backend intent clamp, regex, keyword router, or new dependency; the downstream agent remains responsible for gameplay execution.

description:
## Summary

- God-Mode grants of custom check-triggered mechanics (e.g. "Conqueror's Spark," a `1d[level]` bonus, [#8320](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8320)) were narrative-only prose and drifted/were dropped on later turns.
- Fix extends the existing `player_character_data.resource_registry` store with `trigger_check_types`, `dice_expression`, and `apply_mode` fields instead of restructuring `features[]` — smaller blast radius, reuses proven backend-enforced infra (issue #7233).
- Prompt/schema-only change (`god_mode_instruction.md`, `dice_system_instruction.md`, `game_state_mechanics_appendix.md`, `game_state.schema.json`) plus additive server-side validation/warnings in `narrative_response_schema.py` (no new persistence logic, no state mutation).
- Real-LLM run (2/2 scenarios) confirms the model writes the intended structured entry when granted a custom mechanic via God Mode.

## Background

GH issue [#8320](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/8320) / evidence PR [#8321](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8321): a user's custom "Conqueror's Spark" mechanic (`1d[level]` bonus to Persuasion/Insight checks), granted via God Mode at character creation, was written as narrative-only prose in `god_mode_response`. It was never persisted to any machine-parseable field. By turn 274 of campaign `xK3fp5XrV24oarIINTF7`, the LLM had to re-derive the mechanic from 270+ turns of prose, rolled `1d20+13` and silently dropped the expected `1d17` bonus. The user had to keep re-asserting the rule every turn.

Static-evidence greps (from issue #8320) confirmed zero canonical representation: `player_character_data.features[]` contained the grant only as a plain string, with no trigger, formula, or apply-mode data anywhere.

## Goals

- Give the LLM a structured place to persist a check-triggered custom mechanic at grant time, so it does not need to re-derive the rule from narrative prose on every later turn.
- Stay within this repo's ZFC / root-cause-first policy: the model decides the mechanic; the server only persists, validates, and renders it. No backend regex/heuristic parsing of narrative text.
- Minimize blast radius: reuse existing, already-shipped machinery rather than inventing a new schema.

## Tenets

**Design Decision:** rev-ew20b — see `mvp_site/prompts/game_state_mechanics_appendix.md` for the extended `ResourceEntry` field docs (`trigger_check_types`, `dice_expression`, `apply_mode`) that implement this decision.

- **Root-cause-first**: fix the prompt contract, not a backend adjuster/inference layer.
- **Reuse over invention**: `player_character_data.resource_registry` (issue #7233) already exists precisely for "LLM-defined resource: D&D 5e class features, custom... charges, or anything else the campaign introduces," is already backend-enforced (clamp, reset-on-rest) and already rendered in the session header. Extending it is smaller and safer than restructuring `features[]` from `List[str]` to `List[Dict]` campaign-wide (which would break an invariant several other prompts rely on).
- **Validation-only backend**: the added `narrative_response_schema.py` checks (below) only validate and warn — no new state mutation, inference, or narrative parsing.

## High-level description

Two design options were considered:
- **(A) Extend `resource_registry`** with `trigger_check_types[]`, `dice_expression`, `apply_mode` fields (chosen).
- (B) Restructure `player_character_data.features[]` from `List[str]` to `List[Dict]` (rejected — bigger blast radius, breaks an existing invariant).

Changes:
- `mvp_site/prompts/god_mode_instruction.md`: new **Custom Mechanic Grant Invariant (MANDATORY, issue #8320)** — any check-triggered custom mechanic grant must also write a `resource_registry` entry with the new fields, alongside the existing narrative response. Includes a full worked JSON example using "The Conqueror's Spark".
- `mvp_site/prompts/dice_system_instruction.md` + `mvp_site/prompts/shared/dice_notation_contract.md`: extends the existing narrative-only "separate roll" pattern (Bardic Inspiration / Sneak Attack / Divine Smite) into a **mandatory rule**: scan `resource_registry` for entries whose `trigger_check_types` match the current check, resolve `1d[level]` at roll time, and roll the `dice_expression` as an extra roll (add or reroll per `apply_mode`), reporting `mechanics.combined_total` and decrementing limited-use entries.
- `mvp_site/prompts/game_state_mechanics_appendix.md` + `mvp_site/schemas/game_state.schema.json`: document the 3 new optional `ResourceEntry` fields (`dependentRequired` in JSON Schema — all three travel together or none). `additionalProperties: true` was already set, so this is documentation plus a stricter conditional constraint, not a breaking schema change.

## Production Code Changes

- **`mvp_site/narrative_response_schema.py`** (`_validate_resource_registry`): before → the function validated `current`/`max`/`reset_trigger`/`category` only. Now → it also validates that `trigger_check_types`/`dice_expression`/`apply_mode` appear together (all three or none), that `trigger_check_types` is a non-empty list of non-empty strings, `dice_expression` is a non-empty string, and `apply_mode` is `"add"` or `"reroll"`. Why → the model's own `resource_registry` writes need a validation backstop consistent with this repo's "warnings only, no assertions/retries/default content" error-handling philosophy — bad LLM output surfaces as a warning, it does not silently corrupt game state.
- **`mvp_site/narrative_response_schema.py`** (`action_resolution.mechanics.combined_total`): added a type-check warning when `mechanics.combined_total` is present but non-numeric, since the new dice-notation contract introduces this field for add/reroll bonus totals. Warning-only, matches existing `_warn_on_unclean_action_resolution_dice` pattern in the same class.
- No new persistence logic, no narrative-text parsing, no server-computed game decisions — `_canonicalize_resource_registry_in_place` (`mvp_site/game_state.py:1255`) already passed through unknown dict fields untouched before this PR and continues to do so; the validation added here only warns.

## Test Changes

- **New**: `mvp_site/tests/test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_canonicalization.py` — RED→GREEN prompt-contract tests asserting `god_mode_instruction.md` and `dice_system_instruction.md` contain the new required language.
- **New**: `testing_mcp/test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_resource_registry.py` — real local-server + real-LLM scenario granting "The Conqueror's Spark" via God Mode and asserting the structured `resource_registry` entry appears with the correct trigger/formula/mode fields.
- **Extended**: `mvp_site/tests/test_resource_registry.py` — additional coverage for the new `_validate_resource_registry` mechanic-field checks (paired-field requirement, type/enum validation).

## Testing

### Unit / prompt-contract (RED → GREEN)

`mvp_site/tests/test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_canonicalization.py` — 2 tests asserting `god_mode_instruction.md` and `dice_system_instruction.md` contain the new required language. Confirmed RED (failing) against `origin/main` before the fix, GREEN after.

### Regression

Ran all 6 test files referencing the 3 edited prompt files (`test_agents.py`, `test_compression_lever1.py`, `test_dice_prompt_advantage_disadvantage.py`, `test_god_mode_prompt_time_rules.py`, `test_god_mode_stale_combat_cleanup.py`, `test_prompts.py`) plus `test_resource_registry.py` and `test_god_mode_response_field.py`: **526 passed, 3 skipped, 0 new failures.** 3 pre-existing failures in `test_god_mode_prompt_level_signal_rule.py` confirmed via `git stash` to already exist on `origin/main` HEAD `007f7d3fde`, unrelated to this change.

### Real LLM (testing_mcp, real Gemini API)

`testing_mcp/test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_resource_registry.py`: real local MCP server + real `gemini-3-flash-preview` call (`AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` — AGY needs interactive TTY auth refresh unavailable in this harness, so this uses the documented Gemini-API fallback path, matching sibling test `test_resource_registry_no_rest_refresh_real_llm.py`). Grants "The Conqueror's Spark" via God Mode, then asserts a structured `resource_registry` entry appears.

**Result: 2/2 scenarios PASSED.** The real model produced exactly the intended structure:

```json
"conquerors_spark": {
  "trigger_check_types": ["persuasion", "insight"],
  "dice_expression": "1d17",
  "apply_mode": "add",
  "display_name": "The Conqueror's Spark",
  "current": 1, "max": 1, "category": "custom", "reset_trigger": null
}
```

The model's own `god_mode_response` text confirmed it followed the new contract: *"This feature has been integrated into the character's `resource_registry` with automated trigger logic... Trigger: Any Persuasion or Insight skill check. Effect: Automatically adds 1d17... to the final roll total."*

## Known Limitations

- This PR's real-LLM evidence covers **grant-time persistence** (confirmed). It does not include a second real-LLM scenario proving the dice-roll rubric change (`dice_system_instruction.md`) actually causes the model to roll the bonus on a *later* matching check turn in a long-running campaign — that would require a longer multi-turn real-LLM scenario. The RED/GREEN prompt-contract test does cover that instruction's text.
- Does not touch `player_character_data.features[]` (still `List[str]`) — narrative-only features are unaffected; only check-triggered custom mechanics need the new registry fields.
- Backend changes are additive validation/warnings only (see Production Code Changes) — no new persistence or inference logic.

## Unit Test Evidence

```
$ TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true python3 -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_canonicalization.py -v
Pytest: 2 passed
```

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

Real local-server + real-LLM run, 2/2 scenarios passed. Full console output, story transcript, and resulting game state: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/8bf856aca5283d19fde4b53a2967444a

## Real LLM Evidence

Raw HTTP request/response (Gemini API, `gemini-3-flash-preview`, status 200) and the resulting `player_character_data.resource_registry` entry are in the gist above (`raw_http_request_response.json`, `game_state_after_grant.json`). Evidence bundle also saved locally with checksums: `/tmp/worldarchitect.ai/fix_conqueror-spark-canonical-features/god_mode_custom_mechanic_resource_registry/iteration_003/`.

## Evidence

https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/8bf856aca5283d19fde4b53a2967444a

## User Stories

- As a player who has a custom class feature or mechanic granted via God Mode, I want that mechanic to be reliably applied on every matching check going forward, instead of having to re-explain it to the GM every few turns.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes LLM prompt contracts and game-state shape for dice mechanics; backend impact is validation/warnings only, but incorrect model behavior could still mis-apply bonuses until prompts are followed.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes God-Mode custom check bonuses (e.g. **Conqueror's Spark**) disappearing on later turns by persisting them in **`player_character_data.resource_registry`** instead of narrative-only prose.
> 
> **`resource_registry` entries** gain optional **`trigger_check_types`**, **`dice_expression`**, and **`apply_mode`** (`add` / `reroll`), documented in prompts/schema and enforced as an all-or-nothing tuple. God Mode must write these when granting check-triggered mechanics (including passive unlimited grants with `max: null`).
> 
> **Dice prompts** (`shared/dice_notation_contract.md`, loaded by both dice strategies) require scanning the registry before rolls, resolving `1d[level]` at roll time, separate roll entries, **`mechanics.combined_total`**, and decrementing limited-use entries. Explicit “resolve this check now” requests must not be answered with planning-only text.
> 
> **Server-side** changes are warning-only: registry validation in `narrative_response_schema.py` and a numeric check for `action_resolution.mechanics.combined_total`; **`game_state.schema.json`** adds the new fields plus `combined_total`. Contract hashes and unit/MCP real-LLM tests cover grant persistence and later check application.
>

title: fix(factory): Linux daemon must adopt newly labeled WorldArchitect PRs (jleechanorg/dark-factory)
description:
## Root Cause
When the Linux daemon scans factory-labeled PRs across configured repositories (including non-default repositories such as `jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai` configured under `[repos."jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai"]`):
1. `ExistingPrIntake` only recorded `bead_id`, `pr_number`, `head_ref_name`, `external_ref`, and `newly_created`. It omitted `repo` and `head_sha`.
2. `IntakeOutcome` only recorded `external_ref` and `verdict: IntakeVerdict`. It omitted `repo`, `pr_number`, `branch`, and `head_sha`.
3. Consequently, telemetry events for PR adoptions (`EXISTING_PR_ADOPTED`), branch collisions (`ESCALATION_REQUIRED`), and blocked dispositions (`SKIPPED_DUPLICATE`, `SKIPPED_FORK`, `SKIPPED_INELIGIBLE`, `ERRORED`) omitted explicit attribution for `repo`, `pr_number`, `branch`, and `head_sha`.

## Summary of Changes
- Extended `ExistingPrIntake` with `repo: String` and `head_sha: Option<String>`.
- Extended `IntakeOutcome` with `repo: Option<String>`, `pr_number: Option<u64>`, `branch: Option<String>`, and `head_sha: Option<String>`.
- Updated `normalize_labeled_prs_with_cache`, `normalize_labeled_prs`, and `normalize` in `daemon/src/intake.rs` to propagate `repo`, `pr_number`, `branch`, and `head_sha` across all intake pathways.
- Updated `emit_intake_outcome`, `EXISTING_PR_ADOPTED`, and `adoption_branch_collision` in `daemon/src/tick.rs` to serialize `repo`, `pr_number`, `branch`, and `head_sha` into the telemetry context JSON.
- Preserved duplicate suppression, candidate rotation, and cross-repo isolation.
- Added regression tests in `daemon/tests/intake.rs` and `daemon/tests/tick_integration.rs`.

## Validation
- `cargo test --test intake` (34 passed, 0 failed)
- `cargo test --test tick_integration test_non_default_repository` (2 passed, 0 failed)
- `cargo test -p daemon --lib intake::tests` (8 passed, 0 failed)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Observability-only struct and telemetry enrichment; intake gates and adoption behavior are unchanged aside from richer event context.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **repo / PR / branch / head_sha attribution** to factory intake structs and the JSONL telemetry they feed, so multi-repo sweeps (e.g. `jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai` under `[repos]`) are identifiable in logs without inferring from `external_ref` alone.
> 
> `ExistingPrIntake` gains `repo` and `head_sha`; `IntakeOutcome` gains optional `repo`, `pr_number`, `branch`, and `head_sha`. Every construction site in `normalize_labeled_prs_with_cache`, `normalize_labeled_prs`, and issue `normalize` fills those fields from the scanned repo and PR/issue payload.
> 
> In `tick.rs`, `emit_intake_outcome` merges the new fields into skip/error INTAKE events; **`EXISTING_PR_ADOPTED`** and **`adoption_branch_collision`** escalation context now include the same attributes. Intake control flow (duplicate suppression, rotation, cross-repo isolation) is unchanged.
> 
> Regression tests cover non-default-repo adoption and blocked dispositions in `intake.rs`, plus tick-level `EXISTING_PR_ADOPTED` and branch-collision telemetry in `tick_integration.rs`.
>
