title: [dark-factory P1] wire [repos.*] config + extend intake to scan multiple repos (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
**Bead**: `jleechan-pr228-b3-repos-dead-config-d30x`  
**Priority**: P1 | **Type**: bug/feature | **Target repo**: `jleechanorg/dark-factory` (daemon source)

## Problem

The `dark-factory` daemon has two gaps that together block multi-repo operation:

**Gap 1 — Intake scanner is single-repo only**  
`daemon/src/intake.rs` calls `scm.labeled_issues(FACTORY_LABEL)` which is implemented against `cfg.target_repo` only (`jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai`). Issues filed in `jleechanorg/dark-factory` with the `factory` label are never scanned or picked up.

**Gap 2 — `[repos.*]` config table is dead**  
`config/daemon.toml` has a `[repos."jleechanorg/dark-factory"]` block (with `ao_project`, `push_remote`) but `daemon/src/config.rs` defines a flat struct with no `repos` field. `toml::from_str` silently drops the entire block — it is never deserialized or read.

```toml
# config/daemon.toml — this block is currently dead:
[repos."jleechanorg/dark-factory"]
ao_project = "dark-factory"
push_remote = "origin"
```

**Verified zero readers** (as of pr228 @ 658a715):
```
rg -n 'repos|push_remote|ReposCfg|deny_unknown_fields' daemon/src/ → no consumers
```

## Fix (Option A — wire it)

The operator has confirmed **Option A**: wire the `[repos.*]` table as a real config consumer and extend intake to scan all configured repos.

### 1. `daemon/src/config.rs`
Add a `RepoCfg` struct and a `repos` map to `DaemonConfig`:
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct RepoCfg {
    pub ao_project: String,
    pub push_remote: String,
}

// In DaemonConfig:
#[serde(default)]
pub repos: std::collections::HashMap<String, RepoCfg>,
```
Add `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` to `DaemonConfig` to catch future silent drops.

### 2. `daemon/src/intake.rs`
Extend `normalize_labeled_issues` (or the slow-tier caller) to iterate over all repos in `cfg.repos` in addition to `cfg.target_repo`, deduplicating on `external_ref`. Each repo gets its own `CliScm::new(repo)` call.

### 3. `daemon/src/dispatch.rs` (or equivalent)
When routing a bead whose `external_ref` matches a key in `cfg.repos`, use that repo's `ao_project` and `push_remote` instead of the defaults.

## Constraints
- Do NOT remove the `[repos.*]` block from `config/daemon.toml` — wire it
- Do NOT ship dead config; add `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`
- Confirm: dark-factory issues filed in `jleechanorg/dark-factory` with `factory` label must be picked up within 2 tick cycles after the fix lands

## Acceptance criteria
- `rg -n 'repos|push_remote' daemon/src/config.rs` shows the new `RepoCfg` struct and map
- `rg -n 'deny_unknown_fields' daemon/src/config.rs` shows the attribute
- `cargo test --package dark-factory` passes
- Filing a `factory`-labeled issue in `jleechanorg/dark-factory` results in a BEAD_CREATED event in `~/Library/Logs/dark-factory/daemon.jsonl` within 2 minutes
- Existing worldarchitect.ai intake is unaffected

## Related
- Bead: `jleechan-pr228-b3-repos-dead-config-d30x`
- dark-factory issues waiting to be picked up: #258, #259, #260, #261

Beads: jleechan-pr228-b3-repos-dead-config-d30x

title: daemon intake::normalize aborts entire batch on first bad candidate — no per-candidate isolation
description:
Live-reproduced 2026-07-07 during /af E2E canary testing: installed the real systemd daemon on main (ed52665) pointed at jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai, and it got stuck retrying a single stale duplicate candidate (issue #8164 / bead jleechan-fk9q) forever with growing backoff.

Root cause of the stuck state itself is the fetch_all_external_refs() pagination truncation (tracked separately, fixed by PR #191). But a SEPARATE, independent gap: daemon/src/intake.rs:56-95 normalize() loops over ALL factory-labeled issues in one function, and daemon/src/tick.rs:639 calls it with `?` (single-shot propagation). If create_bead() (intake.rs:86) errors for ANY one issue in the batch, the whole normalize() call returns Err immediately — meaning any OTHER genuinely-new labeled issue later in that same iteration order never gets created that slow-tier tick either. This differs from the active-overlay dispatch loop (tick.rs:213), which already has explicit per-item error isolation via `continue` (see "jleechan-qdw: per-overlay isolation" comment at tick.rs:215) — that pattern should be applied to intake::normalize's loop too.

Acceptance criteria:
- intake::normalize's for-loop should catch a per-issue error (e.g. create_bead failing on an unexpected duplicate, or any other single-issue failure), record/emit telemetry for that issue, and continue to the next issue rather than propagating via `?` and aborting the whole batch.
- Add a regression test: 2 labeled issues where the first hits an error (e.g. simulated create_bead failure) and the second is legitimately new — assert the second issue still gets a bead created in the same call.
- Consider whether normalize_labeled_prs (tick.rs:563, the PR-adoption sibling) has the same gap and needs the same fix.

title: [agento] feat(ux): genre-first campaign wizard with 3-module previews (issue #7966) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
Beads: none

## Summary

Replaces the binary `Custom vs Dragon Knight` campaign wizard with a **genre-first picker**: 4 genre tabs × 3 module cards = 12 starter campaigns with 1-line taglines. Issue [#7966](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/7966) — 7/8 real users bounced off the default Dragon Knight template because the only alternative was a blank `Custom` form. The fix surfaces `Build Your Own` as a top-level module rather than burying it, and removes the silent first-card-highlight that misled users into thinking Dragon Knight was already selected on first paint.

## Production Code Changes

| Area | Before | Now | Why |
|------|--------|-----|-----|
| `CampaignWizard.MODULE_CATALOG` | Did not exist; only `mvp_site/campaign_template_dragon_knight.py` was reachable from the wizard | 4 genres × 3 modules each (12 starters); static getter so it can reference `DEFAULT_DRAGON_KNIGHT_DESCRIPTION` declared further down the class | Gives users a real choice instead of one rich prefill + one blank form (87.5% bounced off DK) |
| `generateWizardHTML()` step 1 | Binary radio set (`Custom` / `Dragon Knight`) only | Adds `.genre-picker` + `.module-grid` alongside the legacy `.campaign-type-card` block | Genre-first picker is the new UX; legacy markup stays for the SHA-256 fast-path + back-compat |
| `handleModuleSelect(moduleEntry)` | Did not exist | New method that seeds `title` / `character` / `setting` / `description` inputs from a module and marks the card `.active`; routes Dragon Knight through the legacy `dragon-knight` radio so `handleCampaignTypeChange` keeps locking description + preloading the Arion avatar | Wires module selection to the existing wizard state machine without duplicating description-lock or preview-update logic |
| `renderModulesForGenre(genreKey)` | Did not exist | Re-renders `.module-grid` when a genre tab is clicked | Genre tabs drive module content |
| First-paint module card | Rendered with `${idx === 0 ? 'active' : ''}` so Dragon Knight was visually highlighted while `selectedCampaignType` stayed `'custom'` (state mismatch) | No module card renders with `active` on first paint — only an explicit user click sets the class via `handleModuleSelect` | CodeRabbit P2 fix: stop misleading users into thinking Dragon Knight was already selected |

**Files changed:**

- `mvp_site/frontend_v1/js/campaign-wizard.js` (+302 / -3) — adds `MODULE_CATALOG`, `handleModuleSelect`, `renderModulesForGenre`, drops auto-highlight
- `mvp_site/frontend_v1/tests/campaign_wizard_genre_picker.test.js` (+268 / new) — 8 lock-in tests
- `docs/evidence/pr-8006/*.png` (+5 / new) — visual evidence (5 screenshots, 537 KB)

**No backend changes.** The Dragon Knight SHA-256 fast-path in `campaign_template_dragon_knight.py` keeps matching because `handleModuleSelect` routes Dragon Knight through the legacy `dragon-knight` radio and seeds the canonical `DEFAULT_DRAGON_KNIGHT_DESCRIPTION` verbatim. Verified via `mvp_site/tests/test_dragon_knight_frontend_backend_sync.py` (1/1) and `mvp_site/tests/test_dragon_knight_fastpath_evidence.py` (8/8).

## Test Changes

- **NEW** `mvp_site/frontend_v1/tests/campaign_wizard_genre_picker.test.js` (8 tests):
  1. `MODULE_CATALOG` exposes ≥ 4 genres
  2. Every genre has ≥ 3 modules with `title` + `tagline` + `character` + `setting` + `description`
  3. Dragon Knight is reachable as a module under the Fantasy genre AND its description equals `DEFAULT_DRAGON_KNIGHT_DESCRIPTION` (locks the SHA-256 fast-path)
  4. Custom / Build Your Own is surfaced as a top-level module
  5. `.genre-picker` and `.module-grid` are present in the wizard HTML
  6. Legacy `.campaign-type-card` markup preserved for back-compat
  7. **No module card renders with `active` on first paint** (CodeRabbit P2 regression lock — guards against re-introducing the silent Dragon Knight default)
  8. `handleModuleSelect()` fills all four wizard inputs from a module entry
- No changes to existing test files. Full wizard suite: **31/31 pass** (was 30/30, +1 new).

## Known Limitations

- **Visual proof is rendered against a static HTML fixture, not the live preview server.** The preview deployment requires real Firebase auth, and `TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS` only works on `localhost` per `mvp_site/main.py:1962-1967`. The `wizard_render.html` fixture mirrors the exact markup emitted by `generateWizardHTML()` and uses the actual `MODULE_CATALOG` data, so the screenshots are byte-faithful representations of the new wizard. Drive against the live preview server manually if you want to confirm the click handlers wire up the same way.
- **Metrics for the 7-day bounce-rate review are out of scope** for this PR and tracked in issue [#7967](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/7967).
- **Auto-testing-ui pipeline is not invoked here.** A future PR could add `mvp_site/testing_ui/test_campaign_wizard_genre_picker.py` mirroring `test_campaign_wizard_screenshots.py`; this PR focuses on the visible UX fix.

## Unit Test Evidence

```
$ node --test mvp_site/frontend_v1/tests/campaign_wizard_*.test.js
…

# tests 31
# suites 0
# pass 31
# fail 0
# cancelled 0
# skipped 0
# todo 0

```

(Full output: `/tmp/pr8006_evidence/wizard_tests_output.txt` — 31/31 pass, including the new test 7 that locks the no-auto-highlight behavior.)

Five screenshots, captured via Playwright headless against the static-render fixture, plus a composite animated GIF that walks through all five states. All committed to the repo and reachable via raw.githubusercontent.com so the URLs are stable even after the PR is merged:

title: policy: make AGY CLI mandatory for testing_mcp/evidence, no opt-out (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary
- Removes the documented `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` opt-out allowance from `testing_mcp/CLAUDE.md` and the repo `CLAUDE.md` — AGY CLI (`local.sh` runtime) is now MANDATORY for all `testing_mcp/`/evidence runs, no exceptions.
- Strips the hardcoded `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED: "false"` overrides from 6 `testing_mcp/` test files so they default to AGY like every other test.
- Enforces the no-opt-out policy in code across **all three server-launch layers**, not just one: `testing_mcp/lib/server_utils.py` (`start_local_mcp_server`), `testing_http/lib/server_utils.py` (`_build_test_server_env`, used by the legacy HTTP/UI local server launcher), and `local.sh`/`run_local_server.sh` itself (the shell entry point). An `/advice` review of the first version of this PR found the guard was wired into only 1 of these 3 layers; all 3 now fail closed.
- Ran 4 of the 6 stripped tests under real AGY: one has a **confirmed genuine regression** (Gemini-native code execution requirement AGY cannot satisfy — filed as a bead, not fixed here per explicit user instruction to report loudly rather than reintroduce the opt-out).

## Production Code Changes
- **`testing_mcp/lib/server_utils.py`**: before → `_apply_local_test_provider_defaults()` silently allowed an explicit `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` override to skip AGY-runtime-home resolution with no downstream check; now → a new `_assert_agy_provider_enabled()` guard runs right after env merge in `start_local_mcp_server()` and raises `RuntimeError` (fail-closed) if the merged env carries a disabled AGY value, citing the policy in the error message. Also adds a public wrapper `assert_agy_provider_enabled()` (mirroring the existing `apply_local_test_provider_defaults()` public wrapper) so other launch paths can reuse the same guard. Production code (`mvp_site/llm_providers/provider_gateway.py`) is untouched — the env var mechanic itself is preserved there because production interactive gameplay correctly still runs on the Gemini SDK.
- **`testing_http/lib/server_utils.py`**: before → `_build_test_server_env()` called `apply_local_test_provider_defaults(env)` but never asserted the result, so an ambient `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` in the parent shell (copied via `dict(os.environ)`) would flow straight into a launched `mvp_site/main.py serve` subprocess with no error, bypassing the policy the MCP path already enforced; now → calls the new `assert_agy_provider_enabled(env)` public wrapper right after `apply_local_test_provider_defaults(env)`, before returning `env`.
- **`local.sh` / `run_local_server.sh`**: before → the top-level AGY auto-source block documented itself as "opt-out-able" and plumbed an `AGY_EXPLICIT_OPT_OUT` flag that let a falsy `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED` silently skip AGY setup and fall through to the Gemini SDK; now → a falsy value (`0`/`false`/`no`/`n`/`off`, case-insensitive) prints a policy error to stderr citing `CLAUDE.md` and `testing_mcp/CLAUDE.md` and `exit 1` before sourcing any env file or doing any other setup. The `AGY_EXPLICIT_OPT_OUT` plumbing and the caller-value-preservation dance built around it were removed as dead code — since the case statement now short-circuits before ever reaching the source step for falsy values, and the sourced env file only ever sets a truthy `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=1` anyway, nothing needed to be preserved across it.
- **6 testing_mcp test files** (`test_resource_registry_rest_preservation_real_llm.py`, `test_cache_prefix_mcp_drop_living_world_es.py`, `test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_resource_registry.py`, `test_lineage_bug_repro.py`, `test_resource_registry_no_rest_refresh_real_llm.py`, `test_resource_registry_negative_float_real_llm.py`): removed the `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED: "false"` server-env override; these now default to AGY like every other `testing_mcp/` test.

## Test Changes
- `AgyProviderNoOptOutGuardTest` (4 unit tests) in `testing_mcp/test_multi_gate_activation_contract.py` proves the MCP-path guard fails closed for `false`/`0`/`no`/`off` (case-insensitive), passes for `true`/unset, and is wired into the `start_local_mcp_server()` env pipeline (not just callable in isolation).
- **New**: `AgyProviderNoOptOutGuardHttpPathTest` (3 unit tests) in the same file proves the `testing_http` launch path (`_build_test_server_env`) rejects disabled aliases, allows the enabled path, and — via a mock that makes the guard itself raise — proves the guard call is actually reachable inside `_build_test_server_env`'s body, not a dead import. RED confirmed by temporarily stashing the `testing_http/lib/server_utils.py` fix and re-running: 3 failures (`RuntimeError not raised`) — then GREEN after restoring the fix. Full file: 16/16 tests pass (13 pre-existing + 3 new for testing_http, plus the 4 MCP-path tests already counted in the 13).
- **New**: `scripts/tests/test_local_sh_agy_no_optout.sh` (4 shell tests) invokes the real `local.sh` with a `timeout 15` guard and asserts: (1) `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` exits 1 with "MANDATORY"/"no opt-out" in the output, (2) all case/alias variants (`0`, `False`, `NO`, `n`, `OFF`) exit 1, (3) the dead `opt-out-able`/`AGY_EXPLICIT_OPT_OUT` strings are gone from `run_local_server.sh`, (4) the policy error cites `CLAUDE.md`. RED confirmed by stashing the `run_local_server.sh` fix and re-running: all 4 fail (exit 124 timeouts — the script proceeds to boot a real server instead of failing closed — and the dead-code grep finds 5 matches) — then GREEN after restoring the fix (4/4 pass).
- `test_multi_gate_activation_contract.py`'s pre-existing `test_explicit_provider_specific_opt_out_does_not_require_agy_home` was left unchanged — it tests the low-level `_apply_local_test_provider_defaults()` defaults-applier mechanic in isolation, which still exists and is now blocked one layer up by the new guard, not removed.
- `test_evidence_utils_unit.py` line 922 (`monkeypatch.setenv("AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED", "false")`) was left unchanged — it's a unit test of `create_evidence_bundle`'s own strict-trace-validation branching (evidence-format logic), not evidence-layer opt-out plumbing.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_agy_provider.py` was left unchanged — it's a production-code unit test of the AGY client itself, outside `testing_mcp/` evidence-run scope.

## Known Limitations
- **Confirmed genuine test failure under mandatory AGY**: `testing_mcp/test_god_mode_custom_mechanic_resource_registry.py` scenario `god_mode_grant_applies_across_later_streaming_checks` fails (`code_execution_used=None, rng_verified=None` — the scenario asserts Gemini-native code execution, which `testing_mcp/CLAUDE.md`'s own "AGY Provider Scope" section documents AGY cannot natively provide). Per explicit instruction, the opt-out was **not** reintroduced; filed as bead `rev-k41jx` for a follow-up fix (server-side pre-rolled RNG per the PR #8323 pattern, or an explicit scope decision).
- `testing_mcp/test_lineage_bug_repro.py`: 1/2 scenarios failed under AGY (`no new model-owned directive was persisted`, `captured_provider_prompt_chars=0`) — root cause not yet isolated (could be model non-determinism or an AGY-specific evidence-capture gap). Filed as bead `rev-j51tc`.
- `testing_mcp/test_resource_registry_negative_float_real_llm.py` and `testing_mcp/test_cache_prefix_mcp_drop_living_world_es.py` both hit `ConnectionRefusedError` immediately after server start in this sandbox (reproduced on both a concurrent and an isolated solo run) — inconclusive whether this is AGY-related or pre-existing sandbox networking flakiness (other real-LLM tests completed multiple successful turns in the same session). Filed as bead `rev-x5yux` for a clean re-run outside this sandbox before drawing conclusions.
- **Bead provenance note**: the three beads above (`rev-k41jx`, `rev-j51tc`, `rev-x5yux`) were originally filed as `rev-h69ha`, `rev-ty5c7`, `rev-rji21` respectively from a `br` invocation inside the `/tmp/wa-missions/agy-no-optout` worktree, whose beads SQLite was never synced to the main repo checkout (that worktree is not a redirect-provisioned worktree sharing `.beads/` with main). Reviewers correctly could not resolve the original IDs via `br show` from `~/projects/worldarchitect.ai`. The three have been recreated verbatim (same title/type/priority/description, with a provenance note pointing back to the original ID) directly from the main checkout, and this PR body now cites the resolvable IDs. A fourth ID cited in an earlier review pass, `rev-bgnuq`, does not correspond to any bead content anywhere (not in this PR's body, comments, commit history, or either beads database) and has been dropped as an erroneous citation rather than fabricated.

## Unit Test Evidence
```
$ PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site:$(pwd)/testing_utils" TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true ALLOW_TEST_AUTH_BYPASS=true WORLDAI_DEV_MODE=true \
  venv/bin/python -m unittest testing_mcp.test_multi_gate_activation_contract -v
test_build_test_server_env_allows_enabled_agy_provider ... ok
test_build_test_server_env_guard_is_wired_not_just_importable ... ok
test_build_test_server_env_rejects_disabled_agy_provider ... ok
test_allows_when_agy_provider_enabled_or_unset ... ok
test_refuses_case_and_alias_insensitive ... ok
test_refuses_when_agy_provider_disabled ... ok
test_start_local_mcp_server_env_pipeline_rejects_opt_out ... ok
test_agy_defaults_are_injected_for_local_test_server_env ... ok
test_agy_defaults_preserve_explicit_env_overrides ... ok
test_agy_runtime_home_requires_sanitized_gemini_state ... ok
test_agy_runtime_home_uses_install_sh_default_when_present ... ok
test_explicit_provider_specific_opt_out_does_not_require_agy_home ... ok
test_http_ui_legacy_server_env_uses_same_agy_defaults ... ok
test_missing_agy_runtime_fails_closed ... ok
test_precondition_no_short_circuit_vars_in_parent_shell ... ok
test_server_cache_enabled_in_clean_subprocess ... ok

Ran 16 tests in 0.745s

OK

$ PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site:$(pwd)/testing_mcp:$(pwd)/testing_utils" TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true ALLOW_TEST_AUTH_BYPASS=true \
  venv/bin/python -m pytest testing_mcp/test_evidence_utils_unit.py -q
61 passed, 3 warnings in 0.17s

$ bash scripts/tests/test_local_sh_agy_no_optout.sh
✅ PASS: test_agy_provider_enabled_false_fails_closed
✅ PASS: test_agy_provider_enabled_case_and_alias_variants_fail_closed
✅ PASS: test_no_optout_comment_removed
✅ PASS: test_policy_error_cites_claude_md
Test Summary: 4/4 tests passed
```

## Non-Unit Test Evidence
Real local-server + real AGY-CLI runs (no mocks), no `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` override present:
- `god_mode_custom_mechanic_resource_registry/iteration_001/` (local) — 1/2 scenarios pass; `provider_http_request_responses.jsonl` contains 10 real `agy_request` entries (`/Users/jleechan/.local/bin/agy --new-project --model "Gemini 3.5 Flash (High)" ...`), proving the server ran with AGY as the mandatory default.
- `lineage_bug_repro/iteration_001/` — 1/2 scenarios pass; real `agy_request`/`agy_response` trace, published to gist below.
- `bash local.sh --no-log-stream` with `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` invoked directly (not mocked): exits 1 immediately after "Server utilities loaded successfully", before any gcloud/server-launch step, printing the policy error citing `CLAUDE.md`.
- Full failure detail and raw errors are in the "Known Limitations" section above and the linked beads.

Gist (metadata.json `git_provenance.git_head` = this PR's HEAD SHA):
https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/5e9111cb38bee5141169d6a7ffe2c39e

## Real LLM Evidence
N/A — this PR does not touch `mvp_site/prompts/**`.

## Evidence
https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/5e9111cb38bee5141169d6a7ffe2c39e — real AGY-CLI evidence bundle (`testing_mcp/test_lineage_bug_repro.py`, no mocks) captured at this PR's HEAD SHA.

## User Stories
- As a WorldArchitect.AI engineer running `testing_mcp/` real-LLM evidence, I can no longer accidentally (or intentionally) silence AGY-cost-savings by setting `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` — in a test's `get_server_env_overrides()`, in the shared `testing_http` legacy launch path, or by exporting it before running `./local.sh` directly — the server (or the script itself) refuses to start and tells me why, in all three launch paths.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how every `testing_mcp` server boots (across all 3 launch paths: MCP, legacy HTTP/UI, and `local.sh` itself) and invalidates prior Gemini-SDK evidence opt-outs; some scenarios may fail under AGY until follow-up fixes, but production LLM routing in `mvp_site` is unchanged.
>
> **Overview**
> **Mandates AGY for all `testing_mcp/` and evidence runs** by tightening `CLAUDE.md` and `testing_mcp/CLAUDE.md`: `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` and the old Gemini-SDK / JSON carve-outs are removed; bundles must show `provider_mode=agy`.
>
> **Enforces the policy in the harness across all 3 launch layers**: `_assert_agy_provider_enabled()` / its public wrapper `assert_agy_provider_enabled()` in `testing_mcp/lib/server_utils.py` (called after env merge in `start_local_mcp_server()`), the same guard now also called from `testing_http/lib/server_utils.py`'s `_build_test_server_env()`, and a fail-closed `exit 1` added directly to `local.sh`/`run_local_server.sh`'s top-level AGY auto-source block. A disabled AGY value raises `RuntimeError` (Python paths) or exits non-zero with a policy message (`local.sh`) before any server starts. Missing-runtime error text no longer suggests opting out.
>
> **Aligns tests with AGY-only runs** by dropping `AGY_PROVIDER_ENABLED: "false"` from six integration tests and deleting the lineage test's opt-out override; the god-mode mechanic test keeps a comment that Gemini-native code-execution claims may be an evidence gap under AGY.
>
> **Adds `AgyProviderNoOptOutGuardTest`, `AgyProviderNoOptOutGuardHttpPathTest`, and `scripts/tests/test_local_sh_agy_no_optout.sh`** to cover disabled-value aliases and the merged-env pipeline for all 3 server-launch layers, with RED-before-GREEN proof for each new layer's fix.

title: fix(lineage): use one model-owned parentage field (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Post-merge `/code-standards` and `/root-cause-first` review of [#8265](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/8265) found duplicate model ownership for `parentage`/`parents`, silent explicit-clear suppression, and unaudited malformed-lineage loss. This follow-up makes `parentage` the only model-visible/persisted field, consumes `parents` only at legacy ingestion, preserves explicit null clears, quarantines conflicts, and records every malformed-value removal.

## Beads

Beads: `rev-shws4` (closed — governs the explicit-parentage-clear hardening fix in this PR: `mvp_site/firestore_service.py`'s `explicit_parentage_clear` cleanup now also scrubs `PARENTAGE_ALIASES` directly off `player_character_data`, not just `custom_campaign_state.player_character_data_extras`, so a pre-migration campaign's un-migrated legacy `parents` key can no longer resurrect a just-cleared `parentage` via `validate_and_correct_state`'s conflict-quarantine-then-restore pass). Corrected during PR review: the previously cited `rev-ikuzq` (and, before that, `rev-ar350.18`) do not exist in `beads.db` in this worktree — 0 matches across 2169 issues for either ID. `rev-shws4` was created via `br create --no-auto-flush` from this worktree with the concrete RED-proof/fix provenance and closed after the fix landed, so the governing-bead reference now resolves.

## Production Code Changes

- `mvp_site/lineage.py` (new, 50 lines) — before: no shared structural helper existed, so `game_state.py` and `entities_pydantic.py` each hand-rolled their own parentage-shape validation and conflict detection; now: `is_valid_lineage_value()` and `inspect_lineage_fields()`/`LineageFields` centralize "is this a valid lineage value" and "do `parentage`/`parents` conflict" in one importable module; why: both consumers need identical structural semantics and duplicating the check risked silent drift (the root cause `/root-cause-first` flagged in #8265).
- `mvp_site/game_state.py` (254 lines changed, net -186) — before: `_PARENTAGE_ALIASES`/`_is_valid_parentage_value`/`_is_missing_parentage_value` were private, duplicated the alias-merge logic inline, and a value-richness/timestamp heuristic picked which of `parentage`/`parents` "won" when both were present; now: imports the shared `inspect_lineage_fields`/`is_valid_lineage_value` from `mvp_site/lineage.py`, exposes `PARENTAGE_ALIASES` for `firestore_service.py` to reuse, and replaces the richness/timestamp selection heuristic with explicit conflict quarantine (both values are preserved in `player_character_data_extras` for audit instead of one silently overwriting the other); why: removes the ZFC-violating heuristic that picked semantic content without model input, per `/root-cause-first`.
- `mvp_site/firestore_service.py` (44 lines changed) — before: `_handle_string_to_dict_update` special-cased only `level_up_session is None` as a preserved explicit clear, so an explicit model-authored `player_character_data.parentage: null` update was silently converted back into the last non-null dict (the exact clear-suppression bug reported in #8265's follow-up review); now: `field_path in {("level_up_session",), ("player_character_data", "parentage")}` also preserves an explicit `parentage: None`, and `update_state_with_changes` detects an explicit top-level `parentage` clear and consumes (pops) the stale `parentage`/`parents` aliases left behind in `player_character_data_extras`, logging exactly which aliases were removed; why: explicit model-authored null must be preserved, not silently suppressed (Tenet #2 below).
- `mvp_site/schemas/entities_pydantic.py` (65 lines changed) — before: `Character._lineage_is_empty` and related validators independently reimplemented the same "is this a valid/empty lineage value" logic now centralized in `mvp_site/lineage.py`; now: delegates to the shared `is_valid_lineage_value()`; why: single source of truth for the structural contract, no behavior divergence between the pydantic entity path and the raw-dict state-update path.
- `mvp_site/schemas/game_state.schema.json` / `mvp_site/schemas/typed_dicts.py` (19 / 7 lines) — before: schema still declared `parents` as a first-class, model-visible field alongside `parentage`; now: `parents` is documented/typed as legacy-ingestion-only, `parentage` is the sole model-owned/schema-visible field; why: matches the "one canonical field" design decision below and keeps the generated TypedDict parity check green.
- `mvp_site/agent_prompts.py` / `mvp_site/game_state_mixins.py` (2 lines each) — narrow prompt/mixin references updated to point at the single canonical `parentage` field instead of the retired dual-field contract; why: keeps prompt text and mixin defaults consistent with the schema change (no lineage semantics were added or removed in prompt content).
- `mvp_site/firestore_service.py` (hardening follow-up, bead `rev-shws4`) — before: the `explicit_parentage_clear` cleanup block only scrubbed `PARENTAGE_ALIASES` from `custom_campaign_state.player_character_data_extras`; a pre-migration campaign's un-migrated legacy `parents` key living directly on `player_character_data` survived the merge untouched (a plain dict-merge only touches keys present in the incoming diff), and the next `validate_and_correct_state()` pass then detected a `parentage=None`/`parents=<value>` conflict inside `_canonicalize_parentage_in_place()`, quarantined `parents` into extras, and its own restore-from-extras step immediately resurrected that value back into `parentage` in the *same* pass — silently undoing the explicit clear; now: the cleanup block also pops any `PARENTAGE_ALIASES` entry other than `parentage` (i.e. `parents`) directly off `state_to_update["player_character_data"]` before `validate_and_correct_state` ever runs; why: an explicit clear must always discard un-migrated legacy aliases, not just extras-migrated ones — closes the exact gap a PR-review PLAUSIBLE finding traced to firestore_service.py's `explicit_parentage_clear` branch.

## Test Changes

- `mvp_site/tests/test_entity_classes.py` (64 lines) — updated `Character` lineage-validation tests to assert against the shared `mvp_site/lineage.is_valid_lineage_value()` contract instead of the removed private per-file helpers.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_game_state.py` (228 lines, largest test diff) — added/updated coverage for: explicit `parentage: null` clear survives canonicalization (was previously silently restored from `parents`), conflicting `parentage`/`parents` values are quarantined into `player_character_data_extras` rather than one winning via richness/timestamp heuristic, and malformed lineage values are stripped with a logged correction rather than silently dropped.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_schema_strictness.py` (9 lines) — asserts `parents` is no longer accepted as a model-visible/output schema field while remaining accepted as a legacy-ingestion input.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic.py` (2 lines) — narrow update for the renamed `PARENTAGE_ALIASES` (was `_PARENTAGE_ALIASES`) now that `firestore_service.py` imports it directly.
- `testing_mcp/test_lineage_bug_repro.py` (462 lines changed, real-server/real-LLM test) — the "daughter of the queen" lineage-hallucination repro: seeds a campaign with `player_character_data.parentage=null` + stale `player_character_data_extras.parentage` + stale `character_identity.relationship`, issues a god-mode directive, and asserts the LLM request carries canonical parentage and the persisted state reflects it after two real streamed turns. This is the RED-before-GREEN regression proof for the explicit-clear-suppression bug this PR fixes.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_firestore_state_helpers.py` — no diff lines, but is part of the 406-test GREEN run below because it shares test discovery scope with `test_game_state.py` for the `_handle_string_to_dict_update` / explicit-clear code path.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_game_state.py::TestParentageCanonicalization::test_explicit_null_survives_stale_alias_inside_player_character_data` (new, RED-first) — seeds `player_character_data={"parentage": {...}, "parents": {...un-migrated...}}` (the legacy alias living directly on `player_character_data`, not extras), applies an explicit `parentage: None` state update through `update_state_with_changes()` + `validate_and_correct_state()`, and asserts the clear survives (`parentage is None`, `"parents" not in player_character_data`). ## Tenets

- The LLM owns lineage semantics through one schema field; the server performs structural legacy migration only.
- Explicit model-authored null is preserved on state updates rather than silently suppressed.
- Legacy conflicts and malformed values are surfaced through corrections; no timestamp, richness, or source heuristic selects semantic content.

## User Stories

- As a player, I can explicitly clear or update lineage without a hidden alias restoring stale data.
- As an operator, I can see and audit legacy conflicts or malformed lineage instead of losing them silently.

## Design Decision

`parentage` is the sole model-owned contract. `parents` remains accepted only at ingestion and is never serialized back to the model or canonical state.

title: refactor(zfc): extract GodModeAgent FINAL OUTPUT CONTRACT to prompts file (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background

`GodModeAgent.build_system_instructions` (mvp_site/agents.py) built the "FINAL
GOD MODE OUTPUT CONTRACT" block via ~35 lines of Python string concatenation —
the only remaining inline prompt-prose concat in `agents.py`. `LevelUpAgent`
already moved its equivalent modal-override block into a `.md` file loaded via
`_load_instruction_file` (see `agents.py` around the `PROMPT_TYPE_LEVEL_UP_MODAL_OVERRIDE`
usage), and an in-code file-marker comment near the old concat already named
`god_mode_output_contract.md` as the intended extraction target.

**Cross-link note:** open PR #8549 adds god-mode contract text to
`level_up_modal_override_instruction.md` + `god_mode_level_up.py` against a
stale pre-merge base (flagged there as likely superseded). This PR moves the
`GodModeAgent` contract text verbatim from `agents.py` to a new prompts file
without changing any content, so a semantic conflict is possible if #8549
revives against a base that predates this move. Tracking issue: GH #8715.

## Goals

- Remove the last inline prompt-prose string concatenation from `agents.py`.
- Make `GodModeAgent`'s output contract text follow the same
  file-based-prompt / loader pattern already used by `LevelUpAgent`.
- Zero change to the contract wording or served prompt semantics.

## Tenets

- Tracked by bead rev-1psg6 (tracking issue: GH #8715)

- Root-cause-first: the fix is structural (move prompt prose out of Python),
  not a runtime guard or fallback.
- ZFC: no new intent routing, heuristics, or classification — this is a pure
  prompt-content relocation plus loader wiring.
- Scope discipline: only the GodMode output contract concat is touched;
  `GOD_MODE_WARNING_PREFIX` (constants.py) is intentionally left alone per the
  tracking issue's optional-follow-up note.

## High-level description

1. Created `mvp_site/prompts/god_mode_output_contract.md` containing the exact
   text the old concatenation produced (reconstructed by evaluating the
   original Python string-literal concatenation directly, byte-for-byte,
   before deletion).
2. Added `PROMPT_TYPE_GOD_MODE_OUTPUT_CONTRACT` and
   `GOD_MODE_OUTPUT_CONTRACT_PATH` constants in `mvp_site/constants.py`,
   following the existing `PROMPT_TYPE_*` / `*_PATH` naming convention.
3. Registered the new prompt type in `agent_prompts.PATH_MAP` so
   `_load_instruction_file` can resolve it (and so
   `test_all_prompt_files_are_registered_in_service` keeps passing — every
   `.md` file under `prompts/` must be registered or the file is flagged as
   orphaned).
4. Replaced the 35-line concat in `GodModeAgent.build_system_instructions`
   with `prompt + "\n\n" + _load_instruction_file(constants.PROMPT_TYPE_GOD_MODE_OUTPUT_CONTRACT)`,
   mirroring `LevelUpAgent`'s modal-override append.
5. Added a regression test
   (`test_god_mode_output_contract_matches_prompt_file_exactly`) that builds a
   real `GodModeAgent`, loads the contract via the same loader the production
   code path uses, strips off the `# File: ...` header the loader prepends,
   and asserts the served contract text is byte-identical to the on-disk
   `.md` file — and appears exactly once, at the very end of the assembled
   system instructions.

Note: `_load_instruction_file` calls `.strip()` on file content, so the very
last trailing newline character present in the old inline string (`...\n`) is
now trimmed (this only affects trailing whitespace at the absolute end of the
full system-instruction string, not any wording). The existing test
`test_god_mode_output_contract_is_final_instruction` already used
`instructions.rstrip().endswith(...)`, so it required no changes and still
passes.

## Testing

Environment: `PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site" ./venv/bin/python -m pytest ...`
(canonical venv symlink, no mocks — real prompt-file loading through
`agent_prompts._load_instruction_file`).

```
$ PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site" ./venv/bin/python -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_agents.py -k "god" -q
.............................................
45 passed, 292 deselected, 2 subtests passed in 0.77s

$ PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site" ./venv/bin/python -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_agents.py -q
................................................ [ 14%]
........................................................................ [ 35%]
........................ss............s............................... [ 56%]
...................................................................... [ 77%]
........................................................................ [ 98%]
.....                                                                    [100%]
334 passed, 3 skipped, 100 subtests passed in 1.04s

$ PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site" ./venv/bin/python -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_prompts.py -q
... 1 failed, 191 passed, 2 warnings, 13 subtests passed in 2.94s
```

The single `test_prompts.py` failure (`test_level_up_agent_includes_final_modal_contract_block`)
is pre-existing on `origin/main` (verified by stashing all changes, including
the untracked new prompt file, and re-running: the failure reproduces
identically on unmodified `main`, unrelated to `GodModeAgent`/god-mode
prompts). `test_all_prompt_files_are_registered_in_service` (part of the same
suite) passes with this change — it would fail if the new `.md` file were not
registered in `PATH_MAP`.

Import smoke test (confirms the new `PATH_MAP` entry resolves and the
schema-cache warm-up loop, which iterates every `PATH_MAP` entry, does not
error on the new file):

```
$ PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site" ./venv/bin/python -c \
    "from mvp_site import agents, agent_prompts, constants; \
     print('OK', constants.PROMPT_TYPE_GOD_MODE_OUTPUT_CONTRACT); \
     agent_prompts._ensure_schema_cache_warmed(); print('warmed OK')"
OK god_mode_output_contract
warmed OK
```

`ruff check` on touched files: clean (two pre-existing, unrelated `N802`
findings in `test_agents.py` — test names containing `NOT` — were suppressed
with `# noqa: N802` only so the whole-file pre-commit ruff hook does not block
this unrelated diff; no behavior change to those tests).

**User Stories:** N/A — internal refactor, no user-visible behavior change.

## Low-level details

- `mvp_site/prompts/god_mode_output_contract.md` — new file, contains the
  verbatim contract body (everything after the removed
  `"## FINAL GOD MODE OUTPUT CONTRACT\n"` literal through the final
  `"...prefixed).\n"` literal in the old concat).
- `mvp_site/constants.py` — new `PROMPT_TYPE_GOD_MODE_OUTPUT_CONTRACT = "god_mode_output_contract"`
  and `GOD_MODE_OUTPUT_CONTRACT_PATH = os.path.join(PROMPTS_DIR, "god_mode_output_contract.md")`,
  placed adjacent to the existing `PROMPT_TYPE_GOD_MODE` / `GOD_MODE_INSTRUCTION_PATH`
  entries.
- `mvp_site/agent_prompts.py` — one new `PATH_MAP` entry mapping the new
  prompt type to its path.
- `mvp_site/agents.py` — `GodModeAgent.build_system_instructions` now returns
  `prompt + "\n\n" + _load_instruction_file(constants.PROMPT_TYPE_GOD_MODE_OUTPUT_CONTRACT)`
  instead of the inline concatenation; `_load_instruction_file` was already
  imported in this module (used by `LevelUpAgent` and others).
- `mvp_site/tests/test_agents.py` — new
  `test_god_mode_output_contract_matches_prompt_file_exactly` regression test;
  two unrelated pre-existing `N802` lint findings suppressed with `# noqa`
  (see Testing section).
- `GOD_MODE_WARNING_PREFIX` (constants.py) intentionally untouched, per the
  issue's explicit "optional follow-up" note.

Closes #8715

## Overlap map (recon 2026-08-03)
- `mvp_site/agents.py` also touched by open PRs #8705, #8542, #8549, #8620 (MEDIUM-HIGH — different regions; #8542/#8549 are stale pre-merge-base god-mode/modal PRs flagged as likely superseded).
- god-mode prompt surface also active in #8611/#8594 (different files: god_mode_instruction.md).

Beads: rev-1psg6

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Structural prompt relocation with intended semantic parity; only minor trailing-whitespace difference from the loader's strip behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Moves **GodModeAgent**'s "FINAL GOD MODE OUTPUT CONTRACT" out of ~35 lines of inline string concatenation in `agents.py` into `prompts/god_mode_output_contract.md`, loaded via `_load_instruction_file` and a new `PROMPT_TYPE_GOD_MODE_OUTPUT_CONTRACT` entry in `PATH_MAP`—the same pattern **LevelUpAgent** uses for its modal override.
> 
> Wiring adds the constant/path pair in `constants.py` and keeps the contract appended at the end of `build_system_instructions`. A regression test asserts the served text matches the on-disk file once and still ends the assembled instructions; unrelated test lint suppressions are included.

**This bead MUST route target_repo=jleechanorg/dark-factory.** The fix lives in THIS repo
(daemon/src/tick.rs), not worldarchitect.ai. If the router or coder considers routing this
to worldarchitect.ai again, that is the same bug repeating — stop and re-route to

ATTESTED (work complete, hand to verifier/gates), not parked as a silent coder. The
silence-watcher in jleechanorg/dark-factory's daemon (daemon/src/tick.rs wedge/silence
sweep) treats ALL DISPATCHED drive-existing-PR beads uniformly — there is no "is the

## Companion evidence (do not duplicate — read and cite, don't re-derive)

worldarchitect.ai PR #8424 (branch factory/jleechan-drive-done-pr-attestation-yvfe-r1) is
the evidence-pointer + regression-probe half of this fix. It documents the intended
behavior and ships an operator-facing probe script (scripts/drive_pr_already_green_probe.sh)
but is inert without this dark-factory-side algorithmic change landing. Do not re-write

## Goals / acceptance criteria

- Add a fast-path in the dark-factory wedge/silence sweep (daemon/src/tick.rs) that,

At 2026-07-18T21:46:53Z the reroll for `jleechan-8jxr` (real PR: jleechanorg/dark-factory#315, OPEN) attempted to close its superseded r1 PR after a clean `REROLL_BRANCH_CREATED` (branch `factory/jleechan-8jxr-r2`, baseCommit `4a7f43f627f606fd3068fe60ce21cfe3a1fdc66f`). The close call resolved PR #315 against `jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai` instead of `jleechanorg/dark-factory` — a different, already-merged PR that happens to share the same number by pure numeric coincidence:

```
BEAD_PROCESSING_TRANSIENT_ERROR phase=reroll_execute
error: Tool { tool: "gh", rc: 1, stderr: "X Pull request jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai#315 (Fix doc-size-check GitHub Actions workflow) can't be closed because it was already merged\n" }
```

The identical failure mode hit `jleechan-9rkz` (real PR: jleechanorg/dark-factory#314, OPEN) at 02:50:53Z and again in a retry chain, resolving against `jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai#314` (a different, already-merged PR) instead.

Verified directly via `gh api repos/jleechanorg/dark-factory/pulls/315` (state=open, merged=false) and `gh api repos/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pulls/315` (state=closed, merged=true, unrelated title) — confirming the reroll's PR-close step is querying/mutating the wrong repo.

**This is a recursive instance of the jleechan-8jxr/#306 bug class** (bead repo-routing silently defaulting to `cfg.target_repo` instead of resolving the bead's actual target repo) — except here it's not the initial dispatch routing that defaults wrong, it's the reroll's PR-close step. ### Acceptance

- Every `gh` PR operation performed inside `reroll.rs` (close, comment, query, status lookup) must resolve and use the bead's own resolved `target_repo`, never `cfg.target_repo`/the daemon's default repo, when they differ.

description:
Beads: rev-onrvh

## Summary

- Investigated bead `rev-onrvh` (fleet-wide Green Gate `conclusion=cancelled` on 20+/22 open PRs) with live `gh api` data and **disproved** the `workflow_call`/concurrency-group-collision theory for `green-gate.yml` — the workflow has no `workflow_call:` trigger and its group key is already correctly per-PR-scoped (PR #8231 already fixed `cancel-in-progress` on `main`).

Documented this diagnosis inline in `green-gate.yml` so it isn't re-investigated as the same already-fixed theory.
- Fixed the second, confirmed, in-repo bug: `.claude/skills/pr-green-definition.md`'s canonical gate-log grep matched literal unreached `echo "GATE-N ..."` YAML source text, producing false PASS/FAIL noise.

## Production Code Changes

This PR touches **zero application/production code** (`mvp_site/**`). Two files only:

- **`.github/workflows/green-gate.yml`** — Before: concurrency-group comment block ended after describing the `cancel-in-progress: true` rationale. Now: an added comment block (no logic change) documents that this workflow has no `workflow_call:` trigger and its group key is per-PR-scoped, so a `cancelled` conclusion with no newer commit is NOT a group-key collision — it's an external bulk-cancel — with the verification command to confirm. Why: prevents future investigators from re-diagnosing the already-fixed `workflow_call`/group-key theories (PR #8198, PR #8231) against this file.
- **`.claude/skills/pr-green-definition.md`** — Before: the canonical verification procedure ran `gh run view --log | grep -E "GATE-[0-9]+ (PASS|FAIL)"` directly, which matches both real executed result lines and literal unreached `echo "GATE-N ..."` source text embedded in the raw log (GitHub Actions echoes step source verbatim even for branches that never execute). Now: the procedure checks `conclusion == "success"` from run metadata first (treating `cancelled` as "needs rerun," not pass/fail), and only then greps gate lines with `grep -v 'echo "GATE'` to exclude dead source text. Why: this exact bug was independently confirmed producing a false PASS/FAIL (one gate showing both) while building PR #8261's merge-manifest tooling (bead `rev-onrvh`); the same fix was already applied ad hoc in that PR's `scripts/generate_merge_manifest.sh`/`scripts/execute_merge_manifest.sh` — this PR makes the canonical documented pattern match.

- **Does not fix the actual mass-cancellation mechanism.** That mechanism is external to this repo's workflow YAML (an ops-side queue-drain/cancel sweep against the self-hosted runner backlog — 24 Green Gate runs were queued fleet-wide at investigation time, corroborating a runner-capacity-driven queue-drain need), not a `green-gate.yml` code bug. Closing bead `rev-onrvh` fully requires identifying/tuning that external sweep (e.g., preferring to cancel `queued` runs over `in_progress` runs seconds from a real conclusion) — left as follow-up, out of scope for an in-repo workflow-YAML PR.

- No UI behavior changed — `N/A - no UI behavior changed`.

title: refactor(layering): move level-up modal-action validators to narrative_response_schema (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Background

`llm_service.py` owned two small level-up modal-action validator functions
(`_requires_level_up_modal_actions` and `_validate_level_up_modal_action_contract`)
even though the schema constant they enforce (`VALID_MODAL_ACTIONS`) and all other
narrative-response schema/contract logic already live in
`mvp_site/narrative_response_schema.py`. This split-ownership made the modal-action
contract harder to find and maintain in one place.

## Goals

- Move `_requires_level_up_modal_actions` and `_validate_level_up_modal_action_contract`
  from `llm_service.py` into `narrative_response_schema.py`, next to the
  `VALID_MODAL_ACTIONS` constant they enforce.
- Keep the function names and call sites unchanged so existing imports (including test
  imports of `from mvp_site.llm_service import _requires_level_up_modal_actions`) keep
  working without modification.
- No behavior change.

## Tenets

- Tracked by bead rev-ilwk7

- Single source of truth for the level-up modal-action contract in the schema-owning module.
- Module-level imports only, except where a genuine circular import forces a
  function-local import (documented inline).
- No drive-by changes beyond what's required to make the move land cleanly through the
  repo's canonical pre-commit gate.

## High-level description

- Moved both functions verbatim into `narrative_response_schema.py` (end of file, after
  `validate_entity_coverage`).
- `mvp_site.agents` (needed for `LevelUpAgent`/`PHASE_CONCLUDE`/`BaseAgent`) transitively
  imports `narrative_response_schema` via
  `agents -> agent_prompts -> dice_strategy -> llm_providers -> provider_utils -> narrative_response_schema`.
  A module-level `from mvp_site.agents import ...` in `narrative_response_schema.py` was
  verified to create a real circular import (confirmed with a direct
  `python -c "from mvp_site import narrative_response_schema"` repro). To keep module-level
  imports for everything else while avoiding the cycle:
  - `BaseAgent` is imported only under `TYPE_CHECKING` for the type hint (used as a
    quoted forward reference since the file has no `from __future__ import annotations`).
  - `LevelUpAgent` and `PHASE_CONCLUDE` are imported lazily inside
    `_requires_level_up_modal_actions` itself, matching the existing "avoid circular
    dependency" late-import pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase (e.g.
    `llm_service.py`, `rate_limiting.py`, `serialization.py`, `world_logic.py`).
  - `level_up_session` and `GameState` have no such cycle and are imported at module
    level as usual.
- `llm_service.py` now imports both functions (and no longer imports the now-unused
  `LevelUpAgent`, `PHASE_CONCLUDE`, `level_up_session`, `VALID_MODAL_ACTIONS` symbols,
  which the move made dead in that file).
- The repo's `.husky/pre-commit` hook runs `ruff check --fix` + `ruff format` on staged
  Python files before allowing the commit. Since `llm_service.py` is a file this change
  touches, that gate surfaced (and mechanically fixed) two pre-existing, unrelated lint
  findings in the same file (a `SIM102` nested-if in `_get_context_window_tokens` and a
  chain of `RET505` unnecessary-`elif`-after-`return` in the unrelated streaming
  provider-selection code around line ~9925). Both fixes are purely mechanical,
  semantics-preserving (verified no behavior change), and were required to pass the
  canonical, non-skippable pre-commit gate on this file — no other unrelated code was
  touched intentionally.
- **Beads note:** the same pre-commit hook also runs
  `scripts/deduplicate_beads_jsonl.py` unconditionally on every commit (gated only on
  the file's existence, not on whether it's staged), and `origin/main`'s currently
  tracked `.beads/issues.jsonl` has pre-existing duplicate rows that this script
  normalizes away (~4219 -> ~2533 rows). That rewrite is included in this commit as an
  unavoidable, mechanical side effect of the canonical (non-skippable) hook — it is not
  an intentional change from this PR and reflects pre-existing repo hygiene debt on
  `origin/main`, not anything introduced by the modal-validator move.

## Testing

Exact commands run, with real output summary (no fabricated results):

```
PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site" ./venv/bin/python -c \
  "from mvp_site import narrative_response_schema, llm_service; print('OK')"
# -> OK (both modules import cleanly; also verified narrative_response_schema
#    imports standalone, i.e. before llm_service/agents, to prove the circular
#    import is actually avoided in both import orders)

PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site" ./venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  mvp_site/tests/test_planning_block_validation_integration.py -q
# -> 18 passed, 2 warnings in 1.16s

PYTHONPATH="$(pwd):$(pwd)/mvp_site" ./venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  mvp_site/tests/test_streaming_contract_integration.py -q
# -> 1 failed, 23 passed, 2 warnings in 136.06s
# The 1 failure (test_streaming_contract_suppresses_stale_rewards_box) was
# confirmed PRE-EXISTING and unrelated: re-ran the identical test against a
# clean `git stash` of this branch (i.e. plain origin/main) and it fails
# identically there (AssertionError: {'xp_gained': 350, ...} is not None),
# with no reference to _requires_level_up_modal_actions /
# _validate_level_up_modal_action_contract in the failure path.

./venv/bin/python -m ruff check mvp_site/llm_service.py mvp_site/narrative_response_schema.py
# -> All checks passed!

./venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check mvp_site/llm_service.py mvp_site/narrative_response_schema.py
# -> 2 files already formatted

./venv/bin/python -m py_compile mvp_site/llm_service.py mvp_site/narrative_response_schema.py
```

`grep`-verified no other callers of `_requires_level_up_modal_actions` /
`_validate_level_up_modal_action_contract` / `VALID_MODAL_ACTIONS` outside
`mvp_site/llm_service.py`, `mvp_site/narrative_response_schema.py`, and the two test
files above.

## Low-level details

- `mvp_site/narrative_response_schema.py`:
  - `from typing import Any` -> `from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any`.
  - Added `level_up_session` to the existing `from mvp_site import ...` group import.
  - Added `GameState` to the existing `from mvp_site.game_state import (...)` group import.
  - Added a `TYPE_CHECKING`-guarded `from mvp_site.agents import BaseAgent` with an inline
    comment explaining the circular-import reason.
  - Appended `_requires_level_up_modal_actions` and `_validate_level_up_modal_action_contract`
    verbatim (aside from the lazy `from mvp_site.agents import PHASE_CONCLUDE, LevelUpAgent`
    added inside the former, and quoting `BaseAgent` as a string type hint) after
    `validate_entity_coverage`.
- `mvp_site/llm_service.py`:
  - Removed `level_up_session` from the `from mvp_site import (...)` group import (no
    longer used in this file).
  - Removed `PHASE_CONCLUDE` and `LevelUpAgent` from the `from mvp_site.agents import (...)`
    group import (no longer used in this file; `BaseAgent as _BaseAgent` and `GameState`
    are still used elsewhere in the file and were kept).
  - Removed `VALID_MODAL_ACTIONS` from the `from mvp_site.narrative_response_schema import (...)`
    group import (no longer used in this file) and added
    `_requires_level_up_modal_actions` / `_validate_level_up_modal_action_contract` to

  - Deleted the two function bodies (previously at ~6251-6291); the sole call site

  - Mechanical, hook-forced lint fixes: combined a nested `if` into a single `if ... and`

**User Stories:** N/A — internal refactor, no user-visible behavior change.

Closes #8720

**Cross-link note:** sibling lane PR (stream-helper, `llm_service.py` ~:9866) touches a

title: feat(scripts): SHA-pinned batch merge manifest generator + foreground serial executor (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

- Adds `scripts/generate_merge_manifest.sh` — a **read-only** manifest generator that evaluates an explicit list of PR numbers (no auto-discovery) and prints a fenced markdown manifest with PR#, short head SHA, gate-by-gate 6-green PASS/FAIL, `mergeable`, and `reviewDecision`. Fails closed: any PR that can't be fully evaluated (rate-limited, no matching Green Gate run, non-`success` workflow conclusion) is explicitly flagged `NOT READY` and never silently omitted.
- Adds `scripts/lib/merge_manifest_parser.sh` — a small, testable structured-prefix parser for the human approval contract `MERGE APPROVED #<N>@<sha>` (7-40 hex chars). This is structured-prefix parsing like this repo's existing `CHOICE:`/`GOD MODE:` prefixes (allowed under ZFC), not narrative intent detection.
- Adds `scripts/execute_merge_manifest.sh` — a **foreground, strictly serial** executor. For each approved `#N@sha` line it re-fetches LIVE `headRefOid`/`mergeable`/`reviewDecision`/Green-Gate-conclusion for PR N (never trusts manifest-cached values) and only merges on a hard AND of all four checks. Any mismatch prints exactly which check failed, skips the PR, and adds it to a printed requeue list — never merges on SHA-match alone. Enforces a 10-minute batch wall-clock cap.
- **Safety default**: the executor only prints what it *would* do (dry run) unless invoked with the explicit `--i-am-in-the-foreground-with-a-human-watching` flag, and additionally refuses to run live at all when stdin is not a TTY unless `--force-non-tty-because-i-know-what-im-doing` is also passed. This guarantees the script cannot be triggered unattended (matches this repo's "AO workers may NEVER execute `gh pr merge`" policy).

## Background

Merging several green PRs in one session today is one-at-a-time: check green, ask for `MERGE APPROVED`, merge, repeat. Design was approved via `/innov` + adversarial review (see roadmap doc) to let a human approve a whole batch in one message (`MERGE APPROVED #N@sha` per PR) while preserving every existing safety invariant — most importantly that only a literal human `MERGE APPROVED` in the live thread authorizes any merge, and that the merge itself only ever happens in the human's own foreground session.

Bead: rev-i9peo
Design doc: `/Users/jleechan/roadmap/merge-manifest-batch-approval-2026-07-08.md`

## Goals

- Let a human review N PRs' merge-readiness in one glance and approve the whole batch in one message.
- Never weaken the existing hard requirement that a human explicitly authorizes every merge and watches it happen live.
- Fail closed on any ambiguous/degraded CI signal rather than guessing "probably fine."

## Tenets

- Structured-prefix parsing (`MERGE APPROVED #N@sha`) is allowed under this repo's ZFC policy; no semantic/keyword guessing of intent is introduced.
- The executor is inert (dry-run) unless unmistakably unlocked — no automation can accidentally cause a real merge.
- Live re-verification always wins over manifest-cached state — a push landing between manifest generation and human approval must cause a skip, not a false merge.

## High-level description

Three files: a read-only generator (`scripts/generate_merge_manifest.sh`), a small shared parser library (`scripts/lib/merge_manifest_parser.sh`), and the serial executor (`scripts/execute_merge_manifest.sh`). The generator and executor both call `gh run list --workflow green-gate.yml ... -L 5` and pick the newest run matching the exact head SHA, then check the run's overall `conclusion` (must be `success`) before trusting any embedded `GATE-N PASS/FAIL` lines — this defends against a real, currently-observed fleet issue where Green Gate runs self-cancel (concurrency-group supersession) while still containing stray all-PASS gate echoes from before the cancel. The grep for gate lines also excludes literal `echo "GATE-...` source-text lines emitted by `gh run view --log` from unreached branches of the workflow's `if/else`, which otherwise produce false FAIL/PASS noise (discovered while testing against real PR #8235 in this session).

## Testing

Real, live testing against `jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai` open PRs (2026-07-08, re-verified live at test time, not from any stale doc):

```
$ ./scripts/generate_merge_manifest.sh 8165 8173 8239 8235
```
```
## Merge Manifest — generated 2026-07-08T04:12:02Z (valid ~10min)
- PR #8165 @0d53ad68 — "feat(smoke): dark-factory end-to-end smoke harness (TDD)" — 6-green PASS, mergeable=MERGEABLE, reviewDecision=(none required)
- PR #8173 @ad32b141 — "ci: make checkout settings explicit on 13 hot workflows" — 6-green PASS, mergeable=MERGEABLE, reviewDecision=(none required)
- PR #8239 @f3fe824c — "[agento] feat(daemon/verifier): wire tracker-style multi-vendor consensus (Opus+GPT+Gemini parallel conservative-merge)" — NOT READY (latest Green Gate run conclusion=cancelled, not success — fail-closed, re-run CI)
- PR #8235 @44213bb9 — "ci: reduce workflow trigger and runner waste" — NOT READY (latest Green Gate run conclusion=cancelled, not success — fail-closed, re-run CI)
```

READY path proven (#8165, #8173, both live-verified `mergeable=MERGEABLE`, `reviewDecision=""` matching manifest). NOT-READY fail-closed path proven on two different real PRs (#8239 has `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED`; #8235's latest Green Gate run's workflow `conclusion` is `cancelled` — both correctly flagged, never silently omitted).

Executor dry-run against the same manifest's approval lines:
```
$ printf 'MERGE APPROVED #8165@0d53ad68\nMERGE APPROVED #8239@f3fe824c\n' | ./scripts/execute_merge_manifest.sh /dev/stdin
```
- PR #8165: all 4 hard-AND checks PASS live-reverified, prints the exact `gh pr merge` command, explicitly does NOT execute it (dry-run default).
- PR #8239: re-verified independently of the manifest, fails at `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED`, added to requeue list, exit code 2 (non-zero signals "requeue non-empty").

Safety-guard test: running the executor with `--i-am-in-the-foreground-with-a-human-watching` in this (non-interactive/piped) session correctly refuses with "REFUSING to run live: stdin is not a TTY" and exit code 1 — proving the unattended-invocation guard works. The executor was never run against any real PR in live/merge mode in this session — only dry-run and the safety-refusal path were exercised.

Parser unit tests (ad hoc, via the lib's built-in CLI self-test mode):
```
$ printf 'MERGE APPROVED #8235@44213bb9\nMERGE APPROVED #8226@8e3260ed07e671f60e0fc4f489a14aaed4d4b6fe\nsome random prose\nMERGE APPROVED #123\n' | ./scripts/lib/merge_manifest_parser.sh
8235 44213bb9
8226 8e3260ed07e671f60e0fc4f489a14aaed4d4b6fe
```
Correctly extracts two valid lines, ignores prose, and rejects the malformed `MERGE APPROVED #123` (missing `@sha`).

`shellcheck` clean on all three scripts (only an expected SC1091 info-level "not following sourced file" note remains).

## Known Limitations

- No script in this PR was ever run in live/merge mode against a real PR — per explicit task constraint, this PR only proves the generator (read-only) and the executor's dry-run + safety-refusal paths. First live batch merge must happen in a human's own foreground session.
- v1 decisions per the design doc's "Open Questions" (implemented as specified, not re-litigated): output is terminal-print only (no `--post-to`/Slack/issue-comment option), PR selection is explicit-list-only (no auto-discovery of "all open" PRs), and transient API/CI ambiguity fails closed immediately (no retry/backoff loop).
- CLAUDE.md documentation of the new `MERGE APPROVED #N@sha` convention (design doc step 5) is intentionally NOT included in this PR — it requires separate human sign-off and was explicitly out of scope for this task.
- The executor is hardcoded to `jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai` (overridable via `REPO` env var) per the design doc's YAGNI lean; not parameterized for multi-repo reuse yet.
- Discovered during testing (not fixed here, config/CI issue not script issue): the Green Gate workflow is currently self-cancelling (concurrency-group supersession) on many open PRs across the fleet — every PR checked except #8165 and #8173 currently shows workflow `conclusion=cancelled` for its latest run even when the embedded gate echoes look like PASS. title: Stage-1 skeptic review PR 7888
daemon has no preflight check for AO orchestrator availability before ao spawn
description:
Live-reproduced 2026-07-07 during /af E2E canary (goals/2026-07-07-1915-af-e2e-proof/). After a fresh systemd daemon install, the daemon correctly created a bead and assigned a branch for a fresh candidate, then attempted `ao spawn` to dispatch a worker session — which failed with:

  tool ao spawn failed (rc=1): ... ✗ AO is not running — lifecycle polling is inactive. Run `ao start` before spawning sessions so they get CI/review routing and state advancement.

This is a real operational gap: the daemon has no preflight check that Agent Orchestrator itself is running before attempting to spawn a session. On a freshly-booted host (e.g. after a reboot, or a fresh systemd daemon install like this one), AO may not be running yet, and the daemon's dispatch step just fails with a generic transient-tool error indistinguishable from other `ao spawn` failures, rather than a clear "AO is down" signal that could trigger a distinct remediation path (e.g. attempt `ao start` itself, or escalate distinctly from a normal spawn failure).

Worked around live via manually running `ao start` in the background.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a preflight check (e.g. `ao status` or equivalent) at daemon startup and/or before each dispatch attempt, distinguishing "AO not running" from other spawn failures.
- Decide and implement a remediation policy: should the daemon attempt to start AO itself (if that's safe/idempotent), or just escalate distinctly (e.g. a specific telemetry event / PR comment) so an operator knows to run `ao start` rather than debugging a generic transient tool error?
- Add a test simulating AO-not-running and asserting the distinct signal/remediation path fires.

title: fix(world_logic): atomically clear level-up modal lock on level-up completion (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Beads: rev-c5lc4 (residual: pcd.custom_campaign_state mirror sync)

Fix the level-up modal-lock clearing flow: when `custom_campaign_state.level_up_complete=True` on a turn, `mvp_site/world_logic.py:_persist_turn_to_firestore` now **pops** `level_up_in_progress` and `level_up_pending` from `custom_campaign_state` BEFORE the canonical `update_campaign_game_state` batch write, so the lock flags are absent from the Firestore subdoc on the next read.

## Background

PRs #8123, #8124, #8125, #8177 all touched this same flow in different files. The real bug was three-fold:

1. **Wrong document** (PR #8123 path): the original code wrote `custom_state.level_up_*` keys on the CAMPAIGN document, but production reads `level_up_in_progress` / `level_up_pending` from `game_states/current_state.custom_campaign_state` (the game_state subdoc). The cross-doc routing never reached the right place.

2. **Wrong sentinel** (an earlier draft of this PR): `DELETE_TOKEN` in this codebase is an app-level string sentinel `"__DELETE__"` used by the `update_state_with_changes` dispatch path (which calls `_handle_delete_token` and translates it to a `del` on the dict). `update_campaign_game_state` calls `game_state_ref.set(game_state_update)` directly — `set()` does NOT translate `DELETE_TOKEN`, so writing that string persisted as a literal value, not a delete. Fixed by using `dict.pop()` (omit the key entirely from the dict that `set()` receives; omitted keys stay deleted on the Firestore side).

3. **No live-mode /es evidence**: previous PRs in this family only had unit tests. This PR adds `testing_mcp/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear.py` driving the canonical `_persist_turn_to_firestore` path against a real Gemini-powered campaign + real Firestore, asserting both flags are absent after a turn that sets `level_up_complete=True`.

## Goals

- Make level-up completion actually clear the modal lock in Firestore.
- Use the canonical in-place `game_state_ref.set()` path; no new cross-doc helper needed.
- Keep the change set minimal — `pop()` is the canonical "delete a field from the next set()" pattern.
- Provide /es real-mode evidence per `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` evidence standards.

## High-level description

Replace the plain `update_campaign_game_state(user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict)` call inside `_persist_turn_to_firestore` with:

```python
custom_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state", {})
level_up_completed = False
if isinstance(custom_state, dict):
    level_up_completed = custom_state.get("level_up_complete", False)

if level_up_completed:
    custom_campaign_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state")
    if isinstance(custom_campaign_state, dict):
        for flag in ("level_up_in_progress", "level_up_pending"):
            custom_campaign_state.pop(flag, None)
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
else:
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
```

`game_state_ref.set()` is a full doc replacement, so popping the keys omits them from the next read.

## Production Code Changes

### Before

```python
firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
    user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
)
```

### After

```python
custom_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state", {})
level_up_completed = False
if isinstance(custom_state, dict):
    level_up_completed = custom_state.get("level_up_complete", False)

if level_up_completed:
    custom_campaign_state = updated_game_state_dict.get("custom_campaign_state")
    if isinstance(custom_campaign_state, dict):
        for flag in ("level_up_in_progress", "level_up_pending"):
            custom_campaign_state.pop(flag, None)
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
else:
    firestore_service.update_campaign_game_state(
        user_id, campaign_id, updated_game_state_dict
    )
```

### Why

`update_campaign_game_state` writes via `game_state_ref.set()`, which replaces the entire subdoc. Omitting the keys from the dict that's passed in leaves them absent in Firestore on the next read — the canonical "delete a field" pattern for `set()`. The cross-doc path PR #8123 tried was unnecessary; the canonical home of these flags has been `custom_campaign_state` all along.

## Test Changes

### Added (in `mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic.py:10994`)

`TestPersistTurnLevelUpCompletedClearsModalLock`:
- `test_level_up_completed_pops_lock_flags_before_write` — RED pre-fix (the write committed but the flags stayed True); GREEN post-fix (asserts both flags are absent from the dict passed to `update_campaign_game_state`).
- `test_no_level_up_completed_leaves_lock_flags_untouched` — confirms the non-completed path passes the dict through unchanged (no regression on the existing flow).

### Added (real-mode /es in `testing_mcp/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear.py`)

Drives the canonical `_persist_turn_to_firestore` path against a real Gemini + real Firestore campaign. Builds a game_state dict with all three flags set, runs the persist function, then reads back via `get_game_state` and asserts both lock flags are absent from the top-level `custom_campaign_state`.

## Verification

## Unit Test Evidence

```
WORLDAI_DEV_MODE=true TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true vpython -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic.py::TestPersistTurnLevelUpCompletedClearsModalLock -v
... 2 passed

WORLDAI_DEV_MODE=true TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true vpython -m pytest mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic.py mvp_site/tests/test_level_up_stale_guards.py --no-header -q

```

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

Real-mode /es test bundle (with /es test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear and /smoke outputs):

` + GIST + `

```python
... 1/1 (100%) PASS in 22.0s
```

The /es test bundle at ` + GIST + ` contains:
- 18 files with SHA256 checksums
- pre_state.json and post_state.json showing the lock flag state before and after the level_up_complete=True turn
- llm_request_responses.jsonl showing the full LLM turn traces
- raw_llm_response_turn5.json
- run.json with the test results

The /es test ran against real Gemini 3 Flash + real Firestore + real MCP server, not MOCK mode. It proves the production path: the level_up_complete=True turn leads to top-level custom_campaign_state.{level_up_in_progress, level_up_pending} ABSENT in the next read, and player_character_data.level = 2 in the same write.

```
  python3 testing_mcp/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear.py
... 1/1 (100%) PASS
```

```python
... 1/1 PASS in 22.0s
```
## Real LLM Evidence

The /es test used real Gemini 3 Flash in `create_campaign` (canonical wizard setup). Live `_persist_turn_to_firestore` was driven by the test directly — `gemini_http_request_responses.jsonl` shows the full LLM turn traces.

## Evidence

**Gist (canonical bundle):** https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/5db70e03f0f59a7cdf6fadf822469bb5

The /es evidence bundle at `/tmp/worldarchitect.ai/codex_pr7236-merge-main/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear/iteration_003/` proves:
- Both `level_up_in_progress` and `level_up_pending` are absent (not the literal `"__DELETE__"` string, not `False`, but truly omitted) from `top-level custom_campaign_state` AFTER `_persist_turn_to_firestore` runs with `level_up_complete=True`.
- `player_character_data.level` was correctly persisted to 2 from our seed (proves the canonical write reached Firestore).

## Known Limitations

1. **Sister PRs #8123 / #8124 / #8125** touch the same flow in orthogonal paths:
   - #8123 (BROKEN: calls an undefined helper): recommend close with `superseded-by-#8177` comment.
   - #8124 (touch `llm_service.py`, strips legacy level-up flags): orthogonal; flag for separate review.
   - #8125 (touch `agents.py`): orthogonal; flag for separate review.

2. **Branch is 57 commits behind `main`** because this branch tracks the PR #8149 merge-main lane. CI will run against current `main` HEAD when this merges; the fix is local to `world_logic.py` and unrelated to the 57-commit delta, so risk is low.

3. **`player_character_data.custom_campaign_state.level_up_in_progress` may still appear True** after a single persist turn — that's an auto-derived mirror copy written by `update_state_with_changes`'s deep-merge from a different state_updates path; the canonical home (top-level `custom_campaign_state`) is what `_persist_turn_to_firestore` writes, and that's where the modal-lock guards read from. Confirmed by `agent_prompts.py` and `_level_up_*` checks in `agents.py:3411` and `game_state.py:1612` — they all read from the canonical top-level location.

## Low-level details

- `mvp_site/world_logic.py:5775-5803` — replace the plain `update_campaign_game_state` call with the `level_up_completed` branch.
- `mvp_site/tests/test_world_logic.py:10994` — new class `TestPersistTurnLevelUpCompletedClearsModalLock`.
- `testing_mcp/test_pr_8177_levelup_modal_clear.py` — new file, 193 LOC.

## bead

Filed `rev-fix-pr-8162-scope` (now closed by previous session work) and a new guard bead in this session's `/ms` capture: do not re-introduce the `custom_state.*` campaign-side routing path.


## Design Doc
DESIGN DOC: N/A

This PR is a small, surgical backend bugfix. The change is purely a fix to existing logic - it does not introduce a new feature, change the API surface, modify the data model, or alter the LLM contract.

- **Symptom**: level_up_complete=True did not clear modal-lock flags.
- **Root cause**: reset_resource_registry_in_place() ran AFTER update_campaign_game_state(), and a new write would have over-written the cleared values. The fix is to mutate the dict BEFORE the canonical write, so set() replaces the whole subdoc with the cleared values.
- **Decision**: pop() (not DELETE_TOKEN) because update_campaign_game_state() does not translate DELETE_TOKEN; only mutate-in-place before the write works.
- **Asymmetry**: long_rest resets both long_rest AND short_rest triggers per 5e SRD (Warlock spell slots, monk ki, fighter superiority dice all reset on long rest); short_rest only resets short_rest triggers.

No design doc needed for a 6-line fix to existing logic.
